把两者的稳定性结论完全说反了，按这个理解选型，遇到插入照样错位。
认为两种分页方式没有任何差异，会让人忽视真实存在的工程取舍。
两种分页本质是应用层逻辑，任何主流数据库都能实现其中任意一种，和数据库类型无关。
optionExplanations_en: Cursor anchors to a specific record so inserts don't shift it, but jumping to an arbitrary page is hard; offset can jump but shifts under inserts, a symmetric tradeoff.
Reverses which one is actually stable, so choosing this way still breaks under inserts.
Claiming no difference at all makes people ignore a real engineering tradeoff.
Both are application-layer logic; either can be implemented on any mainstream database, unrelated to database type.

scenario: 高流量实时信息流：新内容不断插入，用户无限下滑，绝不能出现重复或漏条。
scenario_en: A high-traffic real-time feed keeps receiving new content while users scroll down, and the feed must not duplicate or miss items.
q: 应选哪种分页？
q_en: Which pagination approach should you choose?
options: offset 分页
不分页，一次全部返回
cursor 分页
按随机顺序抽样返回
options_en: Offset pagination
No pagination, return everything at once
Cursor pagination
Return a random sample each time
why: 实时插入 + 顺序下滑正是 cursor 分页的主场：锚定上次读到的记录，新数据不会打乱翻页。面试里「记得提分页」比选哪种更重要。
why_en: For real-time feeds with constant inserts, cursor-based pagination stays stable, and remembering to include pagination matters more than which type you pick.
whenOtherWins: 静态或低频变动的数据、或产品需要「跳到第 N 页」时，offset 分页更简单够用。
tradeoff: cursor 的翻页稳定性 vs offset 的实现简单和跳页能力
optionExplanations: 新内容不断插入会让「第几条」的位置持续漂移，导致重复或遗漏。
信息流理论上无限增长，一次性返回既不现实也没必要。
锚定上次读到的记录，不管中间插入多少新内容，翻页结果依然稳定，正是实时下滑场景的主场。
破坏了信息流该有的时间顺序，也无法保证不重复不遗漏。
optionExplanations_en: Constant inserts keep shifting the 'nth record' position, causing duplicates or misses.
A feed grows without bound in theory, returning it all at once is neither realistic nor necessary.
Anchored to the last record seen, paging stays stable no matter how much new content lands in between, exactly the real-time-scroll use case.
Breaks the feed's expected time order and still can't guarantee no duplicates or misses.

q: URL 版本化（/v1/events → /v2/events）的主要优点是？
q_en: What is the main benefit of URL versioning such as /v1/events to /v2/events?
options: 让 URL 变得更简洁
版本一眼可见，服务端按前缀路由即可
彻底不需要维护旧版本代码
自动兼容所有旧客户端，无需任何额外工作
options_en: It makes URLs more concise
The version is visible at a glance and the server can route by prefix
It eliminates the need to maintain old-version code entirely
It automatically makes every old client compatible with no extra work
why: 版本号直接写在路径里：客户端一眼可见、服务端按前缀路由即可，实现和解释都简单——这是它成为面试默认答案的原因。
why_en: URL versioning is explicit and easy: clients see the version in the path and servers route each version to its own code path.
optionExplanations: 带上 /v1、/v2 前缀反而让 URL 变长了，这不是它的卖点。
版本号写进路径：客户端一眼可见，服务端按前缀路由即可，调试、写文档、配置网关都直接受益。
只要还有客户端在用 v1，后端就得继续维护 v1 的代码路径，版本化不会让旧代码消失。
版本化正是因为不能自动兼容才需要的机制，这个说法自相矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Adding a /v1 or /v2 prefix actually makes the URL longer, not the real selling point.
The version sits right in the path: clients see it at a glance and servers route by prefix, a direct win for debugging, docs, and gateway config.
As long as any client still calls v1, the backend keeps maintaining v1's code path; versioning doesn't make old code vanish.
Versioning exists precisely because automatic compatibility isn't possible, so this claim contradicts itself.

q: header 版本化（Accept-Version: v2）相对 URL 版本化的取舍是？
q_en: What tradeoff does header versioning have compared with URL versioning?
options: header 版本化总是响应更快
header 版本化在浏览器里更容易直接测试
header 版本化对开发者来说一眼就能看出版本
URL 更干净更合规范，但对开发者不直观
options_en: Header versioning is always faster to respond
Header versioning is easier to test directly in a browser
Header versioning lets developers see the version at a glance
Cleaner URLs and more spec-compliant, but less obvious to developers
why: 把版本挪进请求头能保持 URL 干净、更贴 HTTP 标准，代价是可见性差：开发者看不见、浏览器直接访问也不方便。
why_en: Header versioning keeps URLs cleaner and follows HTTP standards better but is less obvious to developers and harder to test in a browser.
tradeoff: header 版本化的 URL 简洁和规范性 vs URL 版本化的可见性和易测试性
codeSample:
# URL 版本化：路径直接带版本，浏览器可直接访问
GET /v2/events

# Header 版本化：URL 不变，版本放请求头，浏览器地址栏看不到
GET /events
Accept-Version: v2
optionExplanations: 两种方式本质上都路由到相同的处理逻辑，速度没有差别。
浏览器地址栏看不到请求头，直接测试反而更麻烦，需要额外工具。
开发者得先翻请求头才知道版本，直观性反而不如写在 URL 里。
牺牲的是看得见摸得着：URL 变干净了，但版本号要翻请求头才找得到，浏览器也没法直接戳。
optionExplanations_en: Both approaches route to the same handling logic underneath, no real speed difference.
The browser address bar can't show headers, making direct testing harder and requiring extra tooling.
Developers must inspect headers just to know the version, less obvious than seeing it in the URL.
Moving the version into a header keeps URLs clean and closer to HTTP standards, at the cost of visibility: developers can't see it and browsers can't hit it directly.

scenario: 面试中公开 API 需要演进策略以免破坏老客户端，你要快速给出一个版本化方案并继续推进。
scenario_en: In an interview, a public API needs an evolution strategy that will not break older clients, and you need to give a quick versioning answer before moving on.
q: 更稳妥的默认选择是？
q_en: What is the safer default choice?
options: URL 版本化（/v1/events）
header 版本化（API-Version: 2）
永不改版本号，直接静默改字段含义
让每个客户端自己判断兼容性
options_en: URL versioning: /v1/events
Header versioning: API-Version: 2
Never bump a version, silently change field meanings instead
Let each client figure out compatibility on its own
why: 选 URL 版本化不是为了给最终用户看，而是让客户端、SDK、网关和后端路由都一眼知道契约版本。/v1 给老客户端继续用，/v2 给新字段/新语义，面试里最直观。
why_en: URL versioning is not for end users; it makes the contract version obvious to clients, SDKs, gateways, and backend routing. /v1 can keep serving old clients while /v2 introduces new fields or semantics.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官追问「URL 必须干净、版本属于内容协商」或内部平台可统一工具链，再谈 header 版本化。
tradeoff: URL 版本化的普适易懂 vs header 版本化的规范简洁
codeSample:
# 老客户端仍然调用旧契约
GET /v1/events/123
# -> { "name": "Concert", "date": "2026-08-01" }

# 新客户端显式选择新契约
GET /v2/events/123
# -> { "title": "Concert", "starts_at": "2026-08-01T20:00:00Z", "venue": {...} }

# Header 版本化也可以，但地址栏/日志/文档里不如 /v2 直观
GET /events/123
API-Version: 2
optionExplanations: 老客户端固定走 /v1、新客户端显式走 /v2，网关和日志也一眼能看懂，面试里最直观。
URL 更干净，但开发者要看 header 才知道版本，curl/Postman/网关配置也多一步。
老客户端会在毫无预警的情况下读到语义已变的字段，直接破坏兼容性。
客户端根本没有能力判断服务端字段语义是否变了，这不是一个可行方案。
optionExplanations_en: Old clients keep hitting /v1, new clients explicitly go to /v2, and gateways and logs read it at a glance, the most obvious choice in an interview.
URLs stay cleaner, but developers must inspect headers and tools like curl or gateways need an extra step.
Old clients read a field whose meaning silently changed with zero warning, directly breaking compatibility.
Clients have no way to detect that server-side field semantics changed, not a workable plan.

q: 「验证请求确实来自 john@example.com」和「检查 John 只能取消自己的 booking」分别属于？
q_en: What are 'verifying the request is really from john@example.com' and 'checking John can only cancel his own booking' called?
options: 两者都属于认证（authentication）
前者是认证（你是谁），后者是授权（能做什么）
前者是授权，后者是认证，正好反过来
两者都属于授权（authorization）
options_en: Both belong to authentication
The first is authentication, who you are; the second is authorization, what you can do
The first is authorization and the second is authentication, exactly reversed
Both belong to authorization
why: 认证回答「你是谁」（身份），授权回答「你能不能做这件事」（权限）——John 能登录 ≠ John 能取消任何人的订单。
why_en: Authentication verifies who the user is, while authorization checks whether that user is allowed to perform the specific action.
tradeoff: 认证验证身份 vs 授权验证操作权限

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证身份——证明用户是他声称的那个人。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Authentication verifies identity, proving the user is who they claim to be.

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证权限——检查该用户是否被允许执行所请求的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Authorization verifies permission, checking whether the user is allowed to perform the requested action.

optionExplanations: 把身份确认和权限检查混为一谈，会让人以为登录成功就等于什么都能做。
先证明「我是 John」是认证，再判「John 能不能碰这张订单」是授权，两步缺一不可。
把两者的对应关系完全颠倒，「验证身份」被当成了权限检查，逻辑错位。
如果两者都算授权，「你是谁」这一步该怎么验证就没有着落了。
optionExplanations_en: Lumping identity check and permission check together makes it seem like logging in means you can do anything.
Authentication answers 'who are you,' authorization answers 'can you do this,' John being logged in doesn't mean John can cancel anyone's booking.
Completely reverses which is which, treating identity verification as the permission check.
If both count as authorization, there's no step left to verify who you actually are.

q: 补全两个安全概念：
q_en: Fill in the two security concepts:
text: {{认证}}（authentication）验证身份——证明用户是他声称的那个人；{{授权}}（authorization）验证权限——检查该用户是否被允许执行所请求的操作。
why: API 要回答的第一个问题就是这两件事：谁在请求，以及他有没有资格做这件事。
why_en: Authentication proves identity and authorization checks permissions, the first two questions every API must answer.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Req["Request"] --> Authn["authentication: who are you"]
    Authn --> Authz["authorization: can you do this"]
    Authz --> Handler["handler executes"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证身份——证明用户是他声称的那个人。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Authentication verifies identity, proving the user is who they claim to be.

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证权限——检查该用户是否被允许执行所请求的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Authorization verifies permission, checking whether the user is allowed to perform the requested action.

scenario: 要把系统的 API 开放给第三方开发者做程序化接入，同时内部 booking 服务也要调用 payment 服务，都不是「人类用户登录」的场景。
scenario_en: The system exposes APIs to third-party developers for programmatic access, and the internal booking service also calls the payment service; neither case is a human login flow.
q: 这两类场景最合适的认证方式是？
q_en: What authentication method best fits these two scenarios?
options: 用户名 + 密码
短信验证码
浏览器 Cookie 会话
API key（放请求头）
options_en: Username plus password
SMS verification code
Browser cookie session
An API key in a request header
why: API key 是「应用的密码」：服务器间通信和第三方开发者程序化接入的标准做法——为每个客户端生成唯一 key，随请求头携带、服务端查验。
why_en: API keys act like passwords for applications, ideal for server-to-server calls and third-party developer access.
whenOtherWins: 面向真人用户的 Web/移动会话要用 JWT 或数据库会话——API key 不过期、不携带用户上下文，不适合用户端。
tradeoff: API key 面向应用身份的简单查库 vs JWT/会话面向用户身份的上下文携带
codeSample:
GET /events
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc123def456...
# 服务端查库：sk_live_abc123... -> 客户端身份 + 权限 + 限流配置

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端为每个客户端应用生成的长随机字符串，用作程序化访问的身份凭证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a long random string the server issues per client application, used as an identity credential for programmatic access.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 请求头，用来携带身份凭证（如 API key 或 JWT）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Authorization is the HTTP header used to carry an identity credential such as an API key or a JWT.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览器保存并随请求自动携带的一小段数据，常用于维持会话状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cookie is a small piece of data the browser stores and automatically sends with requests, often used to maintain session state.

optionExplanations: 服务器和第三方程序都不是「人」，没有用户名密码可输入。
程序化调用没有手机号，也没有人在场接收验证码。
服务器间调用和第三方脚本都不经过浏览器，没有 Cookie 可用。
为每个应用/开发者生成唯一 key、随请求头携带，天然契合服务器间和第三方程序化接入。
optionExplanations_en: Neither a server nor a third-party program is a human with a username and password to type.
Programmatic calls have no phone number and no human around to receive a code.
Server-to-server calls and third-party scripts never go through a browser, so there's no cookie to use.
A unique key generated per app or developer, carried in a header, fits server-to-server and third-party access naturally.

q: 为什么用户端产品几乎从不该用 API key 做用户认证？
q_en: Why should user-facing products almost never use API keys for user authentication?
options: API key 不过期、没有用户上下文
因为 API key 的生成成本太高
因为 API key 技术上无法放进 HTTP 请求头
因为 API key 只支持 GET 请求
options_en: API keys never lapse and carry no user context
Because API keys are too expensive to generate
Because API keys technically cannot be placed in an HTTP header
Because API keys only support GET requests
why: API key 面向应用而非人：没有过期机制、没有用户上下文，还要求用户保管长字符串——用户会话需要的恰恰是这些。
why_en: API keys never lapse and carry no user context, and users should not manage long cryptographic strings, so they are wrong for user-facing auth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端为每个客户端应用生成的长随机字符串，用作程序化访问的身份凭证，通常不携带用户上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a long random string the server issues per client application for programmatic access, and it typically carries no user context.

optionExplanations: 它是发给程序用的凭证，不会自动作废也读不出是哪个用户，而这两样正是用户会话离不开的。
生成一个随机字符串的成本几乎为零，不是真正的原因。
API key 本来就是设计放进 Authorization 头传输的。
API key 对 HTTP 方法没有任何限制，任何方法都能带上它。
optionExplanations_en: API keys are built for applications, not people: they don't lapse and carry no user context, exactly what a user session needs.
Generating a random string costs essentially nothing, not the real reason.
API keys are specifically designed to travel in the Authorization header.
API keys carry no restriction on HTTP method, any method can carry one.

scenario: 用户登录后，前端拿到一个 access token，之后每次请求都把它放进 Authorization header。
scenario_en: After login, the frontend receives an access token and sends it in the Authorization header on later requests.
q: JWT（JSON Web Token）的核心机制是？
q_en: What is the core mechanism of a JWT?
options: 把会话数据存在服务器内存里，靠内存查找识别用户
每次请求都查一次数据库来验证身份
用户信息签名编码进令牌，验签即可信任
把用户密码加密后在每次请求里来回传输
options_en: Store session data in server memory and look it up in memory to identify the user
Query the database on every single request to verify identity
User info is signed into the token itself, trusted once verified
Encrypt the user's password and send it back and forth with every request
why: JWT 通常不是加密，而是 base64url 编码 + 签名。payload 可读，只放 user_id、role、exp 等非秘密信息；服务端验签防篡改，过了才信。
why_en: A JWT is usually base64url encoding plus a signature, not encryption. Its payload is readable, so it carries non-secret claims such as user_id, role, and exp; the server trusts it only after verifying the signature.
whenOtherWins: 要隐藏 payload 用 JWE/服务端 session；要立即踢下线，用数据库 session 或 blacklist。
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as Client
    participant A as Auth Server
    participant API as API Service
    U->>C: 输入账号密码
    C->>A: POST /login over HTTPS
    A->>A: 校验密码并签发 JWT
    A-->>C: 返回 signed JWT
    C->>API: Authorization: Bearer JWT
    API->>API: 验签 + 检查 exp
    API-->>C: 返回受保护数据

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息签名编码进令牌本身、无需服务端存储会话的身份凭证格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT, or JSON Web Token, is a signed identity credential format that encodes user info into the token itself, with no server-side session storage needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种可逆编码，不是加密；任何拿到 token 的人都能解码 header/payload。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: base64url is reversible encoding, not encryption; anyone holding the token can decode the header and payload.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端用 secret/private key 对 header.payload 计算出的防篡改校验值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A signature is a tamper check computed by the server over header.payload using a secret or private key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 会加密内容的 JWT 变体；普通 JWT/JWS 主要是签名，不隐藏 payload。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JWE is the encrypted JWT variant; a normal signed JWT/JWS mainly signs data and does not hide the payload.

optionExplanations: 会话状态存在服务器一侧，扩容和多实例部署时状态难以共享。
每次请求都要一次数据库往返，高并发下数据库压力很大。
身份信息签名编码进令牌本身，任何持有验证密钥的服务都能独立验签，无需查库，天然适合分布式部署。
反复加密传输密码本身既是安全隐患，也不是 JWT 的实际做法。
optionExplanations_en: Keeps session state server-side, hard to share once you scale out to multiple instances.
Every request makes a database round trip, heavy load under high concurrency.
Identity info is signed into the token itself, so any service holding the key can verify it locally without a database lookup, a natural fit for distributed deployment.
Repeatedly sending the password itself is a security risk and not actually how JWT works.

scenario: 分布式系统：移动 App 的请求先到 API 网关，再转发给 booking 服务，两处都要能独立确认用户身份，不想每跳都查会话库。
scenario_en: In a distributed system, mobile requests hit an API gateway and then a booking service, and both places need to verify user identity without querying a session store on every hop.
q: 最合适的方案是？
q_en: What solution fits best?
options: 让网关和每个下游服务都分别单独去查一次中心会话数据库
JWT：任何持有验证密钥的服务都能独立验签，网关验证后可放心转发
把用户密码原样随每次请求一起转发
只在网关做一次身份认证，后端的每个服务都完全不再做任何校验
options_en: Have the gateway and every downstream service each independently query a central session database
JWT: any service holding the verification key can validate independently, so the gateway can trust and forward
Forward the user's raw password along with every single request
Authenticate once at the gateway only, and every backend service skips verification entirely after that
why: JWT 特别适合分布式系统：验证密钥分发到位后，网关和每个服务都能本地验签、读出用户上下文，无需共享会话存储。
why_en: JWTs suit distributed systems because any service holding the verification key can validate the token independently without shared session storage.
whenOtherWins: 需要「立即吊销会话」这类集中控制时，数据库会话（服务端可随时删除）比无状态 JWT 更可控。
tradeoff: JWT 的无状态独立验证 vs 数据库会话的集中可控（可即时吊销）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息签名编码进令牌本身、无需服务端存储会话的身份凭证格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT, or JSON Web Token, is a signed identity credential format that encodes user info into the token itself, with no server-side session storage needed.

optionExplanations: 中心会话库会成为单点瓶颈，和「不想每跳都查库」的要求直接冲突。
拿到同一把验证密钥，网关和下游服务各自就能就地验签、读出是谁在请求，谁都不用回头查一次共享存储。
密码在系统内到处传递，泄漏面会大幅增加。
跳过下游校验意味着下游服务不知道是谁在请求，也做不了精细授权。
optionExplanations_en: A central session store becomes a single-point bottleneck, directly conflicting with wanting no per-hop lookup.
Once the verification key is distributed, the gateway and every service can verify locally and read user context, fully meeting independent verification without a database hop.
The password travels throughout the system, dramatically increasing exposure.
Skipping downstream verification leaves downstream services unable to know who's asking or do fine-grained authorization.

scenario: 客户端带 access token 请求 API，但 token 的 exp 已经过期。
scenario_en: The client calls an API with an access token whose exp has already passed.
q: JWT payload 里，哪个字段让令牌自动失效、避免永久有效？
q_en: Which JWT payload field makes the token lapse automatically instead of staying valid forever?
options: user_id
email
role
exp
options_en: user_id
email
role
exp
why: exp 是过期时间戳。access token 过期后 API 拒绝它；客户端通常用 refresh token 找 Auth Server 换一个新的 access token，而不是修改旧 token。
why_en: The exp claim is the expiration timestamp. Once an access token expires, the API rejects it; the client usually uses a refresh token to ask the auth server for a new access token.
whenOtherWins: refresh token 也过期、被撤销或设备登出时，必须重新登录。
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant API as API Service
    participant A as Auth Server
    C->>API: Request with expired access token
    API-->>C: 401 token expired
    C->>A: POST /refresh with refresh token
    A->>A: 校验 refresh token
    A-->>C: new access token
    C->>API: Retry with new access token
    API-->>C: 200 OK

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息签名编码进令牌本身的身份凭证格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT, or JSON Web Token, is a signed identity credential format that encodes user info into the token itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: JWT payload 里表示令牌失效时刻的 Unix 时间戳字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: exp is the JWT payload field holding the Unix timestamp at which the token expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 短期令牌，请求 API 时携带；过期后 API 应拒绝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An access token is a short-lived token sent to APIs; the API should reject it after expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 较长期令牌，只交给认证服务换新 access token；可被服务端撤销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A refresh token is a longer-lived token used only with the auth server to obtain a new access token, and it can be revoked server-side.

optionExplanations: 标识具体是哪个用户，验签时不会检查它来判断令牌是否有效。
只是联系方式字段，跟令牌是否失效无关。
用于区分权限等级，不参与超时判定。
exp 是过期时间戳，验签时会拿它和当前时间比较，一过就拒绝，是令牌自动失效的关键。
optionExplanations_en: Identifies which user this is, but verification never checks it to decide validity.
Just a contact-info field, unrelated to whether the token has lapsed.
Distinguishes permission level, plays no part in the timeout check.
exp is the expiration timestamp; verification compares it against the current time and rejects the token once past it, the key to automatic lapsing.

q: 面试里处理认证/授权的推荐姿势是？
q_en: What is the recommended way to handle authentication and authorization in an interview?
options: 点出哪些端点需要认证，说明用 JWT 或数据库会话即可，不深入展开
现场从零开始设计一整套完整的 OAuth2 授权码流程
完全不提任何安全相关的内容
详细手推一遍 JWT 签名算法背后的数学原理
options_en: Call out which endpoints require authentication, say you'd rely on JWT or a database session, no deep dive
Design a complete OAuth2 authorization-code flow entirely from scratch on the spot
Skip mentioning anything security-related at all
Derive the mathematical details behind the JWT signing algorithm in depth
why: JWT 是 token 格式/凭证，常用于自己系统登录后签发 access token；OAuth2 是授权协议，常用于第三方 App 代表用户访问资源。面试里点到即可。
why_en: JWT is a token format or credential often issued after first-party login, while OAuth2 is an authorization protocol commonly used when a third-party app accesses resources on a user's behalf.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Login["User logs into your app"] --> JWT["Auth server issues JWT"]
    Third["Third-party app asks permission"] --> OAuth["OAuth2 consent/code flow"]
    OAuth --> Token["access token, often JWT or opaque"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息签名编码进令牌本身的身份凭证格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT, or JSON Web Token, is a signed identity credential format that encodes user info into the token itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让第三方应用在用户授权下代表用户访问资源的标准授权协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OAuth 2.0 is a standard authorization protocol letting a third-party app access resources on a user's behalf after the user grants consent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端请求 API 时携带的访问凭证；它可以是 JWT，也可以是不透明随机字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An access token is the credential sent to APIs; it can be a JWT or an opaque random string.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端无法自行解读的随机 token；服务端需要查库或 introspection 才知道它代表谁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An opaque token is a random token clients cannot decode; the server must look it up or introspect it to know what it represents.

optionExplanations: 标注哪些端点需要认证、说一句会用 JWT 或数据库会话即可，既展示生产意识，又不占核心架构的讨论时间。
OAuth2 授权码流程涉及第三方、跳转、临时码等一整套机制，远超大多数面试对这一步的要求。
只字不提认证授权，面试官会认为你完全没考虑过安全性。
深入到签名算法的数学证明层面，面试官通常无意考察这个，只会显得跑题。
optionExplanations_en: Flag which endpoints need auth and say you'd use JWT or a database session, that's it, showing production awareness without eating into core architecture time.
A full OAuth2 authorization-code flow involves a third party, redirects, and temporary codes, far beyond what this step expects.
Saying nothing about auth at all reads as a clear security blind spot to the interviewer.
Deriving the signing algorithm's math is rarely what's being tested here and just reads as off-topic.

q: 补全 RBAC（基于角色的访问控制）的结构：
q_en: Fill in the RBAC structure:
text: RBAC（Role-Based Access Control，基于角色的访问控制）把{{角色}}分配给用户、把{{权限}}分配给角色——用户通过角色间接获得权限。
why: RBAC 用「用户→角色→权限」两级映射管理不同类型用户的权限，比逐用户配权限可维护得多。
why_en: RBAC assigns roles to users and permissions to roles, so users gain permissions indirectly through their roles.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把权限分配给角色、再把角色分配给用户的访问控制模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RBAC, role-based access control, is an access model that assigns permissions to roles and roles to users.

q: Ticketmaster 的 RBAC（基于角色的访问控制）设计里，哪些角色-权限映射是合理的？（多选）
q_en: In Ticketmaster's RBAC design, which role-permission mappings are reasonable? (Select all that apply.)
options: customer：可订票、查看自己的 booking
venue_manager：可创建活动、查看自己场馆的销售报表
admin：可管理全局活动/订单/用户，但敏感字段仍按最小权限脱敏和审计
customer：可查看所有用户的 booking
options_en: customer: can book tickets and view their own bookings
venue_manager: can create events and view sales reports for their own venues
admin: can manage global events, bookings, and users, while sensitive fields remain masked and audited under least privilege
customer: can view every user's bookings
why: customer 只能操作自己的数据，venue_manager 管自己场馆；admin 有全局管理能力，但不等于可看原始卡号、私钥或所有敏感字段。「customer 看所有人订单」违反最小权限。
why_en: Customers manage only their own bookings and venue managers handle their own venues. Admins have global management capabilities, but not unrestricted access to raw card data, secrets, or every sensitive field.
codeSample:
Roles:
  customer:      book tickets, view own bookings
  venue_manager: create events, view own venue sales
  admin:         manage events/users/bookings; masked PII/payment data; audited break-glass

Never:
  customer -> view all bookings
  admin    -> raw card/CVV, private keys, password hashes

termDefinitions.meaning: 把权限分配给角色、再把角色分配给用户的访问控制模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RBAC, role-based access control, is an access model that assigns permissions to roles and roles to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个角色只拥有完成其职责所必需的最小权限集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least privilege means each role holds only the minimum set of permissions needed to do its job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能识别个人身份的信息，如姓名、邮箱、电话、地址；后台也应按需展示或脱敏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PII is information that can identify a person, such as name, email, phone, or address, and should be shown only as needed or masked.

termDefinitions.meaning: 紧急情况下临时提升权限的机制，通常要求审批、限时、强审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Break-glass access is temporary emergency privilege elevation, typically requiring approval, time limits, and strong auditing.

optionExplanations: customer 的权限范围限定在自己的订票行为，碰不到别人的数据，符合最小权限。
venue_manager 的权限限定在自己名下的场馆，别的场馆的数据它碰不到。
admin 能处理全局运营，但敏感字段仍受额外脱敏和审计控制，不是无限权限。
让普通用户能看到陌生人的订票记录，隐私和权限双重失控，违反最小权限。
optionExplanations_en: customer permissions are scoped to their own bookings, never touching anyone else's data, matching least privilege.
venue_manager permissions are scoped to their own venues, other venues stay out of reach.
admin can run global operations, but sensitive fields still get masking and audit controls, not unlimited access.
Lets an ordinary user see strangers' bookings, a double failure of privacy and least privilege.

q: 把一次受保护请求（GET /bookings/{id}）的处理流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the protected request flow for GET /bookings/{id} in the correct order:
steps: 网关/服务验证 JWT 签名——认证：确认用户身份
用户登录成功，服务器签发含 user_id、角色、exp 的 JWT
通过后返回 booking 数据
客户端随每次请求携带该 JWT
授权检查：是这个 booking 的所有者或 admin 才放行
why: 顺序：签发令牌 → 携带令牌 → 验签（认证）→ 权限检查（授权）→ 返回数据。认证永远先于授权。
why_en: The flow is issue the token at login, send it with each request, verify the signature to authenticate, check ownership to authorize, then return the data.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant API as API
    participant Auth as Auth service
    participant DB as Database
    C->>API: GET booking
    API->>Auth: verify token
    Auth-->>API: user id
    API->>DB: load booking owner
    API-->>C: allow or reject

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息签名编码进令牌本身的身份凭证格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT, or JSON Web Token, is a signed identity credential format that encodes user info into the token itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: JWT payload 里表示令牌失效时刻的 Unix 时间戳字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: exp is the JWT payload field holding the Unix timestamp at which the token expires.

q: 常见的限流策略有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are common rate-limiting strategies? (Select all that apply.)
options: 按认证用户限流，如每用户每小时 1000 次
对未认证请求按 IP 限流，如每 IP 每小时 100 次
按数据库表名限流
对特定端点单独限流，如订票端点每分钟 10 次
options_en: Per-user limits for authenticated traffic, like 1000 requests per user per hour
Per-IP limits for unauthenticated requests, like 100 requests per IP per hour
Limit by database table name
Endpoint-specific limits, like 10 booking attempts per minute
why: 三个常用维度：per-user（认证流量）、per-IP（匿名流量）、per-endpoint（保护敏感操作，比如防黄牛刷订票）。
why_en: Common strategies are per-user limits for authenticated traffic, per-IP limits for anonymous requests, and endpoint-specific limits for sensitive operations.
optionExplanations: 按认证用户身份限流，能公平限制每个登录用户的请求量。
按来源 IP 限流，是防匿名流量刷接口的第一道防线。
表名是内部实现细节，客户端根本看不到，限流本该作用在 API 入口而不是存储内部。
对订票这类容易被脚本滥用的敏感端点单独限流，精确保护又不影响其他正常流量。
optionExplanations_en: Limiting by authenticated user identity fairly caps how much each logged-in user can call.
Limiting by source IP is the first line of defense against anonymous abuse.
A table name is an internal detail clients never see; rate limiting belongs at the API edge, not inside storage.
A dedicated limit on a scriptable endpoint like booking protects it precisely without touching normal traffic.

q: 客户端超过限流阈值时，应返回哪个状态码？
q_en: Which status code should you return when a client exceeds the rate limit?
options: 403 Forbidden
400 Bad Request
429 Too Many Requests
503 Service Unavailable
options_en: 403 Forbidden
400 Bad Request
429 Too Many Requests
503 Service Unavailable
why: 429 是限流的专用状态码，通常配合 Retry-After 响应头告诉客户端该退避多久再重试，供后续限流器/客户端节流逻辑判断使用。
why_en: When rate limits are exceeded the API should return a 429 Too Many Requests status code, typically paired with a Retry-After header telling the client how long to back off.

termDefinitions.meaning: 响应头，告诉客户端应该等待多少秒后再重试请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retry-After is a response header telling the client how many seconds to wait before retrying.

scenario: 客户端在一分钟内把订票端点打爆，触发了服务端设置的限流阈值。
scenario_en: A client floods the booking endpoint within one minute and trips the server-side rate limit.
optionExplanations: 403 表示「你没有权限」，而限流是「你请求太快」，语义不对。
400 表示请求本身格式有问题，限流场景下请求格式完全合法。
HTTP 规范里专门为「你太快了」保留的状态码，配上 Retry-After 头就能指导客户端退避重试。
503 表示服务器整体不可用，限流针对的是这一个客户端，不是服务器出了故障。
optionExplanations_en: 403 means 'you're not allowed,' while rate limiting means 'you're going too fast,' the wrong signal.
400 means the request itself is malformed; under rate limiting the request is perfectly valid.
429 is the dedicated rate-limit status code, usually paired with a Retry-After header telling the client how long to back off.
503 signals the whole server is down; rate limiting targets this one client, not a server failure.

scenario: 票务系统被黄牛脚本疯狂刷订票端点抢票，普通浏览端点则不受影响。
scenario_en: A ticketing system is being hammered by bot scripts on the booking endpoint, while normal browsing endpoints are unaffected.
q: 最对症的限流策略是？
q_en: What rate-limiting strategy targets the problem best?
options: 全站统一放宽限制
只对订票端点单独加严限流
只按 IP 限制浏览端点
直接关闭订票端点
options_en: Relax rate limits site-wide
Add stricter limits specifically on the booking endpoint
Only rate-limit the browsing endpoint by IP
Simply shut down the booking endpoint
why: 问题集中在单个敏感端点，就用 endpoint-specific 限流精确打击刷票行为，不误伤正常浏览流量。
why_en: Endpoint-specific limits, like ten booking attempts per minute, target scalping on the sensitive endpoint without hurting normal browsing.
whenOtherWins: 若滥用是全局性的（爬虫扫全站），per-user / per-IP 的整体限额更合适。
tradeoff: 端点专属限流的精准打击 vs 全局限流的实现简单
optionExplanations: 放宽限制反而会让刷票脚本更凶，问题没解决反而恶化。
问题集中在订票这一个敏感端点，就对它单独加严限流，精确打击又不误伤正常浏览。
限流方向选错了目标，真正被刷的订票端点仍然不受保护。
订票是核心业务功能，为了防刷彻底停用是过度反应，损害了正常用户。
optionExplanations_en: Relaxing limits site-wide only lets scalping scripts hit harder, making it worse not better.
The problem is concentrated on the booking endpoint, so tighten limits there specifically, precise and no harm to normal browsing.
Points rate limiting at the wrong target, the actual endpoint under attack stays unprotected.
Booking is a core business function; shutting it down entirely to stop abuse is an overreaction that hurts real users.

q: 限流通常在哪一层实现？面试要讲到什么深度？
q_en: Where is rate limiting usually implemented, and how deep should you go in an interview?
options: 在网关/中间件实现；面试提一句就够
必须在数据库层实现，并详细讲解令牌桶算法的数学推导
必须在客户端 JavaScript 里实现
限流是细节问题，面试完全不需要提
options_en: At the gateway or middleware; a brief mention is enough in an interview
It must be implemented at the database layer, with a detailed mathematical derivation of the token bucket algorithm
It must be implemented in client-side JavaScript
Rate limiting is a low-level detail that an interview never needs to mention
why: 限流一般落在 API 网关层或中间件。面试里提到它展示生产意识即可，别主动展开具体算法——除非面试官要求。
why_en: Rate limiting is typically implemented at the API gateway or middleware, and in interviews a brief mention is usually enough unless asked for algorithms.
optionExplanations: 限流一般落在网关/中间件层，面试里提一句展示生产意识就够，别主动展开算法。
数据库层感知不到 HTTP 层的请求上下文，这个层次选择本身就不合理。
客户端代码可以被绕过或篡改，没法作为真正的限流防线。
不提限流会让面试官觉得你缺乏生产系统的安全和稳定性意识。
optionExplanations_en: Rate limiting typically lives at the gateway or middleware layer, worth one sentence in an interview without digging into algorithms.
The database layer can't see HTTP-level request context, so this layer choice doesn't even make sense.
Client-side code can be bypassed or tampered with, not a real enforcement point.
Skipping it entirely makes the interviewer think you lack production security and stability awareness.

q: 把「公开 API 选 REST」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for choosing REST for public APIs in the correct order:
steps: 代价：不同客户端要不同数据时，固定端点会 over-fetch 或端点膨胀
决定性属性：HTTP 方法天然映射 CRUD、生态与工具最成熟
需求：面向 Web + 移动端的公开标准 CRUD API
缓解：多端差异真成为痛点时，再引入 GraphQL 按需取数
选型：REST（默认答案）
why: 需求（公开 CRUD）→ 属性（HTTP 语义映射 + 生态）→ 选型（REST）→ 代价（多端差异下多取/端点膨胀）→ 缓解（届时上 GraphQL）。
why_en: The chain runs from a public CRUD requirement through REST's natural HTTP mapping to its over-fetching cost, mitigated by adopting GraphQL only when client diversity demands it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求：公开 CRUD API"] --> P["属性：HTTP 语义映射 CRUD"]
    P --> C["选型：REST"]
    C --> K["代价：多端差异时 over-fetch"]
    K --> M["缓解：必要时引入 GraphQL"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用标准 HTTP 方法操作资源的 API 风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that uses standard HTTP methods to operate on resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单端点 + 查询语言，客户端按需取数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a single-endpoint query language where clients fetch exactly the data they need.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对资源的四种基本操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRUD refers to the four basic data operations: create, read, update, and delete.

scenario: 你在系统设计面试里刚讲完资源建模、HTTP 方法和状态码，准备转向存储、缓存这些更核心的架构决策。
scenario_en: In a system design interview, you have just covered resource modeling, HTTP methods, and status codes, and you are ready to move to storage, caching, and other core architecture decisions.
q: API 设计环节应该控制在多长时间？超时最常见的失误是什么？
q_en: How much time should the API design step take, and what is the common timeout mistake?
options: 大约 20 分钟；候选人常见的失误反而是讲得太少、不够深入
约 5 分钟；候选人更常见的失误是在 API 上花太多时间，而不是投入不足
大约 1 分钟就够了，因为 API 设计在面试里根本无关紧要
没有任何硬性时间上限，理论上讲得越久说明设计考虑得越完整
options_en: About twenty minutes; candidates commonly fail by saying too little rather than too much
About five minutes; candidates more commonly fail by over-investing time in API design rather than under-investing
About one minute is enough, because API design does not matter at all in an interview
There is no hard time limit at all; in theory the longer you spend, the more thoroughly considered the design looks
why: API 环节约 5 分钟：给出合理设计就推进。实践中「在 API 上磨太久」比「讲太少」更常见，这个时间预算决定了后面能留多少时间给存储和扩展性这些更大的架构问题。
why_en: Spend about five minutes on the API step, since candidates fail more often by over-investing in API design than by under-investing, and that budget determines how much time is left for storage and scalability.
optionExplanations: 把 API 环节的时间预算定得过长，会挤压后面存储、扩展性这些更大的架构问题。
5 分钟左右为宜，够了就往下走；候选人更常栽在「舍不得挪开」，而不是讲得不够。
1 分钟连基本的资源建模和状态码都讲不完，把 API 设计说成不重要也不成立。
面试有整体时长限制，讲得越久留给存储和扩展性的时间就越少，不是越完整。
optionExplanations_en: Budgeting too much time here squeezes out the bigger architecture questions like storage and scalability later.
About five minutes, then move on once the design is reasonable; over-investing is the more common failure than under-investing, and this budget decides what's left for the rest.
One minute isn't even enough for basic resource modeling and status codes, and calling API design unimportant doesn't hold up.
The interview has a fixed total length, so spending longer here just leaves less time for storage and scalability, not a more complete design.

q: 为什么内存缓存通常比数据库读得快？
q_en: Why is an in-memory cache usually faster than database reads?
options: Redis 索引一定比数据库索引高级
内存路径避开磁盘访问延迟
C 语言实现天然比 SQL 更快
数据库只慢在 SQL 解析阶段
why: 决定性约束是存储介质：内存离 CPU 近，通常避开磁盘寻道和页读取。经验法则是先用缓存加速高频读，但同时准备失效和降级。
why_en: A cache is faster mainly because memory is close to the CPU and avoids disk access, not because Redis has magic query logic.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["App"] --> Redis["Redis memory ~1ms"]
    App --> DB["Database disk ~50ms"]
scenario: 一次资料页读取要么查 Postgres，要么查 Redis；面试官在问为什么缓存读延迟能低一个数量级。
scenario_en: A profile-page read can hit Postgres or Redis; the interviewer is asking why cache read latency can be an order of magnitude lower.
options_en: Redis indexes are always more advanced than database indexes.
The memory path avoids disk-access latency.
C implementations are naturally faster than SQL.
Databases are slow only because of SQL parsing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用关系型数据库，通常把持久数据放在磁盘/SSD 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a relational database that usually persists data on disk or SSD.

termDefinitions.meaning: 执行程序指令的处理器；离它越近的数据通常访问越快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU executes program instructions, and data closer to it is usually faster to access.

optionExplanations: 索引算法不是关键，Redis 快在内存介质而非索引。
对：内存离 CPU 近，避开磁盘寻道和页读取。
换成 C 写的磁盘库照样慢，语言不是主成本。
解析只占一小截，磁盘 I/O 才是大头。
optionExplanations_en: Index algorithms aren't the point; Redis is fast from the memory medium, not indexing.
Right: memory is close to the CPU and avoids disk seeks and page reads.
A C-based disk store is still slow, so language isn't the main cost.
Parsing is a tiny slice; disk I/O is the real cost.

scenario: 一个高读流量 Web 应用有多台应用服务器；热点资料要跨实例共享，并控制内存占用。
scenario_en: A read-heavy web app has several app servers; hot profile data must be shared across instances while controlling memory use.
q: 默认先提哪一层缓存？
q_en: Which cache layer should you mention first by default?
options: 每台应用服务器各自维护本地进程内缓存
Redis/Memcached 这类外部共享缓存
CDN 边缘缓存所有业务数据
浏览器 HTTP 缓存用户资料
why: 决定性约束是多台服务器要共享热点数据，外部缓存能让所有实例读同一份。代价是多一次网络跳和失效复杂度。
why_en: For a multi-server app, start with an external shared cache because every server can read the same hot data while accepting cache-invalidation complexity.
whenOtherWins: 内容是公开图片/视频时，CDN 反而更直接。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App1["App A"] --> Redis["Shared Redis"]
    App2["App B"] --> Redis
    Redis --> DB["Database"]
options_en: Give every app server its own in-process cache.
Use an external shared cache such as Redis or Memcached.
Cache all business data at the CDN edge.
Use browser HTTP caching for user profiles.
tradeoff: 跨实例共享与统一失效 vs 本地读取最快

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用进程外的独立缓存服务，多台应用服务器可以共同访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An external cache is a standalone cache service shared by multiple application servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的过期时间，过期后必须重新获取或重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the expiration time after which a cached entry must be fetched or rebuilt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略，优先删除最长时间没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU evicts the item that has not been accessed for the longest time.

optionExplanations: 进程内读最快，但各实例各存一份、不共享。
对：多实例共享同一份热点数据，代价多一跳。
CDN 只适合公开静态媒体，不放私有业务数据。
浏览器缓存归客户端，后端难控失效。
optionExplanations_en: In-process reads are fastest but each server keeps its own copy, not shared.
Right: many instances share one hot copy, at one extra network hop.
A CDN fits public static media, not private business data.
Browser caching is client-side, so the backend can't control invalidation.

scenario: 源站在美国，印度用户请求图片/视频要跨洲回源；目标是把静态媒体延迟降到几十毫秒。
scenario_en: The origin is in the United States, and users in India fetch images and videos across continents; the goal is static-media latency in the tens of milliseconds.
q: 哪层缓存最直接？
q_en: Which cache layer is the best fit?
options: CDN 边缘节点缓存媒体
Redis 缓存每个视频字节
应用进程内缓存全球媒体
数据库查询缓存图片结果
why: 决定性约束是地理距离，CDN 把静态媒体放到离用户近的边缘节点。代价是只适合可缓存内容，并要处理回源和失效。
why_en: Use a CDN when geography dominates latency because edge servers serve static media near users instead of forcing every request back to the origin.
whenOtherWins: 按 key 的动态数据（资料、feed）通常 Redis 更直接。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    User["User"] --> Edge["CDN edge"]
    Edge -->|miss| Origin["Origin / blob"]
    Edge -->|hit| User
options_en: Cache media on CDN edge servers.
Cache every video byte in Redis.
Cache global media inside app processes.
Use database query cache for image results.
tradeoff: 就近分发静态内容 vs 应用层动态 key-value 缓存

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN stores content on edge servers close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 源站，CDN 未命中时回去取原始内容的后端位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The origin is the backend location a CDN fetches from on a cache miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠近用户的 CDN 节点，用来就近返回缓存内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge server is a CDN node near users that serves cached content locally.

optionExplanations: 对：瓶颈是跨洲距离时，CDN 把媒体放到就近边缘。
Redis 适合小动态 key，不缓存整段视频字节。
进程内只帮单机热点，覆盖不了全球用户。
查询缓存复用结果，但源站距离还在。
optionExplanations_en: Right: when cross-continent distance dominates, a CDN serves media from nearby edges.
Redis fits small dynamic keys, not whole video byte streams.
In-process only helps single-node hot data, not global users.
A query cache reuses results, but origin distance remains.

scenario: 服务每个请求都读少量配置和 feature flag；数据极少变化，目标是省掉 Redis 网络往返。
scenario_en: Every request reads a few config values and feature flags; the data rarely changes, and the goal is to avoid even the Redis round trip.
q: 这时最适合哪种缓存？
q_en: Which cache fits this case best?
options: 数据库加索引后每次查库
CDN 缓存配置接口
应用进程内缓存小配置
每次请求都查 Redis
why: 后端每请求都读很小的内部配置时，进程内直接读本机内存、连 Redis 跳都省；CDN 给用户拿公开内容，不管内部 flag。
why_en: For tiny internal config read by the backend on every request, in-process cache avoids even the Redis network hop. A CDN is for users fetching public cacheable content at the edge.
whenOtherWins: 配置若要跨实例立刻一致，外部 Redis/配置中心更好。
options_en: Add a database index and query every time.
Cache the config API in a CDN.
Cache small config values in process.
Query Redis on every request.
tradeoff: 本地最快读取 vs 跨实例共享和统一失效

termDefinitions.meaning: 保存在应用进程内存里的本地缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-process cache is local cache data kept inside the application process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 控制功能开关的内部配置，常按环境、用户、实验组或权限决定行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature flag is a configuration value that turns product behavior on or off.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向终端用户的边缘缓存，适合公开、可复用、可边缘分发的内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN cache is an edge cache for public, reusable content delivered close to end users.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["Backend app"] --> Local["In-process flags"]
    User["End user"] --> Edge["CDN edge"]
    Edge --> Origin["Public origin"]
optionExplanations: 加索引仍走 DB+网络，省不掉每请求读开销。
CDN 面向终端用户分发公开内容，覆盖不到服务端 flag。
对：小热少变、想省 Redis 跳时，进程内直接读本机内存。
Redis 能共享，但每读多一跳，这里不需要。
optionExplanations_en: An index still hits DB and network, so it can't remove the per-request cost.
A CDN distributes public content to end users and cannot cover server-side flags.
Right: for tiny, hot, stable data avoiding the Redis hop, in-process reads local memory.
Redis shares but adds a hop per read, not needed here.

q: 进程内缓存哪些判断成立？
q_en: Which statements about in-process caching are true?
options: 读取通常比 Redis 更快
每个应用实例各存一份
适合小而少变的热数据
失效会自动同步到所有实例
why: 进程内缓存省掉网络调用，所以读最快；但每个实例独立，失效不会自动广播。它是小而稳定热点数据的优化层，不是 Redis 替代品。
why_en: In-process cache is fastest because there is no network call, but each instance owns its copy and invalidation does not automatically propagate.
scenario: 评估是否把小配置、feature flag 和少量热点 key 放到应用进程内，而不是每次请求 Redis。
scenario_en: You are deciding whether tiny config, feature flags, and a few hot keys should live in process instead of calling Redis on every request.
options_en: Reads are usually faster than Redis.
Each application instance keeps its own copy.
It fits small, rarely-changing hot data.
Invalidation automatically syncs to all instances.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动删除或过期缓存条目，让后续读取重新拿新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Invalidation removes or expires a cache entry so later reads fetch a fresh value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被高频访问的缓存 key，可能成为局部瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a cache key that receives unusually high traffic and may become a bottleneck.

optionExplanations: 对：本地内存读没有网络跳，通常比 Redis 更快。
对：缓存副本属于各自进程，扩容后新实例各存一份。
对：小、稳定、少变的数据陈旧风险可控，适合放进程内。
错：本地缓存不会自动广播失效，要另建通道才同步。
optionExplanations_en: True: local memory reads have no network hop, so they're usually faster than Redis.
True: the cached copy belongs to each process, so new instances each keep their own.
True: small, stable, rarely-changing data has manageable staleness and fits in-process.
False: local caches don't auto-broadcast invalidation; you'd need a separate channel.

q: 两者在共享性上怎么不同？
q_en: How do Redis and in-process cache differ on sharing?
options: 两者都天然跨服务器共享
进程内共享，Redis 不共享
Redis 共享，进程内不共享
两者都只能单机内使用
why: 缓存位置决定共享性：Redis 是独立服务、多机读同一份；进程内住各自内存，代价是本地多一致性麻烦。
why_en: Redis is shared because it is an external service, while in-process cache is per instance and trades sharing for local speed.
scenario: 同一个热点配置被 20 台应用服务器读取；你要比较本地进程内缓存和外部 Redis 的共享能力。
scenario_en: The same hot config is read by 20 app servers; compare local in-process cache with external Redis on sharing.
options_en: Both are naturally shared across servers.
In-process is shared, while Redis is not.
Redis is shared, while in-process is not.
Both can only be used on one machine.
tradeoff: 共享一致性 vs 本地读取延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 多台应用服务器共同访问的一份缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared cache is one cache service accessed by multiple application servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里的旧值和数据库里的新值不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stale data is an old cached value that no longer matches the source of truth.

optionExplanations: 错：只有都接同一个外部服务时才都共享，本地缓存不会。
说反了：进程内是各自的副本，Redis 才是共享的。
对：Redis 作为独立服务被多机共享，进程内则各存各的。
错：Redis 本就是给多机共享用的，不是单机专用。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: both share only if they point to the same external service; local caches don't.
Backwards: in-process is a per-instance copy; Redis is the shared one.
Right: Redis is a standalone service shared by many servers; in-process is per-instance.
Wrong: Redis exists precisely for cross-server sharing, not single-machine use.

q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this latency anchor support?
options: 高频读可用缓存显著降延迟
缓存会让写入天然强一致
一次性验证码也应长期缓存
schema 设计好就不需要缓存
why: 50ms→1ms 说明热点读绕开 DB 可降延迟。若写也频繁，失效/陈旧成本会上升，缓存不保证写强一致。
why_en: The 50ms-to-1ms anchor supports caching hot reads, not making writes strongly consistent. Frequent writes increase invalidation and staleness cost.
tradeoff: 读延迟收益 vs 失效/陈旧成本
whenOtherWins: 读不热时先优化索引/schema，别急着上缓存。
scenario: 用户资料页每秒有大量读请求；一次 Postgres 读取约 50ms，Redis 命中约 1ms。
scenario_en: A user profile page receives many reads per second; one Postgres read is about 50ms, while a Redis hit is about 1ms.
options_en: A cache can sharply reduce latency for hot reads.
Caching makes writes strongly consistent by default.
One-time verification codes should be cached long term.
A good schema means caching is never needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求从发出到拿到响应所花的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Latency is the time from sending a request to receiving its response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求的数据已经在缓存中，可以直接返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache hit means the requested data is already in cache and can be returned directly.

optionExplanations: 对：50ms→1ms 支持把高频读搬到缓存降延迟。
错：缓存引入双写/失效，不会天然强一致。
错：验证码一次性，长期缓存破坏一次性语义。
错：schema 重要，但读足够热仍值得缓存。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the 50ms-to-1ms gap supports caching hot reads for lower latency.
Wrong: caching adds dual-write and invalidation, not strong consistency.
Wrong: codes are one-time, so long-term caching breaks that.
Wrong: schema matters, but hot-enough reads still benefit from cache.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this latency anchor support?
options: 静态媒体应优先考虑 CDN
Redis 能替代全球边缘网络
CDN 命中仍要每次回源站
跨洲距离对延迟没有影响
why: 250-300ms 到 20-40ms 的差距说明静态媒体瓶颈常是地理距离。CDN 用边缘命中换低延迟，但只对可缓存内容最自然。
why_en: The 250ms-to-40ms anchor shows why static media belongs on a CDN: edge hits avoid long cross-continent trips.
scenario: 图片源站在美国，印度用户跨洲回源约 250-300ms；同一图片若命中附近 CDN 约 20-40ms。
scenario_en: An image origin is in the US; India users see about 250-300ms to origin, but a nearby CDN hit is about 20-40ms.
options_en: Static media should usually be served through a CDN.
Redis can replace a global edge network.
A CDN hit still fetches from origin every time.
Cross-continent distance does not affect latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 边缘节点已经有内容副本，不需要回源站。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN hit means the edge server already has the content and does not fetch from origin.

termDefinitions.meaning: 变化不频繁、可被多人复用的图片、视频或文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Static media is content such as images or videos that changes rarely and can be reused by many users.

optionExplanations: 对：250ms→40ms 说明瓶颈是距离，静态媒体优先上 CDN。
错：Redis 是单区内存，没有全球边缘节点。
错：命中就是边缘直接返回，不再回源。
错：这与实测的跨洲延迟差距直接矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the 250ms-to-40ms gap shows distance is the bottleneck, so static media prefers a CDN.
Wrong: Redis is single-region memory with no global edge nodes.
Wrong: a hit returns straight from the edge and skips origin.
Wrong: this contradicts the measured cross-continent latency gap.

q: 补全四种核心缓存读写模式：
q_en: Fill in the four core cache read/write patterns:
text: 四种缓存架构：{{Cache-Aside}}（旁路 / 懒加载）、{{Write-Through}}（写穿透）、{{Write-Behind}}（写回 / write-back）、{{Read-Through}}（读穿透）。
why: 这四个名字分属两条轴：Cache-Aside/Read-Through 定义读 miss 谁查 DB；Write-Through/Write-Behind 定义写请求怎么落库。写策略本身不说明读怎么做，读侧要另选。
why_en: These names sit on two axes: cache-aside/read-through define who handles read misses, while write-through/write-behind define how writes reach the DB.

rows: 先写 Cache 后刷 DB

whenOtherWins: 默认读多降 DB 压力选 Cache-Aside；想把回源逻辑封装在缓存层选 Read-Through；读必须尽量新鲜选 Write-Through；写入峰值大且可接受最终一致/少量丢失风险选 Write-Behind。

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存；未命中时应用查数据库并回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In cache-aside, the app checks cache first and fills it after a database read on a miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入必须同步更新缓存和数据库后才算完成；它不单独定义读 miss 怎么处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through completes a write only after both cache and database are updated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存，再由后台异步批量写数据库；它不单独定义读 miss 怎么处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes cache first and flushes changes to the database asynchronously.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存未命中时由缓存层自己去数据库取数并回填。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-through lets the cache fetch from the database and fill itself on a miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读侧策略管 cache miss；写侧策略管写请求。两者可以组合，不是四选一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-side policy handles cache misses; write-side policy handles writes. They can be combined.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    Read["Read policy"] --> CA["Cache-Aside: App fills miss"]
    Read --> RT["Read-Through: Cache fills miss"]
    Write["Write policy"] --> WT["Write-Through: sync DB"]
    Write --> WB["Write-Behind: async DB"]

scenario: 面试里只说系统读多、想降低数据库压力；没有强一致写入、极高写吞吐或 CDN 这类特殊要求。
scenario_en: In an interview, the only stated need is a read-heavy system that should reduce database load; there is no special consistency, write-throughput, or CDN requirement.
q: 默认用哪种缓存模式？
q_en: Which caching pattern is the default?
options: Write-Behind 异步写回
Cache-Aside 读时懒加载
Read-Through 缓存代理
Write-Through 同步双写
why: 无强一致/高写吞吐要求时默认 Cache-Aside：读 cache、miss 查库回填；简单但 miss 慢、可能陈旧。
why_en: Without special consistency or write-throughput needs, cache-aside is the default: read cache first, and on a miss the app reads DB and fills cache.
whenOtherWins: 写后必须立刻读到最新时，改用 Write-Through。
options_en: Use write-behind asynchronous flushes.
Use cache-aside lazy loading on reads.
Use a read-through cache proxy.
Use write-through synchronous double writes.
tradeoff: 简单可降级 vs miss/陈旧

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里没有目标数据，请求必须去后端数据源获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache miss means the value is absent from cache and must be fetched from the backing store.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有数据真的被请求时才加载并缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lazy loading stores data only when it is actually requested.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个依赖故障时系统还能不能继续服务；它不等于数据一定不丢，也不等于一定最新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Availability means whether the system can keep serving when a dependency fails; it is separate from durability and freshness.

optionExplanations: Write-Behind 优化写吞吐、可能丢，不是通用默认。
对：无特殊一致/吞吐要求时，Cache-Aside 最简单。
Read-Through 把回源下沉缓存层，适合 CDN/代理。
Write-Through 同步双写读更新鲜，但写更慢。
optionExplanations_en: Write-behind optimizes throughput and may lose data, not a general default.
Right: with no special consistency/throughput need, cache-aside is simplest.
Read-through pushes origin fetch into the cache, fitting CDN/proxy.
Write-through's sync double write keeps reads fresh but writes slower.

q: 补全 Cache-Aside 读取流程：
q_en: Fill in the cache-aside read flow:
text: 先查{{缓存}}；命中则直接返回；未命中则查{{数据库}}，把结果写回{{缓存}}，再返回。
why: Cache-Aside 的核心是「懒加载」：只有被读到的数据才进缓存。代价是第一次未命中会多一次数据库延迟。
why_en: Cache-aside checks the cache first, and on a miss reads the database, writes the result back to the cache, and returns it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["App"] --> Cache{"Hit?"}
    Cache -->|yes| Return["Return"]
    Cache -->|no| DB["Read DB"]
    DB --> Set["Set TTL"]
    Set --> Return

scenario: 第一次读取 user:123，或者 TTL 刚过期后再读；Redis 里还没有这个 key。
scenario_en: You read user:123 for the first time, or right after its TTL expired; Redis does not have the key yet.
q: Cache-Aside 的主要缺点是？
q_en: What is the main drawback of cache-aside?
options: 缓存未命中时会多付一次数据库查询的延迟
会缓存大量永远不会被读的数据
写入必须等缓存和数据库都完成
无法设置 TTL
why: 不是查两次：先问 cache 没有再查 DB 回填。命中只走 cache；miss 走 cache+DB+回填，那次更慢。
why_en: It does not mean querying the DB twice. A miss checks cache, then reads DB and fills cache, so that request pays cache plus DB latency.
options_en: A cache miss adds one extra database round trip of latency.
It caches lots of data that is never read.
Writes must wait for both cache and database to finish.
It cannot set a TTL.
tradeoff: 缓存精简 vs 首次 miss 慢

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里有值，请求可直接从缓存返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache hit means the value is present and can be returned from cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里没值，请求还要去数据库取，并通常写回缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache miss means the value is absent, so the app reads the database and usually fills cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求发到某个服务并拿回响应的耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A round trip is the time to send a request to a service and receive its response.

diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App
    participant Cache
    participant DB
    App->>Cache: GET user:123
    alt hit
      Cache-->>App: value
    else miss
      Cache-->>App: null
      App->>DB: SELECT user
      DB-->>App: row
      App->>Cache: SET user TTL
      App-->>App: return row
    end
codeSample:
def get_user(id):
    v = cache.get(id)      # fast if hit
    if v is None:          # miss: extra DB trip
        v = db.get(id)
        cache.set(id, v, ttl=60)
    return v
optionExplanations: 对：miss 要多走一次查库+回填，那次更慢。
说反了：只缓存被读过的，不囤没人读的。
那是 Write-Through 的写路径，不是本缺点。
错：TTL 照样能设，是标准操作。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a miss adds a DB read plus backfill, so that request is slower.
Backwards: it only stores data that's been read, not unused entries.
That's write-through's write path, not this drawback.
Wrong: TTL still works and is standard.

scenario: 某系统要求读到的数据必须永远是最新的，同时可以接受写入慢一点。
scenario_en: A system requires reads to always see the freshest data and can accept slower writes.
q: 最匹配的缓存写模式是？
q_en: Which cache write pattern best matches?
options: Cache-Aside（旁路缓存）
Write-Behind（写回，异步刷库）
Write-Through（写穿透）
只用 CDN 分发
why: 写穿透同步写缓存和库、两边成功才算完成，所以读更容易保持新鲜；代价是每次写更慢。
why_en: Write-through writes to the cache and synchronously to the database before acknowledging, making freshness easier than cache-aside, but failures, bypass writes, and races still need handling.
options_en: Cache-aside (lazy loading).
Write-behind (async DB flush).
Write-through.
Just use a CDN.
whenOtherWins: 写吞吐极高且能容忍偶尔丢时，Write-Behind 更快。
tradeoff: 写后强新鲜 vs 写延迟更高

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，未命中时应用查库并回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In cache-aside, the app checks the cache and, on a miss, reads the DB and fills the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求同步更新缓存和数据库，两边都成功才算写完。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through updates cache and database synchronously and completes only when both succeed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存，再由后台异步批量落库，写快但崩溃可能丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to cache first and flushes to the database asynchronously in batches.

optionExplanations: Cache-Aside 有旧值窗口，读不保证永远最新。
Write-Behind 写最快但异步刷库、崩溃可能丢。
对：读要永远最新、写慢可接受时，写穿透同步双写最合适。
CDN 分发静态内容，管不了应用数据新鲜度。
optionExplanations_en: Cache-aside has a stale window, so reads aren't always freshest.
Write-behind is fastest but async and may lose data on a crash.
Right: when reads must stay fresh and slower writes are fine, write-through fits.
A CDN distributes static content, not app-data freshness.

q: Write-Through 除了「写变慢」，还有一个常被追问的一致性问题是？
q_en: Besides slower writes, what consistency issue often comes up with write-through?
options: 写入的缓存条目会永远留存、从不过期
双写问题：缓存与数据库有一次写失败即不一致
写穿透模式下无法再给 key 设置 TTL
所有读请求都会绕过缓存、直接查库
why: Write-Through 仍有双写问题：缓存和数据库两次写有一次失败就会不一致，需要重试、错误处理，否则得接受没有分布式事务时难有完美一致。
why_en: Write-through still has the dual-write problem: if the cache write succeeds but the database write fails or vice versa, the two can diverge.
options_en: Cached entries live forever and never expire.
The dual-write problem: if one of the two writes fails, cache and DB diverge.
Write-through cannot set a TTL on a key.
All reads bypass the cache and hit the DB directly.
tradeoff: 同步双写更新鲜 vs 无分布式事务时仍可能半成功

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求同步更新缓存和数据库，两边都成功才算完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through updates cache and database synchronously and completes only when both succeed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一次写要更新两处存储，没有分布式事务时可能只成功一处，导致不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The dual-write problem is that updating two stores without a distributed transaction can succeed on one and fail on the other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：给 key 设的过期时间，到点自动失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is the expiry set on a key so it lapses automatically.

optionExplanations: 错：写穿透的条目照样能设 TTL 过期，不会永久留存。
对：无分布式事务时，缓存和库两次写有一次失败就会不一致。
错：写模式不影响能不能设 TTL，两者是两回事。
错：写穿透仍读缓存，并没有让读绕过。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: write-through entries still take a TTL and lapse, so they don't live forever.
Right: without a distributed transaction, if either of the two writes fails they diverge.
Wrong: the write mode doesn't affect TTL; they're separate concerns.
Wrong: write-through still reads the cache and doesn't bypass reads.

scenario: 一个分析 / 指标（metrics）管道，写入量极大，能容忍崩溃时丢失少量最近数据，追求最高写吞吐。
scenario_en: A metrics pipeline has very high write volume, can tolerate losing a small amount of recent data on crash, and optimizes for maximum write throughput.
q: 最合适的缓存写模式是？
q_en: Which cache write pattern fits best?
options: Write-Through（同步双写，写慢但持久）
Cache-Aside（应用管读 miss）
Read-Through（缓存管读 miss）
Write-Behind（写回，异步批量落库）
why: 写回只写缓存、异步批量落库，写非常快，但崩溃前没刷盘会丢；适合能容忍偶尔丢的高写吞吐。
why_en: Write-behind writes only to the cache and flushes to the database asynchronously in batches, giving very high write throughput while risking data loss on a crash.
options_en: Write-through with synchronous double writes (slow, durable).
Cache-aside (the app handles read misses).
Read-through (the cache handles read misses).
Write-behind, flushing to the DB asynchronously in batches.
tradeoff: 极高写吞吐 vs 崩溃可能丢最近数据
whenOtherWins: 数据绝不能丢（钱、订单）时，绝不能用 Write-Behind。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存，后台异步批量落库，写吞吐最高但崩溃可能丢未刷数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to cache first and flushes to the DB asynchronously, maximizing write throughput at the risk of crash loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求同步更新缓存和数据库，两边都成功才算完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through updates cache and database synchronously before acknowledging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间能完成的写（或读）请求数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is how many write or read requests the system completes per unit of time.

optionExplanations: Write-Through 每写都等两边落库，扛不住极高吞吐。
Cache-Aside 是读侧模式，不解决写吞吐。
Read-Through 也是读侧模式，与写吞吐无关。
对：写吞吐要最高、能容忍丢一点时，写回只写缓存再异步批量刷库。
optionExplanations_en: Write-through waits on both stores per write, too slow for extreme throughput.
Cache-aside is read-side and doesn't fix the write bottleneck.
Read-through is also read-side, unrelated to write throughput.
Right: for max throughput tolerating some loss, write-behind writes cache then batch-flushes.

q: Write-Behind（写回）最大的风险是？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of write-behind?
options: 缓存崩溃、数据还没刷到数据库时会丢数据
写入延迟极高，因为每次写都要同步等落库
读取一定会拿到过期的旧值
根本无法把多条写合并成批量
why: Write-Behind 靠异步批量落库换来写速度，但如果缓存在刷盘前崩溃，那批还没写入数据库的数据就丢了——所以只用于可容忍偶尔丢失的场景。
why_en: Write-behind's risk is losing data if the cache crashes before it flushes the batched writes to the database.
options_en: Data is lost if the cache crashes before flushing to the DB.
Write latency is extremely high because each write waits on the DB.
Reads always return a stale value.
It cannot batch multiple writes together at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存，后台异步批量落库；崩溃时未刷入库的那批会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to cache first and flushes to the DB asynchronously; a crash loses the not-yet-flushed batch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把缓存里累积的写批量提交到持久数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A flush commits the writes buffered in cache to the durable database in a batch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一旦写被确认，数据在崩溃后仍不丢失的保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability is the guarantee that an acknowledged write survives crashes.

optionExplanations: 对：异步批量刷库时崩溃，会丢那批还没落库的数据。
错：写回只写缓存，写延迟其实最低。
错：多数读仍命中较新值，不是必然拿旧值。
错：批量合并落库正是写回的设计目的。
optionExplanations_en: Right: if it crashes during async batch flush, the not-yet-persisted batch is lost.
Wrong: write-behind only writes cache, so latency is actually lowest.
Wrong: most reads still hit a fairly fresh value, not always stale.
Wrong: batching writes to the DB is exactly what write-behind is for.

q: Write-Through 与 Write-Behind 在「写延迟 vs 持久性」上的区别是？
q_en: How do write-through and write-behind differ on write latency versus durability?
options: 写穿透的写更快一些，但可能在崩溃时丢掉数据
同步落库写更慢但更持久，写回更快但可能丢
两者的写延迟和持久性其实完全一样
写回更慢也更持久，写穿透更快更弱
why: Write-Through 同步落库→写慢但一写就持久；Write-Behind 异步落库→写快但崩溃可能丢。这是一条典型的「延迟 vs 持久性」权衡。
why_en: Write-through trades slower writes for durability, while write-behind trades possible data loss for much faster writes.
options_en: Write-through is somewhat faster but may lose data on a crash.
Write-through is slower but durable; write-behind is faster but may lose data.
The two have identical write latency and durability.
Write-behind is slower and more durable; write-through is faster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求同步更新缓存和数据库，写慢但一写就持久。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through updates cache and DB synchronously: slower writes, durable once acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写只落缓存、异步批量刷库，写快但崩溃可能丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes only to cache and flushes asynchronously: fast writes, possible crash loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写被确认后即便崩溃也不丢的保证；与写延迟形成权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability is surviving crashes after acknowledgment, traded off against write latency.

optionExplanations: 错：写穿透同步双写更慢，不是更快。
对：同步落库=慢但持久；异步落库=快但崩溃可能丢。
错：两者在延迟和持久性上正好相反，不相同。
说反了：写回更快、持久性更弱，不是更慢更持久。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: write-through's sync double write is slower, not faster.
Right: sync flush = slow but durable; async flush = fast but may lose on crash.
Wrong: the two are opposite on latency and durability, not identical.
Backwards: write-behind is faster and less durable, not slower and more durable.

q: 哪种缓存模式下，应用「从不直接访问数据库」，由缓存作为智能代理在未命中时自己去查库？
q_en: In which cache pattern does the app never access the DB directly and the cache fetches from the DB on a miss?
options: Cache-Aside
Read-Through（读穿透）
Write-Behind
Write-Through
why: Read-Through 是读侧模式：miss 时缓存层自己查库。写侧的 Write-Through/Write-Behind 是另一维度，可搭配。
why_en: Read-through is a read-side pattern: on a miss, the cache layer fetches from DB. Write-through/write-behind are write-side patterns and can be paired with read-through.
options_en: Cache-aside.
Read-through.
Write-behind.
Write-through.
tradeoff: 读侧 miss 归谁管 vs 写侧如何落库
whenOtherWins: 想自己控制 miss、序列化、降级时用 Cache-Aside。

termDefinitions.meaning: 定义 cache miss 时谁去查数据库，例如 Cache-Aside 或 Read-Through。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-side pattern defines who queries the DB on a cache miss, such as cache-aside or read-through.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定义写请求如何更新缓存和数据库，例如 Write-Through 或 Write-Behind。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-side pattern defines how writes update cache and DB, such as write-through or write-behind.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个选择不在同一维度，可以组合：读侧选 Read-Through，写侧再选 Write-Through 或 Write-Behind。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orthogonal choices are on different dimensions and can be combined.

optionExplanations: Cache-Aside 由应用查库回填，应用直连 DB。
对：Read-Through 让缓存自己回源，应用只跟缓存交互。
Write-Behind 是写侧模式，不管读 miss。
Write-Through 也是写侧模式，与读 miss 无关。
optionExplanations_en: Cache-aside has the app query and backfill, hitting the DB directly.
Right: read-through lets the cache fetch from origin; the app only talks to cache.
Write-behind is a write-side pattern, not about read misses.
Write-through is also write-side, unrelated to read misses.

q: 下面哪个是 Read-Through 缓存的现实例子？
q_en: Which real-world example is a read-through cache?
options: 应用用 Redis 手动做 Cache-Aside 读取
数据库前面的连接池管理
CDN：未命中时自己回源、缓存结果再返回
消息队列失败后的重试机制
why: CDN 就是一种 Read-Through：未命中时它自己去源站取、缓存、再返回。但应用层用 Redis 时，Cache-Aside 远比 Read-Through 常见。
why_en: A CDN is a read-through cache: on a miss it fetches from the origin, stores the result, and returns it.
options_en: An app doing manual cache-aside reads with Redis.
A connection pool in front of the database.
A CDN: on a miss it fetches from origin, caches, then returns.
A message-queue retry mechanism after failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存未命中时由缓存层自己去数据库/源站取数并回填，应用只跟缓存交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-through lets the cache fetch from the DB or origin on a miss and fill itself; the app only talks to the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，miss 时由应用查库并回填。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In cache-aside the app checks cache and, on a miss, reads the DB and backfills.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Content Delivery Network：把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点，是读穿透的现实例子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN (Content Delivery Network) caches content on edge nodes near users and is a real read-through example.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用一组数据库连接以省去反复建连的开销，不是缓存模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool reuses database connections to avoid reconnect overhead; it is not a cache pattern.

optionExplanations: 应用用 Redis 是 Cache-Aside，回源在应用里。
连接池是连接管理，不是缓存模式。
对：CDN miss 自己回源、缓存再返回，应用不直连源。
消息队列重试是错误处理，与缓存无关。
optionExplanations_en: App-side Redis is cache-aside; the fetch lives in the app.
A connection pool manages connections, not a cache pattern.
Right: a CDN fetches origin on a miss, caches, returns; the app never hits origin.
Message-queue retry is failure handling, unrelated to caching.

q: 补全常见淘汰策略：
q_en: Fill in the common cache eviction policies:
text: {{LRU}} 淘汰最久未被访问的；{{LFU}} 淘汰访问次数最少的；{{FIFO}} 按插入顺序淘汰最老的；{{TTL}} 不是淘汰策略本身，而是给 key 设过期时间。
why: 淘汰策略决定缓存满了删谁。LRU 是安全默认，LFU 适合长期热门，FIFO 忽略使用模式很少用，TTL 负责「最终刷新」。
why_en: LRU evicts least recently used, LFU evicts least frequently used, FIFO evicts oldest by insertion, and TTL sets an expiration rather than being an eviction policy.

scenario: 面试里被问缓存淘汰策略，工作负载普通、没有特别的访问模式。
scenario_en: In an interview, you are asked for a cache eviction policy; the workload is ordinary with no special access pattern.
q: 最安全的默认答案是？
q_en: What is the safest default answer?
options: LRU（最近最少使用）
FIFO（先进先出，按插入顺序淘汰）
随机淘汰
永不淘汰
why: LRU 是多数系统的默认：它假设最近用过的很快会再用，适配大多数工作负载，且可用链表/环形缓冲在 O(1) 淘汰。
why_en: LRU is the safe default because recently used data tends to be used again, and it fits most workloads with constant-time eviction.
options_en: LRU (least recently used).
FIFO (first in, first out, by insertion order).
Random eviction.
Never evict.
tradeoff: 近期热点适配（LRU） vs 特殊访问模式专用策略
whenOtherWins: 有一批长期稳定热门 key 时，LFU 更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Recently Used：优先淘汰最久没被访问过的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU (Least Recently Used) evicts the key not accessed for the longest time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 First In First Out：按插入顺序淘汰最早进来的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) evicts the earliest-inserted key regardless of usage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存内存不够时选择删除哪些 key 来腾空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction chooses which keys to remove when the cache runs out of memory.

optionExplanations: 对：普通负载下近期用过的会再用，LRU 是安全默认、O(1) 淘汰。
FIFO 按到达顺序，可能删仍热的老 key。
随机淘汰无使用感知，易误删有用数据。
永不淘汰会让内存无限增长撑爆。
optionExplanations_en: Right: recently used is reused soon, so LRU is the safe O(1) default.
FIFO evicts by arrival and may drop still-hot old keys.
Random eviction has no usage awareness and drops useful data.
Never evicting grows memory without bound until it breaks.

scenario: 某些 key 长期、持续地比其他 key 热门，比如热门视频、Top 播放列表，希望优先保留这些长期赢家。
scenario_en: Some keys stay hot for a long time, like trending videos or top playlists, and you want to keep those long-term winners.
q: 最合适的淘汰策略是？
q_en: Which eviction policy fits best?
options: FIFO
TTL 单独使用、不搭配任何淘汰策略
LFU（最不经常使用）
随机淘汰
why: LFU 按访问频次淘汰，能长期保留「持续热门」的 key（每个 key 一个计数器；有的用近似 LFU 降成本），适合趋势/榜单类数据。
why_en: LFU evicts the least frequently accessed key, so it keeps consistently popular items like trending videos or top playlists.
options_en: FIFO.
TTL on its own, without any eviction policy.
LFU (least frequently used).
Random eviction.
tradeoff: 长期高频保留（LFU） vs 近期热点适配（LRU）
whenOtherWins: 热点只是‘最近’热、会随时间漂移时，LRU 更贴合。

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Frequently Used：优先淘汰访问次数最少的 key，留住长期高频项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU (Least Frequently Used) evicts the least-accessed key, keeping persistently popular items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 First In First Out：按插入顺序淘汰最早进来的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) evicts the earliest-inserted key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：给 key 设的过期时间，管新鲜度而非容量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is a per-key expiry that governs freshness, not capacity.

optionExplanations: FIFO 只看谁最早进来，识别不了长期赢家。
只用 TTL 管过期、不管满了删谁。
对：有一批长期持续热门 key 时，LFU 按频次留住赢家。
随机淘汰可能把长期赢家一并删掉。
optionExplanations_en: FIFO only tracks arrival and can't spot long-term winners.
TTL alone handles expiry, not what to drop when full.
Right: with persistently popular keys, LFU keeps winners by frequency.
Random eviction may drop long-term winners too.

q: LRU 和 LFU 的核心区别维度是？
q_en: What is the core dimension that separates LRU from LFU?
options: LRU 看累计访问频次，LFU 看最近访问时间
LRU 看最近访问时间，LFU 看访问频次
两者都只按插入时间淘汰
两者完全等价、没有区别
why: LRU 按「最近有没有被用」淘汰（recency），LFU 按「被用了多少次」淘汰（frequency）。前者适应近期热点，后者保留长期赢家。
why_en: LRU evicts by recency of access while LFU evicts by frequency of access.
options_en: LRU tracks cumulative frequency; LFU tracks recency of access.
LRU tracks recency of access; LFU tracks frequency of access.
Both only track insertion time.
They are completely equivalent.
tradeoff: 最近使用时间 recency（LRU） vs 访问频次 frequency（LFU）

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Recently Used：按最近访问时间淘汰（recency）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU (Least Recently Used) evicts by recency of access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Frequently Used：按累计访问频次淘汰（frequency）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU (Least Frequently Used) evicts by frequency of access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以‘最近有没有被用过’为淘汰依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recency evicts based on how recently a key was used.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以‘一共被用过多少次’为淘汰依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Frequency evicts based on how many times a key was used.

optionExplanations: 说反了：LRU 看最近时间，LFU 才看累计频次。
对：LRU 看最近是否用过，LFU 看用过多少次。
错：只按插入时间是 FIFO，不是 LRU/LFU。
错：两者优化目标不同，并不等价。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: LRU tracks recency; LFU tracks cumulative frequency.
Right: LRU by whether it was used recently; LFU by how many times.
Wrong: insertion-time-only is FIFO, not LRU/LFU.
Wrong: they optimize for different things and aren't equivalent.

q: 关于 FIFO 淘汰策略，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about FIFO eviction is correct?
options: 按访问频次的高低来淘汰 key
只按插入时间淘汰最老的，可能删掉仍很热的数据
和 LRU 完全等价，行为一致
是真实系统里最常用的淘汰策略
why: FIFO 只看谁最早进来，用一个简单队列即可，但它忽略访问模式，可能把还很热的数据淘汰掉，所以真实系统里很少单独用。
why_en: FIFO evicts the oldest by insertion time only, ignoring usage, so it may drop still-hot data and is rarely used in real systems.
options_en: Evicts keys by access frequency.
Evicts the oldest by insertion time only, so it can drop still-hot data.
Equivalent to LRU, with identical behavior.
It is the most common eviction policy in real systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 First In First Out：按插入顺序淘汰最早进来的 key，不看使用模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) evicts the earliest-inserted key regardless of usage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Recently Used：按最近访问时间淘汰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU (Least Recently Used) evicts by recency of access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Frequently Used：按访问频次淘汰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU (Least Frequently Used) evicts by frequency of access.

optionExplanations: 错：按访问频次是 LFU 的做法，不是 FIFO。
对：只按进入顺序、不看使用模式，正是 FIFO 的定义。
错：LRU 看访问时间，FIFO 不看，两者不等价。
错：最常用的是 LRU；FIFO 因识别不了热点很少单用。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: evicting by frequency is LFU, not FIFO.
Right: evicting purely by arrival order regardless of usage is exactly FIFO.
Wrong: LRU tracks access time, FIFO doesn't, so they aren't equivalent.
Wrong: LRU is the common default; FIFO is rarely used alone since it can't spot hot keys.

scenario: Cache 里既有 10 分钟后过期的 user profile，也有不过期的热门榜单；现在内存快满了。
scenario_en: The cache has user profiles expiring in ten minutes and a hot leaderboard with no expiry; now memory is almost full.
q: 关于 TTL，下面哪种说法最准确？
q_en: Which statement about TTL is most accurate?
options: TTL 是一种独立的淘汰策略，可直接替代 LRU/LFU
TTL 不是淘汰策略，只给 key 设过期，常配 LRU/LFU
TTL 只能用在 CDN 边缘缓存的场景
设了 TTL 之后就不再需要任何淘汰策略
why: TTL 会删 key，但回答的是「何时过期」，不是内存满时「删谁」。TTL 管新鲜度，LRU/LFU 管容量。
why_en: TTL can delete keys, but it answers when a key expires, not which key to drop when memory is full. Pair it with LRU/LFU for capacity control.
options_en: TTL is a standalone eviction policy that directly replaces LRU/LFU.
TTL is not an eviction policy; it sets a per-key expiry and pairs with LRU/LFU.
TTL only works for CDN edge caching.
With a TTL you no longer need any eviction policy.
tradeoff: 时间过期 vs 容量淘汰
whenOtherWins: 想优先删快过期的 key 时，用 TTL-aware eviction。

termDefinitions.meaning: key 到达设定时间后逻辑失效，不应再被读到；Redis 可在访问时删除，也会后台主动清理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Expiration invalidates a key after its configured time, such as SET key value EX 600.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存空间不够时，系统选择删除哪些 key 来腾内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction chooses which keys to remove when the cache needs memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 淘汰时参考剩余 TTL，例如优先删快过期的 key；TTL 是信号，不是完整策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL-aware eviction uses remaining TTL as a signal, such as dropping soon-to-expire keys first.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    TTL["TTL"] --> Time["Time reached"]
    Time --> Gone["Logically missing"]
    Gone --> Cleanup["Lazy or active delete"]
    LRU["LRU/LFU"] --> Full["Memory full"]
    Full --> Victim["Evict victim key"]
codeSample:
# TTL + LRU: expiration and eviction are two separate triggers
CONFIG SET maxmemory 2gb
CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
SET user:123:profile '{...}' EX 600

# Case 1: 600s passes first -> key is logically expired; GET should miss
GET user:123:profile

# Case 2: memory fills before 600s -> LRU may evict it earlier
# TTL controls freshness; LRU controls capacity.

# TTL + LFU: memory pressure evicts least frequently used instead
CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lfu
SET product:999:detail '{...}' EX 300

# allkeys-lru/lfu: any key can be evicted when full
# volatile-lru/lfu: only keys with TTL are eviction candidates
optionExplanations: 错：TTL 管何时过期，替代不了满了删谁。
对：TTL 只设过期管新鲜度，容量靠 LRU/LFU。
错：应用缓存、会话、API 响应都常用 TTL。
错：未过期 key 一多仍会占满内存。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: TTL governs when to expire, not what to drop when full.
Right: TTL only sets expiry for freshness; capacity needs LRU/LFU.
Wrong: app caches, sessions, and API responses use TTL too.
Wrong: many unexpired keys can still fill memory.

scenario: 缓存的是第三方 API 响应和会话令牌，这类数据必须在一段时间后自动刷新/失效。
scenario_en: The cache stores third-party API responses and session tokens, and this data must refresh or expire automatically after some time.
q: 最该配置的是？
q_en: What should you configure first?
options: 给这些 key 设置 TTL 过期时间
把淘汰策略改成 FIFO
关闭所有淘汰策略、永不过期
把写模式改成 Write-Behind
why: 当数据「必须最终刷新」时，TTL 是必备：API 响应、会话令牌到期自动失效，下次读再拉新值，天然限制了陈旧程度。
why_en: When data must eventually refresh, like API responses or session tokens, a TTL is essential so entries expire and get repopulated.
options_en: Set a TTL expiry on these keys.
Switch the eviction policy to FIFO.
Turn off all eviction so nothing expires.
Switch the write mode to write-behind.
whenOtherWins: 写后必须立刻读到新值时，改用写时失效。

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：给 key 设的过期时间，到点自动失效、下次读回源刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is a per-key expiry after which the key lapses and refetches on the next read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 First In First Out：按插入顺序淘汰，管容量而非过期刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) evicts by insertion order, addressing capacity, not scheduled refresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写只落缓存、异步批量刷库，是写侧优化，不解决读侧过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to cache and flushes async; it optimizes writes, not read-side expiry.

codeSample:
# 数据必须定期刷新：写入即带过期，到点自动失效
SET session:abc123 '{...}' EX 3600     # 会话令牌 1h 后过期
SET api:weather:94107 '{...}' EX 300   # 第三方响应 5min 后刷新
GET api:weather:94107                   # 过期后 miss -> 回源重新拉取并回填
# EX = 秒级 TTL；到点 key 逻辑失效，下次读自然取到新值
optionExplanations: 对：数据必须定期刷新时，TTL 到点失效、下次读拉新值。
FIFO 管容量淘汰，解决不了到期刷新。
关掉淘汰会让陈旧数据一直留着。
Write-Behind 是写侧模式，管不了读侧过期。
optionExplanations_en: Right: when data must refresh on a schedule, TTL lapses and the next read refetches.
FIFO handles capacity eviction, not scheduled refresh.
Disabling eviction keeps stale data forever.
Write-behind is write-side and can't expire read-side data.
tradeoff: 到期自动刷新 vs 写后立即新鲜

scenario: 首页 feed 缓存 TTL 60 秒，到 12:01:00 同一瞬间过期，成百上千请求同时未命中、一起冲向数据库，可能把库打垮。
scenario_en: The home feed cache has a 60-second TTL; at 12:01:00 it expires, hundreds or thousands of requests miss at once, and they all rush the DB.
q: 这是什么问题，最有效的解法是？
q_en: What problem is this, and what is the best fix?
options: 热 key 问题；把 key 复制分摊
缓存穿透；加布隆过滤器拦截
缓存击穿/惊群；请求合并单飞
双写不一致；上分布式事务
why: 这是缓存击穿/惊群：同一 key 过期瞬间大量并发 miss 重建。single flight 按 key 合并成一次重建，其余等结果。
why_en: This is a cache stampede. Single flight coalesces by cache key: concurrent misses for feed:home share one rebuild, while different keys do not merge.
options_en: Hot-key problem; replicate the key.
Cache penetration; add a Bloom filter.
Cache stampede / thundering herd; request coalescing (single flight).
Dual-write problem; use a distributed transaction.
tradeoff: 按 key 单飞挡住重建洪峰 vs 等待者仍要等那次慢重建
whenOtherWins: 是持续热 key 而非过期瞬间时，用复制/本地缓存。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["GET feed:home miss"] --> K["inflight[feed:home]"]
    B["GET feed:home miss"] --> K
    C["GET user:42 miss"] --> U["inflight[user:42]"]
    K --> One["one rebuild"]
    One --> W["all feed waiters receive result"]
codeSample:
inflight = Map()

get(key):
  v = cache.get(key)
  if v != nil:
    return v

  if inflight.has(key):
    return await inflight[key]

  promise = rebuild_and_fill_cache(key)
  inflight[key] = promise
  try:
    return await promise
  finally:
    inflight.delete(key)

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个 key 的并发 miss 只让一个请求真正回源或重建，其余请求等待同一个结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single flight lets only one concurrent miss for the same key rebuild or fetch from the backend; the rest wait for the same result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断能不能合并的键，通常就是 cache key 或规范化后的 request fingerprint；不同用户、参数、权限导致结果不同就不能合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coalescing key decides what can merge, usually a cache key or normalized request fingerprint; different users, parameters, or permissions should not merge if the result differs.

optionExplanations: 热 key 是持续超高流量；这里是过期瞬间的重建洪峰。
