q_en: Which index is most efficient for this user-posts query?
options: 复合索引 (user_id, created_at)
只索引 content
两个独立索引，各查各的再内存合并
不加索引，靠全表扫描
options_en: A composite index on (user_id, created_at).
Index content only.
Two separate single-column indexes, merged in memory.
No index at all, relying on a full table scan.
why: 复合索引 (user_id, created_at) 一次覆盖「按用户定位 + 按时间排序」，正对最重要的查询；单列索引组合的效率远不如它。
why_en: A composite index on user id and created at directly serves the query for a user's recent posts.
whenOtherWins: 若查询只按单一维度过滤（只按用户、或只按时间取全站最新），单列索引就够了。
tradeoff: 一次复合索引覆盖过滤+排序 vs 拆成多个单列索引再合并

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个列上联合建立的索引，一次覆盖过滤和排序两种需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is built across multiple columns together to cover both filtering and sorting in one lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐行扫描整张表寻找匹配记录，没有用到索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full table scan reads every row in a table looking for matches, without using an index.

optionExplanations: 按 user_id 过滤、按 created_at 排序是最重要的查询模式，一个复合索引一次性覆盖这两步。
只有搜索帖子正文时 content 索引才有用，但这道题的查询条件根本不是内容。
两个单列索引理论上能被数据库合并，但高频主查询更该直接建一个匹配的复合索引，省掉合并开销。
小表可以靠全表扫描撑过去，但数据一旦变大，延迟就会明显变差。
optionExplanations_en: Filtering by user_id and sorting by created_at is the hot query, and one composite index covers both steps in a single lookup.
An index on content only helps when you search post text, but this query's predicate isn't about content at all.
The database can sometimes merge two single-column indexes, but a hot primary query is better served by one matching composite index that skips the merge cost.
A full table scan can get by on a small table, but latency degrades noticeably once the data grows.

scenario: GET /users/{id}/posts 端点越来越慢，排查发现每次都在全表扫描 posts。
scenario_en: The GET /users/{id}/posts endpoint is getting slow; investigation shows every request scans the whole posts table.
q: 最直接的修复是？
q_en: Which index fixes this slow posts endpoint?
options: CREATE INDEX ON posts(content);
CREATE INDEX ON posts(user_id);
CREATE INDEX ON users(email);
VACUUM posts;
options_en: CREATE INDEX ON posts(content);
CREATE INDEX ON posts(user_id);
CREATE INDEX ON users(email);
VACUUM posts;
why: 端点按 user_id 过滤 posts，就给 posts.user_id 建索引——面试里把索引直接对应到 API 端点，才显得你在考虑真实查询性能。
why_en: The endpoint filters posts by user id, so indexing posts on user id removes the full table scan.
whenOtherWins: 若端点还要按时间取「最近 N 条」，升级为复合索引 (user_id, created_at) 更优。
tradeoff: 索引命中端点真实过滤字段（user_id） vs 索引选错列白白增加写入维护开销

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 的维护命令，回收死元组占用的空间，不是性能索引手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: VACUUM is a Postgres maintenance command that reclaims space from dead rows; it isn't an indexing technique.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个列上联合建立的索引，一次覆盖过滤和排序两种需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is built across multiple columns together to cover both filtering and sorting in one lookup.

optionExplanations: 只有按正文搜索帖子时 content 索引才对得上，端点的查询谓词根本不是内容。
这条端点的查询谓词落在 user_id 上，缺的正是这一列的索引，建上就能去掉全表扫描。
email 在 users 表上，索引对错了表，帮不到 posts 的查询。
VACUUM 是清理膨胀空间的维护操作，补不上缺失索引这个根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: An index on content only matches searching post text, but the endpoint's predicate isn't about content at all.
The slow query is scanning posts to match a user, and there's no index backing that column yet — add one and the full scan disappears.
Email lives on the users table, so indexing it there doesn't help the posts query at all.
VACUUM is maintenance for reclaiming bloated space — it doesn't fix the underlying missing-index problem.

q: 范式化（normalization）的定义是？
q_en: What is the definition of normalization?
options: 把所有表合成一张
给每个字段加索引
把数据压缩存储
每条信息只存一处，防止更新遗漏造成的异常
options_en: Merge all tables into one.
Add an index to every field.
Compress the stored data.
Each fact is stored in exactly one place, preventing update-miss anomalies.
why: 范式化的核心承诺：单一事实来源。信息只有一份，就不存在多副本更新不同步导致的不一致状态。
why_en: Normalization stores each piece of information in exactly one place, preventing anomalies where an update happens in one copy but not another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每条信息只存一份，用外键把表连接起来，避免更新遗漏造成的不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization stores each fact exactly once and links tables with foreign keys, preventing update-miss inconsistencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 因为同一信息存了多份、只更新了其中一份而产生的不一致状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data anomaly is an inconsistency that appears when the same fact is stored in multiple places and only some copies get updated.

optionExplanations: 合表是反范式的方向，跟消除重复事实这个范式化的目标正好相反。
索引加速的是查询，不决定一个事实要存几份，跟范式化不是一回事。
压缩减少的是字节数，不处理改一处漏一处这种更新异常。
每条信息只存一份，不给改一处漏一处的机会——这正是范式化想要达成的目标。
optionExplanations_en: Merging tables is the denormalization direction, the opposite of normalization's goal of eliminating duplicate facts.
Indexes speed up queries; they don't decide how many copies of a fact exist, so that's unrelated to normalization.
Compression reduces byte count; it doesn't address the anomaly where one copy gets updated and another doesn't.
Store each fact exactly once so there's no chance of updating one copy and forgetting another — that's the whole point of normalization.

q: 把 username 反范式冗余进每条帖子记录，会带来什么后果？
q_en: What happens if you denormalize username into every post record?
options: 改名要更新他所有帖子，漏一条就不一致
读帖子会变慢
无法建索引
数据库会拒绝写入
options_en: A rename means updating every one of the user's posts — miss one and it's inconsistent.
Reading posts becomes slower.
You can no longer create indexes.
The database refuses the write.
why: 冗余数据 = 多份需要同步的副本：改名要刷全部历史帖子，任何遗漏都留下永久性的不一致。
why_en: With the username duplicated in every post, a rename must update all of them, and missing one leaves inconsistent data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了读性能主动在多处冗余存储同一份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately duplicates the same data in multiple places to speed up reads.

optionExplanations: 改名意味着要把这个用户名同步进他所有的历史帖子，哪怕漏改一条，那条帖子从此就跟真实用户名对不上。
冗余用户名通常是为了省 join，读帖子应该变快而不是变慢，这个方向反了。
冗余字段照样能建索引，问题不在索引能力，而在一致性维护。
数据库会正常接受这次写入，除非额外加了约束，不会主动拒绝。
optionExplanations_en: A rename means pushing the new username into every one of that user's historical posts, and missing even one leaves that post permanently out of sync with reality.
Redundant username data is usually there to skip a join, so reads should get faster, not slower — this has it backwards.
A redundant field can still be indexed just fine — the problem here is consistency upkeep, not indexing ability.
The database accepts the write normally, unless an extra constraint is added — it won't refuse it on its own.

q: 面试里对范式化/反范式的默认立场应该是？
q_en: What should your default stance be on normalization versus denormalization in interviews?
options: 一开始就全面反范式追求读性能
全部范式化，永不例外
先范式化保正确，确有需要才反范式
随机决定
options_en: Start fully denormalized from day one, chasing read performance.
Always normalize, with no exceptions ever.
Normalize first for correctness, denormalize only when you actually need to.
Decide randomly.
why: 顺序很重要：先规范化保证正确性，性能确实不够时再针对性反范式；反过来做会陷入一致性泥潭。
why_en: Start with a clean normalized model and denormalize only when needed, since consistency problems are harder than the performance problems they replace.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每条信息只存一份，用外键把表连接起来，避免更新遗漏造成的不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization stores each fact exactly once and links tables with foreign keys, preventing update-miss inconsistencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了读性能主动在多处冗余存储同一份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately duplicates the same data in multiple places to speed up reads.

optionExplanations: 读瓶颈还没出现就先反范式，等于提前把同步问题背上身，代价来得太早。
强一致数据确实该规范化，但读性能瓶颈出现时留一点例外空间往往更划算，永不例外太绝对。
从干净的范式化开始保证正确性，只在真的遇到性能瓶颈时才对热点做反范式——重复数据的一致性问题比它解决的性能问题更难缠。
schema 决策应该绑定访问模式和一致性需求，随机决定没有任何依据。
optionExplanations_en: Denormalizing before a read bottleneck even shows up means taking on sync problems too early, for a cost that isn't there yet.
Strongly consistent data should stay normalized, but leaving room for exceptions when a real read bottleneck appears usually pays off — 'never' is too absolute.

Begin from a normalized schema so correctness comes first, then denormalize specific hot spots only once a real performance wall shows up — duplicated data is harder to keep in sync than the query was slow.
Schema decisions should be tied to access patterns and consistency needs — deciding at random has no basis behind it.

q: 哪些场景下反范式是合理的例外？（多选）
q_en: When is denormalization a reasonable exception? (Choose all that apply.)
options: 分析/报表系统：聚合的数据很少变化
事件日志/审计跟踪：本来就是某时间点的数据快照
重读优化系统（如搜索引擎）：速度比一致性更关键
支付账务系统：钱的记录越冗余越安全
options_en: Analytics and reporting systems, where the aggregated data changes rarely.
Event logs and audit trails, which are inherently point-in-time snapshots.
Read-heavy optimized systems like search engines, where speed matters more than consistency.
Payment and ledger systems, where redundant money records are safer.
why: 三类例外的共性：数据不再变（快照/低频变更）或一致性可让位于速度。支付恰恰相反——强一致数据最不该冗余。
why_en: Denormalization suits analytics with infrequent changes, point-in-time event logs, and read-optimized systems like search, but never payments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录谁在什么时候做了什么操作的历史日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An audit trail is a historical log of who did what and when.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个时间点上数据状态的固定拷贝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A snapshot is a fixed copy of data’s state at one point in time.

optionExplanations: 报表聚合数据低频变化，反范式带来的重复计算成本很低，换读性能很划算。
事件日志和审计记录本来就是某一时刻的快照，不需要事后同步字段，冗余没有代价。
搜索这类重读系统能接受短暂旧数据，用一点一致性风险换更快的响应是合理取舍。
支付账务恰恰相反：钱的记录需要强一致和可审计，冗余只会扩大出错和对不上账的风险。
optionExplanations_en: Analytics aggregates change infrequently, so denormalization's recompute cost stays low while read speed improves — a good trade.
Event logs and audit trails are already point-in-time snapshots that never need syncing after the fact, so duplication costs nothing.
A search engine and similar read-heavy systems can live with slightly stale data, so giving up a bit of consistency for snappier responses is a fair trade.
Payment ledgers are the opposite case: money records need strong consistency and auditability, and duplication only expands the risk of mismatched books.

q: 既想要反范式的读性能，又不想弄脏数据模型，标准做法是？
q_en: What is the standard way to get denormalized read speed without dirtying the data model?
options: 把两份 schema 都写进数据库
真相源保持范式化，缓存层放反范式视图
放弃读性能
每天夜里全量同步一次
options_en: Store both schemas directly in the database.
Keep the source of truth normalized, put a denormalized view in the cache layer.
Give up on read performance.
Do a full resync once every night.
why: 两全法：数据库里的真相源永远规范干净，缓存层持有为读优化的反范式视图——预计算 join、聚合、任何让读快的结构。
why_en: Keep the source of truth normalized and put a cache in front holding a denormalized representation with precomputed joins and aggregations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统里被认定为权威、正确的那份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the authoritative copy of data that all other copies must match.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提前算好的汇总结果，读时直接取用不用现算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A precomputed aggregation is a summary calculated ahead of time so reads don’t have to compute it live.

optionExplanations: 把规范化和反范式两份 schema 都落进数据库，只会让同步逻辑和真相源边界更难维护。
数据库本身保持干净规范、当那个唯一权威的数据版本；前面另起一层缓存，专门存一份为读优化过的冗余数据，两边各司其职。
读性能完全可以靠缓存、预计算或索引拿回来，不必彻底放弃。
夜间全量同步适合离线报表，实时读路径等不了一整天的延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Writing both a normalized and a denormalized schema straight into the database just makes sync logic and the source-of-truth boundary harder to maintain.
The database itself stays the single normalized authority, while a cache layer in front carries a copy shaped for fast reads — you get both without compromising either.
Read performance can be recovered with caching, precomputation, or indexing — giving up on it entirely isn't necessary.
A nightly full resync suits offline reporting, but a real-time read path can't wait a full day for fresh data.

scenario: 帖子数据大到单库放不下要分片；系统的主要查询是「取某个用户的帖子」。
scenario_en: Posts are too large for one database, so you need sharding; the main query fetches posts for one user.
q: 分片键应该选？
q_en: Which sharding key should you choose for this posts workload?
options: 按帖子内容哈希
按 created_at 时间范围
按 user_id 分片，同用户帖子落同一分片
随机分片
options_en: Shard by a hash of the post content.
Shard by created_at time range.
Shard by user_id, so one user's posts land on the same shard.
Shard randomly.
why: 按主访问模式分片：查询以用户为单位，就按 user_id 分——相关数据聚在一起，查询单分片即可完成。
why_en: Shard by the primary access pattern: querying posts by user means sharding on user id so a user's posts stay on one shard.
whenOtherWins: 归档/分析型负载（写分散、读集中在时间段）可以用时间范围分区；但写密集系统按时间分片会造出热分片。
tradeoff: 按访问模式(user_id)分片、省掉跨分片查询 vs 时间/随机分片更均匀但打散相关数据

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行数据落在哪个分片上的字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard key is the field that determines which shard a row lives on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 需要同时查询多个分片再合并结果的查询，代价高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-shard query has to hit multiple shards and merge the results, which is expensive.

diagram:
flowchart TD
    Key["Pick shard key"] --> A["matches access pattern"]
    Key --> B["spreads writes"]
    Key --> C["limits cross shard reads"]
    A --> Choice["defensible tradeoff"]
    B --> Choice
    C --> Choice
optionExplanations: 内容哈希能把数据打散均匀，但没法让按用户查帖子落在单个分片，查询照样要扇出。
时间范围适合归档式读取，但写密集场景下最新的时间桶会变成热分片。
主查询是按用户取帖子，按 user_id 分片能让同一用户的数据共址，一个分片就能查完。
随机分片能均匀分散数据，但每次按用户查询都要扫全部分片，代价太高。
optionExplanations_en: Hashing on post content spreads data evenly, but it can't keep one user's posts on a single shard, so the query still has to fan out.
Time-range sharding suits archival-style reads, but under heavy writes the newest time bucket becomes a hot shard.
The primary query fetches a user's posts, and sharding by user_id co-locates that user's data so one shard can answer it.
Random sharding spreads data evenly, but every per-user query would have to scan every shard — too expensive.

q: 写密集系统按时间范围分片，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if a write-heavy system shards by time range?
options: 写入都砸向最新分片，形成热分片
写入被完美均分
读性能下降但写没问题
数据会丢失
options_en: All writes hit the newest shard, creating a hot shard.
Writes get spread out perfectly evenly.
Read performance suffers but writes are fine.
Data gets lost.
why: 「现在」永远只有一个：新写入全部落在最新时间段的分片上，其他分片闲着。时间分区只适合归档/分析这类读重写散的负载。
why_en: With time-range sharding all current writes hit the newest shard, creating a hot shard, which is an anti-pattern for write-heavy systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 绝大多数流量集中打在一个分片上，其它分片却很闲。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot shard is a single shard absorbing most of the traffic while the others sit idle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 表面合理但实践中会持续造成问题的常见设计错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An anti-pattern is a design that looks reasonable but reliably causes problems in practice.

optionExplanations: 任何时刻只有一个当下：新写入统统砸向对应当前时间段的那一个分片，别的分片都在空转，典型的热点。
只有 key 空间被打散时写入才可能均匀，时间范围分片恰恰相反，把当前写入全部堆在一处。
时间范围分片首先冲击的是写路径，而不是读路径，这个方向说反了。
分片策略差会拖慢系统，但不会直接让数据库把已写入的数据丢掉。
optionExplanations_en: There's only one 'now' at any moment — every new write slams into the shard for the current time window while the others sit idle, a textbook hot spot.
Writes only spread evenly when the key space is scattered — time-range sharding does the opposite, piling all current writes onto one shard.
Time-range sharding hits the write path first, not the read path — this has the direction backwards.
A bad sharding strategy makes things slow, but it doesn't make the database drop data it already wrote.

q: 按 user_id 分片后，「时间线要展示所关注的多个用户的帖子」这个功能会遇到什么？
q_en: After sharding by user_id, what problem does a timeline that shows followed users' posts face?
options: 自动变快
无任何影响
数据被自动复制
跨分片查询：查多个分片再合并，代价高
options_en: It automatically becomes faster.
There's no impact at all.
Data gets replicated automatically.
A cross-shard query: hit multiple shards and merge — expensive.
why: 关注列表横跨多个用户 = 横跨多个分片：查询要扇出到各分片再聚合。设计分片键时要预判这类查询并尽量规避。
why_en: A timeline across followed users spans multiple shards, forcing expensive scatter-gather queries that you should design to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 需要同时查询多个分片再合并结果的查询，代价高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-shard query has to hit multiple shards and merge the results, which is expensive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次请求分发给多个分片、再把结果聚合回来的查询模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather fans a single request out to multiple shards and then merges their results.

optionExplanations: 按用户共址只帮到单用户查询，关注流要跨多个用户合并，不会因此自动变快。
分片键决定一次查询要打到几个分片，关注列表跨用户就意味着跨分片，影响很实在。
分片不会自动把被关注用户的帖子复制过来，这不是分片机制提供的能力。
关注的可能是好几十个不同用户，这些帖子分散在各自的分片里，时间线得挨个分片取一遍再拼起来，代价不小，最好设计时就绕开这种查询。
optionExplanations_en: Co-locating by user only helps single-user queries; a followed-users feed spans multiple users and won't get automatically faster.
The shard key decides how many shards a query has to hit, and a cross-user feed means crossing shards — the impact is real.
Sharding doesn't automatically replicate a followed user's posts anywhere — that's not a capability it provides.

You might follow dozens of different users, and their posts live on separate shards, so building the timeline means hitting each shard and stitching results together — costly, and worth designing around.

q: 关于分片键的选择，最重要的提醒是？
q_en: What is the most important reminder when choosing a sharding key?
options: 分片键随时可以换，先随便选一个
分片键选择常是永久的，要先想清楚访问模式
永远按主键分片
分片键越多越好
options_en: You can change the shard key anytime; just pick one for now.
Shard key choice is usually permanent — think through the access pattern first.
Always shard by the primary key.
The more shard keys the better.
why: 分片键一旦定下，迁移成本极高，且所有查询的效率都取决于它——这是 schema 设计里最需要「三思」的决定之一。
why_en: Your shard key choice is often permanent and affects every query, so think carefully about primary access patterns first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行数据落在哪个分片上的字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard key is the field that determines which shard a row lives on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统最常执行的查询方式，比如按用户 ID 取最近帖子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An access pattern is a system’s typical way of querying data, such as fetching a user’s recent posts.

optionExplanations: 分片键一旦定下，迁移往往要搬走海量数据，随时能换低估了这个代价。
分片键几乎影响之后的每一条查询，而迁移代价极高，所以定下来之前必须先想清楚主要访问模式。
主键常常是可用的分片键，但热点分布和真实查询模式有时会要求换一个更合适的键。
分片键越多只会让路由逻辑和一致性维护更复杂，不是数量越多越好。
optionExplanations_en: Once a shard key is set, migrating usually means moving huge amounts of data — 'change it anytime' badly underestimates that cost.
This choice tends to be permanent and touches nearly every query that follows, so nail down how the data will mostly be accessed before locking it in.
The primary key is often a usable shard key, but hot spots and real query patterns sometimes call for a different one instead.
More shard keys just make routing logic and consistency harder to manage — more isn't better here.

q: 范式化 vs 反范式，本质在权衡什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between normalization and denormalization?
options: 存储成本 vs 网络带宽
开发速度 vs 代码质量
反范式用更新风险换读性能，范式化反之
安全性 vs 易用性
options_en: Storage cost versus network bandwidth.
Development speed versus code quality.
Denormalization trades update risk for read performance; normalization does the reverse.
Security versus usability.
why: 一句话：反范式让读变快（数据就地可得），但写变险（多副本要同步）；范式化写安全、读可能要 join。
why_en: Denormalization trades update complexity and consistency risk for read performance, while normalization does the reverse.
tradeoff: 反范式：省 join、读更快 vs 范式化：写安全、更新一致性有保障

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每条信息只存一份，用外键把表连接起来，避免更新遗漏造成的不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization stores each fact exactly once and links tables with foreign keys, preventing update-miss inconsistencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了读性能主动在多处冗余存储同一份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately duplicates the same data in multiple places to speed up reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的行拼接在一起的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join is a query operation that combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

optionExplanations: 存储和带宽确实会受影响，但它们不是范式化真正要权衡的核心轴。
开发速度不是判断数据副本要不要拆的主轴，这把数据建模问题和工程管理问题搞混了。
反范式拿一致性和更新的复杂度换读路径变快；范式化则反过来，靠 join 保证正确但读会多一步开销。
安全性该单独设计，跟数据一致性这个权衡不是同一个话题。
optionExplanations_en: Storage and bandwidth are affected, but they aren't the core axis normalization is actually trading against.
Development speed isn't the axis for deciding whether data should be duplicated — this conflates a modeling question with an engineering-process one.
Denormalization spends consistency and update complexity to buy faster reads; normalization flips that, staying correct through joins at some read-time cost.
Security should be designed separately — it's a different topic from this data-consistency tradeoff.

q: 把面试中引入数据库组件时的 schema 设计步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the schema-design steps in the right order when introducing a database in an interview.
steps: 决定哪些列需要索引（如有）
确定数据库类型
考虑是否需要分片；若要，选匹配主访问模式的分片键
为每个实体列出满足功能需求的字段
决定是否需要为性能反范式
为每个关系指定主键和外键
why: 六步清单：库类型 → 字段 → 主/外键 → 索引 → 反范式与否 → 分片与分片键。按这个顺序讲，白板自然成型。
why_en: Choose the database type, list the columns, specify keys, pick indexes, decide on denormalization, and finally consider sharding with a matching shard key.
tradeoff: 先按顺序锁定正确性（类型/键/索引） vs 过早跳到反范式/分片导致返工

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行数据落在哪个分片上的字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard key is the field that determines which shard a row lives on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个列上联合建立的索引，一次覆盖过滤和排序两种需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index is built across multiple columns together to cover both filtering and sorting in one lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了读性能主动在多处冗余存储同一份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately duplicates the same data in multiple places to speed up reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 外键：一张表中指向另一张表主键的字段，用来维系表间关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key is a column that references another table's primary key to enforce a relationship.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["1 库类型"] --> B["2 字段"]
    B --> C["3 主键/外键"]
    C --> D["4 索引"]
    D --> E["5 反范式?"]
    E --> F["6 分片/分片键?"]

q: 把「反范式化点赞数」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for denormalizing like_count in the right order.
steps: 选择：把 like_count 反范式进 posts 表
缓解：或保持真相源规范化，把反范式视图放到前置缓存层
属性：点赞数是跨表聚合、每次读都算太贵，且点赞可接受最终一致
需求：feed 必须快速加载帖子和点赞数
代价：点赞更新要双写，存在不一致风险
why: 需求（feed 快）→ 属性（聚合贵 + 可最终一致）→ 选择（反范式计数）→ 代价（双写不一致）→ 缓解（缓存层放反范式视图）。
why_en: Fast feeds plus tolerable staleness justify denormalizing like counts, whose dual-write risk is mitigated by keeping the truth normalized behind a cache.
tradeoff: 反范式点赞数换 feed 读取更快 vs 双写带来的不一致风险，靠前置缓存缓解

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了读性能主动在多处冗余存储同一份数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization deliberately duplicates the same data in multiple places to speed up reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时更新两个地方（如反范式字段和真实来源），一个成功一个失败就会不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual write updates two places at once — like a denormalized field and its source — and can diverge if one write fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短时间内各副本可能不同步，但最终会收敛到一致值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas may briefly disagree after a write but converge to the same value over time.

q: 选存储引擎 / 索引结构时，最该先问自己的一组问题是？
options: 内存/磁盘 · 读/写 · 等值/范围 · 超不超 RAM · 要不要持久化
用什么编程语言 · 团队规模多大 · 预算上限是多少
先站队决定要用 NoSQL 还是 SQL，再把它的特性从头到尾硬背下来
无脑默认使用 Postgres 存储所有数据，从来不做针对性分析
why: 选存储结构靠五问：内存/磁盘、读/写、等值/范围、超不超 RAM、要不要持久化。答案通常落在哈希表、B 树、LSM 树三选一，细节见下表。
why_en: You don't memorize storage choices — you ask five questions: (1) memory or disk, (2) read- or write-heavy, (3) exact-match only or need range/sort, (4) will data exceed RAM, (5) need durability. Three core structures: hash table (O(1) exact-match, in-memory), B-tree (read-optimized + range, on disk), and LSM tree (write-optimized, log-structured). This is the master map behind every index/engine card.

rows: O(1) 只等值·无范围（内存）
读优化·原地更新·范围+排序（磁盘）
写优化·顺序写+后台合并

q_en: When choosing a storage engine or index structure, what's the first set of questions to ask?
options_en: Memory or disk · read- or write-heavy · equality or range · fits in RAM or not · needs durability or not.
What programming language to use, how big the team is, what the budget is.
Pick NoSQL vs SQL first, then memorize every one of its features from start to finish.
Default to storing everything in Postgres blindly, never analyzing the access pattern at all.
optionExplanations: 对，这五个问题直接决定该选哪种存储结构：内存还是磁盘、读写比例、等值还是范围、是否超 RAM、要不要持久化。
语言、团队规模、预算是工程管理变量，不影响该选哈希表、B 树还是 LSM——真正决定因素是数据访问模式。
先站队 NoSQL/SQL 再硬背特性是本末倒置：存储结构该看访问模式，不是先选阵营。
跳过分析直接默认 Postgres：它默认走 B 树，遇到全内存等值查找或海量写入摄入这类场景就不是最优选择。
optionExplanations_en: Right — these five questions directly decide which storage structure to use: memory vs disk, read/write mix, equality vs range, fits in RAM, needs durability.
Language, team size, and budget are engineering-management variables — they don't decide between a hash table, B-tree, or LSM tree; the access pattern does.
Picking NoSQL vs SQL first and memorizing its features backwards is the wrong order — the structure choice should follow the access pattern, not a camp.
Skipping analysis and defaulting to Postgres: it defaults to B-tree, which isn't optimal for pure in-memory equality lookups or extreme write ingestion.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 没有索引时，按 email 在百万行的表里找一个用户，为什么慢？
options: 数据库锁竞争太激烈，读写互相阻塞
SQL 解析和优化器耗时太长
无索引只能逐页扫描整张表，每页都要读盘检查
网络往返次数太多，客户端反复请求
why: 无索引时数据库别无选择，只能把每一页数据依次读进内存逐行检查；上百万页就是上百万次相对缓慢的磁盘读，只为找一条记录。
why_en: Without an index the database must sequentially scan every page, loading each from disk into memory, which means millions of slow disk reads to find one record.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Query email"] --> B["Full table scan"]
  B --> C["Check every row"]
  C --> D["Return match"]
options_en: Lock contention is too severe, blocking reads and writes against each other.
SQL parsing and query planning take too long.
Without an index it must scan every page sequentially, reading each into memory to check.
There are too many network round trips between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查找而维护的、独立于主表的结构化数据路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a separate structured data path maintained purely to speed up lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言，用来查询和操作关系型数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, used to query and manipulate relational databases.

q_en: Why is finding a user by email slow in a million-row table with no index?
optionExplanations: 锁竞争影响的是并发写入的等待时间，不会让单条查询本身慢到要扫全表。
SQL 解析和选执行计划确实耗时，但那是毫秒级开销，远不是全表扫描慢的主因。
对，没有索引数据库就只能按物理顺序把每一页读进内存逐行核对，页数越多越慢。
一次请求只有一次网络往返，跟数据库内部要扫多少页无关。
optionExplanations_en: Lock contention affects how long concurrent writers wait, not why a single lookup itself has to scan the whole table.
SQL parsing and planning do cost time, but that's a millisecond-level overhead, not the reason a full scan is slow.
Right — with no index the database has no shortcut, so it loads every page in physical order and checks each row; more pages means more time.
A single request makes one round trip; that has nothing to do with how many pages the database scans internally.

q: 主表数据在磁盘上的典型存储形式是？
options: 堆文件（heap file）：行按写入顺序堆放，没有特定排序
始终严格按主键排序的有序文件，写入时还需要维持排序位置
哈希桶数组，把行按主键的哈希值分散存放各处
按列存储的列式压缩数据块，而非按行组织存储
why: 选堆文件。这里问主表数据，不是主键索引：行通常堆在数据页里；主键 B-tree 另存并指向这些行。
why_en: Choose heap file. This asks about table data, not the primary-key index: rows usually live in heap pages, while a separate primary-key B-tree points to them.
whenOtherWins: 例外：InnoDB 用 clustered index；Postgres 常见是 heap table + separate index。
options_en: A heap file: rows pile up in write order, with no particular sort order.
An always-sorted file strictly ordered by primary key, where each write must also maintain its sort position.
A hash bucket array that scatters rows across buckets based on the primary key's hash value.
Column-oriented compressed data blocks, organized by column rather than by row.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    T["table heap pages\nrows in write order"]
    I["primary-key B-tree\nsorted keys"] --> T
    Q["WHERE id = 42"] --> I
    T --> R["row data"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有特定顺序的行集合，数据按写入先后堆放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heap file is an unordered collection of rows stored in the order they were written.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识一行数据的列或列组合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary key is the column or columns that uniquely identify each row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引顺序就是主表数据顺序的存储方式，MySQL InnoDB 的主键就是典型例子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clustered index stores table rows in the same order as the index; MySQL InnoDB primary keys are the classic example.

q_en: How is the main table data usually stored on disk?
optionExplanations: 对，主表数据默认堆放在数据页里、没有排序要求，插入只管追加；真正维持顺序的是另外那棵主键 B 树索引。
这其实是聚簇索引（clustered index）的做法，如 InnoDB；本题问的是更常见的默认存储：堆文件。
哈希桶数组是哈希索引的结构，不是主表数据默认的存放方式。
列式存储是分析型数据库（如 ClickHouse）的组织方式，OLTP 主表默认按行存放在堆文件里。
optionExplanations_en: Right — by default, rows just pile into heap pages with no order; insert simply appends. Keeping order is the separate primary-key B-tree's job.
That's actually a clustered index, like InnoDB uses; this question asks about the more common default: an unordered heap file.
A hash bucket array is how a hash index is structured, not how the main table's rows are stored by default.
Columnar storage is how analytical databases like ClickHouse organize data; OLTP tables default to row-oriented heap files.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 为什么每次数据库查询都绕不开「从磁盘加载到内存」这一步？
options: 因为内存容量实在太小，根本没办法放下任何持久化的数据
数据落在磁盘上，只有搬进内存（RAM）才能被 CPU 处理
因为磁盘硬件本身设计上完全不支持随机读取
为了保证事务的隔离性级别能够真正达标
why: 数据落在磁盘（如今多为 SSD），而 CPU 只能处理内存里的数据，所以每个查询都要把相关页从磁盘搬进 RAM。索引的价值就是减少要搬的页数。
why_en: Data lives on disk but can only be processed in memory, so every query loads pages from disk into RAM, and indexes minimize how many pages that takes.
options_en: Because memory is supposedly far too small to hold any durable data at all, so everything must live permanently on disk.
Data sits on disk, and only once it's pulled into memory (RAM) can the CPU process it.
Because disk hardware itself is designed to not support random reads at all.
To make sure the transaction isolation level genuinely meets its guarantee.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机存取内存，CPU 能直接处理的高速易失存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAM stands for Random Access Memory, the fast volatile storage the CPU can directly process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器，执行程序指令的核心部件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, executes program instructions.

q_en: Why does every database query have to load data from disk into memory?
optionExplanations: 夸大了：内存确实放不下全部数据，但真正原因是处理器只能操作装在内存里的东西，磁盘上的页得先搬进 RAM 才能被读到。
对，处理器只能读写内存里的内容；磁盘上的页得先被搬进 RAM 才能被访问，这一步谁都跳不过。
现代 SSD/HDD 都支持随机读取，只是比顺序读慢，不是不支持。
隔离级别管的是并发事务互相看不看得到彼此的修改，跟数据要不要从磁盘搬进内存无关。
optionExplanations_en: Overstated — memory can't hold everything, but the real reason is a processor can only operate on what is already loaded into memory; a disk page has to be pulled in first.
Right — the processor can only read and write content sitting in memory; a page on disk always has to be pulled into RAM first, no way around it.
Modern SSDs and HDDs both support random reads — they're just slower than sequential reads, not unsupported.
Isolation levels control whether concurrent transactions see each other's uncommitted changes; unrelated to moving data from disk into memory.

q: 关于 SSD 上「随机访问 vs 顺序访问」，正确的说法是？
options: SSD 上随机访问和顺序访问的速度完全一样，没有任何差距
SSD 上随机访问的速度反而比顺序访问还要更快
只有传统机械硬盘 HDD 才会存在两者的速度差距
SSD 上随机访问仍明显慢于顺序访问——常见误解是这差距已消失
why: 常见误解是 SSD 抹平了差距：其实差距只是比 HDD 小，随机访问依然明显更慢；HDD 上差距更悬殊，所以合理建索引至关重要。
why_en: Even on SSDs random access is still significantly slower than sequential access, a smaller gap than on HDDs but a very real one.
options_en: On an SSD, random access and sequential access are exactly the same speed, with no gap at all.
On an SSD, random access is actually faster than sequential access.
Only traditional mechanical HDDs have a speed gap between the two.
SSD random access is still noticeably slower than sequential — the common misconception is that this gap has vanished.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固态硬盘，无机械部件的闪存存储介质，随机访问比机械硬盘快得多但仍慢于顺序访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSD stands for Solid State Drive, flash-based storage much faster at random access than spinning disks but still slower than sequential access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机械硬盘，靠磁头寻道读写的存储介质，随机访问比顺序访问慢得多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HDD stands for Hard Disk Drive, mechanical storage where random access is much slower than sequential access due to seek time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按不连续、不可预测的顺序读写数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random access means reading or writing data in a non-sequential, unpredictable order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按连续顺序读写数据，通常更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential access means reading or writing data in contiguous order, which is usually faster.

q_en: What is true about random access versus sequential access on SSDs?
optionExplanations: SSD 确实比 HDD 抹平了很多差距，但没抹平到「完全一样」；随机访问仍要付出额外开销（如闪存页/块管理）。
说反了：无论 SSD 还是 HDD，顺序访问都比随机访问快，只是 SSD 上差距被缩小了。
HDD 上差距确实更悬殊（机械寻道），但 SSD 上的差距只是变小，并没有消失。
对，SSD 只是把差距从 HDD 的数量级缩小到更小但依然明显的程度，索引依然重要。
optionExplanations_en: SSDs do narrow the gap versus HDDs, but not to zero — random access still pays extra overhead like flash page/block management.
Backwards — on both SSD and HDD, sequential beats random; SSDs just shrink that gap, they don't invert it.
The gap is bigger on HDDs because of mechanical seek time, but on SSDs it only shrinks — it doesn't disappear.
Right — SSDs shrink the gap from HDD-scale down to something smaller but still real, which is why indexing still matters.

q: 索引让查询变快的本质机制是什么？
options: 把所有数据都压缩得更小，从而节省磁盘空间的占用
提供结构化路径，直接指出数据在哪些页，减少要读的页数
把整张表完整地常驻内存，永远都不用碰磁盘
对所有磁盘页做并行扫描，靠多线程来加速查找
why: 索引是为搜索优化的独立数据结构：它告诉你目标数据具体在哪些页，从而不必逐页检查。就像用书的目录直接翻到相关页，而不是一页页找。
why_en: An index is a separate search-optimized structure that tells the database exactly which pages hold the target data, minimizing pages read from storage.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root page"] --> B["Internal page"]
  B --> C["Leaf page"]
  C --> D["Row pointer"]
options_en: Compress all the data down smaller, saving disk space usage.
Provide a structured path that points straight to the pages holding the data, cutting how many pages you read.
Keep the entire table permanently resident in memory, so disk is never touched.
Parallel-scan every disk page at once, using multiple threads to speed up the search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库读写磁盘的最小单位，典型大小 8KB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disk page is the smallest unit a database reads or writes on disk, typically eight kilobytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查找而维护的、独立于主表的结构化数据路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a separate structured data path maintained purely to speed up lookups.

q_en: What is the core mechanism that makes an index speed up queries?
optionExplanations: 索引确实占额外空间，但目的不是压缩主表——它的作用是加速查找，不是省空间。
对，索引本质是一条结构化路径：直接告诉你目标数据落在哪几页，不用逐页翻找。
常驻内存靠的是缓冲池缓存热数据，不是索引的机制；索引本身也要落盘。
普通查询不会靠多线程并行扫全部页来加速，索引靠的是减少要读的页数，不是加并发。
optionExplanations_en: An index does cost extra space, but its purpose isn't shrinking the main table — it speeds up lookups, not saves space.
Right — an index is fundamentally a structured path: it tells you exactly which pages hold the target data, skipping page-by-page hunting.
Staying resident in memory is the buffer pool caching hot pages, not something the index does — indexes live on disk too.
A normal query doesn't get sped up by parallel-scanning every page with more threads; an index works by cutting pages read, not adding concurrency.

q: 索引不是免费的。它的代价包括哪些？（多选）
options: 额外磁盘空间，有时接近原始数据大小
每次插入/更新除了改主表，还要更新表上的每一个索引
多个索引会让一次写操作触发多次磁盘写
有索引后读取一定变慢
why: 索引的三重代价：占磁盘空间、写入时每个索引都要维护、多索引放大写开销。读取恰恰是索引加速的对象，不会因此变慢。
why_en: Indexes cost extra disk space and slow down writes because every insert or update must also update each index, turning one write into several disk writes.
options_en: It costs extra disk space, sometimes nearly as much as the original data.
Every insert or update must update the main table plus every index on it.
Multiple indexes turn a single write into several disk writes.
Reads always get slower once you add an index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入时同步更新索引结构的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index maintenance is the overhead of keeping index structures updated on every write.

q_en: Indexes are not free. What costs do they add? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 额外磁盘空间是实打实的代价：索引是独立结构，宽字段索引甚至能接近原表大小。
每次 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE 除了改主表，还要同步维护这张表上的所有索引，这是写变慢的主因。
索引越多，一次逻辑写就要触发越多次物理磁盘写，写吞吐随索引数量下降。
错——读取正是索引存在的目的，加索引后同类查询通常更快，不会变慢。
optionExplanations_en: Extra disk space is a real cost — an index is a separate structure, and for wide columns it can approach the size of the original table.
Every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE has to update the main table plus every index on it in sync — that's the main reason writes slow down.
The more indexes there are, the more physical disk writes one logical write triggers, so write throughput drops as index count grows.
Wrong — reads are exactly what an index speeds up; after adding an index, matching queries usually get faster, not slower.

scenario: 一张日志表：持续高频插入新记录，但几乎从不查询旧数据。
q: 对这张表，关于索引的正确判断是？
options: 尽量多建索引以防万一，覆盖所有可能查询
必须建覆盖索引，避免任何回表
索引可能弊大于利：写多读少，维护开销盖过读收益
建哈希索引就能兼顾写入和查询
why: 写频繁、读极少的表是索引伤害大于收益的经典案例：每次插入都要维护索引，却几乎没人来读。这里少建甚至不建索引才对。
why_en: A write-heavy, rarely-read logging table is the classic case where index maintenance overhead outweighs the benefit.
whenOtherWins: 反过来，读多写少的表（用户资料、商品目录）索引收益远超维护成本，应该按查询模式建索引。
options_en: Add as many indexes as possible just in case, to cover every possible query.
You must add a covering index to avoid any table lookup.
Indexes may hurt more than help here: writes dominate, so maintenance overhead outweighs the read benefit.
A hash index alone can satisfy both writing and querying.
tradeoff: 索引维护成本 vs 查询收益

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

q_en: For this table, what is the right indexing judgment?
scenario_en: A log table receives high-frequency inserts, but old records are almost never queried.
optionExplanations: 「多建索引防万一」在读多的表上合理，但这张表几乎没人读，多建的索引只会白白拖慢每次插入。
覆盖索引能省回表，但前提是有实际的高频读查询要优化；这张表读极少，谈不上要不要回表。
对，写多读少时索引维护成本盖过查询收益，应该少建甚至不建索引，把插入吞吐留住。
哈希索引能加速等值查找，但解决不了写入侧的索引维护开销——这张表的痛点在写不在读。
optionExplanations_en: "Index everything just in case" makes sense when reads are frequent, but this table is barely read — extra indexes just slow down every insert.
A covering index saves a table lookup, but only pays off with real high-frequency reads to optimize; this table is barely read at all.
Right — when writes dominate and reads are rare, index upkeep outweighs query gains, so build few or no indexes and protect insert throughput.
A hash index would speed up equality lookups, but it doesn't touch the write-side maintenance cost — this table's pain point is writes, not reads.

scenario: 一张只有几百行的小配置表，被问要不要加索引。
q: 最合理的回答是？
options: 可以不加：表太小，索引维护成本可能超过一次顺序扫描
必须加索引，任何表都不能有任何例外情况
加哈希索引，因为它的查找速度永远是最快的
加覆盖索引，提前避免所有可能出现的回表开销
why: 几百行的小表全扫一遍非常便宜，索引的维护与遍历成本反而可能更高。索引的价值随数据量增长才显现。
why_en: For a tiny table a sequential scan is so cheap that maintaining and traversing an index can cost more than it saves.
whenOtherWins: 当表增长到几十万、上百万行且有明确过滤/排序模式时，就该按查询模式补上索引了。
options_en: Skip it: the table is small enough that index upkeep can cost more than one sequential scan.
You must add an index — no table is ever an exception, no matter how small.
Add a hash index, because its lookup speed is always the fastest, period.
Add a covering index up front to avoid any possible table-lookup cost.
tradeoff: 索引维护成本 vs 顺序扫描成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 从头到尾依次读取表中每一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential scan reads every row of a table from start to end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

q_en: What is the most reasonable answer for this tiny table?
scenario_en: You are asked whether to add an index to a tiny configuration table with only a few hundred rows.
optionExplanations: 对，几百行的表全表扫描几乎不花时间，索引反而多一份维护和遍历成本，得不偿失。
「任何表都要加索引」是教条：数据量小到能整表塞进内存时，索引的收益压根体现不出来。
哈希索引等值查找确实快，但这张表本来扫描就快，谈不上要不要用哪种索引。
覆盖索引是为了省回表开销，但小表回表本身就便宜，这个优化在这里没有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a full scan of a few hundred rows is nearly free, while an index adds real maintenance and traversal cost; not worth it yet.
"Every table needs an index" is dogma — when the whole table already fits comfortably in memory, an index's benefit never shows up.
A hash index is fast for equality lookups, but this table is already cheap to scan, so index type isn't the issue here.
A covering index exists to skip the extra table lookup, but on a small table that lookup is already cheap, so it buys nothing here.

q: 索引对内存占用的实际影响，下面哪个判断最准确？
options: 多一个索引，内存占用就会直接翻一倍变大
索引完全不会占用任何一点点内存空间
内存影响是索引所有代价里最致命的那一个
影响常被夸大：缓冲池管理已很智能，但仍要监控索引使用
why: 内存影响常被夸大：缓冲池是 LRU 缓存，只把热页留在内存，冷索引几乎不占 RAM，不会「翻一倍」。真正该防的是没人查却拖慢每次写的索引。
why_en: This card is only about the MEMORY cost — don't conflate it with the other two. An index has three costs: (1) slower writes — every insert/update/delete must maintain it (write amplification), the main cost; (2) extra disk — a separate B-tree structure; (3) memory — the topic here, and the overhyped one: the buffer pool is an LRU cache that keeps only hot pages, so cold indexes barely occupy RAM (no doubling). The real danger is unused indexes that slow every write for zero read benefit — monitor and drop them.
options_en: Adding one more index directly doubles memory usage.
An index doesn't use even a tiny bit of memory.
Memory impact is the single most damaging cost among everything an index costs.
The impact is often overstated: buffer pool management is already smart, but index usage still needs monitoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库在内存里缓存磁盘页的区域，减少重复磁盘读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The buffer pool is the in-memory area a database uses to cache disk pages and avoid repeated disk reads.

q_en: Which statement best describes how indexes affect memory usage?

rows: 多一份 B 树结构占盘
每次增删改都要多维护它 → 写变慢
只有被频繁读的热页才进缓冲池

optionExplanations: 夸大了：缓冲池只缓存热页，多数索引躺在盘上不占内存，不会让内存直接翻倍。
索引确实要占一点内存（至少缓存部分热页），说完全不占用是走了另一个极端。
内存不是索引最致命的代价——写放大（每次增删改都要同步维护索引）才是主要成本。
对，缓冲池管理已经很智能，内存影响常被高估；真正要盯的是没人用却拖慢写入的索引，靠监控使用率处理。
optionExplanations_en: Overstated — the buffer pool only caches hot pages, and most of an index sits cold on disk, so memory usage doesn't simply double.
An index does use some memory (at least the hot pages it caches), so claiming zero memory use is the opposite extreme.
Memory isn't the most damaging cost of an index — write amplification (keeping the index in sync on every write) is the main one.
Right — buffer pool management is already smart, so memory impact is often overstated; watch for unused indexes slowing writes instead, via usage monitoring.

q: 给一张表新增一个索引，真实代价有哪些？（多选）
options: 写变慢：每次 INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE 都要顺带更新这个索引（写放大）
占磁盘：索引是表旁边一份独立的 B 树结构，需要额外存储
占内存翻倍：多一个索引，RAM 占用就翻一倍
没人用的索引纯亏：白维护 + 白占盘却零读收益，应监控并删除
why: 加索引两类真实代价：写变慢（每次增删改都要同步维护索引）和占磁盘（独立 B 树结构）。内存常被高估——缓冲池只缓存热页，冷索引几乎不占 RAM。真正要防的是没人查却拖慢写入的索引。
why_en: Adding an index has two real costs: slower writes (every insert/update/delete must maintain it — write amplification, the main one) and extra disk (a separate B-tree). Memory is overhyped: the buffer pool is an LRU cache that keeps only hot pages, so cold indexes barely touch RAM (no doubling). The real danger is unused indexes that slow every write for zero read benefit — monitor and drop them.

rows: 多一份 B 树结构占盘
每次增删改都要多维护它 → 写变慢
只有被频繁读的热页才进缓冲池

q_en: Adding an index to a table has real costs — which are they? (select all that apply)
options_en: Slower writes: every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE also has to update this index (write amplification).
More disk usage: an index is a separate B-tree structure next to the table, needing extra storage.
Memory usage roughly doubles: adding one more index doubles RAM usage.
An unused index is pure loss: maintained and stored for zero read benefit, so it should be monitored and dropped.
optionExplanations: 写变慢是主要代价：每次 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE 除了改主表，还要同步维护这个索引，拖慢写入吞吐。
占磁盘是实打实的开销：索引是表旁边一份独立的 B 树结构，宽字段索引甚至能接近原表体积。
错——内存占用常被夸大：缓冲池是 LRU 缓存，只留热页在内存，冷索引几乎不占 RAM，不会「翻一倍」。
对，没人用的索引纯亏：白白维护、白占磁盘，读收益是零，应该靠监控使用率定期清理。
optionExplanations_en: Slower writes are the main cost: every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE has to update the main table plus keep this index in sync, dragging down write throughput.
Extra disk usage is a real cost too — an index is a separate B-tree structure next to the table, and on wide columns it can approach the table's own size.
Wrong — the memory hit is often overstated: the buffer pool only keeps hot pages resident, so a cold index barely touches RAM; it doesn't double usage.
Right — an unused index is pure loss: it's maintained and stored for zero read benefit, so it should be found via usage monitoring and dropped.

q: 补全面试常考的索引家族：
text: 通用默认用 {{B-tree}}；极端写入负载用 {{LSM tree}} 存储引擎；纯精确匹配用 {{hash}} 索引；经纬度邻近搜索用 {{geospatial}} 索引（如 GeoHash / R-tree）；全文搜索用 {{inverted}} 索引（倒排）。
why: 五类索引各解一类问题：B 树是万金油，LSM 吃写入，哈希只做等值，地理空间管 2D 邻近，倒排管文本。面试先想清楚查询形态再选。
why_en: B-trees are the default, LSM trees serve write-heavy workloads, hash indexes do exact matches, geospatial indexes handle proximity, and inverted indexes power text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写的存储引擎，靠内存缓冲和后台合并优化写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a storage engine that turns random writes into sequential writes using an in-memory buffer and background merging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 理解二维空间邻近关系的索引，如 geohash、四叉树、R 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index understands 2D proximity, implemented via approaches like geohash, quadtrees, or R-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

q_en: Fill in the common index families interviewers expect you to know:
text_en: General-purpose default: {{B-tree}}; write-heavy: {{LSM tree}} storage engine; exact-match only: {{hash}} index; lat/lng proximity: {{geospatial}} index (e.g. GeoHash, R-tree); full-text search: {{inverted}} index.

q: B 树节点和二叉树节点的关键区别是？
options: B 树节点和二叉树一样，每个节点最多只能有两个子节点
B 树节点可以有数百个子节点，节点内是有序的键+指针数组
B 树节点只会存储指向子节点的指针，不存储任何键值
B 树虽然名字里带「树」，但本质上根本不是树结构
why: 二叉树每节点最多两个孩子，B 树节点能有数百个孩子，节点内是有序的键+指针数组。扇出大意味着树很矮，找数据只需极少次磁盘读。
why_en: Unlike binary trees, a B-tree node can have hundreds of children with an ordered array of keys and pointers, keeping the tree shallow to minimize disk reads.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root page"] --> B["Internal page"]
  B --> C["Leaf page"]
  C --> D["Row pointer"]
options_en: A B-tree node is just like a binary tree — at most two children per node.
A B-tree node can have hundreds of children, with an ordered array of keys plus pointers inside the node.
A B-tree node only stores pointers to its children — it stores no key values at all.
Despite the name, a B-tree isn't fundamentally a tree structure at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个节点最多两个子节点的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A binary tree is a tree structure where each node has at most two children.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个树节点能指向的子节点数量，扇出越大树越矮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is how many children a tree node can point to; higher fanout means a shallower tree.

q_en: What is the key difference between a B-tree node and a binary-tree node?
optionExplanations: 说反了：这恰恰是二叉树的定义（最多两个孩子），B 树的扇出远不止两个。
对，B 树节点通常能塞下数百个键+指针，扇出大意味着树很矮，几次磁盘读就能到叶子。
B 树节点既存键也存指向子树的指针，键负责在节点内做范围划分，不是只存指针。
B 树确实是树结构，只是节点更宽、扇出更大，跟二叉树是同一族的变体。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards — that's the definition of a binary tree (at most two children); a B-tree's fanout is far larger.
Right — a B-tree node typically holds hundreds of keys plus pointers; that high fanout keeps the tree shallow, so a lookup takes only a few disk reads.
A B-tree node stores both keys and child pointers — keys are what let it partition ranges within the node, not pointers alone.
A B-tree is genuinely a tree — it just has much wider nodes and higher fanout than a binary tree, but it's the same family.

q: B 树的结构性规则包括哪些？（多选）
options: 所有叶子节点必须在同一深度
非根节点通常保持半满到满（约 m/2 到 m 个键）
有 k 个键的内部节点恰好有 k+1 个子节点
节点内的键无需保持有序
why: 选 A/B/C。B 树靠叶子同深保持平衡；节点通常至少半满，避免树变瘦变高；内部节点的 k 个 key 把范围切成 k+1 段。D 错，因为节点内 key 必须有序。
why_en: Choose A/B/C. A B-tree stays balanced by keeping all leaves at the same depth, keeping nodes roughly half-full or fuller, and using k keys in an internal node to split the key space into k+1 child ranges. D is wrong because keys inside a node must stay sorted.
options_en: All leaf nodes must sit at the same depth.
Non-root nodes usually stay between roughly half-full and full, about m/2 to m keys.
An internal node with k keys has exactly k+1 children.
Keys inside a node do not need to stay sorted.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  R["internal node: keys 10 | 20"]
  R --> C0["child 0: < 10"]
  R --> C1["child 1: 10..20"]
  R --> C2["child 2: > 20"]
  C0 --> L0["leaf depth 2"]
  C1 --> L1["leaf depth 2"]
  C2 --> L2["leaf depth 2"]

termDefinitions.meaning: B 树的阶 m 决定节点容量；不同教材有 max keys 或 max children 两种口径，所以面试里记“至少半满、最多装满”更稳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree's order m determines node capacity; textbooks vary between max-keys and max-children conventions, so in interviews remember the practical idea: roughly half-full to full.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非叶子节点，负责用有序 key 把搜索范围分给多个子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An internal node is a non-leaf node that uses sorted keys to route searches to child ranges.

q_en: Which structural rules does a B-tree maintain? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 对，所有叶子必须停在同一层，这正是 B 树「自平衡」的定义，避免某条路径特别深。
对，节点半满到满的约束防止树退化成瘦高结构，保证扇出稳定、树高可控。
对，k 个键把节点的取值范围切成 k+1 段，每段对应一个子指针，这就是内部节点的分支逻辑。
错——节点内的键必须保持有序，这样才能靠二分查找快速定位该往哪个子指针走。
optionExplanations_en: Right — every leaf must sit at the same depth; that's literally the definition of B-tree self-balancing, so no path is disproportionately deep.
Right — keeping nodes half-full to full stops the tree from degenerating into something thin and tall, keeping fanout and height predictable.
Right — k keys split a node's range into k+1 segments, each pointing to one child; that's exactly how internal-node branching works.
Wrong — keys inside a node must stay sorted, which is what makes binary search inside the node possible to pick the right child pointer.

q: B 树节点的大小通常被设计成正好匹配什么？
options: 一个磁盘页，典型为 8KB
一个 CPU 缓存行（64 字节）
一个内存页（4KB 固定）
整个表的大小
why: 8KB 是磁盘页这个硬件给定值，不是公式推导出来的；B 树节点对齐它，一次 I/O 正好读满一个节点，这是后续对比 LSM/哈希索引 I/O 效率的基准。
why_en: Eight kilobytes is a given hardware constant, not a derived number; aligning B-tree nodes to it means one I/O reads one full node, the baseline for later I/O comparisons.
scenario: 面试官追问：为什么 Postgres 把 B 树节点大小固定设计成这个数字，而不是随便选。
options_en: One disk page, typically eight kilobytes.
One CPU cache line, sixty-four bytes.
One fixed four-kilobyte memory page.
The size of the entire table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库读写磁盘的最小单位，典型大小 8KB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disk page is the smallest unit a database reads or writes on disk, typically eight kilobytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对磁盘的一次读或写操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O, or Input/Output, here means one read or write operation to disk.

termDefinitions.term: CPU 缓存行 / CPU cache line
termDefinitions.meaning: CPU 内部的小容量高速缓存行，一般 64 字节，远小于磁盘页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU cache line is a small, very fast on-chip cache unit, typically 64 bytes, far smaller than a disk page.

q_en: A B-tree node is usually sized to match what unit?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why PostgreSQL sizes B-tree nodes to this number instead of choosing an arbitrary size.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: PostgreSQL 用 B 树按 id=350 找一条记录，通常需要读多少个磁盘页？
options: 几十页，需要逐层向下一点点慢慢定位
上百页，几乎等同于一次完整的全表扫描
只需 2-3 页：根节点、内部节点、叶节点各一次
必须读整张表的每一页才能最终确认
why: B 树扇出大、树矮，一次点查通常只读根、内部、叶共 2-3 页——这不是背诵数字，而是后面对比 LSM 读放大的基准线。
why_en: Thanks to high fanout, a B-tree point lookup typically reads only two to three pages — root, internal, leaf — the baseline for later LSM read-amplification comparisons.
scenario: 面试官问：B 树的高扇出到底能把一次点查的磁盘读次数压到多低。
options_en: Dozens of pages, needing to narrow it down layer by layer, slowly.
Hundreds of pages, nearly equivalent to a full table scan.
Only two to three pages: root, maybe one internal node, and one leaf node.
The entire table, every page, must be read to be sure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个树节点能指向的子节点数量，扇出越大树越矮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is how many children a tree node can point to; higher fanout means a shallower tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只查一个精确 key 的查询，例如按主键取一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point lookup is a query for one exact key, such as fetching a row by primary key.

q_en: In PostgreSQL, how many disk pages does a B-tree lookup for id=350 usually read?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how low a B-tree's high fanout can push the disk-page reads for one point lookup.
optionExplanations: 几十页意味着树按层线性慢慢缩小范围；B 树的扇出很大，用不了几十页就能锁定。
上百页已经接近全表扫描的量级，那是没有索引、逐页扫描才会有的代价，不是有索引后的样子。
对，扇出足够大时，从根到叶最多经过一层内部节点，读盘次数被压到个位数。
读整张表是没有索引才会发生的最坏情况，有 B 树索引后不需要这么做。
optionExplanations_en: Dozens of pages implies the tree narrows down layer by layer slowly; a B-tree's fanout is high enough to land the target well before that.
Hundreds of pages is already close to full-scan territory — that's the cost of scanning without an index, not an indexed lookup.
Right — with a large enough fanout, the path from root to leaf crosses at most one internal node, keeping disk reads down to a single digit.
Reading the whole table is the worst case with no index at all; a B-tree index means you never have to do that.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 在 PostgreSQL 里建一张带 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY 和 email UNIQUE 的表，会自动发生什么？
options: 什么索引都不会自动建
自动建两个 B 树索引：主键和 email 各一个
自动创建两个哈希索引来处理
只给主键建索引，唯一约束靠全表扫描检查
why: Postgres 几乎处处用 B 树：主键、唯一约束、常规索引默认都是 B 树。B 树保持有序，同时支撑唯一性检查和范围查询。
why_en: PostgreSQL automatically creates two B-tree indexes for this table, one for the primary key and one for the unique email constraint.
options_en: No index gets created automatically at all.
Two B-tree indexes are created automatically: one for the primary key, one for email.
Two hash indexes get created automatically instead.
Only the primary key gets an index; the unique constraint is checked via full table scan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自增整数主键，PostgreSQL 里的常见写法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIAL PRIMARY KEY is PostgreSQL syntax for an auto-incrementing integer primary key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证某列（组合）在表中不出现重复值的约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A unique constraint guarantees a column or column set never has duplicate values in the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: What happens automatically when you create a PostgreSQL table with SERIAL PRIMARY KEY and email UNIQUE?
optionExplanations: 错——主键和唯一约束都会自动触发建索引，不是什么都不建。
对，SERIAL PRIMARY KEY 和 UNIQUE 各自触发一次自动建索引，两个都默认是 B 树。
Postgres 的默认索引类型是 B 树，不是哈希索引——哈希索引存在但不是默认选项。
唯一约束不是靠全表扫描检查的，Postgres 会专门为它建一个索引来快速判重。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — both the primary key and the unique constraint automatically trigger an index; it's not that nothing gets built.
Right — SERIAL PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE each trigger their own automatic index, and both default to B-tree.
Postgres's default index type is B-tree, not hash — hash indexes exist but aren't the default choice.
A unique constraint isn't checked with a full table scan; Postgres builds a dedicated index so duplicate checks stay fast.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: MongoDB 的索引（如 db.users.createIndex({"email": 1})）底层用的是？
options: 哈希表，靠计算哈希值直接定位到对应的桶
跳表，靠多层链表结构一层层加速跳跃查找
LSM 树，靠顺序写入再合并的方式优化性能
B+ 树：B 树变体，数据全部存在叶节点
why: 即便是文档模型的 MongoDB，索引也用 B+ 树（数据全在叶节点的 B 树变体），把 email 值映射到文档位置。B 树家族无处不在。
why_en: Even document-model MongoDB uses B-plus trees, a B-tree variant storing all data in leaf nodes, to map indexed values to document locations.
options_en: A hash table, using a computed hash value to land directly on a bucket.
A skip list, using multiple layers of linked lists to jump ahead and speed up lookups.
An LSM tree, optimizing performance via sequential writes that later get merged.
A B+ tree: a B-tree variant where all data lives in the leaf nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: B 树的变体，所有实际数据都存放在叶节点，内部节点只存路由键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B+ tree is a B-tree variant where all actual data lives in leaf nodes and internal nodes only store routing keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用多层链表实现快速查找和有序插入的概率性数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A skip list is a probabilistic layered linked-list structure that supports fast ordered search and insertion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档模型的 NoSQL 数据库，索引底层使用 B+ 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-model NoSQL database whose indexes are implemented with B+ trees under the hood.

q_en: What structure backs a MongoDB index such as db.users.createIndex({"email": 1})?
optionExplanations: 哈希表能做等值查找，但 MongoDB 的常规索引要支持范围和排序，用的不是哈希表。
跳表是 Redis 有序集合内部的结构，不是 MongoDB 索引的实现方式。
LSM 树是 RocksDB/Cassandra 这类写优化引擎的做法，MongoDB 默认索引不是这个结构。
对，MongoDB 索引底层是 B+ 树——数据全部挂在叶节点，同样支持等值、范围和排序。
optionExplanations_en: A hash table handles equality lookups, but MongoDB's regular index also needs range and sort — that's not what a plain hash table gives you.
A skip list is the internal structure behind Redis sorted sets, not how MongoDB implements its indexes.
An LSM tree is how write-optimized engines like RocksDB or Cassandra work; that's not MongoDB's default index structure.
Right — under the hood, a MongoDB index is a B+ tree, with all data hanging off the leaf nodes, so it still supports equality, range, and sort.

numberAnchors.risk: shard key 选错导致 scatter query

q: B 树为什么成为数据库索引的默认选择？（多选）
options: 维持有序，范围查询和 ORDER BY 都高效
自平衡，数据增长、随机增删下性能依然可预期
结构贴合磁盘页存储方式，最小化磁盘 I/O
只支持等值查询，不支持范围查询
why: B 树节点通常按磁盘页打包：一次 I/O 读进几百个有序 key 和子指针，树就很矮，点查只需少数几页。它还保持有序、自平衡，所以等值、范围和排序都稳。
why_en: A B-tree node is usually packed to fit a disk page: one I/O brings in hundreds of sorted keys and child pointers, keeping the tree shallow. It is also sorted and self-balancing, so equality, range, and ordering queries stay predictable.
options_en: It keeps data sorted, so range queries and ORDER BY are efficient.
It is self-balancing, so performance stays predictable as data grows or gets randomly inserted and deleted.
Its structure matches how databases store disk pages, minimizing disk I/O.
It only supports equality queries, not range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 中按某列排序结果的子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ORDER BY is the SQL clause that sorts query results by a column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构在插入删除后能自动调整、保持性能稳定的特性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Self-balancing means a structure automatically adjusts after inserts and deletes to keep performance stable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库一次从磁盘读写的固定大小数据块，常见 4KB、8KB 或 16KB；B 树节点会尽量设计成一页大小。

对，自平衡保证了即便数据量暴涨、随机增删，树高也不会失控，性能可预期。
对，节点大小贴合磁盘页，一次 I/O 就能读进几百个键，树矮，点查只需几次读盘。

optionExplanations_en: Right — a B-tree stays sorted internally, so range scans and ORDER BY can read straight along the leaf chain without any extra sort step.
Right — self-balancing keeps the tree's height bounded even as data grows or gets randomly inserted/deleted, so performance stays predictable.
Right — node size matches a disk page, so one I/O pulls in hundreds of keys; that keeps the tree shallow, so a point lookup takes only a few reads.

scenario: 面试中被问「这个查询该用什么索引」，你一时不确定工作负载的特殊性。

不加索引，先观望再决定

why_en: When in doubt in an interview, B-trees are the safe bet because they handle exact matches and range queries efficiently and are what most databases default to.
whenOtherWins: 经纬度邻近搜索该换地理空间索引；全文搜索换倒排索引；每秒十万级写入的摄入型系统考虑 LSM 存储。
options_en: B-trees — the swiss-army-knife default that covers both equality and range queries.
Hash indexes, because O(1) exact-match lookups are fastest.
Inverted indexes, because they cover the most functionality.
No index yet — wait and see.

q_en: When you are unsure, what is the safest default index answer?

optionExplanations: 对，几乎所有数据库都拿 B 树当默认索引，等值、范围、排序它都能应付，不确定时选它基本不会出错。
哈希索引等值确实 O(1)，但一旦查询模式里出现范围或排序，它就彻底帮不上忙——赌错了代价不小。

optionExplanations_en: Right — almost every database defaults to B-tree, and it handles equality, range, and sort all at once, so picking it when unsure is rarely wrong.

An inverted index is purpose-built for full-text search, answering "which documents contain this word" — not the general-purpose default.
"Wait and see" sounds cautious, but interviewers usually want an actionable default answer, and no index at all isn't one.

覆盖索引，省掉回表开销
LSM 树存储引擎：日志结构合并树

An LSM first writes sequentially to the WAL and memtable, then flushes batches into SSTables, turning many random small writes into large sequential writes.

options_en: A regular B-tree index that updates data in place.
A hash index for exact-match lookups only.
A covering index that skips table lookups.
An LSM tree storage engine, the log-structured merge tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写的存储引擎，靠内存缓冲和后台合并优化写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a storage engine that turns random writes into sequential writes using an in-memory buffer and background merging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款云监控 / 可观测性 SaaS 产品，代表高频指标写入的场景。

q_en: Which storage-engine index structure fits this workload best?
scenario_en: You are building a DataDog-style monitoring system: thousands of servers write hundreds of thousands of CPU, memory, and error-count metrics per second; every point must be stored immediately, while reads are rarer and can tolerate slightly higher latency.
optionExplanations: 普通 B 树原地更新在这种写入量下会不断触发随机寻道和页分裂，扛不住几十万/秒的写入。
哈希索引只做等值匹配，解决不了「怎么扛住海量写入」这个问题——它跟写入吞吐无关。
覆盖索引省的是回表开销，是读优化手段；这里的痛点在写入吞吐，不在读。
对，LSM 先顺序写 WAL 和内存 memtable，再批量刷成 SSTable，把随机小写变成顺序大写，正好吃下这种写入洪峰。
optionExplanations_en: A plain B-tree with in-place updates would trigger constant random seeks and page splits at this rate — it can't sustain hundreds of thousands of writes per second.
A hash index only handles equality matching — it doesn't address surviving this much write volume; it's unrelated to write throughput.
A covering index saves a table lookup, a read-side optimization; the pain point here is write throughput, not reads.
Right — LSM writes sequentially to a WAL and an in-memory memtable, then batches flushes into SSTables, turning tiny random writes into big sequential ones.

q: B 树在每秒 10 万级写入下的瓶颈出在哪？
options: 内存空间完全不够，存不下树的根节点数据
每次写要定位叶页、读入、改、写回——随机寻道成瓶颈
树在高并发写入场景下会逐渐失去自身的平衡
键的数量一旦超出限制，就会溢出单个节点的容量
why: O(log n) 只说明很快找到“哪一页要改”。真正贵的是后半段：把散落在磁盘/SSD 各处的小页读进缓存、改成脏页、之后再刷回去；页满了还可能 split。十万级写入会把这些小而分散的页操作放大成随机 I/O 瓶颈。
why_en: O(log n) only means the database quickly finds which page to change. The expensive part comes after that: load scattered small pages, dirty them in cache, flush them back later, and sometimes split full pages. At very high write rates, those scattered page operations become the random I/O bottleneck.
options_en: There isn't nearly enough memory to hold the tree's root node data.
Every write has to locate the leaf page, read it in, modify it, write it back — random seeks become the bottleneck.
Under heavy concurrent writes, the tree gradually loses its own balance.
Once the key count exceeds the limit, it overflows a single node's capacity.

  page = page_cache.load(page_id)      # may touch scattered pages

page_cache.flush_dirty_pages()         # later writes P7, P31, P4...

if memtable.too_large():

termDefinitions.meaning: 不是只指 HDD 磁头；面试里更泛指读写很多不连续的小页。HDD 会物理跳位置，SSD 没磁头但仍要处理大量分散页请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In interview language, random seek often broadly means many non-contiguous small page reads or writes. HDDs physically seek; SSDs do not have heads but still process scattered page requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: B 树最底层、直接存储数据指针的节点所在的磁盘页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leaf page is the disk page holding a B-tree's bottom-level nodes, which point directly to data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里已经被改过、但还没写回磁盘的页；积累太多就要 flush。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dirty page is a cached page that has been modified but not written back to disk yet; too many dirty pages must be flushed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内存里的脏页真正写回磁盘或 SSD。它可以异步发生，但总要付出 I/O 成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flush means writing dirty pages from memory back to disk or SSD. It may happen asynchronously, but the I/O cost still exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 叶页写满时，数据库要把它拆成两个页，并更新父节点；这会让一次写入牵连更多页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A page split happens when a leaf page is full; the database creates another page and updates the parent, making one write touch more pages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 算法层面的树高复杂度，表示访问层数随数据量增长很慢；它不等于物理 I/O 免费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(log n) is the logical tree-height complexity; it does not mean the physical I/O is free.

q_en: Where does a B-tree bottleneck show up at around one hundred thousand writes per second?
optionExplanations: 根节点很小，内存完全放得下；瓶颈不在存不下根节点。
对，O(log n) 只帮你快速定位该改哪一页，真正贵的是把这页从磁盘读入、改成脏页、可能分裂后再写回——十万级写入把这些放大成随机 I/O 瓶颈。
B 树是自平衡结构，高并发写入不会让它失去平衡，split/merge 机制会一直维持平衡。
键数量超出节点容量时节点会分裂（split）成两个，而不是溢出报错。
optionExplanations_en: The root node is tiny and fits in memory easily — that's not where the bottleneck is.

Right — O(log n) only finds the page fast; the expensive part is loading it from disk, dirtying it, maybe splitting it, and writing it back — at six-figure write rates that becomes a random-I/O bottleneck.
A B-tree is self-balancing — heavy concurrent writes don't throw it out of balance; split/merge keeps it balanced continuously.
When a node's key count exceeds capacity it splits into two nodes — it doesn't overflow or error out.

q: B 树和 LSM 树（日志结构合并树）在「索引与表的关系」上的根本差异是？
options: 两者都是可以随意加在任意列上的独立索引结构
LSM 可以随意加在任意列上，B 树反而做不到这点
B 树可建在任意列；LSM 是整表存储格式，按主键排序
两者其实都是整张表的存储格式，都没有独立索引
why: B 树是「一列一棵」的独立索引；LSM 不是这么用的——它是整张表的存储格式，按主键排序，主键查询极快，二级索引要靠额外结构。
why_en: A B-tree is a separate index you can create on any column, while an LSM tree is the storage format for the entire table sorted by primary key.
options_en: Both are standalone index structures you can freely add to any column.
LSM can be freely added to any column, while B-tree oddly can't.
B-tree can be built on any column; LSM is the whole table's storage format, sorted by primary key.
Both are actually whole-table storage formats, and neither has a standalone index.
tradeoff: 按列建索引的灵活性 vs 整表按主键排序换写入吞吐

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写的存储引擎，靠内存缓冲和后台合并优化写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a storage engine that turns random writes into sequential writes using an in-memory buffer and background merging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识一行数据的列或列组合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary key is the column or columns that uniquely identify each row.

q_en: What is the fundamental difference between B-trees and LSM trees in how they relate to the table?
optionExplanations: 「都是可加在任意列的独立索引」只适用于 B 树；LSM 本身就是整表存储格式，不是外挂索引。
说反了：能任意列建索引的是 B 树，LSM 是按主键组织的整表存储格式。
对，B 树是可加在任意列的独立索引；LSM 则是整表本身按主键排序存储，这是两者最根本的区别。
B 树恰恰是独立索引，不是整表存储格式——只有 LSM 才是「表即存储」。
optionExplanations_en: "Both can be freely added to any column" only describes B-tree; LSM itself is the whole table's storage format, not a bolt-on index.
Backwards — it's B-tree that can index any column freely; LSM is the whole table organized and stored by primary key.
Right — a B-tree is a standalone index you can add to any column, while LSM is the table's own storage format sorted by primary key; that's the fundamental split.
A B-tree is exactly a standalone index, not a whole-table storage format — it's LSM where the table itself is the storage.

q: LSM（日志结构合并树）存储引擎上的「二级索引」是什么情况？
options: 需要额外结构支持，如二级索引、GSI/LSI
性能和主键访问完全一样快，两者之间没有任何差别
在 LSM 引擎上从技术上讲完全不可能实现二级索引
会自动对表中每一列生效，完全无需任何额外配置
why: LSM 表按主键排序，主键查找极快；二级索引得靠附加结构（Cassandra、DynamoDB 的 GSI/LSI 等），且性能特征与主键访问不同。
why_en: On LSM storage secondary indexes require additional structures, as in Cassandra or DynamoDB's GSIs and LSIs, with different performance than primary-key access.
options_en: It needs an extra structure to support it, such as a secondary index or a GSI/LSI.
Performance is exactly as fast as primary-key access, with no difference at all.
Implementing a secondary index on an LSM engine is technically impossible altogether.
It automatically applies to every single column, with zero extra configuration needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 除主键外，为其他列建立的额外索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A secondary index is an extra index built on a column other than the primary key.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 里可用不同分区键/排序键查询的附加索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GSI stands for Global Secondary Index, an additional DynamoDB index queryable by a different partition or sort key.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 里在同一分区键下用不同排序键查询的附加索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSI stands for Local Secondary Index, a DynamoDB index sharing the base table's partition key but using a different sort key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源分布式 NoSQL 数据库，存储引擎基于 LSM 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is an open-source distributed NoSQL database whose storage engine is based on LSM trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管 NoSQL 数据库，被广泛认为底层用 LSM 风格存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed NoSQL database, widely believed to use an LSM-style storage engine internally.

q_en: How should you think about secondary indexes on an LSM-tree storage engine?
optionExplanations: 对，LSM 表天生只按主键排序，二级索引必须依赖数据库另外挂载的机制，例如 Cassandra 自带的二级索引，或 DynamoDB 那类系统提供的支持。
错——二级索引要走额外结构，读放大和一致性特征都跟主键访问不一样，谈不上完全一样快。
并非不可能，只是不像主键那样原生——需要靠 GSI/LSI 这类附加结构实现。
二级索引不会自动对每一列生效，通常需要显式创建（如声明 GSI）。
optionExplanations_en: Right — an LSM table is only sorted by primary key on its own; a secondary index needs a mechanism the database bolts on separately, like the one Cassandra ships or the kind DynamoDB offers.
Wrong — a secondary index goes through that extra structure, with different read-amplification and consistency characteristics, so it's not simply as fast.
It's not impossible, just not native the way primary-key access is — it needs an add-on structure like a GSI or LSI to work.
Secondary indexes don't automatically apply to every column — they usually need to be explicitly created, like declaring a GSI.

q: 补全 LSM 树的写入路径：
text: 新写入先进内存中的 {{memtable}}（有序结构）；同时为持久性顺序追加到 {{WAL}}（预写日志）；memtable 写满后冻结、整体刷盘成不可变的 {{SSTable}}；后台的 {{compaction}} 进程定期合并文件、清理重复和已删除条目。
why: LSM 写路径四件套：memtable 吃写入、WAL 保命、SSTable 顺序落盘、compaction 收拾残局。把大量随机小写变成少量顺序大写是全部精髓。
why_en: LSM writes go to an in-memory memtable and a write-ahead log, flush to immutable SSTables when full, and background compaction merges the files over time.

flowchart LR W["写入"] --> M["Memtable
（内存有序结构）"] W --> L["WAL 顺序追加
（持久性）"] M -->|写满冻结| S["SSTable
（不可变有序文件）"] S --> C["Compaction
后台合并去重"]

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 树中在内存里维护有序数据的写入缓冲结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that LSM trees write to before flushing to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志：先把变更顺序写入磁盘日志再确认，保证崩溃后可恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WAL stands for Write-Ahead Log, a sequential on-disk log that records changes before they're considered durable.

termDefinitions.meaning: memtable 刷盘后生成的不可变、内部有序的磁盘文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable, or Sorted String Table, is the immutable sorted on-disk file produced when a memtable is flushed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后台合并多个 SSTable、清理重复和已删除条目的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compaction is the background process that merges SSTables and removes duplicate or deleted entries.

q_en: Fill in the LSM-tree write path:

scenario: LSM 写入先进 memtable；等 memtable 够大后，系统要把它按 key 顺序刷成 SSTable。
scenario_en: In an LSM tree, writes first enter the memtable; when it is large enough, the system flushes it into an SSTable sorted by key.
q: memtable 通常用什么数据结构实现？
options: 无序数组，按插入顺序追加
布隆过滤器，用于快速排除
有序结构，如红黑树或跳表
堆文件，行没有特定顺序
why: 选 C。写入先追加 WAL 保命，再写内存 sorted map：memtable。memtable 因为按 key 有序，写满后 flush 成 SSTable；WAL 只是临时恢复日志。
why_en: Choose C. A write first appends to the WAL for crash recovery, then updates the in-memory sorted map, the memtable. Because the memtable is sorted by key, it can flush into an SSTable; the WAL is only a temporary recovery log.
options_en: An unordered array, appended in insertion order.
A bloom filter, used to quickly rule things out.
A sorted structure such as a red-black tree or skip list.
A heap file, with rows in no particular order.
diagram:
flowchart LR W["writes"] --> M["Memtable
sorted in memory"] M --> G["get(key)"] M --> R["range scan"] M --> F["flush in key order"] F --> S["SSTable
sorted file"]
codeSample:
memtable = SortedMap()  # in RAM; sorted by key
wal = AppendOnlyLog()  # on disk; temporary crash-recovery log

write(key, value):
  # 1. WAL first: if the process crashes, replay this log.
  wal.append("PUT", key, value)

  # 2. Memtable second: latest state, already sorted by key.
  memtable.put(key, value)

flush_memtable():
  frozen = memtable
  memtable = SortedMap()              # new writes use a fresh memtable
  new_sstable = SSTableFile()

  # Memtable becomes the SSTable because it is already sorted.
  for key, value in frozen.items_in_key_order():
    new_sstable.write(key, value)

  new_sstable.fsync()

  # WAL is not converted into an SSTable; it is retired after the SSTable is safe.
  wal.truncate_records_covered_by(new_sstable)

optionExplanations: 无序数组按插入顺序追加确实快，但 flush 成 SSTable 前需要按 key 排序，无序数组做不到。
布隆过滤器是查找 SSTable 时用来快速排除不可能命中的文件，不是内存里承接写入的结构。
对，memtable 是有序结构（红黑树/跳表），保持 key 有序才能写满后直接顺序 flush 成 SSTable。
堆文件是无序存储，跟 memtable 需要保持有序、方便顺序刷盘的要求正相反。
optionExplanations_en: An unsorted append-only array is fast to write to, but flushing to an SSTable requires key order, which an unsorted array can't give you.
A Bloom filter is used later to quickly rule out SSTables that can't contain a key — it's not the in-memory structure that absorbs writes.
Right — a memtable is an ordered structure (red-black tree or skip list); staying key-sorted lets it flush straight into a sorted SSTable once full.
A heap file is unordered storage, the opposite of what a memtable needs — staying ordered so it can flush sequentially.

q: 既然写入已进 memtable，为什么每笔写还要追加到 WAL（预写日志）？
options: 为了让后续的读取速度能够变得更快一些
保证持久性：内存崩溃丢失，WAL 顺序追加磁盘更快
为了把数据压缩得更小、占用更少的磁盘空间
为了额外支持某些特定的二级索引查询场景
why: memtable 在 RAM 里，一崩就没；WAL 把每笔写顺序追加到磁盘上兜底。顺序追加远快于随机写，所以持久性的代价很小。
why_en: Every write is also appended to a write-ahead log on disk for durability, and sequential appends are much faster than random writes.
options_en: To make subsequent reads a bit faster.
To guarantee durability: memory is lost on a crash, and the WAL appends to disk sequentially, which is fast.
To compress the data smaller, using less disk space.
To additionally support certain secondary-index query scenarios.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志：先把变更顺序写入磁盘日志再确认，保证崩溃后可恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WAL stands for Write-Ahead Log, a sequential on-disk log that records changes before they're considered durable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据写入后即使系统崩溃也不会丢失的保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability is the guarantee that written data survives even if the system crashes.

q_en: If a write is already in the memtable, why also append it to the WAL?
optionExplanations: WAL 是为了扛崩溃恢复用的，跟读取速度没关系——它不会让后续读更快。
对，memtable 在内存里，一崩溃就没了；WAL 把每笔写顺序追加到磁盘兜底，持久性代价很低。
WAL 记的是原始写入日志，不是为了压缩数据，它甚至会额外占用磁盘空间。
WAL 只是崩溃恢复的日志，不提供索引查询能力，跟二级索引无关。
optionExplanations_en: WAL exists to survive crash recovery — unrelated to read speed; it doesn't make later reads any faster.
Right — a memtable lives in RAM and vanishes on a crash; the WAL sequentially appends every write to disk as a safety net, and that's cheap.
The WAL records the raw write log, not a compressed form of the data — it actually adds extra disk usage, not less.
The WAL is only a crash-recovery log — it provides no indexed lookup capability and has nothing to do with secondary indexes.

q: 关于 SSTable（有序字符串表）的正确描述是？
options: memtable 写满后冻结，顺序写成不可变的有序文件
这是一份可以在磁盘上随时原地修改内容的普通文件
这是一份只存在于内存中、用完即扔的临时缓存
每写入一条数据都要立刻单独执行一次落盘写入
why: SSTable = Sorted String Table：memtable 写满后冻结，一次顺序写落盘成不可变、内部有序的文件，而不是零散地随机写。
why_en: When the memtable reaches a few megabytes it is frozen and flushed as an immutable Sorted String Table in one large sequential write.
options_en: Once a memtable fills up it freezes and gets written out sequentially as an immutable, sorted file.
An ordinary file whose contents can be edited in place on disk at any time.
A temporary, throwaway cache that only ever exists in memory.
Every single write gets flushed to disk individually, one write at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: memtable 刷盘后生成的不可变、内部有序的磁盘文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable, or Sorted String Table, is the immutable sorted on-disk file produced when a memtable is flushed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后不能再修改，只能整体替换或废弃。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Immutable means once written it cannot be modified, only replaced or discarded wholesale.

q_en: Which statement correctly describes an SSTable?
optionExplanations: 对，memtable 达到阈值就冻结，一次性顺序写成不可变的有序文件，这正是 SSTable 的定义。
SSTable 恰恰是不可变的——写完就不再原地修改，更新靠写新版本、靠 compaction 清理旧的。
SSTable 落在磁盘上，是持久化文件，不是内存里的临时缓存。
逐条落盘是没有 memtable 缓冲时的写法；LSM 恰恰是攒够一批再一次性顺序写出，减少随机 I/O。
optionExplanations_en: Right — once a memtable hits its threshold it freezes and gets written out sequentially as one immutable, internally sorted file, exactly what an SSTable is.
An SSTable is precisely immutable — it's never edited in place; updates are written as new versions and old ones get cleaned up by compaction.
An SSTable lives on disk — it's a durable file, not a temporary in-memory cache.
Writing one record at a time is what happens without a memtable buffer; LSM's whole point is batching writes and flushing sequentially to cut random I/O.

q: compaction（压缩合并）在 LSM 树里负责什么？
options: 把数据加密，保护静态存储安全
把 memtable 直接转换成 B 树
阻止新的写入请求进来
后台合并 SSTable：去重复、清删除、控制文件数
why: SSTable 会越积越多，compaction 在后台把它们合并、去重、清理删除标记，让要检查的文件数可控——这是读性能不崩的关键。
why_en: Compaction periodically merges SSTables in the background, removing duplicates and deleted entries to keep the file count manageable and reads performant.
options_en: It encrypts the data to protect it at rest.
It converts the memtable directly into a B-tree.
It blocks new write requests from coming in.
It periodically merges SSTables in the background, removing duplicates and deletions, and controlling file count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后台合并多个 SSTable、清理重复和已删除条目的过程。

termDefinitions.meaning: memtable 刷盘后生成的不可变、内部有序的磁盘文件。
