q_en: What does compaction do in an LSM tree?
optionExplanations: compaction 是磁盘 I/O 层面的整理工作，跟静态加密（at-rest encryption）是两码事。
memtable flush 成的是 SSTable，不是 B 树——compaction 合并的对象是多个 SSTable。
compaction 在后台运行，正常情况下不会挡住新写入，只是会占用额外的磁盘 I/O 带宽。
对，compaction 在后台合并多个 SSTable、去重、清删除标记，把要查的文件数压下来，这是读性能不崩的关键。
optionExplanations_en: Compaction is disk I/O housekeeping — unrelated to at-rest encryption, which protects stored data, not organizes it.
A memtable flushes into an SSTable, not a B-tree — what compaction merges together is multiple SSTables.
Compaction runs in the background and normally doesn't block new writes — it just competes for extra disk I/O bandwidth.
Right — compaction merges multiple SSTables in the background, dedupes, and clears delete markers, keeping the file count manageable and reads fast.

q: LSM 树（日志结构合并树）上查一个 key，最坏情况下为什么可能很慢？
options: 树的结构会临时短暂失去平衡，读写都受影响
依次查 memtable、待刷盘、全部 SSTable
必须先做一次全量 compaction 才能开始读
WAL 写入时会把所有的读取操作都锁住
why: 数据可能躺在任何一层：当前 memtable、待刷盘 memtable、或任意一个 SSTable，只能从新到旧逐个排查——对比 B 树 2-3 页的点查，这就是读放大。
why_en: A point query must check the memtable, any immutable memtables, and then SSTables from newest to oldest, potentially dozens of files in the worst case.

Check the memtable, then the immutable ones, then every SSTable, in order.

WAL writes lock out every single read operation.

q_en: Why can a key lookup on an LSM tree be slow in the worst case?
optionExplanations: LSM 树本身不会临时失衡——它压根不是靠平衡树结构组织数据的，问题不出在这。

The exact physical disk location of the key.

q_en: What exact promise can a bloom filter make?
optionExplanations: 说反了：布隆过滤器只保证「不在」是绝对准的，「可能在」不代表一定在，还得进一步检查。
布隆过滤器不存位置信息，它只回答「这个 key 有没有可能在这个文件里」这一个概率性问题。
对，布隆过滤器唯一确定的承诺是「一定不在」，可以放心跳过；「可能在」仍要打开文件核实。
布隆过滤器不统计总数，它是一个位数组，只做「在/可能在」的成员判断。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards — a Bloom filter's only guaranteed answer is "definitely not present"; "maybe present" doesn't mean it's actually there.
A Bloom filter doesn't store any location data — it only answers a probabilistic membership question.
Right — the one thing a Bloom filter guarantees is "definitely not in here," so you can safely skip the file; "maybe" still needs a check.
A Bloom filter doesn't track a count — it's a bit array that only answers present-or-maybe-present.

q_en: You are looking for user_id=500, but an SSTable sparse index says it only covers keys 1000-2000. What next?
optionExplanations: 对，稀疏索引已经显示这个文件只含 1000-2000，500 落在范围外，整份文件直接略过，连一次磁盘读都省了。
如果只是为了排除，打开全文件扫描反而是最贵的路径——这正是稀疏索引和范围检查要避免的开销。
compaction 是后台异步整理任务，不是每次点查前都要跑一遍的前置步骤。
布隆过滤器是用来判断成员是否可能存在的，这里已经能直接用键范围排除，不需要再查布隆过滤器。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the sparse index already shows this file spans 1000 to 2000; 500 falls outside that, so the whole file gets skipped, saving even a single disk read.
Opening and scanning the whole file just to rule it out would be the most expensive path — exactly what the range check avoids.
Compaction is asynchronous background housekeeping, not a step that has to run before every point lookup.

q: size-tiered 与 leveled 两种 compaction 策略的取舍是？
options: 两者在写放大和产生的文件数量上完全等价
size-tiered 写放大小、文件多；leveled 相反
leveled compaction 策略的写放大最小、文件数也最少
size-tiered 策略只能被用在纯内存表这种场景上
why: 选 B。size-tiered 像“攒够同尺寸文件再合并”：少搬数据、写放大小，但同一 key 范围可能散在更多文件里。leveled 像“持续整理货架”：读时文件少，但数据会被反复重写到下一层。
why_en: Choose B. Size-tiered compaction waits until similarly sized files accumulate, so it rewrites less data but leaves more files to check. Leveled compaction keeps data organized into levels with fewer files per key range, but it rewrites data more often.
options_en: The two are completely equivalent in write amplification and file count.
Size-tiered has smaller write amplification but more files; leveled is the opposite.
Leveled compaction has the smallest write amplification and the fewest files, both at once.
Size-tiered compaction only works for purely in-memory tables.
tradeoff: 写放大 vs 读时要查的文件数
diagram:
flowchart TD subgraph ST["Size-tiered: write friendly"] S1["many similar SSTables"] --> S2["merge when enough accumulate"] S2 --> S3["fewer rewrites
more overlap"] end subgraph LV["Leveled: read friendly"] L0["L0 new files"] --> L1["L1 organized ranges"] L1 --> L2["L2 larger ranges"] L2 --> L3["more rewrites
fewer files per read"] end

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑读取为了确认结果，需要检查多个内存结构或磁盘文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read amplification means one logical read has to check multiple memory structures or disk files before it can answer.

q_en: What is the tradeoff between size-tiered and leveled compaction?
optionExplanations: 两者在写放大和文件数上并不等价——这正是这两种策略要权衡的地方，选哪个要看读写比例。
对，size-tiered 攒够同尺寸文件才合并，写放大小但文件散；leveled 持续把数据下推到下一层，读时文件少但写放大更高。
leveled 确实文件少，但代价是数据要被反复重写下推，写放大反而更高，不是「最小」。
两种 compaction 策略都是磁盘上的 SSTable 合并策略，跟纯内存表没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: The two aren't equivalent on write amplification or file count — that tradeoff is exactly the point, and it depends on the read/write ratio.
Right — size-tiered waits to accumulate same-sized files before merging, low write amplification but scattered files; leveled keeps pushing down a level, fewer files but more rewrites.
Leveled does keep file count low, but the cost is data getting rewritten and pushed down repeatedly, so its write amplification is actually higher.
Both compaction strategies are about merging on-disk SSTables — neither is limited to a purely in-memory table.

q: 一句话概括 LSM 树（日志结构合并树）的根本交易是什么？
options: 用内存换磁盘
用一致性换可用性
用空间换时间
用读性能换写性能
why: LSM 的一切设计都在为写让路：顺序追加、批量刷盘让写飞快，代价是读要翻多层结构。写远多于读、或读能容忍稍高延迟时，这笔交易才划算。
why_en: LSM trees fundamentally trade read performance for write performance, which pays off when a system writes far more than it reads.
options_en: It trades memory for disk.
It trades consistency for availability.
It trades space for time.
It trades read performance for write performance.

optionExplanations: LSM 确实要靠内存缓冲写入，但这不是它的根本交易——用内存换磁盘更像是缓存的逻辑，不是 LSM 的核心权衡。
LSM 的取舍跟分布式系统的 CAP 权衡是两个维度的问题，它谈的是单机存储引擎内部的读写权衡。
说反了：LSM 没有省空间，反而因为多版本和 compaction 中间态占用更多磁盘，它换的是时间不是空间。
对，LSM 用顺序追加和批量刷盘换来极快的写，代价是读要翻多层结构，这就是「写换读」的核心交易。
optionExplanations_en: LSM does buffer writes in memory, but that's not its fundamental trade — trading memory for disk sounds more like a cache's logic.
LSM's tradeoff is a different axis from the CAP tradeoff in distributed systems — it's about read/write behavior inside one storage engine.
Backwards — LSM doesn't save space; between multiple versions and compaction's in-progress state it often uses more disk, trading time, not space.
Right — LSM trades sequential appends and batched flushes for very fast writes, at the cost of reads checking multiple layers — the core write-for-read trade.

why_en: How LSM writes work: a write goes into an in-memory sorted memtable plus a sequential WAL append (fast, no random writes); when the memtable fills it is flushed as one immutable, sorted SSTable; a background compaction merges SSTables and drops overwritten/deleted entries. Classic LSM systems: Cassandra, RocksDB, DynamoDB; Postgres defaults to B-trees.

q: 哈希索引的本质是什么？
options: 持久化哈希表：索引值映射到行位置，等值查找 O(1)
一棵按哈希值大小排序的普通 B 树结构
一种专门用来压缩数据的特殊编码方式
只存在于内存里、临时使用的布隆过滤器
why: 哈希索引就是落盘的 hashmap：维护桶数组，对索引值取哈希定位桶，桶里放指向行数据的指针。牺牲灵活性换取超快的 O(1) 等值查找。
why_en: A hash index is simply a persistent hashmap mapping indexed values to row locations, trading flexibility for constant-time exact-match lookups.
options_en: A persisted hash table: index values map to row locations, giving O(1) equality lookups.
An ordinary B-tree structure sorted by hash-value size.
A special encoding method built specifically to compress data.
A temporary, in-memory-only Bloom filter.
codeSample:
-- 哈希索引把值哈希到桶，再指向行
buckets[hash('alice@example.com')] -> ptr to page 1
buckets[hash('bob@example.com')]   -> ptr to page 2
-- 冲突：同一桶链式挂接溢出页

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常数时间复杂度，操作耗时不随数据量增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) is constant time complexity, meaning the operation's cost does not grow with data size.

q_en: What is the essence of a hash index?
optionExplanations: 对，哈希索引本质就是落盘版的 hashmap：对值取哈希定位桶，桶里存指向行的指针，换来 O(1) 等值查找。
按哈希值排序这个说法自相矛盾——哈希本身就是打散顺序，排序后就不是哈希索引了。
哈希索引不是压缩编码，它是一种加速查找的数据结构，跟数据压缩是两回事。
布隆过滤器只回答「可能存在/一定不存在」，不存实际的行位置，哈希索引要能真正定位到行。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a hash index is essentially an on-disk hashmap: hash the value to find its bucket, and the bucket holds pointers to the row, buying O(1) lookups.
"Sorted by hash value" is self-contradictory — hashing scatters order on purpose; if it were sorted, it wouldn't be a hash index anymore.
A hash index isn't a compression encoding — it's a lookup-acceleration structure, a different job from compressing data.
A Bloom filter only answers maybe-present-or-definitely-not and stores no actual row location; a hash index has to point to the row.

q: 哈希索引如何处理哈希冲突？
options: 直接丢弃发生冲突的那一整对键值数据
每次发生冲突时都要重建整个哈希索引
一桶多条目、链式挂接溢出页，负载因子合理仍 O(1)
把发生冲突的键转存到一棵独立的 B 树里
why: 常见做法是桶内多条目+链式溢出：Postgres 哈希索引的桶可以链接溢出页。只要哈希函数好、负载因子合理，平均查找仍是 O(1)。
why_en: Collisions are handled by letting buckets hold multiple entries and chain to overflow pages, keeping average lookups constant time with a good hash function.
options_en: Simply drop the entire colliding key-value pair.
Rebuild the whole hash index from scratch on every collision.
Multiple entries per bucket, chaining to overflow pages; average lookup stays O(1) with a reasonable load factor.
Move the colliding key over into a separate B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个不同的值被哈希到同一个桶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash collision is when two different values hash to the same bucket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希表里已用条目数与桶总数之比，越高越容易冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load factor is the ratio of used entries to total buckets in a hash table; higher values mean more collisions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的开源关系型数据库，默认索引几乎都是 B 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is a popular open-source relational database whose default indexes are almost all B-trees.

q_en: How does a hash index handle hash collisions?
optionExplanations: 直接丢弃冲突的键会丢数据，任何正确的索引实现都不会这么做。
冲突只需要处理这一条，不需要重建整个索引——这个代价太夸张了。
对，一个桶能挂多条目、链接溢出页，只要哈希函数分布均匀、负载因子合理，平均仍是 O(1)。
转存到 B 树里处理冲突会让哈希索引退化成一个哈希+树的混合体，不是常见的实现方式。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping a colliding key/value pair would lose data — no correct index implementation would do that.
A collision only needs to be handled for that one entry, not by rebuilding the entire index — that cost would be absurd.
Right — a bucket can hold multiple entries and chain to overflow pages; a well-distributed hash and reasonable load factor keep average lookup O(1).
Spilling collisions into a B-tree would turn a hash index into a hash-plus-tree hybrid, not how it's commonly implemented.

q: 同一个结构让哈希索引快，也让它废——废在哪？
options: 连它最擅长的等值查询也会跟着一起变慢
相似值被打散到不同桶，范围查询和排序都做不了
占用的存储空间会比原表还大出一个数量级
根本没办法处理字符串类型的键，只能处理数字
why: 哈希的意义就是把值均匀打散，于是「相邻」的值天各一方——范围扫描和排序彻底没戏。这正是它输给 B 树的原因。
why_en: The same hashing that makes exact matches fast deliberately scatters similar values across buckets, making range queries and sorting impossible.
options_en: Even the equality lookups it's best at end up slower too.
Similar values get scattered into different buckets, so range queries and sorting are both impossible.
Its storage footprint ends up an order of magnitude bigger than the original table.
It simply can't handle string-typed keys, only numeric ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 查找某个区间内所有值的查询，例如 age > 25。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A range query finds all values within an interval, such as age greater than 25.

q_en: The same structure makes hash indexes fast and limited. Where do they fail?
optionExplanations: 等值查询正是哈希索引擅长的部分，不会因为这个结构而变慢。
对，哈希故意把相似值打散到不同桶，「相邻」值天各一方，范围扫描和排序因此彻底做不了。
哈希索引通常比等价的 B 树索引更紧凑，谈不上大一个数量级。
字符串完全可以哈希，哈希索引对字符串键一样适用，问题不在类型支持。
optionExplanations_en: Equality lookups are exactly what a hash index excels at — this structure doesn't make them slower.
Right — hashing deliberately scatters similar values into different buckets, so range scans and sorting are completely off the table.
A hash index is usually about as compact as an equivalent B-tree index, not an order of magnitude bigger.
Strings hash perfectly fine — a hash index works just as well on string keys; type support isn't the issue here.

q: PostgreSQL 支持哈希索引，却不默认使用，官方理由接近哪句话？
options: 哈希索引完全不支持任何事务相关的操作
哈希索引会占用远超预期的额外内存空间
哈希索引在磁盘上从原理上根本没办法实现
B 树做等值几乎不输哈希索引，还白送范围与排序
why: 关键是 B 树的 O(log n) 很小：扇出约 500，一页装几百 key，几十亿行也就 3-4 层，顶层多在缓存。真正成本是磁盘 I/O，B 树等值只比哈希慢一丝丝，却白送范围和排序。
why_en: A B-tree's O(log n) is tiny: each node is a page holding hundreds of keys, so even billions of rows are only 3–4 levels deep. Since the real cost is disk I/O (not comparisons) and the top levels stay cached, equality lookups are only marginally slower than a hash — but you also get range and sort for free. Hence Postgres calls hash indexes a solution to a problem we rarely have.
options_en: A hash index doesn't support any transaction-related operations at all.
A hash index uses far more extra memory than you'd expect.
A hash index is fundamentally impossible to implement on disk.
B-tree is nearly as fast as a hash index for equality, and it throws in range and sort for free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组要么全部成功要么全部回滚的数据库操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a group of database operations that either all succeed or all roll back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的开源关系型数据库，默认索引几乎都是 B 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is a popular open-source relational database whose default indexes are almost all B-trees.

q_en: PostgreSQL supports hash indexes but does not default to them. Which sentence is closest to the official reasoning?
optionExplanations: 错——哈希索引照样支持事务；它的短板是不支持范围与排序，不是事务。
错——哈希索引内存开销并不夸张；不默认用它是因为收益太小、还丢了范围能力。
错——磁盘哈希索引完全可实现（PostgreSQL 就内置）；问题只是收益不值当。
对，B 树查找要翻的层数极少——几十亿行也就 3-4 层，等值查找只比哈希慢一丝丝，却多拿到范围和排序能力。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — a hash index still supports transactions; its real limit is no range or sort, not transactions.
Wrong — a hash index is not a memory hog; it just is not worth losing range support for a tiny gain.
Wrong — on-disk hash indexes are entirely implementable (Postgres ships one); the payoff is just too small.
Right — a B-tree needs very few levels to search — even billions of rows means 3-4 levels, so equality lookup is barely slower than hash, and range plus sort come free.

scenario: 所有数据都在内存中的键值查找场景——比如 Redis 的主数据结构、MySQL 的 MEMORY 存储引擎。
q: 为什么这里哈希结构反而是对的？
options: 因为内存里根本没办法搭建出一棵完整的 B 树
全内存没有磁盘 I/O 要迁就，哈希 O(1) 优势兑现
因为哈希表占用的内存空间比 B 树要更少一些
因为这个使用场景本身其实还是需要支持范围查询
why: 磁盘上主导成本是 I/O，B 树几乎不输哈希还更全能；纯内存没有 I/O 可挡，哈希 O(1) 优势才真正兑现，这类场景又只需要等值查找。
why_en: Why the winner flips: on disk, I/O dominates and hides hash's O(1) edge, so a B-tree is nearly as fast and more versatile; in pure memory there's no I/O to hide behind, so the O(1) edge finally shows — and this workload is exact-match only, so hash is right. Redis and the MySQL MEMORY engine both default to hash.
whenOtherWins: 数据落磁盘时选 B 树——它对磁盘 I/O 模式的处理效率更高，等值也几乎不慢。
options_en: Because there's supposedly no way to build a complete B-tree structure in memory at all.
With everything in memory there's no disk I/O to dodge, so the hash table's O(1) advantage actually pays off.
Because a hash table supposedly uses less memory than a B-tree would.
Because this use case supposedly still needs range-query support.
tradeoff: 内存中等值查找速度 vs 磁盘场景下的范围查询灵活性

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store whose primary structure is a hash table.

termDefinitions.meaning: MySQL 里把整表数据放进内存的存储引擎，默认用哈希索引。

termDefinitions.meaning: 对磁盘的一次读或写操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O, or Input/Output, here means one read or write operation to disk.

q_en: Why is a hash structure the right fit in this case?
scenario_en: All data lives in memory for key-value lookup, as in Redis's main data structure or MySQL's MEMORY storage engine.

rows: 内存访问 / 操作次数（O(1) 显形）

optionExplanations: 内存里当然能建 B 树（很多语言的 TreeMap 就是），问题不在能不能建，而在没有 I/O 瓶颈时它的优势体现不出来。
对，磁盘场景下 I/O 才是大头，B 树几乎不输哈希；纯内存没有 I/O 要躲，哈希 O(1) 的优势才真正兑现，这里又只需等值。
内存占用不是这里的决定因素——两种结构内存开销相近，真正的分水岭是有没有磁盘 I/O。
这个场景（Redis 主结构、MySQL MEMORY）通常就是纯等值键值查找，不需要范围查询。
optionExplanations_en: You absolutely can build a B-tree in memory (that's what a TreeMap is) — the issue is its advantage doesn't show once there's no I/O bottleneck to dodge.
Right — on disk, I/O dominates and a B-tree barely loses to a hash; in pure memory there's no I/O to dodge, so the hash's O(1) edge finally pays off, and this workload is pure equality.
Memory footprint isn't the deciding factor here — both structures cost about the same in RAM; the real dividing line is disk I/O.
This kind of workload (Redis's core structure, MySQL's MEMORY engine) is typically pure equality key-value lookup, no range query need.

q: 面试中谈哈希索引的正确姿势是？
options: 知道即可、别过度强调，生产很少用
把哈希索引当成默认的答案
声称哈希索引能完全替代 B 树
完全不提，假装从不知道它
why: 哈希索引像买来只用一次的厨房小工具；B 树太全能，覆盖了绝大多数你想用哈希的场合。面试点到为止，别显得不接地气。
why_en: Know hash indexes but do not overemphasize them in interviews, since they are rarely used in production and B-trees cover most of their use cases.
options_en: Know it, but don't overemphasize it — rarely used in production.
Treat it as the default answer.
Claim it can fully replace B-trees.
Never mention it, pretend you never knew it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

q_en: What is the right way to discuss hash indexes in an interview?
optionExplanations: 对，提一句「知道但生产很少用」既show出你懂它的存在，又不会显得不接地气——它确实是个小众工具。
把哈希索引当默认答案风险很大——一旦追问范围查询，这个答案立刻站不住。
哈希索引替代不了 B 树——它天生做不了范围查询和排序，这是结构性限制，不是配置问题。
假装不知道反而显得准备不足；面试官更想看到你知道它、也知道它的局限。
optionExplanations_en: Right — mentioning "I know it exists, but it's rarely used in production" shows awareness without overselling it; it genuinely is a niche tool.
Treating a hash index as your default answer is risky — the moment there's a follow-up about range queries, it falls apart.
A hash index can't replace a B-tree — it structurally can't do range queries or sorting; that's fundamental, not a config limitation.
Pretending not to know it at all reads as under-prepared; interviewers want to see you know it exists and its limits.

q: 给 latitude、longitude 各建一个 B 树索引来做「5 英里内的餐厅」，为什么行不通？
options: 因为 B 树不支持 DECIMAL 数值类型
因为两个索引会互相冲突报错
两个 1D 索引解 2D 问题：交集还是大矩形
经纬度字段根本不能建立索引
why: 先用纬度索引会命中全球同纬度长条上的所有点；两个索引求交则得到远大于目标圆的矩形结果集。2D 邻近问题需要理解空间关系的索引。
why_en: Two separate one-dimensional B-trees cannot solve a two-dimensional proximity problem: the latitude range is a strip around the globe, and intersecting both indexes yields a rectangle far larger than the search circle.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["lat lon"] --> B["geohash prefix"]
  B --> C["B-tree range scan"]
  C --> D["distance filter"]
options_en: B-trees don't support the DECIMAL data type.
The two indexes conflict with each other and error out.
Two 1D indexes solving a 2D problem: the intersection is still a big rectangle.
Latitude and longitude fields cannot be indexed at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 里的定点数值类型，用来存精确小数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DECIMAL is a SQL fixed-point numeric type used to store exact decimal values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一维/二维：这里指索引能理解的维度数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 1D and 2D refer to how many dimensions the index structure can natively understand.

q_en: Why does adding separate B-tree indexes on latitude and longitude not solve restaurants within five miles?
optionExplanations: DECIMAL 类型完全可以建 B 树索引，问题不出在数据类型上。
两个独立索引可以同时存在，不会互相冲突报错——问题在于用它们求交集效率低、结果不准。
对，两个 1D 索引各自只能筛一个维度，求交集得到的是一个远大于目标圆的矩形，不是真正的邻近范围。
经纬度是普通数值列，完全可以建索引，只是普通 B 树索引解不了 2D 邻近这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: A DECIMAL column can absolutely have a B-tree index built on it — the data type isn't the problem here.
Two independent indexes can coexist just fine, no conflict or error — the real problem is intersecting them is slow and imprecise.
Right — two 1D indexes each filter only one dimension; intersecting them gives a rectangle far bigger than the target circle, not true proximity.
Latitude and longitude are ordinary numeric columns and can absolutely be indexed — a plain B-tree index just can't solve 2D proximity.

q: geohash 的核心思想是什么？
options: 把地球投影到平面网格再取模
递归四等分区域并编码，2D 变 1D 字符串
给每个城市分配一个随机数字 ID
用 R 树的矩形逐个包裹坐标点
why: 想象把世界四等分并标号，再对每格继续四等分——geohash 就是这个过程的 base32 编码。近处的两家餐厅往往共享「9q8yyk」这样的前缀。
why_en: Geohash recursively subdivides the world and base32-encodes the path, turning a 2D location into a 1D string where nearby places usually share a prefix.
options_en: Project the earth onto a flat grid and take a modulo.
Recursively quarter regions and encode them, turning 2D into a 1D string.
Assign every city a random numeric ID.
Wrap each coordinate one by one in an R-tree rectangle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维经纬度递归四等分并编码成一维字符串的编码方式，邻近位置通常共享前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively subdivides 2D coordinates and encodes them as a 1D string, so nearby locations usually share a prefix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 32 个字符编码二进制数据的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Base32 is an encoding scheme representing binary data with 32 characters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用可重叠的矩形层层包裹数据的空间索引，矩形形状随数据分布自适应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree indexes spatial data with flexible, overlapping bounding rectangles that adapt to how the data actually clusters.

q_en: What is the core idea behind geohash?
optionExplanations: 投影到网格取模会丢失空间局部性——geohash 的关键恰恰是保留「越近前缀越长共享」这个特性，取模做不到。
对，geohash 就是不断把区域四等分、编号，再把这串编号做 base32 编码，附近的点自然共享长前缀。
geohash 编码的是地理坐标本身，不是给城市分配的任意标识符，跟城市 ID 无关。
R 树才是用嵌套矩形包裹坐标点，这不是 geohash 的思路——geohash 不建树。
optionExplanations_en: Projecting to a grid and taking a modulus loses spatial locality — geohash's whole point is that nearby points share long prefixes, which a modulus can't preserve.
Right — geohash repeatedly quarters a region and numbers it, then base32-encodes that numbering, so nearby points naturally share a long prefix.
Geohash encodes the actual geographic coordinate, not some arbitrary ID assigned to a city — unrelated to city IDs.
Wrapping points in nested rectangles is the R-tree's approach, not geohash's — geohash doesn't build a tree at all.

q: geohash 字符串的长度意味着什么？
options: 长度是随机分配的，没有含义
字符串越长覆盖的范围反而越大
字符串长度代表数据的新旧程度
越长越精确：从城市级到街区级逐层收窄
why: 每多一层四分就多一分精度：4 位字符大约圈住一座城，6 位能定位一个街区。前缀长度就是精度旋钮。
why_en: A longer geohash is more precise, going from a city at four characters down to a specific block at six.
options_en: The length is random and carries no meaning.
A longer string covers a larger area.
The length indicates how old or new the data is.
Longer is more precise: from a whole city down to a single city block.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维经纬度递归四等分并编码成一维字符串的编码方式，邻近位置通常共享前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively subdivides 2D coordinates and encodes them as a 1D string, so nearby locations usually share a prefix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 字符串开头的一段，geohash 前缀相同代表位置相近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prefix is the leading portion of a string; matching geohash prefixes mean nearby locations.

q_en: What does the length of a geohash string mean?
optionExplanations: 长度不是随机的——它直接对应四等分的层数，层数越多，圈住的区域越小。
说反了：字符串越长表示分得越细，覆盖范围应该越小，不是越大。
geohash 编码的是空间位置，跟数据新旧、时间戳无关。
对，每多一位就再四等分一层：4 位大约圈一座城，6 位能到街区级别，长度就是精度旋钮。
optionExplanations_en: Length isn't random — it directly maps to how many quartering rounds happened; more rounds means a smaller enclosed area.
Backwards — a longer string means finer subdivision, so it covers a smaller area, not a bigger one.
Geohash encodes spatial position — unrelated to how old or new the data is, or a timestamp.
Right — each extra character quarters the region one more time: about four characters covers a city, six gets to block-level, so length is the precision dial.

q: geohash 的「真正优雅之处」在于它和什么老朋友的组合？
options: geohash 建 B 树，邻近搜索变前缀扫描
布隆过滤器：概率排除远处的点
哈希索引：O(1) 定位任何坐标
LSM 树：专门吸收高频位置更新
why: 2D 坐标变成有序字符串后，B 树擅长的前缀匹配和范围扫描恰好就是邻近搜索所需；半径查询再补扫相邻单元格即可。复用现有 B 树设施是它流行的根本原因。
why_en: Once locations become ordered strings, a regular B-tree handles proximity search as simple prefix range scans, plus a few adjacent cells for radius queries.
options_en: Index geohash strings with a B-tree; proximity search becomes a prefix scan.
Bloom filters: probabilistically rule out far-away points.
Hash indexes: locate any coordinate in O(1).
LSM trees: absorb high-frequency location updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维经纬度递归四等分并编码成一维字符串的编码方式，邻近位置通常共享前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively subdivides 2D coordinates and encodes them as a 1D string, so nearby locations usually share a prefix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.term: 前缀范围扫描 / prefix range scan
termDefinitions.meaning: 在有序索引里扫描所有共享某前缀的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prefix range scan walks an ordered index for all entries sharing a given prefix.

q_en: What existing index structure makes geohash especially elegant?
optionExplanations: 对，坐标变成有序字符串后，正好用上 B 树最擅长的前缀匹配和范围扫描，复用现成设施而不必发明新结构。
布隆过滤器能排除「一定不在」，但排除不了「有多近」，解决不了邻近排序这个核心问题。
哈希索引会把相邻坐标打散到不同桶，恰恰破坏了 geohash 想保留的空间局部性。
LSM 树是为高频写入设计的存储引擎，跟 geohash 要解决的空间查询问题不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Right — once coordinates become a sorted string, it plugs into what a B-tree is best at: prefix matching and range scans, reusing existing machinery.
A Bloom filter can rule out "definitely not here," but not rank "how close is it," so it doesn't solve the core proximity-ordering problem.
A hash index would scatter neighboring coordinates into different buckets, destroying exactly the spatial locality geohash tries to preserve.
An LSM tree is a storage engine designed for high write volume — a different problem from the spatial query geohash solves.

scenario: 用 Redis 存餐厅坐标，要查「以某点为圆心 5 英里内」的餐厅；Redis 的地理命令内部就是用 geohash 实现的。
q: 当前推荐使用哪条命令做半径搜索？
options: GEORADIUS restaurants -122.4194 37.7749 5 mi WITHCOORD
GET restaurants:nearby:precomputed:list:radius5mi
GEOSEARCH restaurants FROMLONLAT -122.4194 37.7749 BYRADIUS 5 mi
ZRANGEBYSCORE restaurants:distances 0 5 WITHSCORES LIMIT 0 10
why: GEOSEARCH 是现行推荐（GEORADIUS 已废弃），配合 GEOADD 写入坐标；Redis 底层用 geohash 高效找出附近的点。
why_en: Use GEOSEARCH with FROMLONLAT and BYRADIUS since GEORADIUS is deprecated, and Redis implements these geo commands with geohash under the hood.
whenOtherWins: 在 Postgres 生态里做同样的事，则用 PostGIS 的 R 树系空间索引；需要更灵活的形状（多边形、路网）时 R 树更合适。
codeSample:
GEOADD restaurants -122.4194 37.7749 "Restaurant A"
GEOSEARCH restaurants FROMLONLAT -122.4194 37.7749 BYRADIUS 5 mi
options_en: GEORADIUS with WITHCOORD, the deprecated radius-search command that also returns coordinates.
GET on a single precomputed key that supposedly holds a five-mile radius result list.
GEOSEARCH from a lon/lat point with a radius filter, the current recommended command.
ZRANGEBYSCORE with WITHSCORES and a LIMIT clause, a sorted-set range command unrelated to geo radius search.
tradeoff: 现行推荐命令的清晰语义 vs 已废弃命令的历史写法

termDefinitions.meaningEn: GEOSEARCH is Redis's current recommended command for geo radius or bounding-box search.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 早期的地理半径搜索命令，现已废弃。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度坐标写入 Redis 地理数据结构的命令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GEOADD is the Redis command that writes a longitude/latitude coordinate into its geo structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维经纬度递归四等分并编码成一维字符串的编码方式，邻近位置通常共享前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively subdivides 2D coordinates and encodes them as a 1D string, so nearby locations usually share a prefix.

q_en: Which Redis command is currently recommended for radius search?
scenario_en: You store restaurant coordinates in Redis and need to find restaurants within five miles of a point; Redis geo commands use geohash internally.
optionExplanations: GEORADIUS 能工作，但已被 Redis 官方标记为废弃，新代码不该再用它。
这不是一条真实 Redis 命令，只是提前算好结果的占位描述，没法真正执行。
对，做半径搜索该用 GEOSEARCH，配合 GEOADD 写入的坐标查询，底层由 geohash 支撑，GEORADIUS 已经过时。
ZRANGEBYSCORE 按分数区间取有序集合成员，score 不是距离，查不出「5 英里内」这种半径结果。
optionExplanations_en: GEORADIUS still works, but Redis officially marked it deprecated — new code shouldn't reach for it.
This isn't a real Redis command — it's a placeholder for some precomputed result, not something you can actually run.
Right — radius search should use GEOSEARCH, paired with coordinates written via GEOADD, backed by geohash under the hood; GEORADIUS is the outdated way.
ZRANGEBYSCORE pulls sorted-set members by a score range; a score isn't a distance, so it can't produce a five-mile radius result.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: geohash 的主要局限是什么？
options: geohash 无法用字符串表示南半球
两点若落在大网格分界线两侧，前缀可能完全不同
geohash 精度只能到城市级别
geohash 字符串不支持 B 树索引
why: 网格边界效应：马路两边的两家店可能前缀不同。所以半径查询要把相邻单元格也纳入扫描；对多数应用这个边界情况影响不大。
why_en: Locations near each other can get different prefixes if they fall on opposite sides of a major grid boundary, which is why radius queries also scan adjacent cells.
options_en: Geohash cannot represent the southern hemisphere with strings.
Two nearby points on opposite sides of a major grid boundary can get completely different prefixes.
Geohash precision only goes down to the city level.
Geohash strings do not support B-tree indexing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维经纬度递归四等分并编码成一维字符串的编码方式，邻近位置通常共享前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively subdivides 2D coordinates and encodes them as a 1D string, so nearby locations usually share a prefix.

termDefinitions.meaning: geohash 递归四等分产生的方格分界线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A grid boundary is the dividing line between geohash's recursively quartered cells.

q_en: What is the main limitation of geohash?
optionExplanations: geohash 对南北半球都能编码，纬度符号只是编码的一部分，不存在「无法表示」的问题。
对，两点若刚好落在大网格分界线两侧，即使物理上很近，前缀也可能完全不同，这是网格边界效应。
精度由字符串长度决定，可以做到街区甚至更细的级别，不止停在城市级。
geohash 字符串本身就是普通字符串，完全可以直接建 B 树索引，这正是它流行的原因。
optionExplanations_en: Geohash can encode both hemispheres just fine — latitude sign is just part of the encoding; there's no "can't represent" issue.
Right — if two points fall on opposite sides of a large grid boundary, their prefixes can be completely different even though they're physically close.
Precision is set by string length and can go down to block level or finer, not just stop at city-level.
A geohash string is just an ordinary string and indexes fine in a B-tree — that's actually why it's popular.

q: 四叉树（quadtree）如何组织空间？
options: 从一个方块开始，点数超阈值就四等分递归
把空间切成固定大小的均匀网格
用可重叠的柔性矩形层层包裹数据
把二维坐标编码成一维字符串表示
why: 四叉树按需细分：点多的方块继续切四份，稀疏区域保持大格子——自适应分辨率是它的招牌优势。
why_en: A quadtree starts with one square and recursively splits any square holding more than a threshold of points into four quadrants, giving dense areas finer resolution.
options_en: Start with one square and recursively quarter it once a point threshold is exceeded.
Cut space into a fixed-size uniform grid.
Wrap data in flexible, overlapping rectangles.
Encode 2D coordinates into a 1D string.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从一个覆盖全区域的方块开始，点数超阈值就递归四等分的空间索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree starts with one square covering the whole area and recursively splits any square exceeding a point threshold into four quadrants.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用同样的规则不断在更小范围重复应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recursion means repeatedly applying the same rule at smaller and smaller scales.

q_en: How does a quadtree organize space?
optionExplanations: 对，点密集的方块继续切成四份，稀疏区域保持大格子不切，这种自适应细分正是四叉树的招牌。
固定大小的均匀网格切分是另一种更简单的方案，缺点是没法针对热点区域自适应加密。
可重叠柔性矩形是 R 树的做法，四叉树是刚性四等分，不重叠。
把 2D 编码成 1D 字符串是 geohash 的做法，四叉树保留的是真正的树结构，不编码成字符串。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a block with many points keeps splitting into four; sparse regions stay as large cells — that adaptive resolution is the quadtree's signature trait.
A fixed-size uniform grid is a simpler alternative, but can't adaptively get finer resolution around hot spots the way a quadtree does.
Overlapping flexible rectangles is the R-tree's approach; a quadtree splits rigidly into quarters with no overlap.
Encoding 2D into a 1D string is geohash's approach; a quadtree keeps an actual tree structure instead of encoding into a string.

q: 四叉树如今在生产数据库里少见的主要原因是？
options: 它的查询复杂度普遍被认为是一种纯线性增长模式
它根本没有办法用来表示密集聚集的热点区域范围
它受到了专利授权方面相当严格的法律限制约束
需要专门树结构，不像 geohash 复用现成 B 树
why: geohash 借力打力（B 树现成），四叉树却要专门实现和维护一套树结构，实现复杂度让多数数据库转向 geohash 或 R 树。但它的递归细分思想奠定了 R 树的基础，Google Maps 的瓦片也有它的影子。
why_en: Quadtrees require specialized tree structures instead of reusing existing B-trees like geohash does, which is why modern databases prefer geohash or R-tree variants.
options_en: Its query complexity is widely believed to be a purely linear growth pattern.
It supposedly has no way to represent the range of a densely clustered hot spot.
It's supposedly bound by fairly strict patent-licensing legal restrictions.
It needs a dedicated tree structure, unlike geohash which reuses the existing B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从一个覆盖全区域的方块开始，点数超阈值就递归四等分的空间索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree starts with one square covering the whole area and recursively splits any square exceeding a point threshold into four quadrants.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维经纬度递归四等分并编码成一维字符串的编码方式，邻近位置通常共享前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively subdivides 2D coordinates and encodes them as a 1D string, so nearby locations usually share a prefix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: Why are quadtrees less common in production databases today?
optionExplanations: 四叉树的查询复杂度不是纯线性的，它的问题在实现和维护成本，不是算法复杂度差。
四叉树恰恰能通过持续细分来表示密集热点区域，这不是它的短板。
四叉树是公开的经典数据结构，不存在专利限制这回事。
对，geohash 借力现成的 B 树设施，四叉树却要专门实现和维护一整套树结构，这份复杂度让多数数据库转而选择别的方案。
optionExplanations_en: A quadtree's query complexity isn't purely linear — its real problem is implementation and maintenance cost, not algorithmic complexity.
A quadtree is actually good at representing dense hot spots by subdividing further — that's not a weakness of it.
A quadtree is a well-known public data structure — no patent restriction is involved.
Right — geohash rides on existing B-tree infrastructure, while a quadtree needs a dedicated tree implementation, and that complexity pushed most databases elsewhere.

q: R 树是什么、地位如何？
options: 一种把整个空间固定切成四等分的树结构
一种把二维坐标编码压缩成字符串的方案
用灵活重叠矩形包裹数据，是主流数据库默认空间索引
只能用在内存数据库里的一种哈希表变体结构
why: R 树不按固定格子切空间，而是让矩形贴着数据的实际聚集自适应生长、允许重叠；这让它成为现代生产库的空间索引标配。
why_en: R-trees group spatial data into flexible overlapping rectangles that adapt to where data actually clusters, and they are the default spatial index in PostGIS and MySQL.
options_en: A tree structure that rigidly quarters the entire space.
A scheme that encodes two-dimensional coordinates down into a string.
It wraps data in flexible, overlapping rectangles, and is the default spatial index in mainstream databases.
A hash-table variant usable only inside in-memory databases.

q_en: What is inverted in an inverted index?

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引命中后还要去主表数据页取出索引未包含的列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A table lookup, or heap fetch, is the extra step of visiting the main table page for columns the index doesn't include.

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 里给索引附加非键列的语法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCLUDE is PostgreSQL syntax for attaching non-key columns to an index.

q_en: What is a covering index?
optionExplanations: 对，把查询要用的列直接塞进索引（比如再包一个 likes 字段），数据就能直接从索引返回，不用再回表读数据页。
覆盖整表所有列既没必要也不现实，覆盖索引只包含某个查询实际需要的那几列。
没有「自动覆盖所有查询」的智能索引，覆盖索引是针对某个具体查询模式手动设计出来的。
覆盖索引是普通索引的一种设计方式（把用到的列都放进去），不是主键索引的别名。
optionExplanations_en: Right — pack the columns a query needs straight into the index (say, tucking in a likes column too), so it returns from the index alone, no table lookup needed.
Covering every column in the whole table is neither necessary nor practical — a covering index only holds the columns one query actually needs.
There's no such thing as a smart index that automatically covers every query — a covering index is deliberately designed for one query pattern.
A covering index is a design choice for a regular index (including the columns a query needs), not another name for the primary-key index.

q: 2026 年的现实里，覆盖索引该怎么定位？
options: 所有读查询都该用的默认方案
偏小众优化：普通索引已高效，覆盖索引更贵
已被数据库厂商移除的过时特性
覆盖索引只适用于 NoSQL 数据库
why: 覆盖索引在特定场景（读密集、列少的表）收益显著，但存储和维护成本是真的。现代查询优化器已经很聪明，面试建议优先讲简单索引策略。
why_en: Covering indexes are now a niche optimization with real maintenance and storage costs, so favor simpler strategies unless you have a strong specific reason.
options_en: The default choice for every read query.
A niche optimization: regular indexes already do well, and covering indexes cost more.
A deprecated feature removed by database vendors.
It only applies to NoSQL databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库里决定如何执行一条查询的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query optimizer is the database component that decides how to execute a query.

q_en: How should you position covering indexes in real systems in 2026?
optionExplanations: 覆盖索引不是所有读查询的默认方案——它有真实的存储和维护成本，得挑读密集、列少的场景用。
对，覆盖索引在读密集、列少的表上收益明显，但存储和维护是真代价，属于偏小众的优化手段。
覆盖索引没有被厂商移除，主流数据库（Postgres、MySQL）现在都还支持这个特性。
覆盖索引不是 NoSQL 专属概念，关系型数据库的索引 INCLUDE 列同样是覆盖索引的实现。
optionExplanations_en: A covering index isn't the default for every read query — it has real storage and upkeep costs, so it's reserved for read-heavy, narrow tables.
Right — a covering index pays off clearly on read-heavy, narrow tables, but storage and maintenance are real costs, a fairly niche optimization.
Covering indexes haven't been removed by any vendor — mainstream databases like Postgres and MySQL still support the feature today.
A covering index isn't a NoSQL-only idea — a relational index's INCLUDE columns are exactly the same covering-index technique.

scenario: 面试被问「这个场景该用什么类型的索引」，需要一句话给出通用决策规则。
q: 正确的默认决策流是？
options: 永远回答哈希索引最快，闭眼选它
遇到就先去问公司的 DBA
不管什么场景都上 Elasticsearch
默认 B 树；例外：邻近用地理索引，全文用倒排
why: 拿不准就 B 树（等值+范围通吃、各数据库的默认）；空间数据换 geohash 系空间索引，大规模文本搜索换倒排索引。这三板斧覆盖绝大多数索引问题。
why_en: Default to B-trees, switch to a geospatial index like geohash for lat-lng proximity, and use an inverted index for full-text search.
whenOtherWins: 极端写入摄入（指标、日志、IoT）时再引入 LSM 存储引擎的讨论；纯内存等值查找才轮到哈希结构。
options_en: Always answer hash index because it's fastest, no matter what.
Whenever asked, go ask the DBA first.
Reach for Elasticsearch no matter the scenario.
Default to B-trees; exceptions are geospatial for proximity and inverted for full text.
tradeoff: 通用默认覆盖大多数场景 vs 特化索引服务少数场景

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库管理员，负责数据库运维和优化的角色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DBA stands for Database Administrator, the role responsible for operating and tuning databases.

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 理解二维空间邻近关系的索引，如 geohash、四叉树、R 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index understands 2D proximity, implemented via approaches like geohash, quadtrees, or R-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: What is the right default decision flow for choosing an index type?
scenario_en: In an interview, you are asked which index type fits a scenario and need a one-sentence general decision rule.
optionExplanations: 把哈希索引当默认答案风险很高——一旦场景需要范围查询或排序，这个答案立刻站不住。
面试现场没有 DBA 可问，面试官想看的是你自己能不能推出一个合理默认，不是回避决策。
Elasticsearch 是为全文搜索定制的重型方案，普通等值/范围查询场景直接上它是杀鸡用牛刀。
对，拿不准先默认 B 树；邻近查询换地理空间索引，全文检索换倒排索引，这三板斧覆盖了大多数场景。
optionExplanations_en: Treating a hash index as the default answer is risky — the moment the scenario needs range queries or sorting, that answer falls apart.
There's no DBA to ask in an interview — the interviewer wants to see you reason your way to a sensible default yourself, not dodge the decision.
Elasticsearch is a heavyweight tool purpose-built for full-text search — reaching for it on an ordinary equality/range query is overkill.
Right — default to B-tree when unsure; swap to a geospatial index for proximity queries and an inverted index for full-text search.

q: 网络分层（OSI 模型）对应用开发者的根本意义是什么？
q_en: What is the core value of network layering, or the OSI model, for application developers?
options: 规定了所有协议的字节格式
分层是抽象：只需和下一层打交道
让网络传输更快
强制所有系统用 7 层协议
why: 分层就是抽象——像用语言里的 open 而不是手动指挥磁盘读字节。请求网页时你不需要懂物理层，只要会用下一层即可。
why_en: Network layers are abstractions that let developers reason about communication at their own level without knowing how lower layers move the bits.
diagram:
flowchart TB
    A["应用层 L7"] --> B["传输层 L4"]
    B --> C["网络层 L3"]
    C --> D["更底层细节"]
    A -.只依赖下一层.-> B
options_en: It dictates the exact byte format every protocol must use.
Layering is an abstraction — you deal only with the layer below you.
It makes network transmission inherently faster.
It forces every system to implement all seven OSI layers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把网络通信拆成 7 层的参考模型，每层只依赖它下面那一层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OSI is the reference model that splits network communication into seven layers, each depending only on the layer below it.

optionExplanations: 分层从没规定过字节格式，那是具体协议自己的事，分层只是把复杂度切开。
分层的价值就是抽象——你只需要弄懂和你相邻的下一层，不用管物理层怎么搬比特。
分层不会让传输本身变快，它换来的是可维护性和职责隔离，不是性能。
没有系统被强制走满 7 层，很多实现会跳过或合并某些层。
optionExplanations_en: layering never dictates byte formats; that's each protocol's own job, layering just splits up complexity.
layering's value is abstraction — you only need the layer right below you, not how bits move on the wire.
layering doesn't speed up transmission itself; it buys maintainability, not performance.
no system is forced to implement all seven layers; real stacks skip or merge layers freely.

q: 补全面试最常涉及的三个网络层：
q_en: Fill in the three network layers that come up most often in interviews.
text: 第 3 层网络层：{{IP}}，负责路由与寻址；第 4 层传输层：{{TCP}}、UDP、QUIC，提供端到端通信；第 7 层应用层：DNS、{{HTTP}}、WebSocket、WebRTC。
why: 面试聚焦三层：L3 管「送到哪台机器」，L4 管「可靠性/顺序等端到端保证」，L7 是开发者天天用的应用协议。
why_en: Interviews focus on layer three with IP for routing, layer four with TCP and UDP for end-to-end guarantees, and layer seven application protocols like HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建在 UDP 之上的现代传输协议，提供接近 TCP 的可靠性但性能更好、采用率还不够广。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP that offers TCP-like reliability with better performance but is not yet as widely adopted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在一条 TCP 连接上提供持久、双向通信的协议，通过 HTTP upgrade 建立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that provides a persistent, bidirectional channel over one TCP connection, established via an HTTP upgrade.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

q: 网络层（L3）的 IP 协议负责什么？
q_en: What is IP responsible for at the network layer, or L3?
options: 保证数据按序到达
加密通信内容
把数据切成包并尽力而为投递
维护客户端与服务器的会话
why: IP 只管路由和寻址：切包、转发、尽力送达——不保证可靠或有序，那是 L4 的事。ML 训练场景还会见到 InfiniBand，但面试以 IP 为主。
why_en: IP handles routing and addressing by breaking data into packets and forwarding them with best-effort delivery to any destination address.
options_en: It guarantees packets arrive in order.
It encrypts the contents of the communication.
It breaks data into packets and delivers them best-effort.
It maintains session state between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里负责路由和寻址的网络层，主角是 IP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 3, the network layer, handles routing and addressing and is dominated by IP.

optionExplanations: 按序到达是 L4（TCP）的职责，IP 本身不做排序或重传保证。
加密属于更上层（如 TLS），IP 只负责路由寻址，不碰内容加解密。
IP 的职责就是把数据切片打包、尽力路由投递，可靠性和顺序留给上层去做。
会话状态由应用层或传输层维护，IP 是无状态的逐包转发。
optionExplanations_en: ordered delivery is TCP's job at L4 — IP makes no ordering or retransmission promise.
encryption belongs to a higher layer like TLS; IP only routes and addresses, never touches content.
IP's job is chopping data into packets and best-effort routing them, leaving reliability to the layer above.
session state is tracked by transport or application layers, not by stateless, per-packet IP.

q: 传输层（L4）在网络层之上补充了什么？
q_en: What does the transport layer, or L4, add on top of the network layer?
options: 端到端通信服务：可靠性、有序性等特性
域名解析（DNS 查询）
HTML 页面渲染引擎
物理层的信号调制与编码
why: L3 只把包尽力扔到目的地；TCP/QUIC/UDP 这层决定要不要在其上提供可靠、有序、流控等保证——否则你拿到的就是一堆乱序的包。
why_en: The transport layer adds end-to-end services like reliability, ordering, and flow control on top of the network layer's raw packet delivery.
options_en: End-to-end services like reliability and ordering.
Domain name resolution via DNS queries.
The browser's HTML rendering engine.
Modulating and encoding the physical-layer signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: OSI 模型里提供端到端保证（可靠性、顺序、流控）的传输层，主角是 TCP/UDP/QUIC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 4, the transport layer, provides end-to-end guarantees like reliability, ordering, and flow control, dominated by TCP, UDP, and QUIC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构建在 UDP 之上的现代传输协议，提供接近 TCP 的可靠性但性能更好、采用率还不够广。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QUIC is a modern transport protocol built on UDP that offers TCP-like reliability with better performance but is not yet as widely adopted.

optionExplanations: 传输层在 L3 之上加了端到端保证——要不要可靠、要不要保序，由 TCP/UDP/QUIC 决定。
域名解析是 DNS 在应用层做的事，跟传输层没关系。
HTML 渲染发生在浏览器的应用层，传输层根本看不到内容格式。
物理信号调制属于物理层（L1），传输层只处理逻辑上的字节流。
optionExplanations_en: the transport layer adds end-to-end guarantees above L3 — TCP, UDP, or QUIC decide reliability and ordering.
domain resolution is DNS's job at the application layer, unrelated to transport.
HTML rendering happens in the browser's application layer; transport never sees content format.
signal modulation belongs to the physical layer (L1); transport only handles logical byte streams.

q: 以下哪组全是应用层（L7）协议？
q_en: Which group contains only application-layer, or L7, protocols?
options: IP、InfiniBand（网络层）
TCP、UDP、QUIC（传输层）
SYN、ACK、FIN（TCP 标志位）
DNS、HTTP、WebSocket、WebRTC
why: 应用层协议构建在 TCP（或 WebRTC 的 UDP）之上，为 Web 应用的各类数据提供抽象。SYN/ACK/FIN 只是 TCP 的报文标志，不是协议。
why_en: DNS, HTTP, WebSockets, and WebRTC are application-layer protocols built on top of TCP or, in WebRTC's case, UDP.
options_en: IP and InfiniBand (network layer).
TCP, UDP, and QUIC (transport layer).
SYN, ACK, and FIN (TCP flag bits).
DNS, HTTP, WebSocket, and WebRTC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层的高速互联协议，常用于大规模机器学习训练集群，不是面试常考的重点。

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把域名解析成 IP 地址的分布式查找系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。

optionExplanations: IP 和 InfiniBand 都是网络层/更底层的东西，不是应用层协议。
TCP、UDP、QUIC 是传输层协议，应用层协议是建在它们之上的。
SYN、ACK、FIN 属于 TCP 报文的标志位，本身并不构成一种独立协议。
DNS、HTTP、WebSocket、WebRTC 都跑在传输层之上，为具体应用场景提供数据抽象。

TCP, UDP, QUIC are transport protocols — application protocols are built on top of them.

q: 把「浏览器输入 URL 到拿到网页」的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the browser-to-webpage request flow in the correct order.
steps: TCP 三次握手建立连接
DNS 把域名解析成 IP 地址
服务器处理请求并准备响应
客户端发送 HTTP GET 请求
TCP 四次挥手关闭连接
服务器发回 HTTP 响应
why: DNS 解析 → TCP 握手 → 发请求 → 服务器处理（多数工程师唯一控制的延迟）→ 回响应 → 挥手断开。一次「简单」请求背后是多轮包交换，层层都有延迟。
why_en: A web request resolves DNS, performs the TCP handshake, sends the HTTP request, waits for server processing, receives the response, and tears the connection down.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant D as DNS
    participant S as 服务器
    C->>D: 域名解析
    D-->>C: IP 地址
    C->>S: SYN / SYN-ACK / ACK（三次握手）
    C->>S: HTTP GET
    S-->>C: HTTP 响应
    C->>S: FIN / ACK / FIN / ACK（四次挥手）

termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS is the distributed lookup system that resolves domain names into IP addresses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

q: 补全 TCP 三次握手：
q_en: Complete the TCP three-way handshake.
text: 客户端发 {{SYN}} 请求连接；服务器回 {{SYN-ACK}} 确认请求；客户端再发 {{ACK}} 完成连接建立。断开则用 FIN/ACK/FIN/ACK 四次挥手。
why: 三次握手建立、四次挥手拆除——每个不复用连接的请求都要重复这套流程，这是后面讨论持久连接和负载均衡的伏笔。
why_en: TCP opens with a SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK three-way handshake and closes with a four-way FIN and ACK exchange.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server
    C->>S: SYN
    S-->>C: SYN-ACK
    C->>S: ACK
    Note over C,S: 连接已建立

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 报文里的控制标志位，分别用于发起连接、确认收到、结束连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SYN, ACK, and FIN are TCP control flags used to open a connection, acknowledge receipt, and close a connection.

q: TCP 连接是客户端和服务器都要维护的状态：这一事实带来什么设计影响？
q_en: What design consequence follows from TCP connection state living on both client and server?
options: 连接一旦建立就永远免费
状态只存在服务器端，不在客户端
不用 keep-alive 就要重建连接
TCP 连接不占用任何资源
why: 连接即状态，双方都要维护；不复用就得每请求重建，开销可观。设计实时更新类系统（持久连接）时这一点会反复出现。
why_en: Because a connection is state both sides maintain, every request repeats the costly setup unless you use keep-alive or multiplexing, which matters for realtime systems.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["请求 1"] --> B["建连"]
    B --> C["响应"]
    C --> D["断开"]
    D --> E["请求 2 再建连"]
    C -.keep-alive.-> F["复用连接"]
options_en: Once established, a connection is free forever.
The state only lives on the server, never the client.
Without keep-alive you rebuild the connection every time.
A TCP connection consumes no resources at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一条 TCP 连接被多个 HTTP 请求复用，省去重复握手的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP keep-alive lets one TCP connection serve multiple HTTP requests, avoiding repeated handshake overhead.

optionExplanations: 维护连接本身要占内存和文件描述符，从来不是免费的，只是分摊到了每次请求。
TCP 是双方对等维护状态，客户端和服务器都要记住序号、窗口，不是只有服务器。
连接状态双方都要维护，不复用连接（没有 keep-alive）就得每次请求重新握手，开销明显。
每条 TCP 连接都占用服务器内存和文件描述符，大量并发连接会实实在在压垮资源。
optionExplanations_en: keeping a connection alive still costs memory and file descriptors — it's amortized, not free.
TCP state is kept by both sides; client and server both track sequence numbers, not just the server.
both sides hold connection state, so without keep-alive you pay a fresh handshake on every request.
every TCP connection consumes real memory and file descriptors; enough of them exhaust resources.

q: 关于公网 IP，正确的说法是？
q_en: Which statement about public IP addresses is correct?
options: 任何人可以随便自封公网 IP 并被全网路由
公网 IP 由 RIR 分配，全网可路由
公网 IP 只在局域网内部有效，出不了本地网络
公网 IP 由 DNS 服务器直接分配给客户端
why: 私有网络里 IP 随便定，但要让互联网流量找到你，必须用 RIR 分配的可路由地址。互联网路由基础设施针对公网 IP 之间的转发做了优化。
why_en: Public IPs are allocated by regional internet registries and are routable, so the internet backbone knows for example that addresses starting with 17 belong to Apple.
options_en: Anyone can self-assign a public IP and have it routed by the whole internet.
Public IPs are allocated by a RIR and are globally routable.
A public IP only works inside a local network and never leaves it.
Public IPs are assigned directly to clients by DNS servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络层协议，负责给数据包寻址并在网络间转发、尽力而为地投递。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is the network-layer protocol that addresses packets and forwards them across networks on a best-effort basis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责分配可在公网路由的 IP 地址段的区域机构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A RIR is the regional authority that allocates blocks of publicly routable IP addresses.

optionExplanations: 自己乱定的地址不会被互联网骨干路由接受，必须走正规分配才能被全网识别。
公网 IP 由 RIR 统一分配，保证全球唯一、可被互联网路由基础设施转发。
只在局域网内有效的是私有地址段，公网 IP 恰恰是要能被外部路由的地址。
DNS 只负责把域名解析成已有的 IP，它不分配 IP 地址本身。
optionExplanations_en: a self-assigned address won't be accepted by the internet backbone without proper allocation.
public IPs are allocated by RIRs, guaranteeing global uniqueness so routing infrastructure can forward them.
addresses valid only inside a LAN are private ranges — a public IP is exactly one that routes outside.
DNS only resolves a name to an existing IP; it never assigns the IP address itself.

q: UDP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does UDP have?
options: 无连接：没有握手和连接建立，开销小、延迟低
不保证送达：丢包不会有任何通知
不保证顺序：包可能乱序到达
自动去重，保证恰好一次投递
why: UDP 是「机枪式」spray and pray：在 IP 之上几乎不加功能，换来速度。无连接、可能丢、可能乱序，也没有重复保护——收到的就是一坨二进制加上来源/目的地址端口。
why_en: UDP is connectionless with no handshake, offers no delivery or ordering guarantees, and has lower latency precisely because it adds so little on top of IP.
options_en: Connectionless: no handshake or setup, so overhead and latency are lower.
No delivery guarantee: a lost packet triggers no notification.
No ordering guarantee: packets can arrive out of order.
Automatic deduplication with exactly-once delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: 省掉握手意味着发送前不用建立连接状态，直接把开销和延迟降到最低。
丢包发生时发送方和接收方都不会收到提示，应用层必须自己检测和处理丢失。
包可能各走各的路径，到达顺序可能和发送顺序对不上，接收方要自己排序。
UDP 不做任何去重，重复包会原样交给上层，恰好一次投递是应用自己要保证的事。
optionExplanations_en: skipping the handshake means no setup before sending, keeping overhead and latency low.
on loss, neither sender nor receiver is notified — the application must detect and handle it itself.
packets can take different paths, so arrival order can differ from send order; receivers reorder them.
UDP does no deduplication — duplicates pass straight through; exactly-once is the app's job.

scenario: 设计 VoIP 语音通话：偶尔丢一个包只是音频轻微卡顿、对话依然可懂；重传丢失的包反而会用 ACK 堵塞网络。
scenario_en: You are designing a VoIP call: losing one audio packet causes a tiny glitch, but retransmitting it would block newer audio behind ACKs.
q: 传输层该选？
q_en: Which transport protocol should you choose for this VoIP audio call?
options: TCP，保证每个音频包都到
QUIC，等它普及
UDP：速度优先，客户端自己扛丢包
HTTP 轮询
why: 实时音视频、在线游戏、DNS 查询都是 UDP 的主场：应用能自行处理偶发丢包/乱序，低延迟远比完整重传值钱。
why_en: UDP fits VoIP because dropping an occasional packet is a minor hiccup, while retransmitting old audio would only clog the network.
whenOtherWins: 数据完整性关键的场景（支付、文件传输、几乎一切非实时业务）用 TCP——凡是 UDP 不合适的地方基本都是 TCP。
options_en: TCP, to guarantee every audio packet arrives.
QUIC, and wait for it to become mainstream.
UDP: speed over reliability, and the client absorbs the occasional loss.
HTTP polling.
tradeoff: UDP 低延迟可丢包 vs TCP 可靠重传

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: TCP 适合数据必须完整到达的场景（文件传输、支付），但这里重传会让新音频排在旧音频后面，加剧卡顿。
QUIC 具备类似能力且底层用 UDP，值得关注，但客户端/中间件支持还不够普及，直接依赖它超出本题约束。
偶发丢包只造成轻微卡顿，重传反而堵塞后续音频；UDP 让客户端自己容忍丢包，换来实时语音要的低延迟。
轮询天然有请求间隔造成的延迟，不是持续推送，撑不起语音这种连续实时流。
optionExplanations_en: TCP suits data that must arrive whole, but retransmitting audio here queues fresh sound behind stale sound.
QUIC offers similar guarantees over UDP, but support isn't mainstream yet, so betting on it here goes too far.
a dropped packet is a minor glitch, but retransmitting clogs newer audio — UDP trades loss for low latency.
Polling has built-in gaps between requests instead of continuous delivery, so it can't sustain a voice stream.

q: 你想用 UDP（User Datagram Protocol）给 Facebook Live 评论的刷屏点赞做实时推送，要注意什么现实限制？
q_en: What real-world limitation matters if you want to use UDP for Facebook Live reactions in the browser?
options: UDP 无法承载表情数据
浏览器基本只有 WebRTC 支持 UDP
UDP 在移动网络里完全不可用
点赞数必须做到强一致
why: 浏览器除 WebRTC 外基本用不了 UDP。常见设计：App 端吃实时 UDP 流，浏览器端退化为分批 HTTP 流、在 UI 里摊开播放。
why_en: Browsers barely support UDP outside WebRTC, so a UDP-based design needs a fallback like a slower batched HTTP stream for browser users.
options_en: UDP cannot carry emoji/reaction data.
Browsers only really support UDP through WebRTC.
UDP does not work at all on mobile networks.
Like counts must be strongly consistent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让浏览器之间直接进行点对点音视频/数据传输的协议族。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebRTC is a protocol suite that lets browsers exchange audio, video, or data directly, peer to peer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层的请求-响应协议，是 Web 通信的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer request-response protocol that underlies web communication.

optionExplanations: UDP 只是个传输协议，不关心载荷内容，表情、文本、二进制都能装进去。
普通浏览器 JS 没有裸 UDP socket 接口，除了 WebRTC 这个特例，浏览器端基本走不了 UDP。
UDP 在移动网络是能用的，真正的限制来自浏览器 API，不是移动网络本身。
点赞数是可以容忍短暂不一致、最终收敛的计数，不需要强一致，这不是选 UDP 的顾虑点。
optionExplanations_en: UDP just moves bytes and doesn't care about payload — emoji, text, or binary all fit fine.
plain browser JS has no raw UDP socket API; aside from WebRTC, browsers basically can't speak UDP.
UDP works fine over mobile networks — the real constraint is the browser API, not the network.
like counts tolerate brief inconsistency and converge eventually; strong consistency isn't the issue.

q: TCP 的「流（stream）」意味着什么？
q_en: What does it mean that TCP exposes a stream?
options: 数据以视频流的形式传输
服务器可以不经请求主动推送数据
连接是完全无状态的
有状态连接：同流内消息保序，未确认会重传
why: TCP 流是有状态连接，给了我们谈「顺序」的基础：同流内消息保序，接收方必须 ACK，否则发送方重传。可靠、有序、有错误校验。
why_en: A TCP stream is a stateful connection where messages arrive in the order sent and unacknowledged messages are retransmitted until confirmed.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["发送端字节流"] --> B["TCP 分段"]
    B --> C["确认 ACK"]
    C -.丢包.-> D["重传"]
    C --> E["接收端按序读"]
options_en: Data is transmitted like a video stream.
The server can push data without being asked.
The connection carries no state at all.
A stateful connection: messages on the same stream stay ordered, and unacknowledged ones get retransmitted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: 这里的「流」指字节流这个抽象概念，跟视频流媒体没有关系。
服务器主动推送需要 WebSocket 之类机制，普通 TCP 流本身不代表服务器能不请自来发数据。
恰恰相反，TCP 连接是有状态的——双方要记住序号、窗口、未确认的数据。
TCP 的流是有状态连接，同一条流内消息保证顺序，没收到 ACK 的数据会被重传。
optionExplanations_en: 'stream' here means the byte-stream abstraction, unrelated to video streaming.
unsolicited server push needs something like WebSocket; a plain TCP stream alone doesn't grant that.
it's the opposite — TCP is stateful, with both sides tracking sequence numbers and unacked data.
a TCP stream is stateful; messages within it stay ordered, and unacknowledged data gets retransmitted.

q: TCP 的关键特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which properties does TCP provide?
options: 面向连接：传数据前先建立专用连接
可靠投递：保证数据按序、无错到达
流量控制防止淹没接收方 + 拥塞控制适应网络拥堵
头部固定只有 8 字节
why: TCP 四大件：面向连接、可靠有序、流控、拥塞控制——这就是它比 UDP 慢的原因，也是互联网的主力马。8 字节头是 UDP 的，TCP 头是 20-60 字节。
why_en: TCP is connection-oriented with reliable in-order delivery, flow control, and congestion control, while the tiny eight-byte header belongs to UDP.
options_en: Connection-oriented: it establishes a dedicated connection before transferring data.
Reliable delivery: it guarantees data arrives in order and without errors.
Flow control to avoid overwhelming the receiver, plus congestion control to adapt to a congested network.
A fixed 8-byte header.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无连接、尽力而为的传输层协议，不保证送达或顺序，换来更低延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

optionExplanations: TCP 在传数据前先做三次握手，建立起一条双方都认可的专用连接。
TCP 靠序号和 ACK/重传机制保证数据按顺序、无差错地到达接收方。
流量控制防止发送方压垮接收方缓冲区，拥塞控制则根据网络状况动态调整发送速率。
8 字节固定头是 UDP 的特征；TCP 基础头是 20 字节，带 options 能到 60 字节。
optionExplanations_en: TCP does a three-way handshake before sending data, establishing a dedicated agreed-upon connection.
sequence numbers plus ACK-and-retransmit guarantee data arrives in order and without corruption.
flow control stops the sender overrunning the receiver's buffer; congestion control adapts send rate.
an 8-byte header is UDP's trait — TCP's base header is 20 bytes, up to 60 with options.

scenario: 你在解释实时音视频为什么常偏向 UDP：单包头部开销不是主瓶颈，但能反映协议是否在传输层替你记可靠性状态。
scenario_en: You are explaining why real-time media often leans toward UDP: packet-header overhead is not the main bottleneck, but it shows whether the transport layer tracks reliability state for you.
q: UDP/TCP 头部大小差异说明哪个传输层取舍？
q_en: What transport-layer tradeoff does the UDP/TCP header-size difference illustrate?
options: 8B vs 20-60B：少记账、低开销
20-60B vs 8B：把顺序反了
同为 20B：只按带宽选协议
无固定含义：可靠性不需要状态
why: UDP 头固定 8B；TCP 基础头 20B，带 options 可到 60B。这个数字的用途不是背诵，而是提醒你：TCP 用额外字节和状态换可靠性、流控、拥塞控制。
why_en: UDP's 8-byte header versus TCP's 20-to-60-byte header is a reminder that TCP pays extra bookkeeping for reliability, flow control, and congestion control.
options_en: 8B versus 20-60B: less bookkeeping and lower overhead.
20-60B versus 8B: the order is reversed.
Both are 20B: choose only by bandwidth.
No fixed meaning: reliability needs no state.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort transport protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees in exchange for lower latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、可靠有序的传输层协议，靠握手建立连接、对未确认数据重传。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery by retransmitting unacknowledged data.

optionExplanations: UDP 头只需 8 字节记账，TCP 为维护可靠性状态把头部撑到 20-60 字节，这条差距就是「省记账 vs 换可靠」的体现。
把两个协议的头部数字对调了，实际是 UDP 更小（8B）、TCP 更大（20-60B），不是反过来。
两者头部大小并不相等，协议选择的关键也不是带宽，是要不要传输层帮你维护可靠性状态。
头部大小的差异恰恰说明可靠性需要额外状态字段去维护，不是无成本的。
optionExplanations_en: UDP needs only 8 bytes of bookkeeping, while TCP grows to 20-60 bytes to carry reliability state.
this swaps the two numbers — UDP is the smaller one (8B), TCP the larger (20-60B), not reversed.
the headers aren't equal, and the choice driver isn't bandwidth — it's transport-layer reliability.
the header-size gap shows reliability needs extra state fields to maintain — it isn't free.

scenario: 系统设计面试中选择传输层协议，没有特别的实时性要求。

TCP 和 UDP 各占一半

why_en: Interviewers assume TCP by default, and you earn extra points by correctly making the case for UDP only where it genuinely fits.
whenOtherWins: 低延迟至上、可容忍丢包的实时媒体/游戏/遥测才切 UDP，并要交代浏览器端怎么办。
options_en: Explicitly declare QUIC for every connection.
Default to UDP because it's fast.

optionExplanations: QUIC 值得了解，但面试里主动点名每条连接都用它显得刻意——它还不是通用默认。

interviewers usually assume TCP unless the problem calls for real-time or loss-tolerant traffic.

q: 面试语境下该怎么看 QUIC？
q_en: How should you think about QUIC in interview settings?

现代化、性能更好的 TCP，但采用面还不够广
它只是 UDP 换了个名字，本质完全相同
它只能用于内部数据库之间的通信
why: QUIC 提供 TCP 式的保证外加现代化性能优化，但还没有同等的普及基线。面试的真实选择题仍是 TCP vs UDP。
why_en: Treat QUIC as a better modernized TCP that lacks broad adoption, so the real interview choice remains TCP versus UDP.

A modernized, better-performing TCP that isn't broadly adopted yet.
It's just UDP renamed, functionally identical underneath.
