scenario: 设计 Yelp：1000 万个商家，每个约 1KB 数据，候选人一上来就讲要按哪个列分片。
scenario_en: In a Yelp design, there are 10 million businesses at about 1KB each, but the candidate jumps straight to sharding keys.
q: 先算一下数据量，正确判断是？
q_en: After doing the size math first, what is the right call?
options: 数据看起来这么多，必须立刻分片处理
商家数据量大，必须上分布式数据库
算下来约 100GB，单机够用，不用分片
这类数据量太复杂，根本没法估算
why: 10M × 1KB ≈ 10GB，加评论约 100GB——单机轻松装下。过早分片是常见错误：先算术，再决定要不要分。
why_en: Ten million businesses at about one kilobyte each is only ten gigabytes, roughly a hundred with reviews, so sharding is unnecessary.
options_en: That looks like a lot of data, so it must be sharded immediately.
Business data at this volume must go on a distributed database.
It works out to about 100GB, a single node handles it, no sharding needed.
This kind of data volume is too complex to even estimate.
optionExplanations: 错，没算过量级就下结论，其实这批数据加起来才百 GB 级。
错，「必须」是想当然，实际算出来的量级根本用不上分布式。
对，先做算术再判断：约 100GB 单机绰绰有余，不必分片。
错，条数 × 单条大小就是最基础的估算，并不复杂。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, that's a conclusion without doing the math; the total actually lands around a hundred gigabytes.
Wrong, 'must' is an assumption; the computed size doesn't come close to needing distribution.
Right, doing the math first: roughly 100GB fits comfortably on one node, no sharding needed.
Wrong, count times size per record is the most basic estimate, nothing complex about it.

scenario: 面试被问到 Design Yelp，候选人还没算过数据量就想先讲分片方案。
scenario_en: In a Yelp design interview, the candidate wants to discuss sharding before estimating the data size.
q: 补全 Yelp 的容量估算：
q_en: Complete the Yelp capacity estimate:
text: 1000 万商家 × 每个约 1KB ≈ {{10GB}}；再 ×10 计入评论 ≈ {{100GB}}，这个量级单机{{无需分片}}。
why: 把「条数 × 每条大小」算成总量级，是判断要不要分片的第一步；100GB 完全在单机能力内。
why_en: Ten million times one kilobyte is about ten gigabytes, and roughly a hundred with reviews, which fits a single node.

scenario: 面试者一上来就说要给主键查询加缓存层，理由是数据库延迟太高。
scenario_en: A candidate proposes caching primary-key lookups immediately because they assume database reads are too slow.
q: 这个判断哪里错了？

This service has already been running continuously for over a day.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议，对延迟、可用性等指标的承诺目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA is the promised target for a metric such as latency or availability.

optionExplanations: 用户数量本身不是扩容依据，10 个用户完全谈不上任何压力。
对，CPU 持续超 70-80% 或延迟破 SLA，是真正该加机器的硬信号。
内存只用了 10% 恰恰说明资源还很富余，是不该扩容的证据。
运行时长和负载压力无关，跑了一天不代表资源已经吃紧。
optionExplanations_en: User count on its own isn't a scaling signal; ten users puts no real pressure on anything.
Right, CPU sustaining above 70-80% or latency breaching SLA is the actual hard trigger to add machines.
Memory at only 10% usage is evidence resources are still plentiful, an argument against scaling.
Uptime has nothing to do with load pressure; running for a day doesn't mean resources are strained.

scenario: 一个电商大促前，团队在设计自动扩容策略：流量升高就临时加机器，而不是长期超额预置。
scenario_en: Before a shopping event, the team designs auto-scaling that adds machines during traffic spikes instead of permanently over-provisioning.
q: 容器启动速度这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision does this container startup time support?
options: 容器启动普遍要几十分钟，只能靠长期超额预置
启动速度和自动扩容策略完全无关
容器 30-60 秒即可起新实例，可支撑激进自动扩容
容器启动越快，说明可以完全不做健康检查
why: 容器化应用 30-60 秒即可起新实例，这个速度让「激进自动扩容」成为超额预置之外的可行替代方案。
why_en: Containerized apps start in about 30 to 60 seconds, making aggressive auto-scaling practical instead of over-provisioning.
options_en: Containers generally take tens of minutes to start, so only heavy long-term over-provisioning works.
Startup speed has nothing at all to do with auto-scaling strategy.
Containers start in 30-60 seconds, which can support aggressive auto-scaling.
The faster a container starts, the more it means health checks can be skipped entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据负载自动增减实例数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Auto-scaling automatically adds or removes instances based on load.

optionExplanations: 错，几十分钟是虚拟机时代的旧印象，容器启动通常是几十秒级。
错，启动越快，自动扩容才越敢激进地临时加实例来应对峰值。
对，30-60 秒的启动速度让「大促时临时加机器」成为现实选项。
错，启动快慢和要不要做健康检查是两件事，快启动也需要探活。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, tens of minutes is a leftover VM-era assumption; containers typically start in tens of seconds.
Wrong, faster startup is exactly what makes aggressive auto-scaling safe to lean on during spikes.
Right, 30-60 second startup makes 'add machines temporarily for the peak' a realistic option.
Wrong, startup speed and health checks are separate concerns; even fast-starting containers still need liveness checks.

scenario: 一个多可用区部署的服务把主库放在一个 AZ，只读副本放在同区另一个 AZ，报表服务放在另一个大洲。
scenario_en: A multi-AZ service keeps the primary database in one AZ, a read replica in another AZ in the same region, and reporting in another continent.
q: 这组网络延迟量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision do these network latency numbers support?
options: 跨大洲和同 AZ 内部延迟其实相差无几
只要还在同一个区域，延迟就一定小于 1ms
网络延迟高低和可用区怎么划分完全无关
同区跨 AZ 延迟约 1-2ms，是可靠默认架构
why: 同 AZ 内 <1ms，同区跨 AZ 1-2ms，跨区域 50-150ms；这组数字支撑了同区多 AZ 部署这种可靠架构。
why_en: Latency is under a millisecond within an AZ, 1-2ms across AZs in a region, and 50-150ms cross-region, which supports multi-AZ deployment as a reliable default.
options_en: Cross-continent and within-AZ latency are basically the same.
As long as it's the same region, latency is always under 1ms.
Network latency level has nothing to do with how availability zones are laid out.
Cross-AZ latency within a region runs about 1-2ms, a reliable default architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云区域内相互隔离的独立机房。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An availability zone is an isolated data-center location within a cloud region.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从主库同步数据、只处理读请求的副本实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica copies data from the primary and serves read-only traffic.

optionExplanations: 错，跨大洲要到 50-150ms，和同 AZ 内 <1ms 差了两个数量级，不是没区别。
错，「一定 <1ms」太绝对，跨 AZ 还是有 1-2ms 的额外开销。
错，AZ 之间是否跨机房，直接决定延迟落在哪个数量级。
对，同区跨 AZ 稳定在 1-2ms，兼顾了隔离性和可接受的延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, cross-continent runs 50-150ms, two orders of magnitude above the sub-millisecond same-AZ figure, not 'basically the same.'
Wrong, 'always under 1ms' is too strong; crossing AZs still adds roughly 1-2ms of overhead.
Wrong, whether traffic crosses data-center boundaries directly determines which latency tier it lands in.
Right, cross-AZ latency within a region holds steady around 1-2ms, balancing isolation with acceptable delay.

scenario: 一个内存计算引擎打算把 3TB 数据集整个放进单台机器内存里做实时聚合。
scenario_en: An in-memory compute engine wants to keep a full 3TB dataset in one machine's RAM for real-time aggregation.
q: 这组内存量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision does this memory-size number support?
options: 内存优化型实例可到 4TB，3TB 单机能装下
单机内存普遍封顶在 64GB 左右，必须先拆成分布式
内存实例最多 128GB，装不下 3TB 数据集
内存上限高低和实例类型完全没有关系
why: 通用实例已达 512GiB，内存优化型可到 4TB、24TB；3TB 单机可行，很多曾需分布式的应用现在单机就能跑。
why_en: Memory-optimized instances reach 4TB or even 24TB of RAM, so a 3TB dataset fits on a single machine without going distributed.
options_en: Memory-optimized instances reach 4TB, so 3TB fits on one machine.
Single-machine memory generally caps around 64GB, so it must be distributed first.
Memory instances cap at 128GB, too small for a 3TB dataset.
The memory ceiling has nothing at all to do with instance type.
optionExplanations: 对，内存优化型实例能到 4TB 甚至更高，3TB 单机完全装得下。
错，64GB 是很旧的经验值，现在的实例内存规格已经涨了几十倍。
错，128GB 远低于内存优化型实例的真实上限，这个数字过时了。
错，不同实例族配的内存上限差别巨大，两者显然是相关的。
optionExplanations_en: Right, memory-optimized instances reach 4TB or higher, so 3TB fits on one machine with room to spare.
Wrong, 64GB is a stale reference; instance memory specs have grown by dozens of times since then.
Wrong, 128GB is far below what memory-optimized instances actually offer, that number is outdated.
Wrong, memory ceilings vary hugely across instance families, so the two are clearly related.

scenario: 一个日志归档系统单节点数据量已经涨到 40TB 本地磁盘，团队在争论要不要马上上分布式文件系统。
scenario_en: A log-archive system has grown to 40TB of local disk on one node, and the team is debating whether to move to a distributed file system now.
q: 这组存储量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision does this storage-size number support?
options: 本地磁盘普遍封顶 1TB，早该上分布式了
本地 SSD/HDD 上限很高，40TB 单机能装下
只能用网络存储，本地磁盘不可用
存储容量和实例类型无关
why: 本地 SSD 可达 60TB（i3en），HDD 达 336TB（D3en）；40TB 单机可行，存储早已不是主要约束。
why_en: Modern instances offer up to 60TB of local SSD or 336TB of HDD, so 40TB fits on a single machine without going distributed.
options_en: Local disks typically cap at 1TB, so it's overdue for distribution.
Local SSD and HDD ceilings are high, so 40TB fits one machine.
Only network storage works; local disks are not usable.
Storage capacity has nothing to do with instance type.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固态硬盘，比机械硬盘快得多的存储介质。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSD is a solid-state drive, a storage medium much faster than spinning disks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机械硬盘，容量大但比 SSD 慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An HDD is a spinning hard disk drive, higher capacity but slower than SSD.

optionExplanations: 错，1TB 是很旧的经验值，现在本地盘规格已经涨了几十倍。
对，本地 SSD 可到 60TB、HDD 可到 336TB，40TB 单机完全能装下。
错，本地磁盘依然可用，很多高吞吐场景反而更偏好本地盘。
错，不同实例类型配的本地盘规格差别很大，两者高度相关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, 1TB is a stale reference; local disk sizes have grown dozens of times over since then.
Right, local SSD reaches up to 60TB and HDD up to 336TB, so 40TB fits comfortably on one machine.
Wrong, local disks are still very usable, and many high-throughput workloads actually prefer them.
Wrong, local disk sizing varies a lot by instance type, so the two are closely tied together.

scenario: 评估要不要在现有系统里引入消息队列。
scenario_en: You are evaluating whether the current system truly needs a message queue.
q: 消息队列在什么情况下才「真正值得」引入？（多选）
q_en: When is a message queue truly worth introducing? (Select all that apply.)
options: 需要可靠投递：下游故障时消息不丢
事件溯源 / 数据集成等模式
写尖峰超过单机数据库能力（如 >20k WPS）或要解耦生产者与消费者
稳定 5k WPS 的简单插入
why: 队列值得用在：可靠投递、事件溯源、超过单机能力的写尖峰、生产/消费解耦。稳定 5k WPS 的简单写单机就够，不该为它加队列。
why_en: Queues are justified by guaranteed delivery, event sourcing, write spikes beyond a single database, or decoupling, not by a steady 5k WPS.
tradeoff: 真正值得引入队列的硬需求 vs 尚在单机能力内的写量
options_en: Guaranteed delivery: messages must not be lost if downstream fails.
Event-sourcing or data-integration patterns.
Write spikes beyond a single database's capacity, or decoupling producer from consumer.
A steady 5k WPS of simple inserts.

termDefinitions.meaning: Writes per second，数据库每秒成功处理的写入次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WPS is the number of write operations a database completes each second.

optionExplanations: 对，队列在下游挂掉时先接住消息，挡住了「消息直接丢失」这个风险。
对，事件溯源和数据集成天然需要持久、可回放的事件流，这正是队列的强项。
对，写尖峰超过单机或要拆开生产消费节奏时，队列能吸收峰值、解耦两端。
错，稳定 5k WPS 单机 Postgres 就能扛住，加队列反而多了一层要运维的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Right, a queue absorbs messages when downstream is down, blocking the risk of losing them outright.
Right, event sourcing and data integration need a durable, replayable event stream, which is exactly a queue's strength.
Right, when write spikes exceed one node or you need to decouple producer and consumer pace, a queue absorbs the spike and separates the two.
Wrong, a steady 5k WPS is well within what single-node Postgres handles, adding a queue here is one more thing to operate.

scenario: 写吞吐看起来偏高，团队正讨论要不要立刻加消息队列。
scenario_en: Write throughput looks high, and the team is discussing whether to add a message queue immediately.
q: 在为「较高写入」加消息队列之前，应先考虑哪些更简单的手段？（多选）
q_en: Before adding a queue for higher write volume, which simpler tactics should you try first? (Select all that apply.)
options: 批量写入（batch writes）
优化 schema 与索引，减少写放大
有效使用连接池
立刻改造成全异步微服务架构
why: 加队列前先试：批量写、优化 schema/索引、连接池、对非关键写用异步提交。这些比「引入队列或重构成异步架构」简单得多。
why_en: Before adding a queue, try batch writes, schema and index tuning, and connection pooling.
options_en: Batch writes.
Tune schema and indexes to reduce write amplification.
Use connection pooling effectively.
Immediately rebuild everything as fully async microservices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用一批数据库连接，避免每次请求都新建连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool reuses a set of database connections instead of opening a new one per request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写导致的实际底层写入量被放大，常见于索引过多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means one logical write triggers more physical writes underneath, often from excess indexes.

optionExplanations: 对，把多条写合并成一次提交，能直接减少往返次数和 commit 开销。
对，减少多余索引能降低写放大，让每次逻辑写的实际开销更小。
对，复用连接能省掉反复建连的开销，减轻数据库端的压力。
错，直接重构成全异步架构成本极高，跳过了更简单能先试的手段。
optionExplanations_en: Right, batching multiple writes into one commit directly cuts round trips and commit overhead.
Right, trimming redundant indexes reduces write amplification, so each logical write costs less underneath.
Right, reusing connections skips the overhead of repeatedly opening new ones, easing pressure on the database.
Wrong, jumping straight to a fully async microservice rebuild is expensive and skips the simpler options worth trying first.

q: 把「决定要不要分片」的正确思考顺序排好：
q_en: Put the decision steps for whether to shard in the right order:
steps: 先给出数据模型和规模（条数、每条大小、TPS）
做算术：估出总数据量与读写吞吐的量级
对照单机能力（约 50 TiB、10k+ WPS、50k 读 TPS）
只有超出单机能力时才分片，否则保持单机 + 副本
why: 反过来做（先讲怎么分片）是最常见的错误。正确顺序：给规模 → 做算术 → 对照单机上限 → 真超了才分片。
why_en: Decide sharding by stating the scale, doing the math, comparing to single-node limits, and only then sharding if exceeded.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Inputs["records x size x QPS"] --> Math["order math"]
    Math --> Limit["compare limits"]
    Limit --> Decision["simple vs shard"]
tradeoff: 先算术验证单机上限 vs 直接假设需要分片

termDefinitions.meaning: 二进制计量的存储单位，1 TiB 约等于 1.1 TB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB is a binary storage unit, about 1.1 times a decimal terabyte.

termDefinitions.meaning: Writes per second，数据库每秒成功处理的写入次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WPS is the number of write operations a database completes each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: Transactions per second，数据库每秒处理的事务数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS is the number of transactions a database completes each second.

scenario: 一个团队只用一台数据库主实例，没有分片，正在讨论这是不是单点故障。
scenario_en: A team uses one primary database instance without sharding and is debating whether that automatically means a single point of failure.
q: 「单实例数据库」是否就等于单点故障（SPOF）？
q_en: Does a single database instance automatically mean a SPOF?
options: 是，单实例必然是单点故障
只有分片才能避免单点
不是，主库+只读副本能做高可用
副本反而会降低可用性
why: 「不分片」不等于「单点」：主库 + 只读副本（如 Aurora 多 AZ 故障转移）就能做高可用；HA 复制与 scale 分片是两回事。
why_en: A single instance is not a single point of failure, since you still run a primary with read replicas for availability, separate from sharding for scale.
options_en: Yes, a single instance is inherently a single point of failure.
Only sharding can avoid a single point of failure.
No, a primary with read replicas provides high availability.
Replicas actually reduce availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单点故障：某个组件一旦失效，整个系统就不可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single point of failure is a component whose failure takes down the whole system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从主库同步数据、只处理读请求的副本实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica copies data from the primary and serves read-only traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点失效后自动切换到备用节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover automatically switches traffic to a standby node when the primary fails.

optionExplanations: 错，「必然」太绝对；单实例配上副本和故障转移就能做到高可用。
错，分片解决的是容量和吞吐，避免单点靠的是复制和故障转移。
对，主库配只读副本、支持自动故障转移，就不再是单点故障。
错，副本恰恰是提高可用性的手段，不会反过来拖累它。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, 'inherently' is too absolute; a single instance paired with replicas and failover already achieves high availability.
Wrong, sharding addresses capacity and throughput, avoiding a single point of failure comes from replication and failover.
Right, a primary with read replicas and automatic failover is no longer a single point of failure.
Wrong, replicas are exactly what raises availability, they don't work against it.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 面试官问起系统设计时该怎么考虑云成本。
scenario_en: An interviewer asks how cloud cost should be considered in a system-design interview.
q: 在系统设计面试里，关于「成本」的正确态度是？
q_en: What is the right attitude toward cost in a system-design interview?
options: 要背熟 AWS 定价表，精确到美元
完全不用考虑成本
成本是面试的核心评分项
只看数量级，但明显浪费会被挑出来
why: 面试很少纠结精确定价，量级判断就够；但明显浪费（100 台干 1 台的活）会被面试官挑出来。
why_en: Interviews care about order-of-magnitude cost sense, not memorized pricing, though obviously wasteful designs still raise flags.
options_en: Memorize AWS pricing tables down to the dollar.
Cost never needs to be considered at all.
Cost is the core scoring criterion in interviews.
Only order-of-magnitude matters, but obvious waste gets called out.
optionExplanations: 错，面试很少考精确定价，背定价表投入和回报不成比例。
错，完全不管成本会漏掉「100 台机器干 1 台的活」这种明显浪费。
错，成本通常是加分项而非核心评分项，架构判断力才是重点。
对，量级判断就够，但设计里出现明显浪费还是会被挑出来问。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, interviews rarely test exact pricing, memorizing rate tables isn't worth the effort.
Wrong, ignoring cost entirely misses obvious waste, like a hundred machines doing one machine's job.
Wrong, cost is usually a bonus signal rather than the core scoring criterion, architectural judgment is.
Right, order-of-magnitude sense is enough, but obvious waste in the design will still get called out.

scenario: 缓存估算给定锚点：命中延迟约 1ms、单实例约 100k+ ops/s、内存可达约 1TB。
scenario_en: Cache-estimation anchors are about 1ms hit latency, roughly 100k+ ops/s per instance, and up to about 1TB of memory.
q: 这些缓存数字约束哪个扩容判断？
q_en: What scaling judgment do these cache numbers constrain?
text: 这些数字说明：数据集接近 1TB 前先别按内存分片；真正要盯的是 {{ops/s 或网络带宽}}，延迟目标低到亚毫秒时才考虑 {{加节点或分片}}。
why: 1ms、100k+ ops/s、1TB 是缓存容量估算的锚点，不是要背的孤立数字。它们的下游用途是判断单实例是否够用，以及扩容先看吞吐/带宽还是内存。
why_en: These cache numbers are sizing inputs: they tell you whether one instance is enough and whether throughput, bandwidth, or memory is the real bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: Operations per second，缓存每秒处理的读写操作次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ops per second counts the read and write operations a cache handles each second.

scenario: 数据库估算给定锚点：单实例读约 50k TPS、写约 10-20k TPS、缓存命中读 <5ms、存储 64TiB+。
scenario_en: Database-estimation anchors are about 50k read TPS, 10-20k write TPS, sub-5ms cached reads, and 64TiB+ storage per instance.
q: 这些数据库数字约束哪个分片判断？
q_en: What sharding judgment do these database numbers constrain?
text: 这组锚点的用途是判断单机边界：8k TPS 或 8TB 这类规模先 {{保留单实例加副本}}；只有持续逼近写入、读吞吐或存储上限时才 {{分片}}。
why: 读 50k TPS、写 10-20k TPS、存储 64TiB+ 是容量规划输入，不是孤立速记。它们帮你先排除过早分片，再把注意力放到真正逼近的上限。
why_en: These database numbers are planning inputs: they help you avoid premature sharding and focus on the limit you are actually approaching.

termDefinitions.meaning: Transactions per second，数据库每秒处理的事务数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS is the number of transactions a database completes each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二进制计量的存储单位，1 TiB 约等于 1.1 TB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TiB is a binary storage unit, about 1.1 times a decimal terabyte.

scenario: 一个后台任务系统给数据库直接开了 3k 个短连接，没用连接池；候选人在判断这样是否安全。
scenario_en: A background-job system opens 3k short database connections directly without pooling, and the candidate is judging whether that is safe.
q: 这组并发连接量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision does this concurrent-connection number support?
options: 单实例能扛 5k-20k 连接，3k 安全但该上连接池
数据库最多只能扛约 100 个连接，3k 早就超了
并发连接数没有上限，不用管理
连接数和数据库实例类型无关
why: 单实例数据库约支持 5k-20k 并发连接，3k 在安全范围内；连接数常成为运维约束，这也是用连接池的原因。
why_en: A single database instance supports roughly 5,000 to 20,000 concurrent connections, so 3k is safe but still worth pooling.
options_en: A single instance handles 5k-20k connections; 3k is safe but should use pooling.
A database can only handle about 100 connections; 3k is already way over.
Concurrent connections have no ceiling, so no need to manage them.
Connection capacity has nothing to do with instance type.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复用一批数据库连接，避免每次请求都新建连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool reuses a set of database connections instead of opening a new one per request.

optionExplanations: 对，3k 落在单实例 5k-20k 的安全范围，但没连接池还是浪费资源。
错，100 是很旧的经验值，现代单实例常能扛到 5k 以上。
错，连接数是有硬上限的，撞上限后新连接会直接被拒绝。
错，实例规格决定了它能维持多少并发连接，两者密切相关。
optionExplanations_en: Right, 3k sits inside a single instance's 5k-20k safe range, but skipping pooling still wastes resources.
Wrong, 100 is a very old reference; a modern single instance commonly handles well above 5k.
Wrong, connection count has a real hard ceiling, and new connections get rejected once you hit it.
Wrong, instance size determines how many concurrent connections it can sustain, the two are closely linked.

scenario: 一个订单事件系统平均消息体约 5KB，要求保留 3 个月历史用于回放和审计。
scenario_en: An order-event system has messages around 5KB and must retain three months of history for replay and audit.
q: 这组消息大小与保留量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design decision do these message size and retention numbers support?
options: 消息队列一般只能处理小于 1KB 的小消息
队列能高效处理 1KB-10MB，保留数月可行
队列一旦重启数据就会全部丢失，存不了 3 个月
消息大小和保留时长完全互相无关，可以随便设置
why: 队列可高效处理 1KB-10MB 消息，单 broker 存储达 50TB，保留数周至数月；5KB、3 个月都在能力内。
why_en: Modern queues efficiently handle 1KB-10MB messages and retain data for weeks to months, so a 5KB message kept for three months fits easily.
options_en: Message queues typically handle only messages smaller than 1KB.
Queues efficiently handle 1KB-10MB messages, so months of retention works fine.
Once the queue restarts, all data is lost, so three months of retention is impossible.
Message size and retention length are totally unrelated, so set them however you like.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 集群里负责存储和转发消息的单个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broker is a single node in a Kafka cluster that stores and forwards messages.

optionExplanations: 错，<1KB 太窄了，现代队列常规就能处理到 10MB 级的消息。
对，5KB 消息、3 个月保留都在队列的能力范围内，直接可行。
错，持久化正是队列的设计目标，重启不会清空已落盘的数据。
错，消息越大、保留越久，占用的存储自然越多，两者是相关的。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, under 1KB is far too narrow; modern queues routinely handle messages up to 10MB.
Right, a 5KB message with three months of retention both sit comfortably inside a queue's capability.
Wrong, durability is exactly what queues are built for, a restart doesn't wipe data already written to disk.
Wrong, bigger messages and longer retention both directly increase the storage footprint, the two are related.

scenario: 面试里有人纠结「用 2015/2020 年的硬件约束」做扩展估算，动不动就说数据库要在 100GB 拆分。
scenario_en: In an interview, someone keeps using 2015 or 2020 hardware limits and says databases should be split around 100GB.
q: 更专业的做法是？
q_en: What is the more professional approach?
options: 沿用 2015 年的旧数字，宁可保守
完全不做任何容量估算
用现代硬件量级估算，避免过度设计
只相信教科书上的数字
why: 用过时硬件数字是「有书本知识但缺实战」的典型信号，会导致过度设计；应以当下量级（单机 TB 级）做决策。
why_en: Use modern hardware numbers, since quoting outdated constraints signals book knowledge without real experience and leads to over-engineering.
whenOtherWins: 这些是「调优良好系统的典型值」，是容量规划的起点而非硬上限——具体随工作负载、硬件、配置而变。
tradeoff: 现代硬件量级估算 vs 过时教科书约束
options_en: Stick with 2015-era numbers to stay conservative.
Skip capacity estimation entirely.
Estimate using modern hardware scale to avoid over-engineering.
Trust only the numbers printed in textbooks.
optionExplanations: 错，「宁可保守」听着安全，实际会导致按早已过时的上限过度设计。
错，完全不估算会让分片、扩容这些决策失去任何依据。
对，用当下硬件的真实量级估算，才能避免为过时限制过度设计。
错，教科书数字更新慢，照搬容易和现在的硬件能力脱节。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong, 'staying conservative' sounds safe but actually leads to over-designing around limits that no longer apply.
Wrong, skipping estimation entirely leaves sharding and scaling decisions with no grounding at all.
Right, estimating from today's real hardware numbers is what actually avoids over-engineering.
Wrong, textbook numbers update slowly, so leaning on them drifts away from what current hardware can do.

q: 把「面对看似很高的写吞吐，是否加队列」的判断顺序排好：
q_en: Put the steps for deciding whether high-looking write throughput needs a queue in order:
steps: 先量化实际写吞吐与写模式（简单插入还是复杂事务）
对照单机能力：简单写单机 Postgres 约 20k+ WPS
若在能力内，先做批量写/索引优化/连接池等简单手段
只有真正超出单机能力或需要可靠投递/解耦时，才引入队列
why: 顺序：量化写模式 → 对照 20k+ WPS 单机上限 → 先上简单优化 → 真超了或有可靠投递/解耦需求才加队列。避免为 5k WPS 过度设计。
why_en: Quantify the write pattern, compare to the 20k+ WPS single-node limit, try simple tuning first, and only add a queue if truly exceeded.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Measure["Measure writes"] --> Compare["Compare 20k+ WPS"]
    Compare --> Simple["Optimize first"]
    Simple --> Queue["Queue only if needed"]
tradeoff: 先算术验证单机上限 vs 直接假设需要队列

termDefinitions.meaning: Writes per second，数据库每秒成功处理的写入次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WPS is the number of write operations a database completes each second.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 面试估算时，你要把关系型数据库、Redis、Kafka 和分区型 NoSQL 的单节点/单分区吞吐粗略对齐。所有数字都是小 payload、同区网络、调优良好时的数量级，不是 SLA。
scenario_en: In an interview estimate, you need rough throughput anchors for relational DBs, Redis, Kafka, and partitioned NoSQL. These are ballparks for small payloads, same-region networking, and tuned systems, not SLAs.
q: 补全常见系统吞吐锚点：
q_en: Fill in common system throughput anchors:
text: 第一轮估算：RDBMS 读约 {{10k-50k TPS}}、写约 {{10k-20k TPS}}；Redis 简单命令读写约 {{100k-200k+ ops/s}}；Kafka 单 broker 小消息批量摄入约 {{0.3M-1M msg/s}}；NoSQL 总吞吐靠 {{分区}} 扩展，先防热分区。
why: 读写不完全对称：关系型单主写通常低于读；Redis 简单命令读写同量级；Kafka 看消息大小、batch、partition 和 broker。
why_en: Read and write ceilings are not identical: relational single-primary writes are lower than reads, Redis simple commands are similar order, and Kafka depends on message size, batching, partitions, and brokers.
whenOtherWins: 复杂事务、二级索引、Lua/ZSET、大 value、强一致读、跨区复制、acks=all、小 batch 都会把实际吞吐打下来；容量规划要压测并留 2-5x 峰值余量。
tradeoff: 面试估算锚点 vs 真实压测结果
codeSample:
# first-pass interview math, then add headroom
redis_instances = ceil(peak_cache_ops / 100_000)
sql_write_shards = ceil(peak_db_writes / 10_000)
kafka_brokers = ceil(peak_messages / 300_000)

# Then ask: payload size? transactions? indexes? hot keys? replication? batch size?

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒操作数；Redis 里一次 GET、SET、INCR 都算一次操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Operations per second; in Redis, one GET, SET, or INCR counts as one operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒事务数；关系型数据库里一次事务可能包含多条 SQL 和多个索引更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transactions per second; in a relational DB, one transaction may include multiple SQL statements and index updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒消息数；Kafka 吞吐受消息大小、batch、acks、partition 和 broker 数影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Messages per second; Kafka throughput depends on message size, batching, acknowledgments, partitions, and brokers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量读写集中到同一个分区，导致整体可扩展但单点先满。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot partition receives disproportionate traffic, so one partition saturates before the whole system does.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 面试里估算数据库、搜索和消息队列的吞吐，不只问「这个系统能扛多少」，还要先说清楚扩展单位：broker、partition、node、shard、physical partition 各是什么意思。
scenario_en: In an interview, throughput estimates for databases, search, and queues must name the scaling unit first: broker, partition, node, shard, or physical partition.
q: 补全常见存储/队列的扩展单位：
q_en: Fill in common storage and queue scaling units:
text: Kafka 的 {{partition}} 是有序日志和并行度单位，{{broker}} 是承载很多 partition 的服务器；DynamoDB 单物理 partition 约 {{3k RCU / 1k WCU}}；CockroachDB 看 {{range / replica}}；ClickHouse 看 {{shard / part}}。
why: 先说扩展单位再说数字：Kafka 看 partition/broker；DynamoDB 看物理分区；CockroachDB 看 range/Raft；ClickHouse 看 shard/part/merge。
why_en: Name the scaling unit before the number: Kafka uses partition/broker, DynamoDB uses physical partitions, CockroachDB uses ranges and Raft replicas, and ClickHouse uses shards, parts, and background merges.
whenOtherWins: 真实容量必须压测。下面数字只适合小 payload、简单读写、同区网络的第一轮估算；强一致、跨区复制、二级索引、大文档、复杂查询都会降低吞吐。
tradeoff: 扩展单位先行 vs 只背系统名数字
diagram:
flowchart LR
    K["Kafka topic"] --> P["partitions"]
    D["DynamoDB table"] --> PP["physical partitions"]
    CR["CockroachDB table/index"] --> R["ranges + replicas"]
    CH["ClickHouse table"] --> PT["parts on shards"]
    E["Elasticsearch index"] --> S["primary shards"]
codeSample:
# Scaling math should name the unit first
kafka_partitions = ceil(peak_messages / 20_000)
kafka_brokers = ceil(peak_messages / 300_000)

dynamo_partitions = ceil(max(peak_rcu / 3_000, peak_wcu / 1_000))

cockroach_ranges = ceil(table_size_mib / 512)      # ranges split as data grows
clickhouse_batches = ceil(rows_per_second / 50_000) # prefer large batched inserts
elastic_shards = ceil(total_index_size_gb / 30)

termDefinitions.meaning: topic 下面的一条有序日志；同一 consumer group 内，一个 partition 同时只能由一个普通 consumer 处理，所以它限制单 key 顺序和消费并行度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka partition is an ordered log inside a topic; in a normal consumer group, one partition is assigned to one consumer at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 集群里的服务器，负责存储和复制很多 partition；broker 吞吐是它承载的 partition 吞吐之和。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka broker is a server that stores and replicates many partitions; broker throughput is the aggregate of its partitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 内部的物理分区；官方设计目标是每分区约 3,000 RCU 或 1,000 WCU，表会自动拆分但热 key 仍可能卡住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DynamoDB physical partition is an internal partition with about 3,000 RCU or 1,000 WCU of designed capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引的物理分片；Elastic 建议常见 shard 大小约 10-50GB，过多小 shard 会拖垮集群。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elasticsearch shard is a physical piece of an index; Elastic commonly recommends roughly 10-50GB shard sizes.

termDefinitions.meaning: CockroachDB 把有序 KV keyspace 切成连续 range；range 会随数据增长自动 split，并复制到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CockroachDB range is a contiguous chunk of the sorted KV keyspace that splits as data grows and is replicated across nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: ClickHouse 每次插入会创建 table part，后台再 merge；小批量太多会制造 too many parts 和 merge 压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ClickHouse part is a table fragment created by inserts and merged in the background; too many small inserts create too many parts and merge pressure.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流
shard key 选错导致 scatter query
too many parts、merge backlog、分区键过细

q: Sharding 的核心定义是什么？
q_en: What is the core definition of sharding?
options: 把一个表拆成多个逻辑分区，但仍放在同一台数据库机器上
把数据水平拆分到多台独立数据库机器上，每个 shard 持有一部分数据
只把冷数据迁移到对象存储
给单个数据库实例加更多 CPU 和内存
options_en: Split one table into logical partitions but keep it on the same database machine.
Horizontally split data across multiple independent database machines, where each shard holds part of the data.
Just move cold data off to object storage.
Add more CPU and memory to a single database instance.
why: Sharding 在系统设计里通常指数据层/数据库/存储的水平分片：同一张逻辑表按 shard key 分到多台 DB 节点。服务层也会横向扩容，但通常叫 replicas/load balancing，不叫数据库 sharding。
why_en: In system-design interviews, sharding usually means horizontally splitting data across database or storage nodes. Service instances can also scale horizontally, but that is usually called replicas or load balancing, not database sharding.
optionExplanations: 把数据放在单机而不是多台机器上，这是 partitioning 的定义而非 sharding。
这正是 sharding 的核心定义，把数据跨多台机器分散。
这是数据归档而不是分片，不涉及跨机器分布。
这只是垂直扩展，无法扩展到多台机器的吞吐和存储。
optionExplanations_en: Putting data on one machine in partitions is partitioning, not sharding.
This is the core definition of sharding: distributing data across multiple independent machines.
Cold data archival is data management, not distribution across machines.
Vertical scaling with more CPU or memory cannot distribute throughput and storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据水平拆分到多台独立数据库机器上，每个 shard 持有一部分数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding horizontally splits data across multiple independent database machines, each holding a subset of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 部署多个服务实例，由负载均衡器分发请求；它分摊计算请求，但不一定拥有互斥的数据分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Service horizontal scaling runs multiple service instances behind a load balancer; it spreads compute requests but does not necessarily split owned data.

q: Partitioning 和 Sharding 在最关键维度上的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between partitioning and sharding?
options: Partitioning 一定跨机器，Sharding 一定在单机内
Partitioning 通常是在单个数据库实例内拆数据；Sharding 是把数据拆到多台机器
Partitioning 只能拆列，Sharding 只能拆索引
两者没有任何语义差异，永远完全等价
options_en: Partitioning always spans machines and sharding always stays inside one machine.
Partitioning usually splits data inside a single database instance; sharding splits data across multiple machines.
Partitioning can only split columns and sharding can only split indexes.
The two terms have no semantic difference and are always exactly equivalent.
why: 工程实践里两词常被混用，但技术上 partitioning 更常指单实例内分区，sharding 强调跨机器分布。面试里要说明数据到底在一台机器还是多台机器。
why_en: Partitioning usually means splitting data inside one database instance, while sharding means splitting it across multiple machines.
tradeoff: partitioning（单机内组织数据，不加机器）vs sharding（跨机器分布数据，换来更多容量和吞吐）
optionExplanations: 说反了：这描述的是单机内切分，不是 sharding。
判断标准很简单：只要数据跨过不止一台服务器，就该叫 sharding。
拆列和拆索引是两回事，单机切分既能按行也能按列。
口语上常混用，但面试官仍期待你说清楚数据落在几台机器上。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards — that description is splitting inside one machine, not sharding.
Simple test: if the data spans more than one server, call it sharding.
Splitting columns and splitting indexes are different things; single-machine splitting can go either way.
The words get used loosely in practice, but interviewers still expect you to name how many machines the data spans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据水平拆分到多台独立数据库机器上，每个 shard 持有一部分数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding horizontally splits data across multiple independent database machines, each holding a subset of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个数据库实例内部把大表拆成更小的逻辑分区，不增加机器数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioning splits a large table into smaller logical pieces inside a single database instance without adding machines.

q: 关于单机内 partitioning，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about single-machine partitioning are correct? (Select all that apply.)
options: Horizontal partitioning 按行拆，例如按年份拆 orders
Vertical partitioning 按列拆，例如把大字段或冷字段拆到另一张表
Partitioning 本身不会增加数据库机器数量
Partitioning 一定能把写吞吐扩展到多台机器
options_en: Horizontal partitioning splits rows, for example partitioning orders by year.
Vertical partitioning splits columns, for example moving large or cold columns into another table.
Partitioning by itself does not add more database machines.
Partitioning always scales write throughput across multiple machines.
why: 单机内 partitioning 的关键词是「同一台数据库实例」。Horizontal 按行拆，vertical 按列拆；它能减少扫描和维护范围，但不会把写吞吐扩展到多台机器。
why_en: Single-machine partitioning stays inside one database instance. Horizontal partitioning splits rows and vertical partitioning splits columns; it can reduce scan and maintenance scope, but it does not add machines or scale writes across machines.
whenOtherWins: 同一字段可以参与多层 key，但职责不同；高写入系统不要把单调递增的 created_at 同时当 shard key 和 partition key。
codeSample:
# 三个 key 可以不同，各管一层
# shard key: 选哪台数据库机器
# partition key: 选这台机器里的哪个粗粒度分区
# sort/index key: 在分区内快速定位和排序

def route_order(order):
    shard_id = hash(order.user_id) % NUM_SHARDS       # DB machine
    partition = month(order.created_at)               # orders_2026_06
    index_key = (order.user_id, -order.created_at)     # newest first
    insert(shard_id, f"orders_{partition}", order, index_key)

# partition 只把 10 年数据缩小到 1 个月；这个月里仍可能有千万行
# index/sort key 再在 6 月分区内快速找到 user 42，并按 created_at 倒序读
query(user_id=42, month="2026-06", order_by="created_at DESC")
optionExplanations: 正确，水平分片就是按行分组，按条件（如年份）拆表。
正确，垂直分片就是把不同列拆到不同表或存储。
正确，单实例 partitioning 只改善数据组织，不增加机器数。
错误，单机分区不能把写吞吐扩展到多机器，那需要 sharding。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; horizontal partitioning splits rows by condition, for example by year.
Correct; vertical partitioning splits columns into separate tables or storage.
Correct; partitioning within one instance does not add database machines.
Incorrect; partitioning alone cannot scale write throughput to multiple machines; that requires sharding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个数据库实例内部把大表拆成更小的逻辑分区，不增加机器数量；它是分桶，不等于把行都排好序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioning splits a large table into smaller logical pieces inside a single database instance without adding machines; it is bucketing, not automatically sorting every row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行落入哪个分区的字段或表达式；它是存储/路由规则，不是 foreign key，也不是 secondary index。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition key is the field or expression that decides which partition a row lands in; it is a storage/routing rule, not a foreign key or secondary index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定同一分组或索引内记录的读取顺序；它不负责选机器，常见例子是 created_at DESC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sort key controls the order of records within a group or index; it does not choose the machine, and a common example is created_at DESC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区内部的快速查找结构；partition 先缩小到一个大桶，index 再在桶里精确定位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a fast lookup structure inside a partition; partitioning narrows to a large bucket, then the index locates rows inside it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按行拆分表，每个分区行数更少但列相同，例如按年份拆 orders。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal partitioning splits a table by rows, so each partition has fewer rows but the same columns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列拆分表，把大字段或冷字段挪到另一张表，行数不变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical partitioning splits a table by columns, moving large or rarely used columns into a separate table.

scenario: 一个 orders 表有 500M 行、2TB 数据，查询上月订单经常扫描大量历史数据，但单机 CPU/存储/写入还没有到上限。
scenario_en: An orders table has 500M rows and 2TB of data. Last-month queries scan a lot of history, but single-node CPU, storage, and write capacity are not yet maxed out.
q: 这个阶段优先考虑什么？
q_en: What should you prioritize at this stage?
options: 跳过分区，直接引入 64 个 shard 做水平扩展
先在单机内按时间做 partitioning，让查询只扫相关分区
删掉表上的所有索引来提升扫描速度
把全部历史订单迁移进 Redis 当主存储
options_en: Skip partitioning and jump straight to 64 shards for horizontal scaling.
First partition by time inside the single instance so queries only scan the relevant slice.
Delete every index on the table to speed up scans.
Move all historical orders into Redis as the primary store.
why: 如果瓶颈是大表扫描、索引/维护范围或历史数据清理，单机 partitioning 可能足够。它不会加机器，但能让数据库少扫、少维护、好清理。
why_en: If the bottleneck is large-table scans, index or maintenance scope, or historical-data cleanup, single-machine partitioning may be enough. It does not add machines, but it lets the database scan less, maintain less, and clean up data more easily.
whenOtherWins: 当单机存储、写吞吐或读吞吐已经接近上限，即使分区也不够时，才应进入 sharding 讨论。
tradeoff: partitioning（轻量，先解决扫描范围问题）vs sharding（更重，只有单机容量/吞吐真撑不住才值得）
optionExplanations: 64 台机器太重：瓶颈只是扫描范围，不是单机容量或吞吐。
对：按时间分区能让查询只扫相关时间段，先减轻单机扫描压力。
删索引只会让大表扫描更慢，方向反了。
Redis 是缓存，不是能顶替持久化订单历史的主存储。
optionExplanations_en: Sixty-four shards is overkill when the bottleneck is scan scope, not machine capacity.
Correct; time-based partitioning lets queries skip irrelevant periods, easing the single-machine scan load first.
Dropping indexes would make large-table scans slower, the wrong direction entirely.
Redis is a cache, not a durable primary store for the full order history.

q: 一个好的 shard key 通常需要满足哪些性质？（多选）
q_en: What properties does a good shard key usually need? (Select all that apply.)
options: 高基数，有很多不同取值
数据和流量分布尽量均匀
和主要查询模式对齐，使常见查询命中单个 shard
值越少越好，最好只有 true/false
options_en: High cardinality, with many distinct values
Data and traffic distribute evenly across shards
It matches primary query patterns, so common queries hit a single shard
The fewer values the better — ideally just true and false
why: Shard key 决定数据如何被分组。高基数、均匀分布、贴合查询模式能减少热点和跨 shard 查询。
why_en: A good shard key has high cardinality, balanced distribution, and matches the dominant query patterns.
optionExplanations: 正确，高基数意味着 key 有很多可能值，能打散数据。
正确，均匀分布能避免热点 shard 和数据倾斜。
正确，贴合查询模式的 shard key 能减少跨 shard 操作。
错误，基数太低反而会导致严重倾斜和热点。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; high cardinality means many distinct values, distributing data better.
Correct; balanced traffic distribution avoids hotspot shards and data skew.
Correct; a shard key aligned with query patterns reduces cross-shard operations.
Incorrect; low cardinality keys cause severe imbalance and hot spots.

q: 为什么用 boolean 字段 `is_premium` 做 shard key 很差？
q_en: Why is a boolean field like `is_premium` a poor shard key?
options: boolean 不能被数据库存储
只有两个取值，最多天然分成两个大组，且很容易严重倾斜
boolean 会让所有查询变成跨 shard
boolean 字段无法建立索引
options_en: Booleans can't be stored in a database.
It only has two values, so at most it splits into two groups, and one easily ends up far larger than the other.
A boolean shard key forces every query to become cross-shard.
Boolean fields can't be indexed.
why: `is_premium` 基数太低，只能把数据分成 premium 和 free 两堆；如果大多数用户是 free，一个 shard 会远大于另一个。
why_en: A boolean shard key has extremely low cardinality and tends to create only two imbalanced shards.
optionExplanations: 错误，boolean 可以被存储，问题出在它作为 shard key 的特性。
正确，boolean 基数只有 2，容易导致数据严重不平衡。
不准确，boolean shard key 会导致倾斜和热点，但不一定所有查询都跨 shard。
错误，boolean 字段完全可以建立索引。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; databases can store booleans; the issue is their low cardinality as shard keys.
Correct; a boolean has only two values, creating at most two imbalanced groups.
Not quite; a boolean key causes skew and imbalance, but not all queries necessarily fan out.
Incorrect; boolean fields can be indexed like any other column.

q: 按 country 分片时，如果 90% 用户都在美国，直接后果是什么？
q_en: If you shard by country and 90% of users are in the US, what is the direct consequence?
options: 所有 shard 一定完全均匀
美国 shard 变热点，其他相对空闲
查询会自动变成 O(1)
数据库不再需要索引
options_en: All shards will necessarily stay perfectly balanced.
The US shard becomes a hotspot while the others sit relatively idle.
Queries automatically become O(1).
The database no longer needs indexes.
why: Shard key 的取值频率如果高度倾斜，会把数据量和请求量压到少数 shard。分片数量多也救不了一个倾斜的 key。
why_en: A skewed shard key like country can overload the dominant value's shard while others remain underused.
optionExplanations: 错：country 高度倾斜时，均匀性直接被打破。
对：90% 用户集中在美国，等于把绝大部分数据和请求压到一个 shard 上。
错：倾斜的 key 只会让延迟变差，不会把查询降到常数时间。
错：分片内部仍然需要索引来加速本地查询。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; a highly skewed country field directly breaks shard balance.
Correct; ninety percent concentration in one region overloads that shard while others stay idle.
Incorrect; skewed keys make latency worse, not constant-time.
Incorrect; individual shards still need indexes for fast local queries.

scenario: 一个用户中心型应用，大多数请求都是“查某个用户资料”“查某个用户订单”“更新某个用户状态”。
scenario_en: In a user-centered app, most requests read a user profile, read a user's orders, or update that user's status.
q: 默认最合理的 shard key 是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable default shard key?
options: user_id
is_premium
created_at
country
options_en: user_id
is_premium
created_at
country
why: user_id 高基数，通常分布较均匀，而且最常见查询都天然按用户作用域访问，能命中单个 shard。
why_en: For user-scoped access patterns, user_id is a strong shard key because common queries stay on one shard.
whenOtherWins: 如果核心查询是按订单号独立查订单，order_id 可能更好；如果是严格按 tenant 访问，tenant_id 或 tenant range 也可能更贴合。
tradeoff: user_id（贴合用户作用域查询，分布均匀）vs order_id/tenant_id（当核心访问模式不是按用户时更贴合）
optionExplanations: 正确，user_id 高基数、分布均匀，最常见查询都按用户作用域，能命中单 shard。
错误，boolean 基数太低，会导致 premium/free 用户严重倾斜。
错误，按创建时间分片会让新用户写入都打到最新 shard，形成热点。
错误，地理分布可能高度倾斜（如 90% 在美国），且用户级查询需要跨国 fan-out。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; user_id has high cardinality, even distribution, and user-scoped queries hit one shard naturally.
Incorrect; boolean cardinality is too low, causing severe premium versus free user imbalance.
Incorrect; creation-time sharding puts all new user writes on the newest shard, creating a hotspot.
Incorrect; geographic distribution may be highly skewed, and per-user queries would need cross-country fan-out.

q: 按 `created_at` 对持续增长的写入表做 range sharding，最常见的问题是什么？
q_en: What is the common problem with range sharding a constantly growing write table by `created_at`?
options: 所有新写入都打到最新时间范围的 shard，形成写热点
所有历史 shard 都会被均匀写入
短时间内不能查询最近数据
时间字段不能用于排序
options_en: All new writes land on the shard for the newest time range, creating a write hotspot.
All historical shards get written to evenly.
You can't query recent data for a while.
Time fields can no longer be used for sorting.
why: 你的理解对：持续写入表里的 `created_at` 基本都是 now，所以 range router 会把新写入都送到最新时间范围的 shard。旧 shard 主要读历史，新 shard 扛全部写入，热点就出现了。
why_en: Because new rows have created_at close to now, a range router sends almost all inserts to the newest time-range shard. Older shards mostly serve historical reads, while the newest shard carries the write load.
whenOtherWins: 按时间 range sharding 适合历史归档、按时间范围扫描、冷数据分层；高写入主链路更常用 hash(user_id/order_id/tenant_id) 打散，或用 time bucket + hash 子分片。
codeSample:
Shard A: created_at < 2026-07-01
Shard B: 2026-07-01 <= created_at < 2026-07-08
Shard C: created_at >= 2026-07-08

INSERT order(created_at = now()) -> Shard C
INSERT order(created_at = now()) -> Shard C
INSERT order(created_at = now()) -> Shard C
# 新写入全挤到最新时间段，Shard C 变成写热点
optionExplanations: 正确，时间范围分片会让新数据都写到最新时间范围的 shard，导致写热点。
错误，历史 shard 往往只接收读流量，新 shard 会被写入压垮。
错误，可以立即查询最近数据，他们就在最新 shard 上。
错误，时间字段本身仍可用于排序。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; time-range sharding concentrates all new writes in the newest time-range shard.
Incorrect; older shards receive mostly reads while the newest shard is overwhelmed with writes.
Incorrect; you can query recent data immediately; it lives in the newest shard.
Incorrect; time fields can still be used for sorting just fine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 shard key 的连续值区间分配给不同 shard，例如 user_id 1–1M 到 shard 1。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range-based sharding assigns continuous ranges of the shard key's values to different shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 shard 承担的流量或数据量远高于其他 shard，成为整体系统的瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot spot is a shard that receives far more traffic or data than the others and becomes the system's overall bottleneck.

q: Range-based sharding 是怎么分配数据的？
q_en: How does range-based sharding assign data?
options: 对 shard key 取 hash 后再取模决定 shard
按连续的 key 值区间分配到不同 shard
先查目录服务，得到映射后才路由到 shard
每次写入随机挑一个 shard
options_en: Hash the shard key and take it modulo the shard count.
Assign continuous ranges of the key's values to different shards.
Look up a directory service to get the mapping before routing.
Pick a random shard for every write.
why: Range sharding 把连续 key 区间分给不同 shard，简单且保留范围查询能力；代价是访问模式一旦倾斜，流量会挤在少数 shard。
why_en: Range-based sharding assigns continuous key ranges to shards, which is simple and supports range scans.
codeSample:
Shard 1 -> user_id 1        - 1,000,000
Shard 2 -> user_id 1,000,001 - 2,000,000
Shard 3 -> user_id 2,000,001 - 3,000,000
# a range query like id 500K-600K only touches Shard 1
optionExplanations: 错，先 hash 再取模是 hash sharding 的做法。
对：这题描述的正是把连续区间分配给 shard 的做法。
错，先查目录服务才能定位数据是 directory sharding。
错，随机写入会让你彻底找不到数据在哪个 shard。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; hash-then-modulo is how hash sharding routes.
Correct; this describes assigning continuous ranges to shards.
Incorrect; looking up a directory first is the directory-based sharding approach.
Incorrect; random writes make it impossible to know which shard holds a given row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 shard key 的连续值区间分配给不同 shard，例如 user_id 1–1M 到 shard 1。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range-based sharding assigns continuous ranges of the shard key's values to different shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 做 hash 后再取模，把结果映射到某个 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and maps the result to a shard, typically via modulo.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一张查找表或目录服务记录每个 key 当前在哪个 shard 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table or service that records which shard each key currently lives on.

scenario: 一个 SaaS 多租户系统，每家公司用户只访问自己公司的数据，并且可以给每个 tenant 分配一段 ID 范围。
scenario_en: In a multi-tenant SaaS system, each company's users only access their own company's data, and each tenant can receive a dedicated ID range.
q: 哪种分片策略可能很合适？
q_en: Which sharding strategy may fit this case well?
options: Range-based sharding
每次请求随机选 shard
所有 tenant 都写一个 shard
只按 created_at 最新时间分片
options_en: Range-based sharding
Randomly pick a shard on every request
Write every tenant into one shard
Shard only by the newest created_at range
why: 你的直觉对：shard key 应该贴近 tenant/company_id。这里选 range-based 指的是分布策略：给每个 tenant 一段连续 ID 范围，再按这些范围路由到 shard。
why_en: The shard key should align with tenant or company identity; range-based here refers to the distribution strategy, where each tenant receives a continuous ID range that maps to a shard.
whenOtherWins: 如果 tenant 大小极不均匀、少数 tenant 特别热，或需要频繁迁移单个租户，directory-based 或 hash 方案更容易重平衡。
codeSample:
tenant A -> id range 1_000_000 - 1_999_999 -> Shard 1
tenant B -> id range 2_000_000 - 2_999_999 -> Shard 2

GET /tenants/B/users
# router sees tenant B / its ID range -> Shard 2

# 不是按 created_at 排序；是按 tenant 分配的连续 ID 段路由
tradeoff: range sharding（tenant 范围路由简单可预测）vs hash/directory sharding（tenant 大小差异悬殊或热租户迁移时更灵活）
optionExplanations: 正确，但要说清楚：company/tenant_id 是访问边界，range 是这些 ID 段到 shard 的映射方式。
错误，随机选择会破坏数据定位和任何可预测的分布。
错误，单一 shard 无法扩展，会导致严重热点。
错误，只按最新时间分片无法分隔多租户，也会导致新租户写热点。
optionExplanations_en: Correct, but be precise: company or tenant id is the access boundary, and range is how those id ranges map to shards.
Incorrect; random selection destroys data location and any predictable distribution.
Incorrect; a single shard cannot scale and creates severe hotspots.
Incorrect; time-only sharding cannot isolate tenants and creates new-tenant write hotspots.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 shard key 的连续值区间分配给不同 shard，例如 user_id 1–1M 到 shard 1。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range-based sharding assigns continuous ranges of the shard key's values to different shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来决定一条记录应该路由到哪个 shard 的字段；本题通常是 tenant_id/company_id 或其分配到的 ID 段。

q: Hash-based sharding 的基本路由方式是什么？
q_en: What is the basic routing rule for hash-based sharding?
options: shard key 取 hash 取模选 shard
按当前日期所在月份决定 shard
由用户手动指定 shard
数据库每次随机选一个 shard
options_en: Hash the shard key, then take it modulo the shard count.
Decide the shard from the current calendar month.
Let the user manually specify the shard.
Have the database pick a random shard every time.
why: Hash sharding 把 key 打散到 hash 空间，再映射到 shard。常见表达是 `hash(user_id) % N`。
why_en: Hash sharding hashes the shard key and maps the hash result to a shard, often using modulo.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Request key"] --> B["hash key"]
  B --> C["route to shard"]
  C --> D["read or write row"]
codeSample:
shard = hash(user_id) % 4

User 42  -> hash(42)  % 4 = 2   # Shard 2
User 99  -> hash(99)  % 4 = 3   # Shard 3
User 123 -> hash(123) % 4 = 1   # Shard 1
optionExplanations: 对：这是 hash sharding 的标准路由公式。
错，这是时间范围分片，不是 hash 分片。
错，手动选择不可靠且不可扩展。
错，随机决定会导致数据定位困难且增加路由开销。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; this is hash-based sharding's standard routing formula.
Incorrect; that is time-range sharding, not hash sharding.
Incorrect; manual selection is unreliable and does not scale.
Incorrect; random routing makes data location unpredictable and routing expensive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 做 hash 后再取模，把结果映射到某个 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and maps the result to a shard, typically via modulo.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取模运算，用除法余数决定映射到哪个桶；shard 数一变，几乎所有余数都会变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo is the remainder of division; when the divisor (shard count) changes, almost every key's remainder — and target shard — changes too.

错误，只用最新时间分片会导致写热点且无法均衡历史数据。

optionExplanations_en: Correct; hash-based sharding is the common default for distributing large numbers of keys evenly.
Incorrect; time-only range sharding creates write hotspots and leaves historical shards idle.
Incorrect; directory sharding is flexible but adds lookup latency and is usually not the default.

q: 简单 `hash(key) % N` 在从 4 个 shard 扩到 5 个 shard 时有什么问题？
q_en: What goes wrong with simple `hash(key) % N` when scaling from 4 shards to 5?
options: 几乎所有 key 的映射都可能改变，需要迁移大量数据
所有 key 都继续留在原 shard
只能新增空 shard，永远不迁移
会自动保证只迁移 1/N 数据
options_en: Almost every key's mapping can change, requiring large-scale data migration.
All keys stay on their original shard.
You can only add empty shards and never migrate anything.
It automatically guarantees only 1/N of the data moves.
why: N 改变会改变取模结果，大量 key 会重新映射到新 shard。扩容前必须有 resharding 计划。
why_en: Modulo-based hashing remaps many keys when the shard count changes, causing massive data movement.
optionExplanations: 正确，N 从 4 变到 5 后，取模结果改变，大量 key 会重新映射。
错误，取模改变后 key 的目标 shard 会改变，需要迁移。
错误，无法只新增 shard，之前数据仍需要重映射。
错误，简单模运算不能自动控制迁移量，一致性哈希才能做到。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; changing N from four to five alters the modulo result for most keys.
Incorrect; keys remapped to different shards require data migration.
Incorrect; you cannot just add new empty shards without remapping existing data.
Incorrect; simple modulo hashing does not automatically limit migration volume; consistent hashing does.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 做 hash 后再取模，把结果映射到某个 shard。

termDefinitions.meaning: 取模运算，用除法余数决定映射到哪个桶；shard 数一变，几乎所有余数都会变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo is the remainder of division; when the divisor (shard count) changes, almost every key's remainder — and target shard — changes too.

scenario: 你用 hash sharding，但希望新增或移除 shard 时只迁移一小部分数据。
scenario_en: You use hash sharding, but you want adding or removing a shard to move only a small fraction of the data.
q: 应该引入什么思想？
q_en: What idea should you introduce?
options: Consistent hashing
Boolean shard key
全表扫描
只写单库
options_en: Consistent hashing
A boolean shard key
A full table scan
Write to a single database only
why: 公式不是 `hash(key) % N`，而是 `h = H(key)` 后在 hash ring 上找顺时针第一个节点。新增节点只接走它前一个节点到自己之间的 key 范围。
why_en: The rule is not hash(key) % N. Compute h=H(key), then choose the first node clockwise on the hash ring. A new node only takes the key range between its predecessor and itself.
whenOtherWins: 节点集合固定且很小时，简单 modulo 更容易；节点会频繁增减时，一致性哈希更稳。
tradeoff: consistent hashing（扩缩容迁移少）vs modulo（实现简单但改 N 后大量重映射）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  K["H(key)=42"] --> A["clockwise"]
  A --> B["first node >= 42"]
  B --> C["Shard B"]
optionExplanations: 对：环上只有相邻的一小段 key 会被重新分配，其余留在原地，这是它比简单取模稳的原因。
错，boolean shard key 基数太低，和扩容迁移量无关。
错，全表扫描是查询方式，不解决节点增减时的迁移问题。
错，单库没法扩容，也就没有'加节点减少迁移'这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; only a small neighboring slice of the ring gets reassigned, which is why it's steadier than plain modulo.
Incorrect; a boolean shard key's low cardinality is unrelated to migration volume during resizing.
Incorrect; a full table scan is a query pattern, not a fix for node-change migration.
Incorrect; a single database can't be resized, so there's no 'add a node, migrate less' problem to solve.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps nodes and keys onto the same hash ring, so adding or removing a node only remaps a small neighboring range.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一台物理节点放到 hash ring 的多个位置，让数据分布更均匀。

q: Directory-based sharding 的核心机制是什么？

只能按时间范围切分，没有其他方式
完全不需要任何路由层来定位数据
options_en: Compute the shard directly with a fixed formula such as hash-and-modulo.
Look up a mapping table that records which shard each key currently lives on.
It can only split data by time ranges.
It needs no routing layer at all to locate data.
why: Directory sharding 不用公式，而是查一张映射表来定位某个 key 当前在哪个 shard；最大优点是灵活，可以单独搬迁任意一条记录。

user_to_shard
-------------
15  -> shard-1
87  -> shard-4
204 -> shard-2
# every request queries this table before routing

对：先查映射表，再决定去哪个 shard，这就是 directory 的核心机制。
错，只按值区间切分是 range sharding 的特征；directory 用的是显式映射。
错，directory 恰恰需要一层路由/查找服务，否则没人知道数据在哪。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; routing by a fixed formula is how hash or range sharding works, not directory sharding.
Correct; looking up the mapping table first, then routing, is directory sharding's core mechanism.
Incorrect; splitting only by value ranges is range sharding's trait; directory sharding uses an explicit map.
Incorrect; directory sharding specifically needs a routing or lookup layer, or nobody knows where data lives.

q: Directory-based sharding 相比 hash/range 的典型取舍是什么？（多选）
q_en: What are the typical tradeoffs of directory-based sharding compared with hash or range sharding? (Select all that apply.)
options: 更灵活，可以单独迁移热用户或复杂分配
每次请求多一次目录查找，增加延迟
目录服务变成关键依赖，故障会影响全系统路由
完全没有任何可用性风险
options_en: More flexible — it can migrate a single hot user or apply complex assignment logic.
Every request adds one extra directory lookup, increasing latency.
The directory service becomes a critical dependency; its failure breaks routing system-wide.
It carries no availability risk whatsoever.
why: Directory 的灵活性来自显式映射：可以把 user 42 单独指到 shard-9。但请求路径多了一步查目录；目录服务慢或挂了，即使数据 shard 正常也不知道该去哪。
why_en: Directory sharding is flexible because explicit mappings can route user 42 to shard-9. But the request path adds a directory lookup; if the directory is slow or down, healthy data shards still cannot be reached.
tradeoff: directory-based sharding（灵活迁移热 key，但多一次 lookup）vs hash/range sharding（无需查表，路由更快，但迁移不灵活）
codeSample:
# hash/range: 不查目录，直接算
shard = hash(user_id) % N
query(shard, user_id)

# directory: 先查映射，再访问 shard
shard = directory.get(user_id)   # extra lookup: Redis/DB/config service
query(shard, user_id)

# 好处：可以单独改一条映射，把热用户搬走
directory.set(celebrity_user_id, 'dedicated-shard-9')
optionExplanations: 正确，directory 记录显式映射，可以灵活单独迁移热 key。
正确，每次请求都要查目录，必然增加延迟。
正确，目录服务是系统关键路径上的单点依赖。
错误，目录服务故障或高延迟会直接影响系统可用性。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; explicit mappings make directory sharding flexible for migrating hot keys.
Correct; every request adds a directory lookup, increasing latency.
Correct; the directory service becomes a critical dependency in the request path.
Incorrect; the directory service is a critical dependency with real availability risks.

q: Sharding 里的 hot spot 指什么？

所有 shard 都完全均衡
某 shard 数据/流量远超其他，成为瓶颈
某个 shard 的数据永远不被访问

All shards are perfectly balanced.
One shard's data or traffic far exceeds the others and becomes the bottleneck.
One shard's data is never accessed.

正确，热点就是指某个 shard 超负荷，成为整体系统的瓶颈。
错误，这是冷数据或未使用的 shard，与热点问题反向。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; cache hit rate is not directly related to shard hotspot issues.
Incorrect; balanced shards are the opposite of hot spots.
Correct; a hot spot is an overloaded shard that becomes the overall system bottleneck.
Incorrect; unused shards are the opposite problem from hot spots.

q: Cross-shard operation 是什么？
q_en: What is a cross-shard operation?
options: 只在单机 partition 内扫描一个分区
一次请求只命中一个 shard
一次查询要跨多个 shard，还要在应用层合并结果
数据库启动时加载配置
options_en: It only scans one partition inside a single machine.
A single request only ever hits one shard.
A single query has to reach multiple shards and merge their results in the application layer.
It's the database loading its configuration at startup.
why: 跨 shard 操作要发多次网络请求、等待多个数据库响应并合并结果。它比单 shard 查询更慢、更复杂。
why_en: A cross-shard operation touches multiple shards and requires coordinating or aggregating their results.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Request"] --> B["Shard 1"]
  A --> C["Shard 2"]
  A --> D["Shard 3"]
  B --> E["Merge result"]
  C --> E
  D --> E
optionExplanations: 错误，这是单机 partition，不涉及多 shard。
错误，这是单 shard 操作的定义。
正确，跨 shard 操作需要发多次数据库请求并合并结果。
错误，这是数据库启动流程，与跨 shard 无关。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; that is within-instance partitioning, not cross-shard.
Incorrect; that is a single-shard operation.
Correct; a cross-shard operation touches multiple shards and requires coordinating results.
Incorrect; database startup configuration is unrelated to cross-shard operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次查询或写入需要访问多个 shard，并在应用层等待和聚合结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-shard operation touches more than one shard and requires the application to coordinate or merge their results.

q: 如果按 user_id 分片，哪类查询最可能只命中一个 shard？
q_en: If you shard by `user_id`, which query is most likely to hit only one shard?
options: 所有用户的总数精确实时统计
全站 top 10 最热帖子
获取 user 12345 的 profile
全站 trending 搜索词
options_en: An exact real-time total user count
The top 10 most popular posts site-wide
Fetch user 12345's profile
Site-wide trending search terms
why: 按 user_id 分片时，用户作用域查询可以直接路由到该用户 shard。全局聚合类查询通常要扫多个 shard。
why_en: With user_id sharding, a single user's profile lookup routes to one shard, while global aggregates span many shards.
tradeoff: 按 shard key 命中单 shard 的查询（快）vs 需要跨用户聚合的全局查询（要 fan-out 到多个 shard）
optionExplanations: 错误，用户总数需要从所有 shard 扫描和聚合。
错误，top 10 帖子可能来自各个用户 shard，需要跨 shard 查询。
正确，用户资料在该用户对应的 shard 上，单 shard 查询。
错误，trending 词汇需要从全站数据聚合。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; total user count requires scanning and aggregating all shards.
Incorrect; the top posts span multiple user shards, requiring cross-shard queries.
Correct; a single user's profile is on their shard, a simple single-shard lookup.
Incorrect; trending terms require aggregating data from all shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条记录被分到哪个 shard 的字段，例如 user_id。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key is the field, such as user_id, that determines which shard a record is routed to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求被同时发给所有或多个 shard，然后等待汇总结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one request is sent to all or many shards at once and their results are merged.

q: 按 user_id 分片后，要实时计算“全站 top 10 posts”为什么昂贵？
q_en: Why is real-time “global top 10 posts” expensive after sharding by `user_id`?
options: top 10 查询不会访问数据库
只需要查任意一个用户 shard
需要查询所有或许多 shard，等待响应后再合并排序
hash sharding 会自动预计算 top 10
options_en: A top-ten query never touches the database.
It only needs to query any single user's shard.
It requires querying all or most shards, then waiting on responses and merging + sorting them.
Hash sharding automatically precomputes the top ten.
why: 全局 top 10 的数据散在所有用户 shard，直接查询会放大为 N 个 shard 请求，并把排序/聚合复杂度推到应用层。
why_en: A global top-ten query is expensive because candidates are spread across shards and must be merged.
optionExplanations: 错，算全站 top 10 本来就需要读数据库里的帖子和互动数据。
错，一个用户 shard 里的 top 10 只是这个用户圈子的结果，不是全站结果。
对：候选帖子分散在每个用户的 shard 上，要拿全站排名就得问遍所有 shard、再合并排序。
错，hash sharding 只负责分布数据，不会替你预计算聚合指标。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; computing the global top ten obviously requires reading post and engagement data from the database.
Incorrect; one user shard's top ten is only that user's circle, not the site-wide result.
Correct; candidate posts are scattered across every user's shard, so a global ranking means querying all of them and merging.
Incorrect; hash sharding only distributes data — it does not precompute aggregate metrics for you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次查询或写入需要访问多个 shard，并在应用层等待和聚合结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-shard operation touches more than one shard and requires the application to coordinate or merge their results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 做 hash 后再取模，把结果映射到某个 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and maps the result to a shard, typically via modulo.

q: 降低常见跨 shard 查询成本的办法有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are ways to reduce the cost of common cross-shard queries? (Select all that apply.)
options: 缓存结果，例如 trending/top 10 缓存 5 分钟
预计算或用后台任务维护聚合结果
反范式化，把常一起读的数据放在同一 shard
每个用户请求都实时查询所有 shard
options_en: Cache the results, e.g. cache trending/top-10 for five minutes
Precompute results or maintain aggregates with a background job
Denormalize by keeping frequently co-read data on the same shard
Query all shards live for every single user request
why: 常见跨 shard 查询应尽量缓存、预计算或重塑数据模型。频繁 fan-out 到所有 shard 通常是设计需要重想的信号。
why_en: Common cross-shard queries should be cached, precomputed, or avoided through denormalization.
optionExplanations: 对：像 trending 这种能接受几分钟延迟的结果，缓存能挡掉后面几千次重复的全 shard 查询。
对：后台任务提前算好聚合结果，用户请求时直接读，不用现场 fan-out。
对：把常一起读的数据复制到同一个 shard，一次查询就能拿全，代价是多存一份、更新更复杂。
错：每个用户请求都现查所有 shard，正是要避免的高成本模式。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; for results like trending that tolerate a few minutes of staleness, caching blocks thousands of repeat all-shard queries.
Correct; a background job precomputes the aggregate ahead of time, so requests just read it instead of fanning out live.
Correct; copying frequently co-read data onto one shard makes it a single query, at the cost of extra storage and harder updates.
Incorrect; querying all shards live on every request is exactly the expensive pattern to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-shard operation touches more than one shard and requires the application to coordinate or merge their results.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization copies frequently co-read data onto the same shard so a query no longer needs to cross shards.

scenario: 全站 trending posts 允许几分钟延迟，但请求量很高，直接每次 fan-out 到 64 个 shard 很贵。
scenario_en: Global trending posts can be a few minutes stale, but read traffic is high and fanning out to 64 shards on every request is expensive.
q: 最合理的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable handling strategy?
options: 删除 trending 功能
每个请求实时查询所有 64 个 shard
缓存或后台预计算 trending 结果，定期刷新
把 shard key 改成 boolean
options_en: Remove the trending feature entirely.
Query all 64 shards live on every request.
Cache or precompute the trending results in the background and refresh them periodically.
Change the shard key to a boolean field.
why: Trending 内容通常不需要强实时，适合 eventual consistency。缓存/预计算能把昂贵 fan-out 从每个请求中移走。
why_en: Trending results tolerate slight staleness, so caching or precomputing avoids fan-out on every request.
whenOtherWins: 如果是低频管理员报表，偶尔慢查询所有 shard 可以接受；如果必须实时且高频，可能要重新设计数据管道。
tradeoff: 缓存/预计算 trending（容忍几分钟延迟，省掉重复 fan-out）vs 每次都现查所有 shard（强实时但成本很高）
optionExplanations: 错误，删除功能是逃避，而不是解决方案。
错误，每次 fan-out 到 64 个 shard 会大幅增加延迟和数据库压力。
正确，trending 内容通常允许几分钟延迟，缓存或预计算能避免每次 fan-out。
错误，boolean key 会导致倾斜，不能解决跨 shard 查询问题。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; deleting the feature is avoidance, not a design solution.
Incorrect; fanning out to sixty-four shards on every request causes significant latency.
Correct; trending tolerates slight staleness, so caching avoids expensive fan-out on every request.
Incorrect; boolean keys cause imbalance and do not solve cross-shard query problems.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means one request is sent to all or many shards at once and their results are merged.

q: 为什么 sharding 会让原本简单的数据库事务变复杂？
q_en: Why does sharding make formerly simple database transactions more complex?
options: 索引在分片后完全无法用于事务
分片后数据库彻底不再支持任何写入操作
相关数据分落不同 shard，单库事务盖不住
分片后所有查询都被迫变成只读模式
options_en: Indexes can never be used in transactions after sharding.
The database completely stops supporting any writes after sharding.
Related data may live on different shards, so a single-database transaction can't cover all of them.
Every query is forced to become read-only after sharding.
why: Sharding 常是因为单库容量或读写压力不够；事务复杂是副作用。单库事务只覆盖一个数据库实例，如果账户在 shard 1、交易记录在 shard 2，就要跨 DB 协调一致性。
why_en: Sharding is often introduced for capacity or read/write pressure; transaction complexity is a side effect. A single-database transaction covers one database instance, so related writes on different shards need coordination.
optionExplanations: 错误，索引在分片后的单 shard 内仍能正常用于事务。
错误，分片后仍然支持写入，只是写入可能跨多个 shard。
正确，sharding 后相关数据可能在不同数据库，需要跨 shard 协调。
错误，分片后查询仍可读写，只是可能需要跨 shard 协调。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; indexes still work normally within a single shard for transactions.
Incorrect; sharded databases still support writes, though they may span multiple shards.
Correct; sharding puts related data on independent databases, breaking single-database transactions.
Incorrect; sharding does not make queries read-only.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-shard operation touches more than one shard and requires the application to coordinate or merge their results.

q: Two-phase commit 在跨 shard 事务中的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff of two-phase commit for cross-shard transactions?
options: 不需要协调者
极快且没有故障模式
只能用于缓存，不能用于数据库
强一致但慢，协调者/shard 故障会卡住
options_en: It requires no coordinator.
Extremely fast with no failure modes at all.
It only works for caches, never for databases.
Strong consistency, but slow and fragile — a coordinator or shard failure can stall the whole process.
why: 2PC 解决的是跨多个 DB 的原子提交：要么所有 shard 都提交，要么都回滚。代价是多轮网络通信、锁等待，以及协调者或参与者故障时可能卡住。
why_en: Two-phase commit provides atomic commit across multiple databases: either every shard commits or all abort. The cost is extra network rounds, lock waiting, and blocking under coordinator or participant failures.
tradeoff: 2PC（强一致提交，但慢、协调者/参与者故障会卡住）vs 避免跨 shard 事务或用 saga（更快更有弹性，只拿 eventual consistency）
optionExplanations: 错，2PC 需要一个协调者来管理准备/提交流程。
错，2PC 本身不快，而且有明确的故障模式。
错，2PC 主要用于跨数据库的分布式事务，不是缓存。
对：2PC 提供强一致性，但有性能和可用性开销，故障会让流程卡住。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; two-phase commit requires a coordinator to run the prepare/commit flow.
Incorrect; two-phase commit is neither fast nor failure-free.
Incorrect; two-phase commit is for distributed database transactions, not caches.
Correct; two-phase commit provides strong consistency but has real performance and availability costs, and failures can stall it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PC（Two-Phase Commit，两阶段提交）：协调者先问所有参与者能否提交，全部 READY 才统一 COMMIT，否则统一 ROLLBACK。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator first asks every participant to prepare, then tells them all to commit or abort together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PC 里的决策者，负责收集 READY/失败投票，并广播最终 COMMIT 或 ROLLBACK。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coordinator is the 2PC decision maker that collects READY or failure votes and broadcasts the final COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

scenario: 你按 user_id 分片，常见操作需要更新用户资料、账户余额和该用户自己的交易历史。
scenario_en: You shard by `user_id`, and common operations update the user profile, account balance, and that same user's transaction history.
q: 最好的事务设计方向是什么？
q_en: What is the best direction for transaction design?
options: 只写缓存，不写数据库
故意把每个字段放到不同 shard
所有操作都用 2PC
同用户数据聚合到一个 shard
options_en: Write only to the cache, never to the database.
Deliberately spread every field across different shards.
Use two-phase commit for every operation.
Aggregate one user's data onto a single shard.
why: 避免跨 shard 事务是首选。把同一聚合边界的数据放在同一 shard，可以继续用普通单库事务，简单且可靠。
why_en: The best design keeps related user data on one shard so normal single-shard transactions still work.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务天然跨用户或跨 tenant，例如转账，就需要 saga、异步补偿或接受更复杂的一致性方案。
tradeoff: 同一用户数据聚合在一个 shard（保持普通单库事务，简单可靠）vs 拆到不同 shard（灵活分布，但事务要靠 2PC/saga）
optionExplanations: 错误，缓存不能替代数据库作为持久化。
错误，分散数据会导致强制需要跨 shard 事务。
错误，不是所有操作都需要 2PC，只有必要时才用。
正确，把用户相关数据聚合在同一 shard，可以用普通单库事务。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; caches cannot replace the database for durability.
Incorrect; scattering data forces unnecessary cross-shard transactions.
Incorrect; not all operations need two-phase commit; use it only when necessary.
Correct; keeping related user data on one shard lets you use normal single-shard transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PC（Two-Phase Commit，两阶段提交）：协调者先让所有参与者准备好，再统一提交或回滚的分布式事务协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator first asks every participant to prepare, then tells them all to commit or abort together.

q: 按正确顺序排列跨 shard 转账的 saga 补偿流程：
q_en: Put the saga compensation flow for a cross-shard transfer in the right order.
steps: 如果给 User B 加钱失败，执行补偿动作
从 User A 所在 shard 扣钱
把钱加到 User B 所在 shard
补偿动作把 User A 的扣款退回
why: Saga 把跨 shard 操作拆成独立步骤，并为已完成步骤准备补偿。它提供 eventual consistency，而不是 2PC 那种原子提交。
why_en: A saga coordinates cross-shard work through independent steps plus compensating actions on failure.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Debit shard"] --> B["Credit shard"]
  B --> C{"Failed?"}
  C -->|"no"| D["Commit outcome"]
  C -->|"yes"| E["Compensate debit"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一次跨 shard 操作拆成多个独立步骤，每一步都配一个失败时的补偿动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A saga breaks a cross-shard operation into independent steps, each paired with a compensating action that undoes it on failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PC（Two-Phase Commit，两阶段提交）：协调者先让所有参与者准备好，再统一提交或回滚的分布式事务协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator first asks every participant to prepare, then tells them all to commit or abort together.

scenario: 用户 follower_count 被反范式化到多个 shard 以加速 profile 读取，短时间内不同 shard 显示的计数可能不一致。
scenario_en: A user's `follower_count` is denormalized across several shards to speed up profile reads, so counts may disagree briefly across shards.
q: 这类场景通常可以接受什么一致性模型？
q_en: What consistency model is usually acceptable for this kind of scenario?
options: 所有读都锁住全站
每次读都必须 2PC
禁止缓存和反范式化
最终一致，异步收敛
options_en: Lock the entire site for every read
Every read must go through two-phase commit
Ban caching and denormalization entirely
Eventually consistent, converging asynchronously
why: 计数类展示通常允许几秒延迟，最终收敛即可。为了这类低风险数据强行做分布式事务，复杂度不值得。
why_en: Denormalized counters often tolerate eventual consistency because brief inconsistencies are acceptable.
whenOtherWins: 库存扣减、资金转账这类强正确性场景不能轻易接受短暂错误，需要更强事务或补偿设计。
tradeoff: eventual consistency（快、简单，短暂不一致）vs 强一致/2PC（每次读写都准确，但要跨 shard 协调，慢且脆弱）
optionExplanations: 错：全站锁会把所有并发读写都串行化，代价极大。
错：给每次读加 2PC，性能代价远超这类展示型数据值得的程度。
错：反范式化和缓存正是为了减少昂贵的跨 shard 查询，不该禁止。
对：几秒内不同 shard 数字略有出入没关系，后台任务最终会把它们收敛成同一个值。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; a site-wide lock serializes all concurrent reads and writes at a huge cost.
Incorrect; adding two-phase commit to every read costs far more than this display-only data is worth.
Incorrect; denormalization and caching exist precisely to cut expensive cross-shard queries, not to be banned.
Correct; a few seconds of disagreement between shards is fine, since a background job eventually converges them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短时间内不同副本/shard 数据不一致，但保证最终会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows replicas or shards to briefly disagree, as long as they are guaranteed to converge to the same value over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了减少跨 shard 查询，把常一起读的数据复制一份放到同一个 shard 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization copies frequently co-read data onto the same shard so a query no longer needs to cross shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PC（Two-Phase Commit，两阶段提交）：协调者先让所有参与者准备好，再统一提交或回滚的分布式事务协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit is a distributed transaction protocol where a coordinator first asks every participant to prepare, then tells them all to commit or abort together.

q: 现代数据库通常如何帮你处理 sharding？（多选）
q_en: How do modern databases usually help you handle sharding? (Select all that apply.)
options: 让你指定 partition key 或 shard key
自动处理路由、分裂/迁移或再平衡中的一部分
完全消除 shard key 选择带来的所有后果
在不同产品中使用完全相同的内部机制
options_en: Let you specify a partition key or shard key
Automatically handle part of the routing, splitting/migration, or rebalancing
Completely eliminate every consequence of your shard key choice
Use exactly the same internal mechanism across different products
why: Cassandra、DynamoDB、MongoDB、Vitess/Citus 等会帮你处理很多路由和再平衡细节，但 shard key 选择仍会决定热点和查询形状。
why_en: Modern databases automate routing and balancing work, but they do not remove the need to choose a good key.
optionExplanations: 正确，现代数据库通常要求你指定 partition/shard key。
正确，现代数据库自动处理很多分片细节，减少手动工作。
错误，即使自动处理，shard key 选择仍会影响热点和查询形状。
错误，不同数据库用不同内部机制，虽然对用户来说大致相似。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; modern databases let you specify a partition or shard key.
Correct; they automate routing, splitting, migration, and rebalancing work.
Incorrect; automation does not eliminate the impact of shard key choice.
Incorrect; different databases use different internal mechanisms under the hood.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 里等价于 shard key 的字段，决定一条数据落在哪个内部分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition key is DynamoDB's term for the shard key that determines which internal partition an item lands on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条记录被分到哪个 shard 的字段，例如 user_id。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The shard key is the field, such as user_id, that determines which shard a record is routed to.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流
shard key 选错导致 scatter query

scenario: 面试官追问 Cassandra、DynamoDB、MongoDB 这三款常见 NoSQL 数据库，是不是都靠同一套一致性哈希在背后自动分片。
scenario_en: An interviewer asks whether Cassandra, DynamoDB, and MongoDB all use the exact same consistent-hashing mechanism for automatic sharding.
q: 关于它们的 sharding 机制，哪种说法更准确？
q_en: Which statement about their sharding mechanisms is more accurate?
options: 它们都用完全相同的 classic ring 一致性哈希实现
它们都按 key 分布数据，但内部分片机制并不相同
它们都只能手工路由查询，没有自动分片
它们都不支持后续扩容
options_en: They all use exactly the same classic-ring consistent hashing implementation.
They all distribute data by key, but their internal sharding mechanisms differ.
They can only be routed manually and have no automatic sharding.
None of them support scaling up capacity later.
why: 三者都按 key 分布数据，但内部单位不同：Cassandra 看 token/vnode，DynamoDB 看内部 partition，MongoDB 看 chunk。别把它们都说成同一套一致性哈希。
why_en: All three distribute data by key, but the internal unit differs: Cassandra uses tokens/vnodes, DynamoDB uses internal partitions, and MongoDB uses chunks. Do not describe them as one identical consistent-hashing implementation.
tradeoff: 假设三者机制'都一样'（省事但会答错扩容细节）vs 认真区分它们的路由/再平衡机制（面试官追问时更站得住脚）
codeSample:
# same idea: choose a key; different internal units

# Cassandra
partition_key = user_id
token = Murmur3(partition_key)
node = token_ring.owner(token)      # vnode/token range owns it

# DynamoDB
pk = user_id
internal_partition = aws_hash(pk)   # AWS may split/merge hot or large partitions

# MongoDB
shard_key = user_id                 # range or hashed shard key
chunk = find_chunk(shard_key)
shard = chunk.owner                 # balancer can migrate chunks
optionExplanations: 误解——三者里只有 Cassandra 真正接近经典 hash ring，DynamoDB 和 MongoDB 各有自己的分片单位，不能一概而论。
对，说清楚了共性和差异：都按 key 路由，但 Cassandra 用 token、DynamoDB 用 partition、MongoDB 用 chunk，各自迁移和再平衡方式不同。
误解——这三款都提供自动分片和路由，不需要工程师自己写路由层。
误解——它们都支持在线扩容，只是各自触发拆分/再平衡的方式不同。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — only Cassandra really resembles a classic hash ring; DynamoDB and MongoDB track distribution through their own internal units instead.
Right — the shared idea is key-based routing, but each engine tracks distribution differently: token ranges in Cassandra, hash partitions in DynamoDB, and migratable chunks in MongoDB.
Wrong — all three provide automatic partition routing, so you never hand-write a routing layer for any of them.
Wrong — all three support online scaling, they just differ in what triggers a split or rebalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款开源分布式 NoSQL 数据库，用 partitioner 和虚拟节点做一致性哈希风格的分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is an open-source distributed NoSQL database that uses a partitioner and virtual nodes for consistent-hashing-style distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 数据库，按 partition key 自动分布和扩展数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed NoSQL database that automatically distributes and scales data by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款文档型数据库，按 range 或 hash 分片键把数据切成 chunk，由后台 balancer 迁移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document database that splits data into chunks by a range or hashed shard key, migrated by a background balancer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把节点和 key 映射到同一个 hash 环上，节点增减时只影响相邻的一小段范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps nodes and keys onto the same hash ring, so adding or removing a node only remaps a small neighboring range.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 用来把 key 映射到 token 环上的组件，例如 Murmur3Partitioner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partitioner is the Cassandra component that maps keys onto the token ring, such as Murmur3Partitioner.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 里 token 是 hash 空间位置；vnode 是一台物理节点拥有的多个 token 范围，用来平衡数据和迁移压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In Cassandra, a token is a position in hash space; a vnode is one of many token ranges owned by a physical node to balance data and movement.

termDefinitions.meaning: MongoDB sharding 的迁移单位，是一段 range 或 hashed shard key 范围；balancer 会把 chunk 在 shard 间搬迁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A MongoDB chunk is the unit of migration: a range of the range or hashed shard key that the balancer can move between shards.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流
