q: 关于 DynamoDB 的加密，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about DynamoDB's encryption is correct?
options: 需要手动开启静态加密
静态加密默认开启，TLS 强制传输。
只加密传输，不加密存储
加密需要额外付费开通
why: 静态加密和传输加密是两件事：数据写入持久存储前默认已加密；TLS 则保护到 DynamoDB API 路上的请求和响应。
why_en: Split it into two layers: encryption at rest is on by default before data reaches durable storage, and TLS protects requests and responses on the way to the DynamoDB API.
options_en: You must manually enable encryption at rest.
Encryption at rest is on by default and TLS is enforced in transit.
Only data in transit is encrypted, not data at rest.
Encryption requires an extra paid add-on.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTPS 底层的传输加密协议:在客户端和 DynamoDB API 之间建加密通道,防请求/响应在网络上被窃听或篡改
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS (Transport Layer Security) is the transport encryption under HTTPS: it builds an encrypted channel between the client and the DynamoDB API so requests/responses cannot be sniffed or tampered with in transit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 静态加密:数据落盘存储时被加密。DynamoDB 从建表起默认开、不能关、不额外收费,底层用信封加密+KMS。防的是「磁盘/备份被拿走」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encryption at rest: data is encrypted when stored on disk. DynamoDB has it on by default from table creation, cannot disable, no extra cost, using envelope encryption + KMS. Protects against stolen disks/backups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输加密:数据在网络上传输时被加密,靠 TLS。DynamoDB API 强制 HTTPS。防的是「网络路上被窃听/篡改」。和静态加密是两个阶段:一个存着时、一个传输时
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encryption in transit: data is encrypted while moving over the network, via TLS. The DynamoDB API is HTTPS-only. Protects against eavesdropping/tampering on the wire — a different stage from at-rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 信封加密(密钥分两层):①用一把「数据密钥(DEK)」加密真正的数据 ②再用「主密钥(在 KMS 里)」把这把数据密钥加密(=「装进信封」)③加密后的数据密钥跟数据存一起。好处:主密钥永不离开 KMS;轮换主密钥只需重新加密那些小小的数据密钥、不用重加密全部数据;数据密钥做大批量对称加密(快)、主密钥只封套
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Envelope encryption (two key layers): (1) a data key (DEK) encrypts the actual data; (2) a master key (in KMS) encrypts that data key ("wrapped in an envelope"); (3) the encrypted data key is stored with the data. Benefits: the master key never leaves KMS; rotating it only re-encrypts the small data keys, not all data; the data key does fast bulk symmetric encryption.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真正用来加密数据的那把密钥。它本身以「被主密钥加密后」的形态存着(信封加密);读数据时先用 KMS 里的主密钥把它解开,再用它解数据
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The data key (DEK) is the key that actually encrypts the data. It is stored in encrypted form (wrapped by the master key); to read, the master key in KMS unwraps it, then it decrypts the data.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  App["应用/服务"] -->|"TLS / HTTPS\n传输中加密"| API["DynamoDB API"]
  API -->|"服务端静态加密\n写入前加密"| Store["密文数据\n表 / 索引 / 备份"]
  KMS["KMS / wrapping key"] -->|"加密 data key"| DK["encrypted data key"]
  DK -.-> Store
scenario: 系统里存有用户的敏感信息。
scenario_en: The system stores sensitive user information.
optionExplanations: 静态加密其实从建表起就默认打开，不需要用户手动做任何配置。
落盘前默认做静态加密，加上 API 路上强制走 TLS，两层保护同时覆盖存储和传输。
这只说对了一半，静态加密同样是默认行为，不是只加密传输。
两层加密都不额外收费，是服务默认自带的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Encryption at rest is actually on by default from the moment the table is created -- no manual setup required.
Data is encrypted by default before it's written to storage, and TLS is enforced for every API call, covering both storage and transit.
This only gets half right -- encryption at rest is equally the default, not just transit.
Neither layer costs extra -- both come included with the service by default.

q: DynamoDB 提供哪些访问控制/网络安全手段？（多选）
q_en: Which access-control/network-security mechanisms does DynamoDB provide? (select all)
options: IAM 集成：细粒度策略控制谁能访问、能做什么操作
VPC endpoint：从 VPC 内安全访问，不暴露到公网
静态数据默认加密
内置用户名密码表
why: 访问控制走 IAM 策略，网络隔离走 VPC endpoint，存储安全靠默认加密；DynamoDB 没有自己的用户名密码体系。
why_en: Access control comes from IAM policies, network isolation from VPC endpoints, and storage safety from default encryption at rest.
options_en: IAM integration: fine-grained policies control who can access what and which actions they can perform.
VPC endpoints: access securely from within a VPC without exposing traffic to the public internet.
Data at rest is encrypted by default.
A built-in username/password table.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的身份与权限管理服务，用策略控制谁能访问哪些资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IAM is AWS's identity and access management service, controlling who can access which resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 内的隔离虚拟网络；VPC endpoint 让流量不经公网访问服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A VPC is an isolated virtual network in AWS, and a VPC endpoint reaches a service without crossing the public internet.

optionExplanations: 谁能访问、能做什么操作，全靠 IAM 策略挡住越权请求，而不是数据库自带的权限系统。
请求路径完全留在 AWS 内网，VPC endpoint 挡住了暴露到公网的风险，不用额外配防火墙规则。
静态数据默认加密兜底存储安全，不需要额外配置就能挡住裸盘泄露的风险。
身份认证统一交给 IAM，DynamoDB 本身不维护账号密码这类东西。
optionExplanations_en: Who can access what and do what is entirely gated by IAM policies, not a database-native permission system.
The request path stays entirely inside AWS's network -- a VPC endpoint blocks public-internet exposure with no extra firewall rules needed.
Default encryption at rest backstops storage security, blocking raw-disk leakage with no extra configuration.
Identity authentication is delegated entirely to IAM -- DynamoDB itself keeps no accounts or passwords.

scenario: 两个业务：A 流量高度不可预测、忽高忽低；B 流量稳定可预测、长期在线。分别选 DynamoDB 计费模式。
scenario_en: Two workloads: A has highly unpredictable, spiky traffic; B has steady, predictable, always-on traffic. Choose a DynamoDB billing mode for each.
q: 正确的搭配是？
q_en: What's the right pairing?
options: A 用 on-demand，B 用 provisioned。
都用 on-demand
A 用 provisioned；B 用 on-demand
都用 provisioned
why: on-demand 按请求计费，适合不可预测的负载；provisioned 预先指定 RCU/WCU 按小时计费，可预测负载下更省，但低谷期会有闲置容量。
why_en: On-demand per-request pricing suits unpredictable workloads while provisioned capacity is more cost-effective for predictable steady traffic.
whenOtherWins: 稳定负载硬用 on-demand 会明显更贵；波动负载用 provisioned 则要么限流要么大量闲置。
options_en: A uses on-demand, B uses provisioned capacity.
Both use on-demand.
A uses provisioned; B uses on-demand.
Both use provisioned capacity.
tradeoff: 按请求付费应对波动 vs 预置容量应对稳定负载

termDefinitions.meaning: 按实际请求量计费的容量模式，适合不可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-demand capacity bills per request, which suits unpredictable traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先指定读写容量单位、按小时计费的模式，适合稳定可预测流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Provisioned capacity bills hourly for pre-specified read and write units, which suits steady, predictable traffic.

optionExplanations: A 波动就按请求付费，避免为峰值预留浪费；B 稳定就用预置容量，按小时计费更省钱。
稳定负载 B 硬用 on-demand 会持续按请求单价付费，比预置容量明显更贵。
把两种负载和计费模式的搭配整个对调了，波动负载用 provisioned 要么限流要么闲置，两头都不划算。
波动负载 A 硬用 provisioned，遇到尖峰会限流、遇到低谷又浪费闲置容量。
optionExplanations_en: A is bursty, so pay-per-request avoids over-provisioning for peaks; B is steady, so hourly provisioned capacity is cheaper.
Forcing steady-load B onto on-demand keeps paying the per-request premium continuously, clearly costlier than provisioned.
This swaps the two workload-to-mode pairings entirely -- provisioned under bursty load throttles or sits idle either way.
Forcing bursty A onto provisioned capacity means throttling at peaks and wasted idle capacity in the quiet periods.

q: 补全容量单位的定义：
q_en: Fill in the definitions of the capacity units:
text: 1 个 RCU = 每秒读取最多 {{4KB}} 数据（强一致 1 次 / 最终一致 2 次）；1 个 WCU = 每秒写入最多 {{1KB}} 数据。
why: RCU 以 4KB 为读取单位、WCU 以 1KB 为写入单位；同一个 RCU 能换 2 次最终一致读，这是最终一致省一半钱的由来。
why_en: One read capacity unit covers four kilobytes per second and one write capacity unit covers one kilobyte per second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读容量单位：一个 RCU 每秒最多读 4KB（强一致 1 次或最终一致 2 次）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

scenario: 在预估某张表的读写成本之前，需要先搞清楚 RCU 和 WCU 各自的计量单位。
scenario_en: Before estimating a table's read/write cost, you first need to know what RCU and WCU each measure.

q: DynamoDB 底层会怎么应对这个写入需求？
q_en: How will DynamoDB handle this write load under the hood?
options: 自动把数据横向拆分到足够多的分区，让总吞吐超过单分区上限
让单个分区强撑全部吞吐，靠更快的磁盘顶住
必须手工申请分区扩容工单，AWS 才会拆分
自动把访问模式降级为最终一致读来省吞吐
why: 单分区上限约 3,000 RCU / 1,000 WCU；超过时 DynamoDB 靠 auto-sharding 自动拆分并重新分布数据，这是估算需要多少分区的依据。
why_en: A single partition caps out around three thousand RCUs and one thousand WCUs, so DynamoDB automatically splits data across more partitions once demand exceeds that limit.
scenario: 一张表预计需要持续 5,000 WCU 的写入吞吐（已知单分区写入上限约 1,000 WCU）。
scenario_en: A table needs to sustain 5,000 WCU of write throughput (given that a single partition caps out around 1,000 WCU).
options_en: Automatically split the data horizontally across enough partitions so total throughput exceeds the single-partition cap.
Let a single partition absorb all the throughput by relying on faster disks.
Require a manual capacity-expansion ticket before AWS will split the partition.
Automatically downgrade reads to eventual consistency to save throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读容量单位：一个 RCU 每秒最多读 4KB（强一致 1 次或最终一致 2 次）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Read Capacity Unit reads up to four kilobytes per second, once with strong consistency or twice with eventual consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写容量单位：一个 WCU 每秒最多写 1KB，不足 1KB 也按 1KB 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write Capacity Unit writes up to one kilobyte per second, rounded up to the nearest kilobyte.

optionExplanations: 单分区吞吐撞到约 1,000 WCU 的天花板后，系统会自动把数据横向拆到更多分区并重新分布，让总吞吐突破这个限制。
单分区的读写上限是固定的，不管磁盘多快都顶不住持续超限的吞吐。
全托管的意义就是消灭这种人工工单，拆分是自动完成的，不需要申请。
降级一致性等级不会改变写入吞吐上限，跟这个写入需求的问题完全不相关。
optionExplanations_en: Once a single partition's throughput hits its roughly 1,000 WCU ceiling, auto-sharding automatically splits and redistributes data, pushing total throughput past that per-partition limit.
A single partition's read/write ceiling is fixed -- no disk speed can sustain throughput past it indefinitely.
Being fully managed exists to eliminate this kind of manual ticket -- splitting happens automatically, no request needed.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis Data Firehose loads streaming data into S3, Redshift, or OpenSearch, but cannot read DynamoDB Streams directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 内置的 CDC 功能，把表变更记录成可消费的 stream record。

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的实时数据流服务，常作为 DynamoDB Streams 与 Firehose 之间的中间层。

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的无服务器函数计算服务，常被 Streams 事件触发执行。

Firehose can't read DynamoDB Streams directly -- it needs Kinesis Data Streams or a Lambda as a relay, a hop that's easy to leave off the diagram.
Manual export directly contradicts the real-time analytics goal -- Streams itself is already automatic.

q: 推荐的同步方案是？
q_en: What's the recommended way to keep them in sync?

每晚全量重建 ES 索引
让 ES 直接查询 DynamoDB
用 Streams 消费变更同步 ES。

whenOtherWins: 若搜索数据量极小且更新极少，定期批量重建索引反而简单，不必上流式管道。
options_en: Have the application double-write to both DynamoDB and Elasticsearch.
Rebuild the entire Elasticsearch index from scratch every night.
Let Elasticsearch query DynamoDB directly.
Consume Streams events to keep Elasticsearch in sync.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源全文搜索与分析引擎，常与 DynamoDB Streams 搭配做搜索索引同步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an open-source full-text search engine often kept in sync with DynamoDB via Streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 内置的 CDC 功能，把表变更记录成可消费的 stream record。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams is the built-in CDC feature that records table changes as consumable stream records.

optionExplanations: 双写引入了「两次写入部分失败」的经典一致性风险，还得自己写补偿逻辑。

Between rebuilds users search against stale data, and a full rebuild itself burns significant resources -- poor freshness.

q: 为什么在面试里 DynamoDB「几乎可以胜任任何持久层」？（多选）
q_en: Why is DynamoDB 'good for nearly any persistence layer' in an interview? (select all)
options: 高可扩展、高持久
支持 ACID 事务（含跨表）
单毫秒级延迟，配 DAX 可到微秒级
自带 DAX 缓存和 Streams，方便做低延迟读与异步派生视图/CDC
免费且无供应商锁定
why: 扩展、事务、低延迟、附带缓存与 CDC——这套组合覆盖很多持久层需求；但 DAX/Streams 分别是缓存和异步变更流，不提供跨存储强一致，且 DynamoDB 不免费、也深度绑定 AWS。
why_en: DynamoDB pairs high scalability and durability with transactions and single-digit-millisecond latency, though it is not free and still ties you to AWS.
options_en: Highly scalable and highly durable.
Supports ACID transactions, including across tables.
Single-digit-millisecond latency, down to microseconds with DAX.
Ships with DAX caching and Streams, making low-latency reads and async derived views or CDC easy.
Free and has no vendor lock-in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专给 DynamoDB 用的全托管「内存缓存」,挡在 DynamoDB 前面:命中的读从毫秒降到微秒级、还省 RCU。是「加速读」的缓存,不是变更流
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator) is a fully-managed in-memory cache in front of DynamoDB: cached reads drop from milliseconds to microseconds and save RCUs. It is a read cache, not a change stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 的 CDC:把每次 item 的增/改/删按顺序变成一串变更事件,供下游(Lambda/Kinesis)实时消费——用来做异步派生视图(更新搜索索引、维护聚合、复制、触发通知)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB Streams is CDC: every item insert/update/delete becomes an ordered stream of change events for downstream consumers (Lambda/Kinesis) to build async derived views (search index, aggregates, replication, notifications).

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 支持 ACID 事务(TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems):可对多个 item(含跨表)原子写入,要么全成要么全回滚。预订/下单可一步原子完成,不必自己写 saga 补偿。代价:2 倍容量、单事务最多 100 item
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB supports ACID transactions (TransactWriteItems/TransactGetItems): atomically write multiple items, even across tables, all-or-nothing. Booking/order flows become one atomic step with no manual saga. Cost: 2x capacity, up to 100 items per transaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获数据库的变更(增/改/删)并变成一串事件、供下游实时消费的机制——下游不用轮询,DB 把变更「推」出来。常用来把变更喂给 Elasticsearch 建索引、维护物化视图、复制数据。DynamoDB Streams、Debezium(读 MySQL/PG 的 binlog/WAL)都是 CDC
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC (Change Data Capture) captures a database inserts/updates/deletes as a stream of events for downstream real-time consumption — no polling; the DB pushes its changes. Often used to feed Elasticsearch, maintain materialized views, or replicate. DynamoDB Streams and Debezium (MySQL/PG binlog/WAL) are CDC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 别混:DAX=缓存,加速「读」(毫秒→微秒);Streams=CDC,把「写/变更」变成事件流给下游。一个管读得快、一个管变更传播,方向不同
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Do not confuse: DAX is a cache that speeds up reads (ms→μs); Streams is CDC that turns writes/changes into an event stream for downstream. One is read speed, the other is change propagation.

tradeoff: 全托管强能力 vs 成本与供应商锁定的代价
optionExplanations: 扩展和持久是几乎任何持久层都要的底线诉求，DynamoDB 天然满足，不用自己搭分片方案。
跨表原子写入让预订、下单这类场景不必自己实现补偿逻辑。
默认单毫秒级延迟已经很快，配 DAX 还能进一步压到微秒级，覆盖大部分低延迟诉求。
不用额外引入 Redis 做缓存，也不用自建 CDC 管道去同步搜索索引或做实时分析。
这把「功能强大」和「免费无锁定」混为一谈了，DynamoDB 是收费的托管服务，且深度绑定 AWS。
optionExplanations_en: Scalability and durability are baseline needs for almost any persistence layer, and DynamoDB meets them natively without hand-rolling sharding.
Atomic cross-table writes mean booking or checkout flows don't need their own compensation logic.
The default single-digit-millisecond latency is already fast, and DAX pushes it further down to microseconds, covering most low-latency needs.
No need to bring in Redis separately for caching or build a custom CDC pipeline to sync search indexes or feed real-time analytics.
This conflates 'feature-rich' with 'free and lock-in-free' -- DynamoDB is a paid managed service deeply tied to AWS.

q: 哪些情况会让你不选 DynamoDB？（多选）
q_en: Which situations should make you avoid DynamoDB? (select all)
options: 成本：每秒几十万写的高量负载下，按读写计费可能贵得离谱
复杂查询：需要 JOIN、ad-hoc 聚合等灵活查询能力
建模信号：发现自己频繁依赖大量 GSI/LSI——说明关系型（如 PostgreSQL）可能更合适
供应商锁定：面试官要求保持 vendor-neutral
需要毫秒级读延迟
why: 四大不选理由：成本、查询灵活性、建模约束（索引泛滥是换关系库的信号）、AWS 锁定。毫秒级延迟恰恰是它的强项，不是短板。
why_en: Avoid DynamoDB for cost-heavy write volumes, complex query needs, index-heavy modeling better served by Postgres, or when vendor neutrality is required.
options_en: Cost: at hundreds of thousands of writes per second, pay-per-request billing can get absurdly expensive.
Complex queries: the system needs joins or ad-hoc aggregation that flexible querying provides.
A modeling signal: leaning on a pile of GSIs and LSIs suggests a relational database like PostgreSQL may fit better.
Vendor lock-in: the interviewer wants a vendor-neutral, open-source choice.
Needing millisecond-level read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引：分区键与主表不同，独立物理分区，只支持最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Global Secondary Index has its own partition key and its own physical partitions, and it only supports eventually consistent reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Local Secondary Index shares the table's partition key but uses a different sort key, and is co-located with the base table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持 JOIN 和灵活查询，是 DynamoDB 建模复杂时的常见替代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database that supports joins and flexible queries, a common alternative when DynamoDB modeling gets too complex.

tradeoff: 键值建模的高效 vs 关系型查询的灵活
optionExplanations: 几十万写/秒的量级下，按请求计费可能高到不现实，这时候要重新算一笔账。
DynamoDB 支持跨表事务，但没有 SQL 式的灵活联表和即席聚合能力，复杂报表类查询会很吃力。
索引堆到七八个说明访问模式本质上是关系型的，硬撑不如直接换库。
有些面试官明确要求避免绑定单一云厂商，这时该考虑开源的替代方案。
这把它的强项当成了弱项——毫秒甚至微秒级（配 DAX）延迟恰恰是选它的理由，不是避开它的理由。
optionExplanations_en: At hundreds of thousands of writes per second, pay-per-request billing can get unrealistically expensive, worth re-running the numbers.
DynamoDB supports cross-table transactions but lacks SQL-style flexible joins and ad-hoc aggregation, so complex reporting queries get painful.
Piling on seven or eight indexes signals the access patterns are fundamentally relational -- better to switch databases than force it.
Some interviewers explicitly want to avoid single-vendor lock-in, which points toward open-source alternatives.
This turns a strength into a weakness -- millisecond, even microsecond with DAX, latency is a reason to pick it, not avoid it.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 设计过程中发现：为了支撑各种查询，一张 DynamoDB 表上已经挂了七八个 GSI 和多个 LSI。
scenario_en: While designing the system, you notice a DynamoDB table already carries seven or eight GSIs plus several LSIs to support various queries.
q: 这个信号说明什么？
q_en: What does this signal mean?
options: 设计很成功，索引越多越好
应该把所有查询改成 Scan
访问模式关系化，超出键值建模舒适区。
应该删掉所有索引
why: DynamoDB 要求围绕少数明确访问模式精心建模；索引堆到这个程度说明查询需求本质上是关系型的，硬撑不如换关系库。
why_en: Leaning heavily on many GSIs and LSIs signals relational access patterns that a database like PostgreSQL would serve better.
whenOtherWins: 若只是两三个清晰的次要访问模式，正常使用 GSI/LSI 完全合理，不必换库。
options_en: The design is a success -- more indexes are always better.
Every query should be switched to a Scan.
The access patterns are relational, past key-value modeling's comfort zone.
All the indexes should simply be deleted.
tradeoff: 硬撑键值建模的索引堆积 vs 换用关系库的灵活查询

termDefinitions.meaning: 全局二级索引：分区键与主表不同，独立物理分区，只支持最终一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Global Secondary Index has its own partition key and its own physical partitions, and it only supports eventually consistent reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地二级索引：分区键与主表相同、排序键不同，与主表同分区共存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Local Secondary Index shares the table's partition key but uses a different sort key, and is co-located with the base table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持 JOIN 和灵活查询，是 DynamoDB 建模复杂时的常见替代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database that supports joins and flexible queries, a common alternative when DynamoDB modeling gets too complex.

optionExplanations: 索引越多通常意味着写入时要多付好几倍的维护开销、运维和账单一起被拖累，不是越多越好。
把所有查询都换成 Scan 会让每次查询代价随表增长线性上升，是明显的反模式，跟索引堆积的问题无关。
索引堆到七八个说明查询需求本质上已经关系化了，超出了键值建模能舒服覆盖的范围，这时候该考虑换关系库而不是硬撑。

optionExplanations_en: More indexes usually means paying several times the write-time maintenance overhead, dragging down operations and cost -- not simply better.
Switching every query to a Scan makes each query's cost grow linearly with the table, a clear anti-pattern unrelated to the actual index-pileup problem.

Piling up to seven or eight indexes means the query needs have effectively gone relational, past what key-value modeling can comfortably cover -- time to consider a relational database instead of forcing it.

q: 把「选用 DynamoDB」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for 'choosing DynamoDB' in the correct order:
steps: 代价：按量计费在超高写入下昂贵、查询灵活性差、绑定 AWS
需求：海量数据 + 高可用 + 低延迟，团队不想管运维
缓解：围绕访问模式精心建模、控制索引数量、用估算核对成本
选型：DynamoDB
决定性属性：全托管、自动分片扩缩、单毫秒延迟、支持事务
why: 决策链：需求（大规模+免运维）→ 决定性属性（托管、自动扩展、事务）→ 选 DynamoDB → 代价（成本/查询/锁定）→ 缓解（建模+成本估算）。
why_en: Massive scale with no ops burden points to DynamoDB's managed auto-scaling and transactions, whose cost and query limits are mitigated by careful modeling and estimation.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Access patterns known"] --> K["design PK and SK"]
    K --> I["add GSI or LSI only if needed"]
    I --> C["choose consistency per path"]

q: 补全「一致性按路径拆分」这条 DynamoDB 推理：
q_en: Fill in this DynamoDB reasoning about splitting consistency by path:
text: 预订/下单这类关键路径用 {{ConsistentRead=true}} 的强一致读（走 {{leader}} 节点、消耗 2 倍 RCU）；读多、延迟敏感的路径默认{{最终}}一致（任意副本可服务、0.5 RCU/4KB）。
why: 按请求可调一致性让一个系统里两类路径各取所需：正确性优先的花钱买强一致，性能优先的享受默认的便宜和快。
why_en: Critical paths request strongly consistent reads from the leader at double cost while latency-sensitive paths keep the cheap eventually consistent default.
tradeoff: 强一致读的正确性优先 vs 最终一致读的性能优先

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读的一致性开关。默认 false=最终一致(任意副本服务、可能读到略旧、0.5 RCU/4KB);设 true=强一致(必须读 leader 副本、保证最新、1 RCU/4KB=2倍)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB read consistency flag. Default false = eventually consistent (any replica, may be slightly stale, 0.5 RCU/4KB); true = strongly consistent (must read the leader replica, latest data, 1 RCU/4KB = double).

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 读容量单位。1 RCU=每秒一次强一致读(≤4KB)=每秒两次最终一致读(≤4KB)。所以强一致读花 1 RCU、最终一致只花 0.5 RCU→强一致=2倍成本
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read Capacity Unit. 1 RCU = one strongly-consistent read/sec (≤4KB) = two eventually-consistent reads/sec; a strong read costs 1 RCU, an eventual read 0.5 — strong is 2x.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 每个 item 存多个副本(通常 3 个跨 AZ),其中一个是 leader:写先落 leader 再复制给 follower。强一致读必须读 leader(它一定有最新写);最终一致读可读任意副本(follower 可能略滞后→读到旧值)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB stores each item on multiple replicas (usually 3 across AZs); one is the leader — writes hit it first, then replicate. A strongly consistent read must read the leader (it has the latest write); an eventually consistent read may read any replica (a follower may lag).

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 在「分区内索引结构」上，DynamoDB 与 Cassandra 的对比是？
q_en: On 'in-partition index structure', how do DynamoDB and Cassandra compare?
options: 两者都用 LSM 树
前者 B-tree，后者 LSM（写优化）。
DynamoDB 用 LSM，Cassandra 用 B-tree
两者都不用索引
why: DynamoDB 走 B-tree 路线（读写均衡、范围查询高效），Cassandra 走 LSM 路线（极致写吞吐）——同为宽列/键值家族但存储引擎哲学不同。
why_en: DynamoDB indexes each partition with a B-tree by sort key while Cassandra relies on an LSM tree optimized for writes.
options_en: Both use LSM trees.
The former uses a B-tree, the latter a write-optimized LSM tree.
DynamoDB uses LSM, Cassandra uses a B-tree.
Neither uses any index structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平衡树索引结构，支持高效的有序遍历和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced tree index that supports efficient ordered traversal and range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写优化的树形存储结构：先写内存再顺序刷盘合并，Cassandra 等系统使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized storage structure that buffers writes in memory and merges them to disk sequentially.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源宽列存储数据库，分区内用 LSM 树、面向高写入吞吐设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is an open-source wide-column database that uses LSM trees internally and is optimized for high write throughput.

tradeoff: DynamoDB 读写均衡的 B-tree vs Cassandra 写优化的 LSM
scenario: 对比 DynamoDB 和 Cassandra 在分区内部索引结构上的设计差异。
scenario_en: Comparing how DynamoDB and Cassandra each structure the index inside a partition.
optionExplanations: DynamoDB 分区内部实际走的是 B-tree 路线，不是 LSM，这个说法混淆了两者的存储引擎哲学。
DynamoDB 选 B-tree 换来读写均衡和高效范围查询，Cassandra 选 LSM 换来极致写吞吐，同属宽列/键值家族但存储引擎的取舍方向不同。
这把两者的存储引擎选型完全对调了，方向说反了。
两者其实都有精心设计的索引结构，只是选择的路线不同，说没有索引不成立。
optionExplanations_en: DynamoDB's partitions actually take the B-tree route, not LSM, so this conflates the two systems' storage-engine philosophies.

DynamoDB's B-tree route trades for balanced read/write and efficient range queries, while Cassandra's LSM route trades for maximum write throughput -- same wide-column/key-value family, different storage philosophy.
This swaps the two systems' storage-engine choices entirely -- the direction is reversed.
Both actually have carefully designed index structures, just different routes -- claiming neither uses indexing doesn't hold.

q: DynamoDB 的 attribute 支持哪些类型形态？
q_en: What type shapes does a DynamoDB attribute support?
options: 只支持字符串
只支持数字和布尔
标量、集合类型皆支持，且可嵌套表达复杂结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引的 schema，定义每个字段的类型和处理方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mapping is the index's schema, defining each field's type and how it is processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档里的一个键值对，mapping 决定它是否可搜索、按什么类型搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A field is a key-value pair in a document, whose searchability and type are set by the mapping.

q_en: What happens if a User object has 10 fields but only 2 are searched, and all 10 are mapped?
optionExplanations: mapping 大小不影响算分正确性，它带来的是资源开销问题，不是排序算错。
多余字段不会导致写入被拒绝，只是白白占用了内存。
8 个用不到的字段一样占索引和内存，query 性能和成本都会被拖累。
每个映射字段都有实打实的内存代价，「完全没影响」不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Mapping size doesn't affect scoring correctness — the real cost is resource overhead, not broken ranking.
Extra fields don't get writes rejected; they just waste memory silently.
Those 8 unused fields still get indexed and held in memory, dragging down query performance and driving up cost.
Every mapped field carries real memory cost — 'no impact at all' isn't true here.

q: 用一个不带参数的简单 PUT 创建索引时，默认配置是？
options: 无 mapping、5 个 shard、0 个 replica
动态 mapping、1 个 shard、1 个 replica（之后可再改）
必须先手动给出完整 mapping 才能创建
动态 mapping、10 个 shard、3 个 replica
options_en: No mapping, five shards, zero replicas
Dynamic mapping, one shard, one replica, all adjustable later
You must supply a complete mapping before the index can be created
Dynamic mapping, ten shards, three replicas
why: 默认是动态 mapping + 1 分片 + 1 副本，这些参数创建后还能更新；多数字段不该被搜索时就该显式设置 mapping。
why_en: A bare PUT creates an index with dynamic mapping, one shard, and one replica, all adjustable later.
codeSample:
PUT /books
# 不带 body：动态 mapping + 1 shard + 1 replica
# 等价于显式指定：
PUT /books
{ "settings": { "number_of_shards": 1, "number_of_replicas": 1 } }

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引的 schema，定义每个字段的类型和处理方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mapping is the index's schema, defining each field's type and how it is processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引水平拆分出的一份数据与索引结构，1:1 对应一个 Lucene 索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is a horizontal slice of an index's data and index structures, mapping one-to-one to a Lucene index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片的完整拷贝，用于故障恢复和分担查询流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a full copy of a shard, used for failover and to share query load.

q_en: What are the defaults when you create an index with a simple PUT and no extra parameters?
optionExplanations: 默认不是 5 个分片、0 副本，这个数字记错了。
没给参数时会先套上动态 mapping、1 个分片和 1 个副本这三项起步配置，之后都能再调整。
mapping 可以留给动态推断，不是创建索引前必须先手写的东西。
10 个分片、3 个副本不是默认值，要显式配置才会有。
optionExplanations_en: The default isn't 5 shards and 0 replicas — that number is just wrong.
Leave the parameters out and you start with dynamic mapping, 1 shard, and 1 replica — all three stay adjustable later.
Mapping can be left to dynamic inference — it isn't a prerequisite you must hand-write before creating an index.
10 shards and 3 replicas aren't the default; you'd have to configure that explicitly.

scenario: 书店系统：评论(review)很少被更新，但查书时经常要带着评论条件一起查。要决定评论放哪。
q: 更合适的建模是？
options: 把评论作为 nested 字段嵌进 book 文档
把评论拆分出来，单独建一个 review 专属 index
把评论整体存进 Redis 这样的键值缓存里
评论只落地在文件系统里，不做任何索引
options_en: Nest reviews as a nested field inside the book document
Split reviews out into their own dedicated review index
Store the whole reviews blob in a key-value cache like Redis
Land reviews only on the file system with no indexing at all
tradeoff: 查询效率（嵌套一起查）vs 更新代价（改评论要重写整个文档）
why: 评论「少更新、常随书一起查」时嵌套进 book 文档更高效——这是搜索版的范式化/反范式化取舍。
why_en: When reviews are rarely updated but frequently queried with books, nesting them inside the book document is the more efficient call.
whenOtherWins: 评论更新频繁时应单独建 index——嵌套方案每次改一条评论都要重写整个 book 文档，更新代价大。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把子文档数组当作独立文档索引的字段类型，保证多条件命中同一个子对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A nested field indexes each array element as its own hidden document so multiple conditions can match the same sub-object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被搜索的最小数据单元，本质是一个 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document is the smallest unit you search over, essentially a JSON object.

q_en: Which data model is the better fit?
scenario_en: In a bookstore system, reviews are rarely updated but are often queried together with books, so you need to decide where reviews should live.
optionExplanations: 评论少更新、又常跟书一起查时，嵌进 book 文档最省事：一次查询就拿到书和评论。
评论更新很频繁，或者要单独搜索评论本身时，才值得拆成独立 index。
Redis 能缓存热点读，但撑不起这里需要的全文和多条件搜索。
纯文件存储没有倒排索引，做不了条件过滤，等于放弃搜索能力。
optionExplanations_en: When reviews change rarely and are almost always queried alongside the book, nesting them in is simplest — one query returns both.
It's worth splitting reviews into their own index only when they update frequently or need to be searched independently.
Redis can cache hot reads, but it can't carry the full-text and multi-condition search this needs.
Plain file storage has no inverted index and can't do conditional filtering — that gives up search entirely.

scenario: 只想把某本书的 price 改成 14.99，不想读取和重发整个文档。
q: 该用哪个 API 调用？
options: PUT /books/_doc/{id} 并附上完整文档，把没改的字段也一起重写一遍
DELETE 后重新 POST 整个文档，中间会有短暂的数据空档期
POST /books/_update/{id}，body 只放 { "doc": { "price": 14.99 } }
PUT /books/_mapping 修改 price，但这改的是字段类型定义不是具体值
options_en: PUT the full document to /books/_doc/{id}, rewriting every unchanged field too
DELETE the document then POST the whole thing again, leaving a brief gap with no document
POST to /books/_update/{id} with only { "doc": { "price": 14.99 } }
PUT /books/_mapping to change price, but that changes the field's type definition, not its value
tradeoff: 部分字段更新（_update）vs 整文档替换（PUT）
why: _update 端点支持只传变更字段，不必先取整个文档；ES 是分布式、异步、并发系统，显式的更新语义能保证结果符合预期。
why_en: The update endpoint patches only the given fields without fetching the whole document first, which matters in a distributed, concurrent system.
whenOtherWins: 如果本来就要整体替换文档（全字段重建），直接 PUT 完整文档更直接，但要注意并发覆盖风险。

termDefinitions.meaning: 被搜索的最小数据单元，本质是一个 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A document is the smallest unit you search over, essentially a JSON object.

q_en: Which API call should you use?
scenario_en: You only want to change one book’s price to 14.99, without reading and resending the full document.
optionExplanations: 要整体替换文档、且手上已有完整内容时才用 PUT；这里只改一个字段，白白多一次读。
先删后建等于人为制造一个数据空档期，纯粹是更差的写法。
_update 端点只传变更字段，不用先取整份文档，就是为这种局部改动设计的。
_mapping 改的是字段类型定义，不是某篇文档里的具体值。
optionExplanations_en: PUT the full document only when you're replacing it wholesale and already have the complete content — here it's one field, so that's a wasted round trip.
Delete-then-recreate manufactures a gap where the document doesn't exist — strictly worse than updating in place.
The _update endpoint only needs the changed field, no need to fetch the whole document first — built exactly for a partial edit like this.
_mapping changes a field's type definition, not the value inside one document.

q: 写入返回的 _version 字段配合 ?version=N 更新，实现的是什么机制？
options: 悲观锁：更新前必须先锁住整份文档才能写
乐观并发控制：版本不匹配就报错，客户端处理冲突后重试
服务端自动合并两个并发写入的冲突内容
只是写入成功后的持久化确认回执而已
options_en: Pessimistic locking that must lock the entire document before it can be written
Optimistic concurrency control: a version mismatch fails the write for the client to retry
The server automatically merges the conflicting content of two concurrent writes
Merely a durability acknowledgment sent back after the write succeeds
why: 带版本条件的更新只在版本匹配时生效，否则抛错——这是乐观并发控制的典型例子，把冲突交给客户端重试。
why_en: Conditional updates on the version field are optimistic concurrency control: a mismatch fails the write and lets the client retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 给每个文档维护的版本号，配合乐观并发控制使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The version field is a per-document counter Elasticsearch uses for optimistic concurrency control.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先假设不会冲突，写入时校验版本号，不匹配就报错让客户端重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic concurrency control assumes no conflict and lets a version mismatch fail the write for the client to retry.

q_en: What mechanism do _version and ?version=N implement for updates?
optionExplanations: 校验不持锁，不会阻塞其他并发写入，这不是悲观锁。
版本号对不上就直接报错，冲突交给客户端处理后重试——典型的乐观并发控制。
ES 不会替你合并两个并发写，它只拒绝携带过期版本号的那次写。
持久化确认是另一件事，跟这里的版本校验无关。
optionExplanations_en: The check doesn't hold a lock and won't block other concurrent writers — this isn't pessimistic locking.
A version mismatch just errors out and pushes conflict resolution back to the client to retry — textbook optimistic concurrency control.
Elasticsearch won't merge two concurrent writes for you; it only rejects the one carrying a stale version.
Durability confirmation is a separate concern, unrelated to this version check.

q: 不带版本条件、直接 PUT 整个文档来更新，主要风险是？
options: 文档会被拆成两份
索引会损坏
写入必然失败
并发更新时悄悄覆盖别人的修改（丢更新）
options_en: The document gets split into two copies
The index becomes corrupted
The write is guaranteed to fail
It silently overwrites a concurrent writer's changes, a lost update
why: 另一个进程同时更新同一文档时，不带版本条件的整文档 PUT 会把对方的修改直接覆盖；用 _version 条件更新能防住。
why_en: A full-document PUT without a version check can silently overwrite a concurrent writer's changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 给每个文档维护的版本号，配合乐观并发控制使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The version field is a per-document counter Elasticsearch uses for optimistic concurrency control.

q_en: What is the main risk of updating a whole document with PUT and no version condition?
optionExplanations: 一次 PUT 不会把文档拆成两份，这个说法编造了不存在的行为。
并发写不会损坏索引结构，Elasticsearch 不会因此崩掉。
写入通常还是会成功，只是悄悄覆盖了别人的修改，而不是直接失败。
另一个进程同时改同一文档时，不带版本条件的 PUT 会把对方的修改整体覆盖掉。
optionExplanations_en: A single PUT doesn't split a document into two — that behavior is made up.
Concurrent writes don't corrupt the index structure; Elasticsearch doesn't break that way.
The write usually still succeeds — it just quietly overwrites someone else's change instead of failing outright.
If another process updates the same document at the same time, an unconditioned full-document PUT silently overwrites its change.

scenario: 要找标题含 "Great" 且价格不超过 15 美元的书。
q: 正确的查询写法是？
options: { "query": { "match": { "title": "Great", "price": { "lte": 15 } } } }
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "match": { "title": "Great" } }, { "range": { "price": { "lte": 15 } } } ] } } }
{ "query": { "term": { "title": "Great" } }, "term": { "price": 15 } }
SELECT * FROM books WHERE title LIKE '%Great%' AND price <= 15
options_en: { "query": { "match": { "title": "Great", "price": { "lte": 15 } } } }
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "match": { "title": "Great" } }, { "range": { "price": { "lte": 15 } } } ] } } }
{ "query": { "term": { "title": "Great" } }, "term": { "price": 15 } }
SELECT * FROM books WHERE title LIKE '%Great%' AND price <= 15
tradeoff: 单一 match 查询 vs bool 组合多条件
why: 多条件组合用 bool 查询：must 数组里放 match（全文匹配）和 range（数值范围）；查询 DSL 是 JSON 化的，思路和 SQL 类似。
why_en: Combine conditions with a bool query whose must clause holds a match on title and a range on price.
whenOtherWins: 只有单一条件时，直接用一个 match 或 term 查询即可，不必套 bool。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 must/should/filter 组合多个查询条件的容器查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bool query combines multiple conditions using must, should, or filter clauses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 text 字段做全文匹配的查询子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A match query performs full-text matching against a text field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对数值或日期字段做区间过滤的查询子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A range query filters a numeric or date field within bounds.

q_en: What is the correct query shape?
scenario_en: You need books whose title contains "Great" and whose price is at most 15 dollars.
optionExplanations: match 一次只认一个字段，塞两个条件进去不会按 price 过滤。
两个条件要同时成立，就把 match 和 range 都放进 must 数组里，各自负责一段判断。
term 是精确匹配单值，硬塞成两个字段会直接语法错乱。
这是 SQL 语法，ES 的搜索端点只接受 JSON 化的查询 DSL。
optionExplanations_en: match only understands one field at a time — cramming two conditions in there won't filter by price.
When two conditions both need to hold, put match and range together inside must, each handling its own condition.
term does exact single-value matching — forcing two fields into it isn't even valid syntax.
That's SQL syntax; Elasticsearch's search endpoint only accepts the JSON query DSL.

scenario: reviews 是 nested 类型。要找「某一条评论同时满足：内容提到 excellent 且评分 ≥ 4」的书。
q: 正确的查询是？
options: nested 查询：指定 path=reviews，内部再套 bool must
顶层 bool 直接 match reviews.comment 并 range reviews.rating
term 查询 reviews 字段
先查出所有书，再在应用层过滤
options_en: A nested query with path=reviews wrapping a bool must inside
A top-level bool matching reviews.comment and ranging reviews.rating directly
A term query on the reviews field
Fetch every book and filter in the application layer
tradeoff: nested 查询（同一子文档校验）vs 顶层字段查询（跨子文档误匹配）
why: nested 查询保证多个条件落在同一条嵌套评论上；nested 文档有独立的字段空间，必须用 path 指定进入。
why_en: A nested query with the reviews path ensures both conditions apply to the same nested review object.
whenOtherWins: 如果 reviews 不是 nested 类型，或者条件不要求命中同一条评论，顶层字段查询就够了。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把子文档数组当作独立文档索引的字段类型，保证多条件命中同一个子对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A nested field indexes each array element as its own hidden document so multiple conditions can match the same sub-object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 must/should/filter 组合多个查询条件的容器查询。

q_en: What is the correct nested query shape?
scenario_en: The reviews field is nested, and you need books where one review both mentions "excellent" and has rating at least 4.
optionExplanations: 指定 path=reviews 再套 bool must，能保证两个条件落在同一条评论上。
顶层字段各自匹配，会把不同评论各命中一个条件也算通过，语义就错了。
reviews 是数组对象，不是能整体 term 精确匹配的单值字段。
查出全部书再在应用层过滤，等于放弃了索引的优势，自己重写一遍过滤逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: Scope with path=reviews and nest a bool must inside it so both conditions must hit the same review.
Matching each field at the top level lets two different reviews each satisfy one condition and still count as a hit — wrong semantics.
reviews is an array of objects, not a single value that term can match exactly.
Pulling every book back and filtering in the app layer throws away the index and reimplements the filtering yourself.

q: 搜索响应 hits 里的 _source 是什么？
options: 响应里单独统计查询耗时的字段
描述文档具体落在哪个分片的路由信息
写入时的原始文档 JSON（默认随结果返回）
衡量文档匹配程度的相关性得分字段
options_en: A field in the response that reports query timing on its own
Routing information describing which shard a document lives on
The original JSON document you indexed, returned by default
The relevance score field measuring how well a document matches
why: _source 是你存进去的原始文档；结果同时还带 _id 和相关性 _score，不显式排除的话默认一起返回。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source field is the original JSON document you indexed, returned with search hits by default.

q_en: In search hits, what is _source?
optionExplanations: 耗时统计在响应顶层的 took 字段，不在 hits 里的 _source。
分片路由信息不会作为 _source 返回给客户端。
_source 就是写入时存进去的原始文档 JSON，不显式排除时默认随结果一起返回。
相关性得分在 _score 字段，跟 _source 是并列的两个字段，不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Timing lives in the top-level took field, not inside hits._source.
Shard routing info is never returned as _source.
_source is exactly the original document JSON you indexed, returned by default alongside each hit unless you exclude it.
The relevance score lives in the separate _score field, not inside _source.

q: 关于「GET /_search 带请求体」这个用法，正确的说法是？
options: 按 HTTP 规范，GET 请求永远不能带请求体，这个示例写法从头到尾都是错的
Elasticsearch 接受带请求体的 GET；遇到较真的代理时可改用 POST 或把查询放进 query string
必须改用 PUT 方法，而且要带上完整的索引配置才能发起搜索请求
Elasticsearch 只能通过 WebSocket 协议发起搜索，HTTP 接口完全不支持
options_en: By the HTTP spec, a GET request can never carry a body, so this example is wrong from start to finish
Elasticsearch accepts a GET with a body; a strict proxy can be worked around with POST or a query string
You must switch to PUT and attach a full index configuration to issue a search request
Elasticsearch can only search over WebSocket, the HTTP interface is not supported at all
why: Elasticsearch 的搜索端点会响应带请求体的 GET；遇到较真的代理时用 POST 端点或 query string 也能达到同样效果。

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP 方法对资源做操作的接口风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that operates on resources using standard HTTP methods.

q_en: What is true about sending a request body with GET /_search?
optionExplanations: HTTP 规范上确实少见，但这个搜索端点实际能接受带请求体的 GET，不是「从头到尾都错」。
这个端点接受带请求体的 GET；遇到较真代理挡住时，换成 POST 方法或把参数放进 URL 查询串照样能行。
PUT 的语义是替换资源，不是发起搜索，用错了方法。
ES 的搜索走标准 HTTP REST 接口，不需要依赖 WebSocket。
optionExplanations_en: It's unusual by strict HTTP convention, but this search endpoint actually accepts a GET with a body — it isn't 'wrong from the start.'
This endpoint accepts a GET with a body; if a strict proxy blocks that, switching to POST or moving the params into the URL works just as well.
PUT means replace a resource, not run a search — that's the wrong method for this.
Elasticsearch search runs over standard HTTP REST, no WebSocket dependency needed.

q: geo_point 与 geo_shape 两种地理字段类型的分工是？
options: geo_point 用来存多边形区域，geo_shape 用来存单个坐标点
无论 geo_point 还是 geo_shape，都只能存储单个坐标点
geo_shape 类型已经被官方废弃，不建议再使用
geo_point 存单个经纬度点（餐厅位置、签到）；geo_shape 存任意几何（配送区、城市边界）
options_en: geo_point is used to store a polygon area while geo_shape stores a single coordinate point
Whether geo_point or geo_shape, both can only store a single coordinate point
The geo_shape type has been officially deprecated and should no longer be used
geo_point stores one lat-lon point like a restaurant location; geo_shape stores arbitrary geometries like a delivery zone
tradeoff: geo_point 单点查询 vs geo_shape 几何相交查询
why: 点用 geo_point（位置、地址），面/线/圆等任意几何用 geo_shape（配送区域、服务覆盖范围）。
why_en: Use geo_point for a single coordinate like a restaurant location, and geo_shape for arbitrary geometries like delivery zones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存单个经纬度坐标的字段类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geo_point field stores a single latitude-longitude coordinate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存多边形、线、圆等任意几何图形的字段类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geo_shape field stores arbitrary geometries like polygons, lines, or circles.

q_en: How do geo_point and geo_shape split responsibilities?
optionExplanations: 说反了：实际是 geo_point 存单点、geo_shape 才存多边形区域。
geo_shape 明确支持多边形、线、圆这些复杂几何，不是只能存单点。

optionExplanations_en: search_after is stateless — the server doesn't hand out a token for it.
The client pulls the last hit's sort values from the previous page (say, timestamp plus _id) and sends them back on the next request.
Multiplying page number by page size is the from/size algorithm, not how search_after works.
A PIT snapshot ID is a separate parameter — search_after doesn't depend on it by itself.

q: 关于 search_after 分页，哪些说法正确？（多选）
options: 深分页高效：每页只取上一页之后的文档
只能向前翻页，不能随机跳到第 N 页
服务端为每个客户端保存游标状态
客户端要自己记住上一页最后一条的 sort 值
options_en: Deep paging stays efficient because each page only fetches documents after the previous one
You can only page forward, never jump to page N
The server keeps per-client cursor state
The client must remember the previous page's last sort values
why: search_after 把状态放在客户端（记 sort 值）、只能前进；若底层数据更新删除，之前页的文档还可能被漏掉——要一致快照得用 PIT。
why_en: Search-after is efficient and duplicate-free but forward-only, with the client keeping the last sort values rather than the server holding cursor state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的排序值作为下一页起点的分页方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Search-after paginates by using the previous page's last sort values as the starting point for the next page.

q_en: Which statements about search_after pagination are correct? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 深分页高效：每页只处理上一页之后的增量部分，不用重新排前面的文档。
只能往前翻，不支持随机跳到第 N 页——这是它比 from/size 少的能力。
实际上服务端不保存游标状态，是无状态机制，这个说法反了。
游标状态在客户端：要自己记住并传回上一页最后一条的 sort 值。
optionExplanations_en: Deep paging stays fast because each page only processes the increment after the last one — no re-sorting everything before it.
It's forward-only — no jumping to page N — that's the capability it trades away versus from/size.
The server actually doesn't hold cursor state — search_after is stateless, so this claim is backwards.
The cursor state lives on the client: it has to remember and resend the previous page's last sort value.

scenario: 要在索引持续写入的同时完整导出一批搜索结果，翻页过程中不能因数据变动而漏掉或重复文档。
q: 最合适的分页机制是？
options: 继续沿用最基础的 from/size 分页
不带 PIT、只用纯粹的 search_after
每翻一页都独立重新跑一次搜索查询
PIT（point in time）+ search_after 组成的游标
options_en: Keep using the most basic from/size pagination
Plain search_after with no PIT attached
Independently re-run the search query fresh on every page
A cursor built from PIT plus search_after
tradeoff: 一致性快照的额外开销 vs 翻页期间数据可能变动
why: PIT 固定一个时间点视图（keep_alive 续期，用完 DELETE 释放），配合 search_after 翻页，即使索引在更新也能保持一致——代价是更多服务端开销。
why_en: A point-in-time snapshot combined with search-after gives a consistent view across pages even while the index is being updated.
whenOtherWins: 不要求一致快照时，纯 search_after 更轻量——PIT 的状态维持是实打实的额外开销。

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定一个时间点的数据快照，配合 search_after 实现一致的深分页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point-in-time snapshot fixes a consistent view of the data for paging with search-after.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的排序值作为下一页起点的分页方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Search-after paginates by using the previous page's last sort values as the starting point for the next page.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最简单的分页方式，from 是起始偏移，size 是每页条数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: From-size pagination specifies a starting offset and a page size.

q_en: Which pagination mechanism best fits this export job?
scenario_en: You need to export a full batch of search results while the index is still receiving writes, without missing or duplicating documents during paging.
optionExplanations: 浅分页、索引不太变时还能用，但这里翻页又慢又不保证一致，不满足要求。
只要高效前进、不要求跨页一致时可以单用它，但索引更新期间仍可能漏掉或重复文档。
每页独立重新查询，不同页可能基于不同时刻的数据，结果会漂移。
PIT 固定住一个时间点视图，配合游标翻页，导出全程基于同一份快照，索引更新也不受影响。
optionExplanations_en: Fine for shallow paging with a stable index, but here it's both slow and non-consistent — doesn't meet the requirement.
Good enough alone when you only need forward efficiency, not cross-page consistency — index updates mid-export can still drop or duplicate rows.
Re-running the query independently each page means different pages can reflect different moments — the result drifts.
PIT pins a fixed point-in-time view, and paging through it with a forward cursor means the whole export runs against one consistent snapshot even while the index keeps changing.

q: Elasticsearch 与 Apache Lucene 的分工是？
options: Elasticsearch 是 Lucene 之上的分布式编排层：负责集群协调、API、聚合、实时能力；核心搜索由 Lucene 完成
Elasticsearch 完全从零实现了自己的搜索内核，压根不依赖 Lucene 这个库
Lucene 承担分布式集群协调的职责，Elasticsearch 负责底层倒排索引
Elasticsearch 和 Lucene 是市场上互相竞争的两款独立产品
options_en: Elasticsearch is a distributed orchestration layer over Lucene, handling cluster coordination, APIs, aggregations, and real-time features, while Lucene provides the core search
Elasticsearch built its entire search core from scratch and does not depend on the Lucene library at all
Lucene takes on distributed cluster coordination while Elasticsearch handles the underlying inverted index
Elasticsearch and Lucene are two independent products competing in the market
why: 把 Elasticsearch 理解为「Lucene 的高层编排框架」：分布式、API、聚合是 Elasticsearch 的活，搜索之心是 Lucene。
why_en: Elasticsearch is a distributed orchestration layer over Apache Lucene, which provides the core low-level search functionality.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 底层的高性能搜索库，负责倒排索引等核心搜索能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lucene is the low-level search library underneath Elasticsearch that provides core search structures like the inverted index.

q_en: How do Elasticsearch and Apache Lucene split responsibilities?
optionExplanations: 它是搭在 Lucene 之上的分布式编排层：集群协调、接口、聚合和实时能力归它管，核心搜索交给 Lucene 完成。
实际上 ES 深度依赖 Lucene 做底层搜索，不是从零自研的内核。
分布式协调是 ES 的职责，倒排索引才是 Lucene 的活，这里说反了。
Lucene 是被嵌入使用的库，不是和 ES 竞争的独立产品。
optionExplanations_en: It's the distributed orchestration layer sitting on top of Lucene — cluster coordination, the API surface, aggregations, and real-time features are its job, while core search execution belongs to Lucene.
Elasticsearch actually depends heavily on Lucene for search internals — it isn't a from-scratch engine.
Distributed coordination is Elasticsearch's job and the inverted index is Lucene's — this has it backwards.
Lucene is an embedded library, not an independent product competing with Elasticsearch.

q: 以下哪些是 Elasticsearch 的节点类型？（多选）
options: Master 节点
Gateway 节点
Coordinating 节点
Ingest 节点
options_en: Master node
Gateway node
Coordinating node
Ingest node
why: 五种节点类型：Master（集群管理）、Data（存数据）、Coordinating（请求协调）、Ingest（数据摄入转换）、Machine Learning；没有 Gateway 节点。
why_en: Elasticsearch nodes come in five types: master, data, coordinating, ingest, and machine learning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责集群级操作（增删节点、创建/删除索引）的管理节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The master node is the admin node responsible for cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating indices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coordinating node is the entry point that receives client requests, routes queries, and merges results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责数据写入前转换和预处理的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ingest node transforms and prepares data before it is indexed.

q_en: Which of these are Elasticsearch node roles? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: Master 节点负责增删节点、创建删除索引这类集群级操作。
Elasticsearch 并没有「Gateway 节点」这个类型，这是编出来的。
Coordinating 节点是客户端请求的入口，负责分发查询并合并各节点的结果。
Ingest 节点在数据落地前做转换和预处理。
optionExplanations_en: The master node handles cluster-level operations — adding/removing nodes, creating and deleting indices.
There's no such thing as a 'gateway node' in Elasticsearch — this type is invented.
The coordinating node is where client requests land — it fans queries out and merges results from other nodes.
The ingest node transforms and preprocesses data before it's stored.

q: Master 节点的职责是？
options: 把集群里所有文档的数据都存在自己节点上
集群级操作：增删节点、创建/删除索引——集群的「管理员」
独自承担集群里全部的搜索请求执行工作
专门负责跑机器学习模型的推理任务
options_en: Storing every document's data in the cluster on itself
Cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating and deleting indices, the cluster's admin
Single-handedly executing every search request in the cluster
Dedicated to running machine learning model inference jobs
why: Master 是唯一能执行集群级操作的节点；数据存储在 Data 节点，搜索入口在 Coordinating 节点。
why_en: The master node is the cluster admin, the only node that performs cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating indices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责集群级操作（增删节点、创建/删除索引）的管理节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The master node is the admin node responsible for cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating indices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际存储文档和索引结构的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data node is where documents and their index structures are actually stored.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coordinating node is the entry point that receives client requests, routes queries, and merges results.

q_en: What is the Master node responsible for?
optionExplanations: 存文档是 Data 节点的职责，Master 不背这个锅。
唯一能做增删节点、创建删除索引这类集群级操作的就是它——集群的「管理员」。
接收和分发搜索请求是 Coordinating 节点的活，不归 Master 管。
机器学习推理任务由专门的 ML 节点承担，跟 Master 无关。
optionExplanations_en: Storing documents is the data node's job, not Master's.
It's the only node type that can add/remove nodes or create/delete indices — the cluster's admin.
Receiving and dispatching search requests is the coordinating node's work, not Master's.
ML inference is handled by dedicated ML nodes, unrelated to Master.

q: Coordinating 节点在请求路径中扮演什么角色？
options: 把分片的原始数据实际存储在本地磁盘上
参与 master-eligible 节点之间的选主投票
集群前端：接收客户端请求、解析查询、分发到相应节点、合并结果返回
只负责处理写入请求，不管搜索请求
options_en: Physically storing shard data on local disk
Taking part in the leader-election vote among master-eligible nodes
The cluster's front end: receiving requests, parsing queries, routing, and merging results
Handling only write requests, never search requests
why: Coordinating 节点是用户请求的入口：解析查询、决定该问哪些节点、汇总排序结果——搜索的「前台」。
why_en: The coordinating node is the cluster's front end, receiving client requests, routing them to the right nodes, and merging the results.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Client search"] --> B["Coordinating node"]
  B --> C["Shard 1"]
  B --> D["Shard 2"]
  C --> E["Merge top hits"]
  D --> E

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coordinating node is the entry point that receives client requests, routes queries, and merges results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际存储文档和索引结构的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data node is where documents and their index structures are actually stored.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责集群级操作（增删节点、创建/删除索引）的管理节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The master node is the admin node responsible for cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating indices.

q_en: What role does a Coordinating node play in the request path?
optionExplanations: 把分片数据存本地磁盘是 Data 节点的职责。
参与选主是 master-eligible 节点之间的事，不是 Coordinating 的活。
它是请求入口：解析查询、分发到相应分片、把结果合并排序后返回。
它既处理搜索也处理写入请求，不是只管写不管搜。
optionExplanations_en: Storing shard data on local disk is the data node's job.
Participating in leader election is between master-eligible nodes, not coordinating's role.
It's the request front door: parses the query, fans it out to the right shards, merges and sorts the results, and returns them.
It handles both search and write requests — it isn't write-only.

q: 数据在被索引前的转换和预处理由哪种节点负责？
options: Ingest 节点
Master 节点
Data 节点
Coordinating 节点
options_en: Ingest node
Master node
Data node
Coordinating node
why: Ingest 节点负责数据摄入管道：转换、预处理，然后交给 Data 节点存储索引。
why_en: Ingest nodes transform and prepare incoming data before it is indexed on data nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责数据写入前转换和预处理的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ingest node transforms and prepares data before it is indexed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际存储文档和索引结构的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data node is where documents and their index structures are actually stored.

q_en: Which node role handles transformation and preprocessing before indexing?
optionExplanations: 它负责摄入管道里的转换和预处理，处理完的数据才轮到 Data 节点落盘索引。
Master 管的是集群级操作，不负责数据转换。
Data 节点接收已经处理好的数据存储，本身不做转换。
Coordinating 负责查询路径，不负责写入前的预处理。
optionExplanations_en: It runs the ingestion pipeline's transform-and-preprocess step; only after that does a data node take over to store and index it.
Master handles cluster-level operations, not data transformation.
Data nodes store already-processed data — they don't do the transforming themselves.
Coordinating handles the query path, not pre-write processing.

q: 关于节点角色的部署，正确的说法是？
options: 每台物理实例在整个生命周期里只能固定担任一种节点类型，配置好之后永远不能再变更，哪怕运维想调整也做不到
一台实例可身兼多种角色（如 master-eligible + coordinating）；大型部署会为不同角色配不同硬件（ingest 偏 CPU、data 偏磁盘 I/O 和内存）
集群里所有节点的 CPU、内存、磁盘配置必须完全保持一致，不允许有任何差异，哪怕承担的角色完全不同也一样
为了均衡负载，节点类型会按固定的周期每天自动轮换一次，不需要人工干预，运维只要坐等它自己切换角色
options_en: Each physical instance is permanently locked into a single node type for its whole lifetime, with no way to change it even if ops wants to
An instance can combine multiple roles, such as master-eligible plus coordinating, and large deployments give each role matched hardware
Every node's CPU, memory, and disk configuration must be perfectly identical across the cluster, no matter how different their roles are
To balance load, node types automatically rotate on a fixed daily schedule with no manual intervention needed at all
why: 节点类型由配置决定、可叠加；成熟部署会按角色特点选硬件——ingest 吃 CPU，data 吃磁盘和内存。
why_en: A node's roles come from configuration and can be combined, while serious deployments give each role hardware matched to its bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有资格被选为 master 的节点，参与选举但同一时刻只有一个当选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A master-eligible node can be elected master, though only one is active at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coordinating node is the entry point that receives client requests, routes queries, and merges results.

q_en: What is true about deploying Elasticsearch node roles?
optionExplanations: 实际上一个实例可以同时兼任多种角色，不是固定死只能选一种。
一台实例能身兼多角色（如 master-eligible + coordinating），大型集群还会按角色特点配不同硬件。
不同角色瓶颈不一样——处理数据摄入的偏 CPU 密集，负责存储的偏磁盘和内存密集——统一硬件没必要。
节点类型由配置决定，不会按周期自动轮换。
optionExplanations_en: In practice one instance can hold several roles at once — it isn't locked to a single fixed type.
One instance can wear multiple hats (say master-eligible plus coordinating), and large deployments often pick different hardware per role.
Different roles hit different bottlenecks — the ingestion-heavy role leans on CPU, the storage role leans on disk and memory — so uniform hardware isn't necessary.
Node type is set by configuration; it doesn't auto-rotate on a schedule.

q: Data 节点的 hot / warm / cold / frozen 分层依据是什么？
options: 数据中心机房当天的实际温度高低
这个分片当前占用的磁盘空间大小
数据被查询的可能性（新旧程度）以及是否还会变化
这份数据当前配置了多少个副本
options_en: How hot the physical data-center room actually runs that day
How much disk space this particular shard currently occupies
How likely the data is to be queried, usually by recency, and whether it can still change
How many replicas this piece of data is currently configured with
why: 越新越常查的数据放 hot 层（好硬件），越旧越冷的数据下沉到 warm/cold/frozen——按访问概率和可变性分层省成本。
why_en: Data tiers are chosen by how likely the data is to be queried, usually by recency, and whether it can still change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际存储文档和索引结构的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data node is where documents and their index structures are actually stored.

q_en: What determines hot, warm, cold, and frozen tiers for Data nodes?
optionExplanations: 这几层名字只是访问模式的比喻，不是机房的字面温度。
分片占用的磁盘空间大小不是分层的决定因素。
分层看的是数据被查询的可能性（新旧程度）和是否还会变化，越冷的数据下沉到更便宜的层。
副本数量是独立配置项，跟数据分层没关系。
optionExplanations_en: The layer names are just a metaphor for access patterns, not literal server-room temperature.
How much disk a shard uses isn't what decides its tier.
Tiering follows how likely the data is to be queried (how fresh it is) and whether it still changes, sinking colder data onto cheaper hardware.
Replica count is a separate setting, unrelated to which tier data sits in.

q: 集群启动时 master 是怎么产生的？
options: 指定一批 master-eligible 的种子节点跑选举算法，同一时刻只有一个活跃 master，其余待命
集群里所有节点会同时并列担任 master 角色，谁都能做集群级操作
由发起请求的客户端直接指定哪个节点当 master，服务端不参与决策
单纯比较各节点的 IP 地址大小，取数值最小的那个当 master
options_en: Seed master-eligible nodes run a leader election so exactly one active master leads while the rest stand by
All nodes in the cluster serve as master simultaneously, and any of them can run cluster operations
Whichever client sends the request directly designates which node is master, with the server not deciding
Simply compare every node's IP address and pick whichever has the smallest value
why: seed nodes（master-eligible）之间执行 leader election 选出唯一 master；其余 master-eligible 节点 standby 等待接管。
why_en: Seed nodes run a leader election so exactly one active master leads the cluster while other master-eligible nodes stand by.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有资格被选为 master 的节点，参与选举但同一时刻只有一个当选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A master-eligible node can be elected master, though only one is active at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责集群级操作（增删节点、创建/删除索引）的管理节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The master node is the admin node responsible for cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating indices.

q_en: How is the master chosen when the cluster starts?
optionExplanations: 有资格当选的种子节点之间跑选举算法，同一时刻只有一个活跃 master，其余待命接管。
多主会让集群级操作互相冲突，Elasticsearch 不允许同时存在两个活跃 master。
客户端不参与集群内部的选主过程，这是节点之间自己决定的。
选主基于选举协议，不是简单比较 IP 地址大小。
optionExplanations_en: The eligible seed nodes run a leader-election algorithm among themselves; only one master is active at a time, with the rest on standby to take over.
Two active masters would collide on cluster-level operations, which Elasticsearch simply doesn't allow.
The client has no say in cluster-internal leader election — the nodes settle it among themselves.
Election runs on a proper voting protocol, not a plain comparison of IP addresses.

q: 一次搜索请求在数据节点上分成哪两个阶段？
options: 先经过写入阶段，再进入刷盘落盘阶段
query 阶段（用索引结构找出相关文档 ID）+ fetch 阶段（按需取回文档内容）
先做请求解析阶段，再进入结果缓存阶段
借用 MapReduce 的说法，分成 map 阶段和 reduce 阶段
options_en: First a write phase, then a flush-to-disk phase
A query phase that finds matching document ids, plus a fetch phase that retrieves content
First a request-parsing phase, then a result-caching phase
Borrowing MapReduce terminology, a map phase followed by a reduce phase
why: 先 query（在优化的索引结构里定位文档），后 fetch（可选地把文档从节点拉回来）；_source 与 Lucene 索引是分开存的。
why_en: Search runs a query phase that identifies matching document ids via index structures, then a fetch phase that optionally retrieves the documents.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Query phase"] --> B["Top doc ids"]
  B --> C["Fetch phase"]
  C --> D["_source hits"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用索引结构定位相关文档 ID 的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query phase locates matching document ids using index structures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按需把文档内容从节点取回的阶段。

query 阶段在索引结构里定位出匹配的文档 ID，fetch 阶段再按需把文档内容取回来。

The query stage locates matching document IDs inside the index structure, then the fetch stage retrieves the document content on demand.
Elasticsearch search has no separate 'result caching' stage of its own.
ES query execution isn't a MapReduce model — borrowing those two names doesn't fit.

Joining across ten indices

q_en: What kind of Elasticsearch query is ideal?

Elasticsearch has no relational-style join, so this option imagines a scenario that doesn't exist.
Deep pagination is exactly the inefficient pattern to avoid, not what an ideal query looks like.
Never touching the source document and answering purely from indexed fields means the result is ready at the query stage, skipping the fetch cost entirely.

q: 补全 Elasticsearch 的「俄罗斯套娃」存储层级：

q: 分片（shard）给 Elasticsearch 带来的核心能力是？
options: 把文档和对应索引结构水平拆到多台节点；搜索在相关分片上并行执行，由协调节点合并排序
自动对写入的每份文档做加密存储，保证数据在磁盘上不可读
让索引从此不再需要定义 mapping，字段类型全部自动推断
让所有分片和副本之间在任意时刻都保证强一致性
options_en: Splitting documents and their index structures horizontally across nodes, with the coordinating node merging parallel searches
Automatically encrypting every document on write so it is unreadable on disk
Making an index no longer need a mapping defined at all, inferring every field type
Guaranteeing strong consistency across every shard and replica at every instant
why: 分片让数据和索引横向分布、查询并行化，是 ES 扩展性的基础；结果由 coordinating 节点归并。
why_en: Sharding spreads documents and their index structures across nodes so searches run in parallel and the coordinating node merges the results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。

q_en: What core capability do shards give Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 分片把文档和索引结构水平拆到多台节点，搜索在相关分片上并行执行，由协调节点合并排序。
分片和数据加密是两回事，ES 不会因为分了片就自动加密存储。
有多个分片，每个索引依然需要 mapping，分片不能免掉这一步。
Elasticsearch 是最终一致，分片不会把它变成强一致系统。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding splits documents and index structure horizontally across nodes; search runs in parallel across the relevant shards and the coordinating node merges the results.
Sharding and data encryption are unrelated — having shards doesn't automatically encrypt storage.
Every index still needs mapping regardless of shard count — sharding doesn't remove that step.
Elasticsearch is eventually consistent; sharding doesn't turn it into a strongly consistent system.

q: 副本（replica）的两大用途是？
options: 对存储的数据做压缩处理，从而节省磁盘空间和成本
加快主分片自身的写入速度，同时减少段合并的次数
高可用（分片挂了有备份）+ 提高读吞吐（协调节点在主副本间负载均衡搜索）
只是用来做离线备份归档，完全不参与实时的查询流量
options_en: Compressing stored data to save both disk space and cost
Speeding up the primary shard's own writes while reducing segment merges
High availability plus higher read throughput by load-balancing searches across primary and replica shards
Only for offline backup archiving, taking no part in live query traffic at all
why: replica 是分片的完整拷贝：既是故障备份，又能分担搜索流量——协调节点把查询分散到主分片和所有副本上。
why_en: Replicas provide high availability and extra read throughput, since the coordinating node balances searches across primary and replica shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片的完整拷贝，用于故障恢复和分担查询流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a full copy of a shard, used for failover and to share query load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引水平拆分出的一份数据与索引结构，1:1 对应一个 Lucene 索引。

q_en: What are the two main uses of replicas?
optionExplanations: 副本是完整数据拷贝，不做压缩处理，跟节省磁盘空间无关。
副本不参与主分片自身的写入路径优化，也不会减少段合并次数。
副本挂了有备份保高可用，协调节点还能把查询分散到主副本间提高读吞吐。
副本同时服务实时查询流量，不只是拿来做离线归档。
optionExplanations_en: A replica is a full copy of the data, not a compression trick — it has nothing to do with saving disk space.
Replicas don't speed up the primary shard's own write path or cut down merge counts.
Replicas back up the shard for high availability, and the coordinating node spreads search load across primary and replicas to boost read throughput.
Replicas also serve live query traffic — they aren't just an offline backup copy.

scenario: 线上一个 primary shard 独立能扛住 X 的查询 TPS，运维给这个索引配置了 Y 个 replica。
q: 这时集群大致能扛住多少查询 TPS？
options: X + Y
还是 X
X 的平方
options_en: X plus Y
X times (Y plus one)
Still just X
X squared
why: 1 个 primary + Y 个 replica 共有 Y+1 份可服务查询的分片拷贝，读吞吐近似按 X*(Y+1) 扩展；写入不受此加成。
why_en: With one primary shard and Y replica shards, there are Y+1 shard copies that can serve reads, so read throughput scales to roughly X times Y plus one.

q_en: Roughly how much query TPS can this setup handle?
scenario_en: One primary shard can independently serve X query TPS, and operations configures Y replicas for this index.
optionExplanations: 把 replica 当成简单加法项，漏算了每个副本其实是一份完整可服务的拷贝。
1 个主分片加 Y 个副本，一共 Y+1 份可服务查询的拷贝，读吞吐按这个倍数扩展。
只算主分片吞吐，等于当副本完全不分担查询流量，忽视了它的读扩展作用。
吞吐不会因为多几个副本就变成平方增长，这里把线性关系算错了。
optionExplanations_en: Treating replicas as a simple add-on undercounts them — each replica is actually a full, independently servable copy.
One primary plus Y replicas means Y+1 servable copies total, so read throughput scales by roughly that multiple.
Counting only the primary's throughput assumes replicas carry zero query traffic, which ignores their read-scaling role.
Throughput doesn't square just because you add replicas — this mistakes a linear relationship for a quadratic one.

q: Lucene 的 segment 最核心的性质是？
options: 可以就地修改
只存在于内存里
不可变（immutable）的已索引数据容器
每个文档单独一个 segment
options_en: It can be modified in place
It only exists in memory
An immutable container of indexed data
Every document gets its own segment
why: segment 是搜索引擎的基本单元，且一旦写成就不可变——增删改都是靠新 segment、软删除和合并来间接实现的。
why_en: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, and all updates happen through new segments, soft deletes, and merges.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["New docs"] --> B["New segment"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
