q_en: What is the most important property of a Lucene segment?
optionExplanations: 这里正好说反了 segment 最核心的性质——它写成后就不可变。
segment 会落盘持久化，不是只存在于内存里。
segment 是一旦写成就不可变的已索引数据容器，增删改都靠新 segment 间接实现。
segment 是批量构建的，不是每个文档单独一个。
optionExplanations_en: This has it exactly backwards — the whole point of a segment is that it's immutable once written.
Segments get flushed to disk; they don't live only in memory.
A segment is an immutable, already-indexed data container once written — inserts, deletes, and updates all happen indirectly through new segments.
Segments are built in batches, not created one per document.

q: 插入一个新文档时，Lucene 实际做了什么？
options: 先攒批：文档进入待写批次，凑够一批构建成新 segment 刷到磁盘
把新文档直接插进已有 segment 的中间位置
每插入一条文档就重写一遍整个索引
文档只写进内存，永远不会刷到磁盘
options_en: Batch first: documents accumulate and get built into a new segment flushed to disk
Insert the new document directly into the middle of an existing segment
Rewrite the entire index for every single document inserted
Write the document only to memory and never flush it to disk
why: 写入是批量构建新 segment 的过程，不修改既有 segment——这是不可变设计下高写入吞吐的来源。
why_en: Inserts are batched into new segments that get flushed to disk, never modifying existing segments.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What does Lucene actually do when inserting a new document?
optionExplanations: 新文档先进待写批次，攒够一批后构建成一个新 segment 刷到磁盘。
segment 一旦写成就不再被修改，不能把新文档插进已有 segment 中间。
写入只影响新构建的 segment，不会碰既有索引的全量重写。
数据最终会被刷到磁盘，不是永远只留在内存里。
optionExplanations_en: New documents first queue up in a pending batch, and once enough accumulate they get built into a brand-new segment flushed to disk.
A segment can't be modified once written, so a new document can't be inserted into the middle of an existing one.
A write only produces a new segment — it never rewrites the whole existing index.
The data does eventually get flushed to disk — it doesn't stay in memory forever.

q: segment 数量太多时，Lucene 怎么处理？
options: 为了腾出空间，自动把最老的几个 segment 直接删掉
在合并完成之前直接拒绝任何新的写入请求
把多余的 segment 打包上传到远端对象存储归档
merge：把多个 segment 合并成一个新 segment，并移除旧的
options_en: Automatically delete the oldest segments outright to free up space
Reject any new write requests until the merge finishes
Package the excess segments and upload them to remote object storage for archiving
Merge: combine several segments into a new one and remove the old ones
why: 段合并把碎片化的 segment 归并成大 segment，顺带物理清理软删除的数据。
why_en: Lucene merges numerous small segments into a new larger one and removes the old segments.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What does Lucene do when there are too many segments?
optionExplanations: 合并不会把最老的数据直接删掉，它只是重新组织数据。
segment 太多会拖慢查询，但不会导致 Lucene 拒绝新的写入请求。
段合并是本地磁盘上的操作，不涉及上传到远端对象存储。
merge 把多个 segment 合并成一个新的更大 segment，并顺带移除旧的、清理软删除的数据。
optionExplanations_en: Merging doesn't drop the oldest data outright — it just reorganizes it.
Too many segments slows queries, but it doesn't make Lucene reject new writes.
Segment merging is a local-disk operation, not an upload to remote object storage.
A merge folds several segments into one larger new segment, removing the old ones and cleaning up soft-deleted data along the way.

q: segment 不可变，删除文档是怎么实现的？
options: 就地重写那个 segment 文件的内容，把这条记录去掉
维护「已删除 ID 集合」做软删除：查询时假装不存在，数据仍在，merge 时才真正清理
删除请求一到就立即把数据从磁盘上物理抹除干净
把被删除的文档统一挪到一个专门的回收站索引里保存
options_en: Rewrite that segment file's content in place to drop the record
Maintain a deleted-id set for a soft delete: the query hides it while the data stays until a merge cleans it up
Physically erase the data from disk the instant the delete request arrives
Move deleted documents into a dedicated trash index for safekeeping
why: 每个 segment 带一个删除标记集合；被删文档查询时被跳过但数据还在，直到段合并时才物理清除。删除因此非常快。
why_en: Deletes are soft: the segment marks the document as deleted and hides it from queries, and merges later physically remove it.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: If segments are immutable, how is a document delete implemented?
optionExplanations: segment 不可变，不会被就地重写去掉一条记录。
维护一份「已删除 ID」集合做软删除：查询时跳过它，数据本体保留到 merge 才真正清掉。
物理数据其实还留在原地，直到 merge 才被清除，不是删除请求一到就抹除。
Elasticsearch 没有专门的回收站索引这种设计。
optionExplanations_en: Segments are immutable, so a record never gets removed by rewriting the file in place.
It keeps a set of deleted IDs as a soft-delete marker — queries skip that document, but the data stays on disk until a merge actually clears it.
The physical data actually stays put until a merge runs — it isn't wiped the instant a delete request arrives.
There's no dedicated 'recycle bin' index in Elasticsearch's design.

q: 为什么在 Elasticsearch 里「更新」比「插入」性能更差？
options: 更新操作需要给整个集群加上一把全局互斥锁才能进行写入操作
更新操作必须同步等待数据真正刷盘落地完成之后才能返回结果
更新 = 软删旧文档 + 插入新文档，多出软删除的簿记，且在 merge 清理前留下持续的性能拖累
一次更新会让集群里全部的查询缓存瞬间统统失效并重新构建
options_en: An update requires taking a global mutex lock across the whole cluster before it can proceed
An update must synchronously wait for the data to actually flush and land on disk before it can return
An update is a soft delete plus a new insert, adding bookkeeping that lingers until a merge cleans it up
A single update instantly invalidates and forces a rebuild of every query cache in the cluster
why: 更新不改 segment，而是软删 + 重插，代价高于纯插入；这正是 ES 不适合「频繁更新的数据」的底层原因。
why_en: An update soft-deletes the old document and inserts a new one, adding bookkeeping overhead that lingers until segments merge, which is why Elasticsearch dislikes rapidly updating data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: Why are updates slower than inserts in Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 更新路径不涉及给整个集群加全局互斥锁。
刷盘策略对插入和更新是一致的，不是更新独有的额外负担。
更新 = 软删旧文档 + 插入新文档，多出一份簿记，在 merge 清理前一直拖着性能。
这里说的是索引层机制，不会让全部查询缓存瞬间失效重建。
optionExplanations_en: The update path doesn't involve taking a global cluster-wide lock.
Flush policy is the same for inserts and updates — it isn't an update-specific tax.
An update is really a soft-delete of the old document plus an insert of a new one, adding bookkeeping that drags on performance until the next merge cleans it up.
This is an index-layer mechanism, not something that invalidates and rebuilds every query cache at once.

q: 不可变 segment 带来哪些好处？（多选）
options: 新文档直接进新 segment，写入吞吐高
可以放心缓存和更高效压缩，无一致性顾虑
读操作不怕数据中途被改，并发和崩溃恢复都更简单
更新可以就地修改文档，最高效
options_en: New documents go straight into new segments for high write throughput
Data can be safely cached and compressed with no consistency worries
Reads never worry about data changing mid-query, simplifying concurrency and crash recovery
Updates can modify documents in place for maximum efficiency
why: 不可变换来：快写入、安全缓存、优化压缩、简化并发、易恢复、更快搜索。代价是要周期性 merge，且清理前占用额外存储。
why_en: Immutability speeds writes, enables safe caching and better compression, and simplifies concurrency and recovery, at the cost of periodic merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: Which benefits come from immutable segments? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 新文档直接进新 segment，不用碰旧数据，写入吞吐因此更高。
数据写成后不会再变，缓存和压缩都能放心做，不用担心失效一致性问题。
读不用处理数据被并发改写的情况，崩溃恢复的逻辑也更简单。
这里正好和不可变性矛盾——segment 恰恰不支持就地修改文档。
optionExplanations_en: New documents land straight in a fresh segment without touching old ones, which is why write throughput stays high.
Once data is written it never changes again, so caching and compression can proceed without worrying about invalidation.
Reads never have to handle data being modified underneath them, which also makes crash recovery simpler.
This directly contradicts immutability — segments specifically don't support editing a document in place.

q: 不可变 segment 设计的主要代价是？
options: 需要周期性段合并，且清理完成前暂时占用更多存储
所有的读请求都会因此明显变慢
这套设计导致完全没法做全文搜索
这套设计导致索引没办法再配置副本
options_en: Periodic segment merging is required, with temporarily higher storage until cleanup finishes
Every read request would become noticeably slower because of this
This design makes full-text search completely impossible
This design makes it impossible to configure replicas for the index
why: 软删除的数据在 merge 前一直占着空间、拖着查询，merge 本身也消耗 I/O 和 CPU——这是拿空间和后台工作换读写性能。
why_en: The price of immutability is periodic segment merging and temporarily higher storage until deleted data is cleaned up.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What is the main cost of immutable segments?
optionExplanations: 需要周期性段合并，且在清理完成前，软删数据会暂时多占存储空间。
不可变设计整体上是为了让读更快更简单，不是让读请求变慢。
不可变性不影响全文搜索这个能力本身，两者没有冲突。
副本机制是独立配置，跟 segment 是否可变没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: It needs periodic segment merges, and until cleanup finishes, soft-deleted data temporarily takes up extra storage.
Immutability is meant to make reads faster and simpler overall — it doesn't slow requests down.
Immutability doesn't take away full-text search capability itself — the two aren't in conflict.
Replica configuration is independent of whether segments are mutable.

q: 倒排索引（inverted index）是什么？它为什么让关键词搜索快？
options: 把全部文档按照 ID 从小到大排好序，存成的一份列表
从「词 → 含该词的文档列表」的映射：把 O(n) 全量扫描变成近似 O(1) 的查找
对文档的原始内容整体做一次 gzip 压缩后存起来
把出现过的所有词，都存进一棵普通的平衡二叉树里
options_en: A list of every document sorted from smallest to largest id
A mapping from term to the documents containing it, turning an O(n) scan into a near O(1) lookup
A single gzip compression pass run over the raw document content
Storing every term that ever appeared in an ordinary balanced binary tree
why: 为每个唯一词记录它出现在哪些文档里——找「含 lazy 的书」不再扫 10 亿本书，直接查表。这是「复制数据并按检索方式重排」的经典应用。
why_en: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning a linear scan into a near constant-time lookup.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["term bill"] --> B["doc 1"]
  A --> C["doc 7"]
  D["term nye"] --> C
  D --> E["doc 9"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

q_en: What is an inverted index, and why does it make keyword search fast?
optionExplanations: 按 ID 排好序的一份列表不能直接支持按关键词查找。
从「词→含该词的文档列表」的映射入手，把全量扫描变成近似 O(1) 的直接查表。
gzip 压缩解决的是存储体积问题，不解决查找效率问题。
平衡二叉树擅长范围顺序查询，不是词到文档集合的映射结构。
optionExplanations_en: A list simply sorted by document ID can't directly support keyword lookup.
It maps each word to the list of documents containing it, turning a full scan into an almost O(1) table lookup.
gzip compression solves a storage-size problem, not a lookup-efficiency problem.
A balanced binary tree is good at ordered range queries, not at mapping a word to its set of documents.

q: doc values 是什么结构？解决什么问题？
options: 写入的同时自动生成一份文档的备份副本存起来
专门缓存最近几次查询结果、加速重复查询的查询缓存
在倒排索引基础上做进一步压缩得到的一个压缩版本
某个字段跨全段文档的列式连续存储：让「对匹配结果按 price 排序」不必读整行文档
options_en: A backup copy of the document automatically generated alongside the write itself
A dedicated query cache that speeds up repeated queries by storing recent results
A further-compressed version built on top of the inverted index
A columnar contiguous store of one field across all documents in a segment, so sorting by price avoids reading whole rows
why: 行式存储取单列也要读整行；doc values 像 Spark/Redshift 一样按列连续存储单字段，排序聚合时只读需要的那一列。
why_en: Doc values store one field for all documents in a columnar contiguous layout, so sorting and aggregations read only that column instead of whole rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字段列式连续存储的结构，支撑排序和聚合而不必读整行文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Doc values store one field for all documents in a columnar layout so sorting and aggregation avoid reading whole rows.

q_en: What structure are doc values, and what problem do they solve?
optionExplanations: doc values 不是写入时自动生成的备份副本，它是查询期要用的结构。
它不是缓存最近查询结果的东西，而是持久化落盘的列式数据。
它和倒排索引是两个独立结构，不是在倒排基础上再压缩出来的版本。
它把某个字段跨全段文档按列连续存储，排序聚合时只读这一列，不必读整行文档。
optionExplanations_en: doc values aren't an automatic backup copy generated at write time — it's a structure used during queries.
It isn't a cache of recent query results, it's persisted, on-disk columnar data.
It's a separate structure from the inverted index, not a further-compressed version built on top of it.
It stores one field contiguously by column across a whole segment, so sorting or aggregating only reads that column instead of the entire row.

q: 倒排索引与 doc values 在一次「搜索 + 按价格排序」里的分工是？
options: 倒排索引负责找出匹配的文档，doc values 提供这些文档的 price 列做最终排序
倒排索引和 doc values 其实都是用来找文档的
反过来，doc values 负责找文档，倒排索引负责排序
倒排索引只在写入文档时用到，查询时用不上
options_en: The inverted index finds matching documents while doc values supply the price column for the final sort
Both the inverted index and doc values are actually used to find documents
The reverse: doc values find documents and the inverted index does the sorting
The inverted index is only touched during writes and plays no role at query time
tradeoff: 倒排索引找文档（行方向）vs doc values 排序聚合（列方向）
why: token → 文档靠倒排索引；文档 → 排序字段值靠 doc values。一个管「找到谁」，一个管「按什么排」。
why_en: The inverted index finds which documents match, and doc values supply the field values needed to sort those matches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字段列式连续存储的结构，支撑排序和聚合而不必读整行文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Doc values store one field for all documents in a columnar layout so sorting and aggregation avoid reading whole rows.

q_en: How do the inverted index and doc values split work in search plus price sorting?
optionExplanations: 关键词先靠倒排索引找出候选文档，doc values 再给这些文档的排序字段值——两步各管一段。
只在不需要排序聚合的纯词项查询时，doc values 可能才不参与。
doc values 是列式取值结构，负责不了从 token 找文档这一步。
倒排索引在查询的 query 阶段同样要用，不是只在写入时起作用。
optionExplanations_en: Keywords first find candidate documents through the inverted index, then doc values supply the sort field values for those documents — two separate steps.
doc values might sit out only for a pure term-match query that needs no sorting or aggregation at all.
doc values is a columnar lookup structure — it can't do the token-to-document step.
The inverted index gets used during the query stage too, not only while writing.

q: coordinating 节点上的查询规划器（query planner）靠什么决定执行方式？
options: 每次都在几种候选执行计划里完全随机挑选一个来执行
永远严格按照查询语句里写下来的先后顺序依次执行
统计信息：字段类型、热门关键词、文档长度等，动态选出最省时间的执行顺序
执行方式的选择只取决于集群里一共有多少个节点
options_en: Randomly picking one of several candidate execution plans completely at random each time
Always strictly executing step by step in the exact order the query was written in
Statistics like field types, popular terms, and document lengths, to dynamically pick the cheapest execution order
The choice of execution style depends only on how many nodes the cluster happens to have
why: 规划器基于统计选择用哪个索引、按什么顺序执行、如何合并多节点结果；「数据依赖」的自适应正是数据库系统强大的原因。
why_en: The query planner uses statistics on fields, term popularity, and document lengths to pick the cheapest execution order dynamically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 coordinating 节点上依据统计信息选择最优执行方式的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query planner is the component on the coordinating node that uses statistics to choose the cheapest execution plan.

q_en: What does the query planner on a coordinating node use to choose an execution plan?
optionExplanations: 真要随机挑，性能会完全不可预测，跟实际表现不符。
严格按语句写下的顺序执行等于忽视统计信息，会错失很大的优化空间。
规划器基于字段类型、热门关键词、文档长度等统计信息，动态选出最省时间的执行顺序。
节点数只是集群拓扑信息，不是查询代价估算依赖的关键统计量。
optionExplanations_en: If it really picked at random, performance would be unpredictable, which doesn't match reality.
Strictly following the order written in the query would ignore statistics and miss a lot of optimization headroom.
The planner uses statistics like field type, popular terms, and document length to dynamically pick the fastest execution order.
Node count is just cluster topology, not a key statistic for estimating query cost.

q: 搜索 "bill nye"：倒排索引里 "bill" 有几百万条、"nye" 只有几百条。高效的执行方式是？
options: 先把 "bill" 那几百万条候选文档全部扫一遍再处理
从小集合入手：以 "nye" 的几百条为基础做交集/验证，避免碰几百万条的大集合
干脆放弃倒排索引带来的优势，直接全表扫描所有文档
把两个词各自的候选集都并行全量展开出来，再求交集
options_en: Scan through all of bill's millions of candidate documents first and process from there
Start from the small set: intersect against nye's few hundred postings and avoid touching the millions for bill
Give up the inverted index's advantage entirely and just full-scan every document
Fully expand each term's own candidate set in parallel and then intersect them
why: 不同执行顺序性能差几个数量级；从稀有词的小结果集出发再验证短语，是规划器靠词频统计做的典型优化。
why_en: Starting from the rare term's few hundred postings and intersecting is orders of magnitude cheaper than expanding the common term's millions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 coordinating 节点上依据统计信息选择最优执行方式的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query planner is the component on the coordinating node that uses statistics to choose the cheapest execution plan.

q_en: For the search "bill nye", with millions of "bill" hits and hundreds of "nye" hits, what is efficient?
optionExplanations: 先碰几百万条候选，后续交集运算的基数被拉得很高，代价最大。
从 "nye" 的几百条小集合入手做验证，避免一上来就处理几百万条的大集合。
全表扫描是最慢的兜底方式，规划器不会主动放弃索引优势去选它。
两边都并行全量展开，等于百万级集合的开销一分没省。
optionExplanations_en: Starting from the few-million-document set makes every downstream intersection operate on a huge base — the most expensive path.
Starting from "nye"'s small few-hundred set and verifying against it avoids ever touching the million-document set.
A full scan is the slowest fallback — the planner wouldn't deliberately give up the index's advantage for it.
Expanding both terms in full in parallel still pays the full cost of the million-row set — nothing is saved.

q: 面试中 Elasticsearch 最常见的接入方式是？
options: 通过 CDC（Change Data Capture）挂在权威数据库（如 Postgres / DynamoDB）旁边做搜索层
把 Elasticsearch 当成系统里唯一的持久化数据库长期使用
用 Elasticsearch 直接替换掉 Kafka 这一类消息队列系统
仅仅把 Elasticsearch 当成前端页面渲染用的缓存层而已
options_en: Attached as a search layer via change data capture next to an authoritative store like Postgres or DynamoDB
Used long-term as the system's sole persistent database
Used as a direct replacement for an entire message queue system like Kafka
Used merely as a cache layer for rendering front-end pages, nothing more
why: 权威数据留在主库，变更通过 CDC 流进 Elasticsearch 供搜索——Elasticsearch 是「衍生数据」层，不是 source of truth。
why_en: In interviews Elasticsearch is usually attached via change data capture to an authoritative store like Postgres or DynamoDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续捕获权威数据库变更并同步到下游系统的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change data capture continuously streams changes from an authoritative database to downstream systems.

q_en: What is the most common way to connect Elasticsearch in a system-design interview?
optionExplanations: 权威数据留在主库，靠 CDC 把变更流实时同步进它做搜索层，这是最稳妥的接入方式。
ES 的持久性历史上不够稳固，不该把它当成系统唯一的持久化数据库。
ES 不提供消息队列那种持久投递语义，替代不了 Kafka 这类系统。
它确实能加速查询，但角色是搜索引擎，不只是给前端渲染用的缓存层。
optionExplanations_en: Authoritative data stays in the primary store, and CDC streams changes into it in real time as the search layer — the steadiest way to wire it in.
Elasticsearch's durability has historically been shaky, so it shouldn't be the system's sole persistent database.
Elasticsearch doesn't offer the durable delivery guarantees of a message queue — it can't replace something like Kafka.
It does speed up queries, but its role is a search engine, not just a rendering cache for the frontend.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 把 Elasticsearch 当主数据库（唯一持久存储）的问题是？
options: 主要问题只是查询响应速度太慢
它是搜索引擎不是数据库：历史上有一致性与持久性问题，需要持久的数据应放在别处
Elasticsearch 根本没办法存储 JSON 格式的数据
主要问题在于它的存储成本太贵
options_en: The main issue is simply that query response would be too slow
It is a search engine, not a database, with a history of consistency and durability issues, so data that must persist belongs elsewhere
Elasticsearch simply has no way to store JSON-formatted data
The main issue is that its storage cost would be too high
why: Elasticsearch 首先是搜索引擎；早期版本的持久性/一致性问题（类似 CouchDB 踩过的坑）说明：需要保证不丢的数据别只放 Elasticsearch。
why_en: Elasticsearch is a search engine first, with a history of consistency and durability issues, so data that must persist belongs in a real database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一个历史上曾有持久性与一致性争议的文档数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CouchDB is another document database with a historical reputation for consistency and durability issues.

q_en: What is wrong with using Elasticsearch as the only primary database?
optionExplanations: 查询速度不是把它当主库的主要风险，一致性和持久性才是。
它首先是搜索引擎不是数据库，历史上有一致性和持久性问题，需要保证不丢的数据不该只放这里。
ES 的文档本身就是 JSON，这个说法本身就不成立。
存储成本不是核心问题，数据安全性才是真正的风险点。
optionExplanations_en: Query speed isn't the main risk of using it as the primary store — consistency and durability are.
It's a search engine first, not a database — it has a history of consistency and durability gaps, so data you can't afford to lose shouldn't live only here.
Elasticsearch documents are JSON by nature, so that claim doesn't hold.
Storage cost isn't the core issue — data safety is the real risk.

scenario: 社交产品想在搜索结果里展示帖子的点赞数和曝光数，这些计数每秒都在变，有人提议直接在 ES 文档里加字段实时更新。
q: 更合理的做法是？
options: 照做，每次用户点赞都实时更新一次 Elasticsearch 文档
改成每隔一小时，把整个索引从头到尾全量重建一次
计数放权威存储/缓存，经写缓冲批量异步刷进 Elasticsearch（或查询时再取计数）
干脆在搜索结果页面里，把这些计数字段全部隐藏不展示
options_en: Do it anyway, updating the Elasticsearch document in real time on every single like
Switch to rebuilding the entire index from scratch, start to finish, once every hour
Keep counters in an authoritative store or cache and batch-flush them into Elasticsearch asynchronously, or fetch counts at query time
Simply hide these count fields entirely and stop showing them on the results page
tradeoff: 高频写入的实时性 vs Elasticsearch 更新（软删+重插）的代价
why: Elasticsearch 面向读多写少：更新 = 软删+重插，高频计数更新会让它挣扎。写缓冲/批量同步或读时补充计数才是对的。
why_en: Elasticsearch is built for read-heavy workloads, so rapidly changing counters should be buffered and batched into it rather than written per event.
whenOtherWins: 字段更新频率低（如商品标题偶尔改）时，直接更新 Elasticsearch 文档完全没问题。

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What is the more reasonable design?
scenario_en: A social product wants likes and impression counts in search results; those counters change every second, and someone suggests updating the ES document on every event.
optionExplanations: 计数更新频率很低、能容忍短暂旧值时可以直接写 ES；这里是每秒都变，每次点赞都触发软删+重插，会拖垮集群。
只有离线批处理、能接受长时间旧数据时才适合整索引重建；一小时一次实时性太差。
计数放权威存储/缓存，写缓冲批量异步刷进 ES，或查询时再补充计数——把高频写路径和搜索索引解耦。
产品能接受不展示计数时才算需求层的取舍；这里是回避问题，不是方案。
optionExplanations_en: Direct real-time writes are fine when counters change rarely and staleness is tolerable — here they change every second, so each like triggers a soft-delete-plus-reinsert that would bog the cluster down.
A full index rebuild only fits offline batch work that can tolerate long staleness — once an hour is far too stale here.
Keep counts in an authoritative store or cache and flush them into Elasticsearch in async batches (or fetch them at query time) — decoupling the hot write path from the search index.
Hiding the counters is only a legitimate product tradeoff if the business accepts it — here it just avoids the problem instead of solving it.

q: 使用 Elasticsearch 时必须向面试官承认的一致性事实是？
options: 搜索结果一定是最终一致的，会读到过期数据，有时滞后明显；不能容忍就要换方案
Elasticsearch 对跨文档操作提供可串行化事务保证
Elasticsearch 每次写入都是同步落盘的强一致操作
主分片和副本之间的数据永远保持瞬时一致
options_en: Search results are eventually consistent and can be stale, sometimes noticeably, so an intolerant use case needs a different approach
Elasticsearch provides serializable transaction guarantees across documents
Every Elasticsearch write is a synchronously flushed, strongly consistent operation
Data between the primary shard and its replicas is always instantaneously in sync
why: 从写入到可搜索有延迟，CDC 同步又加一层滞后——结果「必然」stale。设计时要明说这一点并确认业务能容忍。
why_en: Elasticsearch is eventually consistent, so search results will be stale, sometimes significantly, and the design must tolerate that.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后不保证立刻可见，短暂之后各副本才收敛到一致状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a write is not guaranteed to be immediately visible, only visible after some delay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片的完整拷贝，用于故障恢复和分担查询流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a full copy of a shard, used for failover and to share query load.

q_en: What consistency fact must you acknowledge when using Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 结果必然是最终一致的，会读到过期数据，有时滞后还很明显——不能容忍就得换方案。
Elasticsearch 不提供跨文档的可串行化事务保证。
写入到可搜索之间存在刷新延迟，不是同步落盘的强一致操作。
主副本之间的同步也有延迟窗口，不是瞬时一致。
optionExplanations_en: Results are necessarily eventually consistent — you can read stale data, sometimes noticeably delayed, and if the business can't tolerate that you need a different approach.
Elasticsearch doesn't offer serializable transactions across documents.
There's a refresh delay between writing and being searchable — it isn't a synchronous, strongly consistent write.
Replica sync also has a delay window — it isn't instantaneously consistent either.

q: 在 Elasticsearch 里建模数据的指导原则是？
options: 像关系型数据库一样，严格遵守三范式，尽量避免出现任何数据冗余
把数据拆分到多个不同的索引里，查询时再手动跨索引做 join 关联
每个文档只放一个字段，字段和字段之间各自单独建一份文档存储
尽量反范式化：Elasticsearch 不是关系库，目标是 1-2 个查询就拿到结果，宁可写入侧多做转换
options_en: Strictly follow third normal form like a relational database, avoiding any data redundancy at all costs
Split data across many different indices and manually join across them at query time
Put only one field per document, with every field living in its own separate document
Denormalize aggressively, since Elasticsearch is not relational and the goal is one or two queries per request, even if the write side does more transformation
why: Elasticsearch 没有 join，把数据按查询模式摊平（denormalize），写入时做转换，换取查询侧的高效。
why_en: Denormalize aggressively since Elasticsearch is not relational, aiming to answer each request with one or two queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为查询效率牺牲数据冗余，把关联数据摊平进同一文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization trades data redundancy for query efficiency by flattening related data into one document.

q_en: What is the guiding rule for modeling data in Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 严格三范式会迫使查询侧做大量关联，而 ES 并不擅长这个。
ES 没有原生 join，跨索引关联要靠应用层自己拼，这个前提假设不成立。
一个字段一个文档会让最基本的查询都要多次往返，粒度切得太碎。
尽量反范式化：目标是 1-2 个查询就拿到结果，宁可写入时多做转换，把关联成本挪到写路径。
optionExplanations_en: Strict third normal form forces the query side to do heavy joining, which isn't what Elasticsearch is good at.
Elasticsearch has no native join — cross-index relations have to be stitched together in the app layer, so this assumption doesn't hold.
One field per document would make even the simplest query take multiple round trips — the grain is cut too fine.
Lean toward denormalizing: aim for 1-2 queries to get an answer, doing the extra transformation at write time instead of query time.

scenario: 内部工具要给不到 10 万条、很少变化的记录加个搜索框。
q: 合理的第一步是？
options: 直接部署三节点 Elasticsearch 集群
先用主数据库的简单查询/全文索引，确实不够再考虑 Elasticsearch
上 Kafka + Elasticsearch + CDC 全家桶
自研倒排索引
options_en: Deploy a three-node Elasticsearch cluster right away
Start with a simple query or full-text index on the primary database, and only reach for Elasticsearch if that's insufficient
Bring in the full Kafka plus Elasticsearch plus CDC stack
Build a custom inverted index from scratch
tradeoff: 架构简洁性 vs 提前引入专用搜索引擎的能力上限
why: 数据小（<100k 文档）或极少变化时，主库查询往往又快又省事；Elasticsearch 的运维和同步成本只在确有必要时才值得。
why_en: For under a hundred thousand rarely changing documents, a simple query on the primary store usually suffices before reaching for Elasticsearch.
whenOtherWins: 数据量大、需要相关性排序/faceting/模糊匹配时，就该升级到 Elasticsearch 了。

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续捕获权威数据库变更并同步到下游系统的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change data capture continuously streams changes from an authoritative database to downstream systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

q_en: What is the reasonable first step?
scenario_en: An internal tool needs a search box over fewer than 100k records that rarely change.
optionExplanations: 搜索已成为核心路径、主库明显扛不住时才值得部署专用集群；不到 10 万条、很少变化的数据这样做是过度设计。
数据小、变化少、搜索需求简单时，先用主数据库自带的查询或全文索引最省事，不够用再升级。
需要可靠变更流和独立搜索集群时才上 CDC 全链路；这个规模同步链路和运维成本都不值当。
只有教学目的或极特殊约束才自研倒排索引，正常场景直接用现成实现。
optionExplanations_en: A dedicated cluster is worth deploying once search becomes the critical path and the primary database clearly can't keep up — for under 100k rarely-changing records, that's over-engineering.
When the data is small, rarely changes, and search needs are simple, start with the primary database's own query or full-text features and upgrade only if that stops being enough.
The full CDC pipeline earns its keep when you need a reliable change stream and an independent search cluster — at this scale the sync plumbing and ops cost aren't worth it.
Rolling your own inverted index only makes sense for teaching or very unusual constraints — normal cases should just use an existing implementation.

scenario: 商品、帖子或店铺的权威数据存在主库里，CDC 把变更同步到 Elasticsearch，ES 只负责搜索索引。
q: Elasticsearch 与底层权威数据的同步失败，会导致什么？如何应对？
options: Elasticsearch 会自动知道哪里漂移，并自己回源修复
同步失败只会稍微拖慢一点点写入速度，完全不影响查询结果的正确性
搜索索引与 source of truth 发生 drift，要监控同步并从真相源对账/重建
同步只要一失败，整个集群就会立刻直接宕机彻底崩溃，谁都没法恢复
options_en: Elasticsearch automatically knows which records drifted and repairs itself from the source
A sync failure only slows writes down a little and does not affect the correctness of query results at all
The search index drifts from the source of truth, so sync monitoring plus reconciliation or reindexing is needed
The instant sync fails, the entire cluster crashes hard and completely, with no way to recover
why: drift 是 ES 索引和主库真相不一致：搜索可能漏新数据、显示旧数据或搜到已删除数据。修复依赖真相源或可 replay 的变更日志，而不是 ES 自己凭空恢复。
why_en: Drift means the Elasticsearch index no longer matches the source of truth; repair depends on the primary store or replayable change log, not Elasticsearch magically healing itself.
whenOtherWins: 如果权威数据或可重放事件日志也丢了，就不能可靠重建 ES；只能从备份、审计日志或业务补录里恢复。

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续捕获权威数据库变更并同步到下游系统的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change data capture continuously streams changes from an authoritative database to downstream systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真相源：系统认定最权威、可用来恢复衍生数据的主数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the authoritative store used to recover derived data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漂移：衍生索引里的数据和权威数据源不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drift is when a derived index no longer matches the authoritative source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对账：定期比较 ES 与主库，找出缺失、过期或多余的索引记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reconciliation compares Elasticsearch with the primary store to find missing, stale, or extra indexed records.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重建索引：从权威数据源重新生成 Elasticsearch 索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reindexing rebuilds the Elasticsearch index from the authoritative data source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重放：从 CDC、Kafka 或事件日志重新应用遗漏的变更。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replay reapplies missed changes from CDC, Kafka, or an event log.

q_en: What happens if Elasticsearch falls out of sync with the source of truth, and how do you handle it?
scenario_en: Products, posts, or stores live in a primary database; CDC syncs changes into Elasticsearch, which is only the search index.
optionExplanations: ES 不知道主库最新状态，不会自己发现漂移并回源修复，这个说法夸大了它的能力。
影响不只是拖慢写入速度那么轻，用户可能搜不到新数据、看到旧数据甚至搜到已删数据。
搜索索引会和 source of truth 产生 drift，要靠监控发现、再从真相源（重建或 CDC/Kafka replay）对账修复。
同步失败不会让整个集群立刻宕机，只是索引内容变得不可信，服务仍在跑。
optionExplanations_en: Elasticsearch doesn't know the primary's latest state and won't self-detect drift and heal itself — that overstates what it can do.
The impact isn't just a minor write-speed hit — users can miss new data, see stale data, or even find results that were already deleted.
The search index drifts away from the source of truth; you need monitoring to catch it and a reconcile/rebuild from the true source (or CDC/Kafka replay) to fix it.
Sync failures don't crash the whole cluster outright — the service keeps running, it's just the index contents that become untrustworthy.

q: 把「为什么用 ES 并挂 CDC」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 代价：双存储、最终一致，索引可能与主库漂移
需求：全文搜索 + 多条件过滤 + 相关性排序 + faceting
缓解：CDC 从权威库持续同步，加监控与对账
选型：Elasticsearch 作为搜索层，权威数据留在主库
tradeoff: 衍生搜索层的开发效率 vs 双存储带来的最终一致性代价
why: 需求（复合搜索）→ 选型（ES 做衍生搜索层）→ 代价（stale/漂移）→ 缓解（CDC + 监控）。这是面试里 ES 的标准叙事。
why_en: Complex search needs lead to Elasticsearch as a derived search layer, whose staleness and drift are mitigated with change data capture and monitoring.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    R["需求：复合搜索"] --> C["选型：ES 搜索层"]
    C --> K["代价：最终一致/漂移"]
    K --> M["缓解：CDC + 监控对账"]

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change data capture continuously streams changes from an authoritative database to downstream systems.

q: 把一次「文档更新」在 Lucene 内部的过程排成正确顺序：
steps: 新版本作为新文档写入新的 segment
后台段合并时物理清理被软删的数据
客户端发出文档更新请求
旧版本文档被打上软删除标记
why: 更新 = 软删旧 + 写新 + merge 清理。理解这条链就明白为什么更新比插入贵、为什么删除很快但有滞后代价。
why_en: An update soft-deletes the old version, writes the new version into a fresh segment, and relies on a later merge to physically clean up.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Update doc"] --> B["Mark old deleted"]
  B --> C["Index new version"]
  C --> D["Merge cleans later"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

scenario: 查询 keyword=redis 时，Lucene 先要在词典里找到 redis 这个 term，再跳到它对应的 postings list（文档列表）。
q: 补全 Lucene 倒排索引用到的辅助数据结构：
text: 除倒排表本身，Lucene 还用 {{skip list}}（跳表）和 {{finite state transducer}}（有限状态转换器，FST）等专用结构加速词项查找与合并。
why: 这里的“补全”是填空，不是 autocomplete。FST 优化的是 term dictionary：用很小的自动机判断词是否存在，并映射到 postings list 的位置。
why_en: Here, completion means filling the blank, not autocomplete. An FST optimizes the term dictionary: it compactly checks whether a term exists and maps it to the posting-list location.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Q["query term: redis"] --> FST["FST term dictionary"]
    FST -->|"exists + pointer"| P["postings list"]
    P --> D["doc IDs + positions"]
    P --> S["skip list jumps"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有已索引词项的有序词典，负责把查询词定位到对应倒排表的位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The term dictionary is the sorted vocabulary of indexed terms; it maps a query term to the location of its postings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许跳跃式查找的有序链表结构，加速倒排表内的定位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A skip list is an ordered linked structure that allows jump-ahead lookups to speed up posting list traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种像压缩 trie 的有限状态机：沿字符路径走到词尾，同时输出一个值，例如 postings list 的指针。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A finite state transducer is a compact trie-like automaton: it follows characters to a term and outputs a value such as a postings pointer.

q: 即使不用 ES，也能从它的设计里借鉴哪些经验？（多选）
options: 在合适的层使用不可变数据，换取缓存、压缩与并发的简化
把查询执行与数据存储分离，各自独立优化（协调节点 vs 数据节点）
按最常见的查询模式组织甚至复制数据（倒排索引、doc values）
分布式架构会自动带来强一致，无需权衡
options_en: Use immutable data at the right layer to simplify caching, compression, and concurrency
Separate query execution from data storage so each can be optimized independently, like coordinating vs data nodes
Organize or even duplicate data around the most common query patterns, like inverted indexes and doc values
Distributed architecture automatically gives you strong consistency with no trade-off
why: immutability、执行/存储分离、面向查询的索引结构是三大可迁移经验；分布式恰恰要求你直面 CAP 权衡而不是免除它。
why_en: Elasticsearch teaches immutability, separating query execution from storage, and structuring data for query patterns, while distribution still forces CAP trade-offs.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字段列式连续存储的结构，支撑排序和聚合而不必读整行文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Doc values store one field for all documents in a columnar layout so sorting and aggregation avoid reading whole rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统在网络分区下，一致性和可用性最多只能二选一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

q_en: Even if you do not use Elasticsearch, which design lessons are reusable? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 在合适的层用不可变数据，换来缓存、压缩和并发处理的简化，这是 segment 设计给的经验。
把查询执行和数据存储分离、各自独立优化——协调节点和数据节点的分工就是直接例子。
按最常见的查询模式组织甚至复制数据——倒排索引和 doc values 就是两个具体产物。
这个说法和 CAP 矛盾：分布式系统必须直面一致性和可用性的权衡，不能靠架构自动免除它。
optionExplanations_en: Using immutable data at the right layer buys simpler caching, compression, and concurrency — that's the lesson segment design teaches.
Separating query execution from data storage so each can be tuned independently — the coordinating/data node split is a direct example.
Organizing or even duplicating data around the most common query patterns — the inverted index and doc values are two concrete products of that.
This contradicts CAP: distributed systems have to face the consistency/availability tradeoff head-on, not get it waived by architecture.

q: 在「读写职责分离」维度上，data 节点与 coordinating 节点的关系是？
options: data 节点和 coordinating 节点做的其实是完全一样的工作
反过来，coordinating 节点负责存数据，data 节点负责管路由
data 节点专注存储与本地搜索执行，coordinating 节点专注解析、分发与合并——各自优化、互为补充
data 节点只负责处理写入请求，不参与搜索执行
options_en: Data nodes and coordinating nodes actually do exactly the same work
The reverse: coordinating nodes store data and data nodes handle routing
Data nodes focus on storage and local search execution while coordinating nodes focus on parsing, routing, and merging, each optimized independently
Data nodes only handle write requests and take no part in search execution
tradeoff: 存储与本地执行（data 节点）vs 请求编排与合并（coordinating 节点）
why: 存储与查询编排分离让两类节点可按各自瓶颈独立扩展和调优，是 Elasticsearch 架构的一条核心设计经验。
why_en: Data nodes focus on storage and local search execution while coordinating nodes parse, route, and merge, letting each be optimized independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实际存储文档和索引结构的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data node is where documents and their index structures are actually stored.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coordinating node is the entry point that receives client requests, routes queries, and merges results.

q_en: On read/write responsibility separation, how do Data nodes and Coordinating nodes relate?
optionExplanations: 若真的完全一样，就没必要区分出两种节点类型了。
这是把职责说反了：实际是 data 存数据、coordinating 管路由，不是反过来。
存储瓶颈和查询编排瓶颈往往不同，分给两类节点各自独立扩展调优时最合适。
data 节点既参与写入也执行本地搜索，不是只处理写请求。
optionExplanations_en: If the two really did identical work, there'd be no reason to have two node types at all.
This has the roles reversed — data actually stores data and coordinating handles routing, not the other way around.
Storage bottlenecks and query-orchestration bottlenecks are usually different, so splitting them across two node types lets each scale and tune independently.
Data nodes both take writes and execute local search — they aren't write-only.

scenario: 业务方要一份「每天早上出的昨日点击报表」，有人提议直接上 Flink 流处理集群来生成它。
scenario_en: The business wants a report for yesterday's clicks every morning, and someone proposes generating it with a Flink streaming cluster.
q: 更合理的选择是？
q_en: What is the better choice for this daily click report?
options: 上 Flink 集群，反正流处理什么都能算
自己再写一套流处理框架来算这份报表
批处理（如 Spark）——先问「真的需要实时延迟吗？」
把报表聚合逻辑直接塞进 Kafka broker 里跑
options_en: Stand up a Flink cluster — stream processing can compute anything anyway.
Build a custom streaming framework just for this report.
Batch processing like Spark — first ask whether you really need real-time latency.
Push the report aggregation logic straight into the Kafka broker.
why: 「昨日报表」是天级延迟，流处理省下的秒级实时性完全用不上，却背上一整套额外运维成本。
why_en: A once-a-day report has day-level latency tolerance, so streaming buys you nothing while adding a full extra ops burden.
whenOtherWins: 当业务确实要求秒级/分钟级的实时结果（实时风控、实时大盘），才值得引入 Flink。
tradeoff: 批处理的简单省钱 vs 流处理的实时性

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Spark，一个通用的批处理/微批计算引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Spark is a general-purpose batch and micro-batch compute engine.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Kafka，一个分布式消息队列/日志系统，常作为流处理的数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Kafka is a distributed log-based message queue commonly used as a streaming data source.

optionExplanations: 流处理确实什么都能算，但要为此背上整套 Flink 集群的运维投入，日级报表根本用不上这份实时性。
自己重写一遍流处理框架比直接用现成的 Flink 还费工时，日级报表更犯不着为此造轮子。
先问业务真的需要秒级刷新吗——不需要就选批处理，部署和运维都轻得多，这正是本题该走的路。
Kafka broker 只负责转发消息，把聚合计算逻辑硬塞进去会打破它作为消息中间件的职责边界。
optionExplanations_en: Streaming can technically compute anything, but paying for a full cluster just to produce one report each morning is overkill.
Hand-rolling your own streaming framework takes even more effort than adopting Flink, and one morning report justifies neither.
Second-level freshness isn't needed for a report that only has to exist by morning, so the lighter batch path wins here.
A Kafka broker only relays messages; cramming aggregation logic into it breaks its job as a message-routing layer.

scenario: 只需要从 Kafka topic 读点击事件、做一次简单格式转换、写进数据库——无状态、无窗口。
scenario_en: You only read click events from a Kafka topic, do one simple format transformation, and write to a database: stateless, no windows.
q: 最合适的方案是？
q_en: What is the best fit for this stateless Kafka transformation?
options: 部署一整套 Flink 集群来跑这个转换
写一个普通的 Kafka 消费者服务即可
用 Hadoop MapReduce 批量跑这个转换
先把数据落进数仓，再回流处理一遍
options_en: Deploy a full Flink cluster to run this transformation.
Just write a plain Kafka consumer service.
Run the transformation as a Hadoop MapReduce batch job.
Land the data in a warehouse first, then stream it back out.
why: 无状态的逐条转换用一个普通消费服务就够了，Flink 的价值在「有状态」的流处理，这里是 overkill。
why_en: For a trivial stateless transformation, a plain Kafka consumer service suffices and Flink is overkill.
whenOtherWins: 一旦要维护跨事件的状态（窗口计数、会话、模式检测），Flink 的状态管理和容错就开始值回票价。
tradeoff: 普通消费服务的轻量 vs Flink 的状态管理能力

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Kafka，一个分布式消息队列/日志系统，常作为流处理的数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Kafka is a distributed log-based message queue commonly used as a streaming data source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 早期的分布式批处理生态，常与 HDFS、MapReduce 一起出现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hadoop is an early distributed batch-processing ecosystem, typically paired with HDFS and MapReduce.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把计算拆成 map 和 reduce 两阶段、按批处理数据的编程模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MapReduce is a programming model that splits computation into map and reduce phases and processes data in batches.

optionExplanations: 部署一整套 Flink 集群来做一次无状态转换，等于为了拧螺丝搬来一台起重机，运维成本完全不划算。
无状态的逐条转换本身没有跨事件的依赖，一个普通消费服务就能接住，这正是本题的答案。
MapReduce 面向的是批量历史数据，对一条条实时到达的 Kafka 消息反而不是趁手的工具。
先落数仓再回流处理等于多绕一圈，对一次简单转换来说徒增延迟和存储成本。
optionExplanations_en: Standing up a whole cluster just to reshape one field per message is bringing a crane in to turn a single screw.
A single transform with nothing to remember across events fits fine in an ordinary Kafka reader, no cluster needed.
MapReduce targets batches of historical data, making it an awkward fit for messages arriving one at a time from Kafka.
Landing data in a warehouse first before streaming it back out adds an extra hop, just piling on delay and storage for a simple transform.

q: 需求从「逐条转发点击」变成「统计每用户最近 5 分钟的点击数」，本质上给系统引入了什么？
q_en: What does changing from forwarding clicks to counting each user over the last five minutes introduce?
options: 引入了状态（state），不能再逐条独立处理
服务需要的网络带宽变得明显更大、成本上升
统计过程需要额外引入强一致性事务保证
每条消息本身的消息体也随之变得更大
options_en: It introduces state — messages can no longer be handled independently.
The service now needs noticeably more network bandwidth, raising cost.
The counting process now needs an extra strong-consistency transaction.
Each message's own body also grows larger as a result.
why: 时间窗口意味着要跨事件记忆——这一步把简单消费服务变成了有状态系统，崩溃恢复、扩缩容、乱序处理全都变难。
why_en: A five-minute window introduces state, so each message can no longer be processed independently and crash recovery, scaling, and ordering all get hard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 算子跨事件维护的内部数据；必须交给 Flink 管理才能被 checkpoint 和恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State is data an operator maintains across events, and Flink must manage it to checkpoint and restore it.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

optionExplanations: 统计最近 5 分钟点击数意味着算子要跨事件记住历史计数，这就是引入了状态，这正是本题的答案。
统计逻辑本身不会突然拉高带宽占用，带宽变化只是部署规模的问题，不是这次需求变更引入的。
一个内存计数窗口不涉及跨系统的多步写入，用不到强一致性事务这种更重的保证。
计数需求只是多维护一个数字状态，不会让原始点击事件本身的消息体变大。
optionExplanations_en: Counting each user's clicks over five minutes means the operator must remember counts across events — that is state, and it's the answer here.
The counting logic itself doesn't suddenly demand more bandwidth; bandwidth is a deployment-scale concern, not something this requirement change introduces.
An in-memory counting window has no multi-step cross-system write, so it doesn't need a heavyweight strong-consistency transaction.
Counting just means keeping one more numeric state; it doesn't make the original click event's own message body any bigger.

q: 自己在普通服务里用内存计数器实现 5 分钟窗口统计，会遇到哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: What problems come from implementing a five-minute in-memory counter in a plain service?
options: 服务崩溃就丢掉全部状态，重读整个 Kafka topic 恢复既慢又贵
扩容加实例时要把状态在实例间重新分配，失败场景一大堆
事件乱序或迟到会影响计数准确性
Kafka 会因此无法存储点击事件
options_en: A crash loses all state, and re-reading the whole Kafka topic to recover is slow and expensive.
Adding instances requires redistributing state between them, with many failure modes.
Out-of-order or late events hurt the accuracy of the counts.
Kafka would become unable to store click events.
why: 崩溃丢状态、扩缩容的状态再分配、乱序/迟到事件——这三座大山正是 Flink 这类框架帮你搬走的。
why_en: Hand-rolled stateful consumers face state loss on crashes, painful state redistribution when scaling, and accuracy problems from late or out-of-order events.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Kafka，一个分布式消息队列/日志系统，常作为流处理的数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Kafka is a distributed log-based message queue commonly used as a streaming data source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 算子跨事件维护的内部数据；必须交给 Flink 管理才能被 checkpoint 和恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: State is data an operator maintains across events, and Flink must manage it to checkpoint and restore it.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

optionExplanations: 内存计数器一崩溃就清零，靠重读整条 Kafka topic 补回状态既慢又要重新处理全部历史数据。
多加实例意味着要把原本挂在单机内存里的计数在实例间重新切分，手写这层逻辑容易漏边界。
事件乱序或迟到时，逐条累加的内存计数器没有等待或修正机制，统计结果会直接算错。
这道题问的是自建方案本身的缺陷，跟 Kafka 能不能存数据无关，Kafka 存储能力完全不受影响。
optionExplanations_en: An in-memory counter loses everything on crash, and rebuilding it by replaying the whole Kafka topic is slow and reprocesses all history.
Adding instances means the counts that lived in one process's memory now need splitting across instances, and hand-rolled logic easily misses edge cases.
A naive running counter has no way to wait for or fix records that show up out of turn, so the totals simply come out wrong.
This question is about the DIY approach's own flaws, not Kafka's storage — Kafka's ability to store events is completely unaffected.

scenario: 解释 Flink 时，先把它当成一张持续运行的计算图来理解。
scenario_en: When explaining Flink, first think of it as a continuously running computation graph.
q: 「Flink 是一个 dataflow 引擎」具体是什么意思？
q_en: What does it mean that Flink is a dataflow engine?
options: 计算被描述成有向图：节点是操作，边是流动的数据
它被限制成只能处理数据库 CDC 变更流
它本质上只是一个消息队列产品
它的执行方式是逐行解释执行 SQL 语句
options_en: Computation is described as a directed graph: nodes are operations, edges are the flowing data.
It is limited to only processing database CDC change streams.
It is essentially just a message-queue product.
It executes by interpreting SQL statements row by row.
why: 开发者的任务是定义 dataflow 图，Flink 负责安排资源执行这张图；图的入口叫 source，出口叫 sink。
why_en: Flink is built around a directed dataflow graph where nodes are operators and edges are streams, and Flink arranges the resources to execute it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    S["Source"] --> O1["map or filter"]
    O1 --> K["keyBy"]
    K --> W["window or state"]
    W --> Sink["Sink"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把计算表达成有向图的模型，节点做操作，边传递数据流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dataflow models computation as a directed graph where nodes perform operations and edges carry streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: dataflow 图的入口节点，把外部系统的数据读成 Flink 流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A source is the entry node of a dataflow graph that reads external data into a Flink stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: dataflow 图的出口节点，把 Flink 流写到外部系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sink is the exit node of a dataflow graph that writes a Flink stream out to an external system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获数据库变更（增删改）并转成事件流的技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC, change data capture, turns database inserts/updates/deletes into a stream of events.

optionExplanations: Flink 把计算描述成一张有向图：节点是算子、边是流动的数据，这正是 dataflow 引擎的定义。
CDC 只是众多 source 类型之一，Flink 能接的数据源远不止数据库变更流，这个限制并不存在。
消息队列只负责存储和转发消息，而 Flink 还要负责编排计算图、调度和状态管理，二者定位不同。
Flink 是把算子编排成执行图后并行调度执行，不是像数据库那样逐行解释一条条 SQL 语句。
optionExplanations_en: Describing computation as a graph — boxes that transform data, connected by arrows the data flows along — is what makes something a dataflow engine.
CDC is just one of many possible source types; Flink can ingest far more than database change streams, so this limitation doesn't hold.
A message queue only stores and forwards messages, while Flink also orchestrates the computation graph, scheduling, and state — different jobs entirely.
Flink compiles operators into an execution graph and schedules it in parallel, not by interpreting SQL statements row by row like a database.

q: 补全 Flink dataflow 图的术语：
q_en: Fill in the terms in a Flink dataflow graph:
text: 图中的节点叫 {{operator}}（算子），边叫 {{stream}}（流）；图的入口节点叫 {{source}}，出口节点叫 {{sink}}。
why: 这四个词是讨论任何 Flink 作业的基本词汇：source 读入、operator 加工、stream 传递、sink 写出。
why_en: In Flink the nodes are operators, the edges are streams, and the entry and exit nodes are called sources and sinks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对一个或多个流做变换、可能带状态的计算单元（算子）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An operator is a potentially stateful unit that transforms one or more streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: dataflow 图的入口节点，把外部系统的数据读成 Flink 流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A source is the entry node of a dataflow graph that reads external data into a Flink stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: dataflow 图的出口节点，把 Flink 流写到外部系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sink is the exit node of a dataflow graph that writes a Flink stream out to an external system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在算子之间流动的数据边，即 dataflow 图里连接节点的连线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stream is the data edge flowing between operators in the dataflow graph.

q: 以下哪些是 Flink 常见的 source？（多选）
q_en: Which systems are common Flink sources?
options: Kafka（消息队列）
Kinesis（AWS 流数据服务）
文件系统（常用于批式输入）
Snowflake（它通常是数仓 sink，不是常见 source）
options_en: Kafka, a message queue.
Kinesis, AWS's streaming-data service.
File systems, commonly used for batch input.
Snowflake — it is usually a warehouse sink, not a common source.
why: source 把外部系统的数据读成 Flink 流：Kafka、Kinesis、文件系统、自定义集成都是常见来源；数仓一般出现在 sink 侧。
why_en: Common sources are Kafka, Kinesis, and file systems, while data warehouses like Snowflake usually appear as sinks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Kafka，一个分布式消息队列/日志系统，常作为流处理的数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Kafka is a distributed log-based message queue commonly used as a streaming data source.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 上的托管流数据服务，功能上类似 Kafka。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kinesis is AWS's managed streaming-data service, functionally similar to Kafka.

termDefinitions.meaning: dataflow 图的入口节点，把外部系统的数据读成 Flink 流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A source is the entry node of a dataflow graph that reads external data into a Flink stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云原生的数据仓库产品，常作为 Flink 的 sink 而不是 source。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Snowflake is a cloud-native data warehouse, usually a Flink sink rather than a source.

optionExplanations: Kafka 作为分布式日志，天然适合被 Flink 持续拉取增量事件，是最常见的流式 source。
Kinesis 是 AWS 托管的流数据服务，接口语义和 Kafka 类似，同样常被用作实时 source。
文件系统能提供一批批静态数据，Flink 也能把它当 source 读入做批式或有限流处理。
Snowflake 这类数仓通常是计算结果落地的终点，Flink 更常把它当 sink 而不是数据来源。
optionExplanations_en: As a distributed log, Kafka is naturally suited for Flink to continuously pull incremental events from, making it the most common streaming source.
Kinesis is AWS's managed streaming service with source semantics similar to Kafka, so it is also a common realtime source.
A file system provides batches of static data, and Flink can read it as a source for batch or bounded-stream processing too.
Something like Snowflake, a data warehouse, is normally where finished output ends up, so it plays the exit role far more than the entry.

scenario: 一个作业已经把事件流算完，最后要把结果交给外部系统使用。
scenario_en: A job has finished computing an event stream and now needs to hand results to an external system.
q: sink 在 Flink 应用里的职责是？
q_en: What is the role of a sink in a Flink application?
options: 把流中的数据写出到外部系统，如数据库或消息队列
负责从外部系统读取数据并转换进流里
负责在集群里发起并完成 leader 选举
负责存储和管理 checkpoint 的快照文件
options_en: Write data from the stream out to an external system, such as a database or queue.
Read data from an external system and convert it into the stream.
Initiate and carry out leader election within the cluster.
Store and manage checkpoint snapshot files.
why: sink 是数据的出口：MySQL/Postgres/Mongo、Snowflake/BigQuery/Redshift、Kafka/RabbitMQ、HDFS/S3 都是常见去处。
why_en: Sinks write data from Flink streams out to external systems such as databases, warehouses, message queues, and file systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: dataflow 图的出口节点，把 Flink 流写到外部系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sink is the exit node of a dataflow graph that writes a Flink stream out to an external system.

termDefinitions.meaning: dataflow 图的入口节点，把外部系统的数据读成 Flink 流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A source is the entry node of a dataflow graph that reads external data into a Flink stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个候选协调者里选出唯一主节点的分布式协调机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leader election is a coordination mechanism that chooses one active leader from multiple candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: HDFS：Hadoop 的分布式文件系统，常用于批处理的数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HDFS stands for Hadoop Distributed File System, commonly used for batch-processing storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: Flink 对全局状态做的周期性分布式快照，用于故障后恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint is Flink's periodic distributed snapshot of state, used to recover after a failure.

optionExplanations: sink 是计算结果离开 Flink 的出口，负责把流写到数据库、消息队列这类外部系统。
从外部系统读数据并转换进流里是 source 的职责，这一步发生在计算图的入口而不是出口。
leader 选举是集群协调层的工作，交给 JobManager 的高可用机制处理，跟 sink 无关。
checkpoint 快照的存储由状态后端和作业容错机制负责，不是 sink 这个数据出口该管的事。
optionExplanations_en: A sink is the exit where results leave Flink, responsible for writing the stream out to systems like databases or queues.
Pulling records in from the outside world belongs to a different node, the one that sits at the front of the pipeline, not the back.
Leader election belongs to cluster coordination, handled by the JobManager's high-availability mechanism, unrelated to sinks.
Storing checkpoint snapshots is the state backend and job fault-tolerance machinery's job, not something a sink — a data exit point — handles.

scenario: 面试里设计实时事件管道时，入口常被设成 Kafka topic。
scenario_en: In interviews, real-time event pipelines often start from a Kafka topic.
q: 为什么面试里的 Flink 设计绝大多数从 Kafka 起步？
q_en: Why do most Flink interview designs start with Kafka?
options: Flink 在设计上只支持 Kafka 这一种 source 类型，别的消息系统都接不了
因为用 Kafka 部署起来的成本是所有候选方案里最便宜的一个
topic/partition 划分与 Flink 的 keyBy、并行度天然衔接
因为 Kafka 自带窗口聚合和状态管理功能，不用 Flink 处理
options_en: Flink is designed to support only Kafka as a source type, and no other system can connect.
Because deploying Kafka is the cheapest option among all the candidates here.
Topic and partition layout maps naturally onto Flink's keyBy and parallelism.
Because Kafka has built-in window aggregation and state management, so Flink is unneeded.
why: Kafka 的 topic/partition 划分和 Flink 的 key 分区、并行执行天然衔接，是面试里最顺手的组合。
why_en: Kafka forces you to think about topics and partitions, which maps naturally onto reasoning about your Flink job.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Kafka，一个分布式消息队列/日志系统，常作为流处理的数据源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Kafka is a distributed log-based message queue commonly used as a streaming data source.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 中按名称组织的一类消息日志，生产者写入，消费者读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka topic is a named message log that producers write to and consumers read from.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka topic 的分片日志，提供并行读写和分区内有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka partition is a shard of a topic log that enables parallelism and preserves order within the partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按给定键把流分区成 KeyedStream，之后状态和窗口按 key 独立维护。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KeyBy partitions a stream by a key into a keyed stream, so state and windows are maintained independently per key.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

optionExplanations: Flink 能接入的 source 类型很多，Kafka 只是其中最常见的一种，并不是唯一支持的类型。
部署成本从来不是选它的主因，面试里也很少纠结这类基础设施报价，这个理由站不住脚。
分区结构本身就是设计并行处理逻辑的现成起点，讲 Kafka 起步的方案最容易跟面试官讲清楚。
窗口聚合和状态管理是 Flink 自己的能力，Kafka 只是消息中转，并不会替 Flink 把这些做掉。
optionExplanations_en: Flink can ingest many source types; Kafka is only the most common one among them, not the sole supported type.
Deployment cost is rarely the deciding factor, and interviews rarely dwell on infrastructure pricing — this reasoning doesn't hold up.
A partition layout is already a ready-made starting point for splitting up parallel work, which is the easiest story to tell an interviewer.
Window aggregation and state management are Flink's own capabilities; Kafka just relays messages and does none of that work for Flink.

scenario: 题目只是离线跑一批历史数据，没有秒级实时要求。
scenario_en: The problem only runs over historical data offline, with no second-level realtime requirement.
q: 在面试里用 Flink 做「批处理」为什么不推荐？
q_en: Why is Flink usually not the interview choice for batch processing?
options: Flink 在技术架构上根本不支持批处理这种运行模式
技术上可行，但面试官不熟、维持最优性也更难，批场景直接用批框架
批处理这类场景在任何情况下都必须只能用 Hadoop 来完成
Flink 一旦切到做批处理模式就必然会丢失数据
options_en: Flink's architecture technically cannot support the batch-processing mode at all.
It works technically, but interviewers know it less and keeping it optimal is harder — use a batch framework for batch work.
Batch-processing scenarios must under all circumstances only be done with Hadoop.
Flink is bound to lose data the moment it switches into batch-processing mode.
why: Flink 能做批，但在面试里讲批处理用 Spark 这类更常规的工具，沟通成本低、也更稳。
why_en: Flink can technically do batch work, but interviewers understand it less and keeping it optimal is harder, so use a batch framework instead.
tradeoff: Flink 的流批统一能力 vs Spark 批处理的低沟通成本

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 早期的分布式批处理生态，常与 HDFS、MapReduce 一起出现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hadoop is an early distributed batch-processing ecosystem, typically paired with HDFS and MapReduce.

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Spark，一个通用的批处理/微批计算引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Spark is a general-purpose batch and micro-batch compute engine.

optionExplanations: Flink 的执行模型本来就能跑批处理，这个说法把它的能力边界搞反了。
技术上 Flink 能做批，但面试官更熟悉 Spark 这类专门的批框架，讲批处理选它沟通成本更低，这正是本题答案。
Hadoop 只是众多批处理方案之一，说批处理场景必须用它太绝对，其它批引擎同样能胜任。
Flink 做批处理不会必然丢数据，它同样有完善的容错机制，这个说法没有依据。
optionExplanations_en: Flink's execution model can absolutely run batch jobs; this claim gets its capability boundary backwards.
Capability isn't the blocker here — familiarity is; a dedicated batch tool is the story whoever is grading the design already knows.
Hadoop is just one of many batch options; saying batch scenarios must only use it is too absolute since other batch engines work fine too.
Running batch on Flink doesn't inherently lose data — it has the same solid fault-tolerance machinery, so this claim has no basis.

q: Flink 里的 stream（流）最准确的定义是？
q_en: What is the most accurate definition of a stream in Flink?
options: 无界的数据元素序列，像无限长的事件数组在流动
一张行列数量都固定、大小已知的静态表
一个持久化存储在磁盘上的日志文件
一个指向数据库的长连接对象
options_en: An unbounded sequence of data elements, like an infinite array of events flowing through the system.
A static table with a fixed, known number of rows and columns.
A log file persisted durably on disk.
A long-lived connection object pointing at a database.
why: 流是无界序列；Flink 提供切分、变换、聚合、重组等工具来加工它。
why_en: A stream is an unbounded sequence of data elements flowing through the system, like an infinite array of events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无界的数据元素序列，是 Flink dataflow 图上流动的数据边。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stream is an unbounded sequence of data elements flowing along the edges of a Flink dataflow graph.

optionExplanations: 流是无界的数据元素序列，像不断延伸的事件数组，这正是 Flink 对 stream 的定义。
表的行列数量是固定已知的，这更接近批处理里的静态数据集，不是流的特征。
日志文件是持久化在磁盘上的静态记录，流则是持续到来、边到边处理的动态数据。
数据库连接对象只是访问某个存储的句柄，不携带持续到来的事件序列这层含义。
optionExplanations_en: There is no end in sight for a stream — it keeps growing like an array with no final length, which is the shape Flink assumes.
A table has a fixed, known row and column count, which is closer to a static batch dataset, not a stream's defining trait.
A log file is a static record persisted on disk, while a stream is dynamic data that keeps arriving and gets processed as it goes.
A database connection object is just a handle to access some storage; it carries no notion of a continuously arriving event sequence.

scenario: 同样叫“流”，Kafka topic 是外部日志，Flink stream 是作业内部的数据边。
scenario_en: Although both sound like streams, a Kafka topic is an external log while a Flink stream is an internal data edge.
q: Flink 的 stream 和 Kafka 的 topic 在抽象上的关键区别是？
q_en: What is the key abstraction difference between a Flink stream and a Kafka topic?
options: Flink 流对单条消息允许的字节大小上限比 Kafka 更大一些
Kafka topic 在设计上完全不具备任何持久化落盘的能力
两者其实是同一套抽象，工程上可以完全互换着理解使用
Flink 流没有 offset，靠 checkpoint 保证持久性
options_en: A Flink stream allows a somewhat larger maximum byte size per message than Kafka.
A Kafka topic is designed with absolutely no capability to persist data to disk at all.
The two are really the same abstraction and can, engineering-wise, be used interchangeably.
A Flink stream has no offsets; durability instead comes from checkpoints.
why: Kafka 的日志有 offset 和持久化语义；Flink 流只是计算图上的数据边，容错靠 checkpoint 机制而不是流本身。
why_en: Unlike Kafka's append-only log with offsets, a Flink stream promises no persistence, and durability comes from periodic checkpoints instead.
tradeoff: Kafka topic 的持久化日志 vs Flink stream 的瞬时数据边

termDefinitions.meaning: Apache Flink，一个开源的分布式流处理框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Apache Flink is an open-source framework for distributed stream processing.
