termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash interleaves longitude and latitude into one-dimensional order; Redis uses a similar idea for the sorted-set score.

termDefinitions.meaning: R-tree：一种按外接矩形组织的空间索引树，Redis 地理索引并不用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree is a spatial index tree organized by bounding rectangles, which is not what Redis's geo index uses.

termDefinitions.meaning: quadtree 把二维平面递归四等分；它是常见地理索引思路，但不是 Redis GEO 的底层结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits a 2D plane into four quadrants; it is common for geo indexes, but not Redis GEO's underlying structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 有序集合，每个 member 对应一个 score，可按 score 范围查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set maps each member to a score and supports range queries by score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用把地图切成 cell，并维护 cellId 到点集合的映射；这是一种可自建的 geo 索引，不是 Redis GEO 的存储形态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fixed grid table maps each cellId to its points. It is a possible custom geo index, but not the storage shape of Redis GEO.

q_en: What's the underlying implementation of Redis's geospatial index?
optionExplanations: 错：R-tree 是按外接矩形层层嵌套的空间索引结构，不是 Redis GEO 的底层实现。
错：四叉树是递归四等分平面区域的结构，Redis GEO 用的不是这一套。
对：底层做法是把经纬度算成一个可排序的类 geohash 数值，直接塞进一个有序集合里，借用它本来就有的排序能力。
错：把平面切成固定大小格子的网格表也不是这里用的方案，真正的底层数据结构其实就是一个 sorted set。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an R-tree is a nested-bounding-box spatial index — not what Redis GEO uses under the hood.
Wrong: a quadtree recursively splits the plane into quarters — not Redis GEO's implementation either.
Right: Redis GEO encodes lat/lon into a sortable geohash-like score and stores it directly in a sorted set.
Wrong: a fixed-size grid cell table isn't Redis GEO's underlying structure — the actual backing structure is a plain sorted set.

q: GEOSEARCH 复杂度 O(N + log M) 里为什么同时出现 N（包围盒内候选数）和 M（半径内命中数）？
options: 两遍过滤：先取网格对齐包围盒里的 N 个候选，再精确筛出半径内的 M 个
因为底层排序算法本身需要跑完整两趟
N 其实指的是 Redis 集群里的节点数量
这是文档笔误，N 和 M 其实是同一个数
why: geohash 的盒子是方形、网格对齐的，无法精确贴合圆形半径，所以先粗筛候选、再逐个精确算距离。
why_en: Geohash boxes are grid-aligned squares, so a first pass grabs candidates inside the boxes and a second pass filters to those within the exact radius.
options_en: Two passes: grab N candidates inside grid-aligned boxes, then precisely filter to the M within radius
Because the underlying sort algorithm itself needs two full passes
N actually refers to the number of nodes in the Redis cluster
It's a documentation typo, and N and M are actually the same number
q_en: Why does GEOSEARCH's O(N + log M) complexity involve both N (candidates in the bounding box) and M (hits within the radius)?
optionExplanations: 对：编码出来的格子是方的、对齐网格的，圆形的搜索半径根本套不进去，所以得先粗筛出一批候选，再挨个精确算距离挑出真正命中的。
错：跑两趟不是排序算法本身的要求，是「先粗筛候选、再精确过滤」这个两阶段查询策略带来的开销。
错：N 指的是包围盒内的候选成员数，跟集群里有多少个节点没有关系。
错：N 和 M 分别对应两个不同阶段筛出的数量（候选数 vs 命中数），不是同一个数，也不是笔误。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a geohash box is square and grid-aligned, so it can't exactly match a circular radius — first coarse-filter N candidates, then precisely check distance for M hits.
Wrong: running two passes isn't a property of the sort algorithm — it comes from the two-stage coarse-then-precise filtering strategy.
Wrong: N refers to candidate members inside the bounding box, unrelated to how many nodes are in the cluster.
Wrong: N and M come from two different filtering stages (candidates vs actual hits) — not the same number, and not a typo.

q: Redis Stream 的本质是？
options: 追加写日志（append-only log），类似 Kafka 的 topic
一个固定大小、写满就自动覆盖旧数据的环形缓冲区
一个按分数排序、支持弹出最小值成员的优先队列
一个不保留任何状态、消息即发即失的广播信道
why: Stream 是追加日志：配合消费组可以做事件溯源和工作队列，是 Redis 里最接近 Kafka 的原语。
why_en: A Redis stream is an append-only log similar to a Kafka topic, and consumer groups coordinate who processes what.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["XADD"] --> B["Stream log"]
  B --> C["Consumer group"]
  C --> D["ACK or pending"]
options_en: An append-only log, similar to a Kafka topic
A fixed-size ring buffer that automatically overwrites old data once full
A score-ordered priority queue that supports popping the lowest-score member
A stateless broadcast channel where messages fire and are gone

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：Apache Kafka，一个支持长期保留、多消费者重放的分布式日志系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is Apache Kafka, a distributed log system built for long retention and replay by many independent consumers.

q_en: What is a Redis Stream, fundamentally?
optionExplanations: 对：它本质是一份只增不减的日志，跟消费组搭配能当事件溯源或任务队列用，是 Redis 里长得最像 Kafka topic 的东西。
错：Stream 不是写满就自动覆盖旧数据的环形缓冲区，它靠 XADD 持续追加，要清理得显式 XTRIM/裁剪。
错：按分数排序、弹出最小值是 sorted set 的能力，Stream 靠 ID 顺序追加，不是分数排序。
错：不留状态、即发即失是 Pub/Sub 的特征，Stream 恰恰相反——它持久保留条目，能被后来的消费者读取历史。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Stream is an append-only log; paired with consumer groups it supports event sourcing and job queues — closest to a Kafka topic.
Wrong: Stream isn't a fixed-size ring buffer that auto-overwrites old data — XADD keeps appending, and trimming needs explicit XTRIM.
Wrong: score-ordered pop-the-minimum describes a sorted set; Stream appends by ID order, not by score.
Wrong: no retained state and fire-and-forget describes Pub/Sub — Stream durably keeps entries so later consumers can read history.

q: 补全 Stream 工作队列的命令分工：
text: 生产者用 {{XADD}} 追加条目；工作者通过消费组用 {{XREADGROUP}} 领取条目；超时未确认的条目可被其他工作者用 {{XCLAIM}}（或 XAUTOCLAIM）抢过来重做。
why: 工作队列链路是：XADD 入流，XREADGROUP 分给 worker，成功后 XACK；没 XACK 会留在 PEL，超时后用 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管。
why_en: The queue loop is XADD to append, XREADGROUP to deliver, XACK to finish, and XCLAIM or XAUTOCLAIM to recover idle pending entries.
codeSample:
XGROUP CREATE jobs workers $ MKSTREAM
XADD jobs * kind email user 42
XREADGROUP GROUP workers worker-1 COUNT 1 STREAMS jobs >
# worker-1 dies before XACK; entry stays in PEL
XCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 {entry-id}
XAUTOCLAIM jobs workers worker-2 60000 0-0 COUNT 10
XACK jobs workers {entry-id}

termDefinitions.meaning: XADD：向 Stream 追加一条新记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XADD appends a new entry to a stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: XREADGROUP：消费组里的 worker 用它领取 Stream 里的新条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XREADGROUP is how a worker in a consumer group reads new entries from a stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: XCLAIM：把一个超时未确认的条目转交给另一个 worker 重新处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XCLAIM transfers a stalled, unacknowledged stream entry to another worker to reprocess.

termDefinitions.meaning: XAUTOCLAIM：从某个起点开始扫描，并批量接管 idle 超时的 pending 条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XAUTOCLAIM scans and claims pending stream entries that have been idle too long.

termDefinitions.meaning: XACK：worker 处理成功后确认条目，Redis 会把它从 PEL 中移除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK acknowledges a processed entry and removes it from the pending list.

termDefinitions.meaning: PEL：消费组记录已投递但还没 XACK 的条目，以及 owner 和 idle 时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The PEL tracks entries that were delivered to a consumer group but not yet acknowledged.

q_en: Fill in the command division of labor for a Stream-based work queue:

q: Redis Streams 工作队列里，worker 取到任务后崩溃，未确认任务如何恢复？
scenario: 生产者用 XADD 写入任务，worker 用 XREADGROUP 领取任务；只有处理成功并 XACK 后，这条任务才算完成。
options: 未 XACK 的任务永久丢失，不再恢复
Redis 自动重启崩溃 worker，再继续原任务
idle 超时后，用 XCLAIM 转给其他 worker 重做
主节点重新广播任务，让所有 worker 抢处理
why: 未 XACK 的条目会留在 PEL，记录 owner 和 idle。idle 超阈值后，其他 worker 用 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管并重做。
why_en: Unacknowledged stream entries stay in the PEL, so another worker can claim an idle entry with XCLAIM or XAUTOCLAIM and retry it.
tradeoff: 故障恢复与至少一次处理 vs 重复执行风险
whenOtherWins: 若任务不能重复执行，业务层要加去重键或状态机；Redis 重新交付，但不保证只执行一次。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P[Producer XADD] --> S[(Redis Stream)]
    S --> G[Consumer group]
    G --> W1[worker1 XREADGROUP]
    W1 --> PEL[PEL: delivered, not XACKed]
    W1 -. crashes .-> PEL
    PEL -- idle exceeds threshold --> W2[worker2 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM]
    W2 --> R[redo work]
    R --> A[XACK removes from PEL]

rows: 其他 worker 发现超时

options_en: The unacknowledged task is lost forever
Redis restarts the crashed worker and continues the task
After the idle timeout, XCLAIM moves it to another worker
The primary rebroadcasts the task to all workers

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Streams：Redis 里的追加式消息日志，可用来做轻量工作队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Streams is an append-only message log in Redis that can act as a lightweight work queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: XREADGROUP：消费组里的 worker 用它领取还没分配的新任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XREADGROUP lets a worker read entries through a Redis consumer group.

termDefinitions.meaning: XACK：worker 处理成功后确认任务完成，并把条目移出 PEL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK acknowledges that a stream entry was processed and removes it from the PEL.

termDefinitions.meaning: Pending Entries List（PEL）：记录已交付但还没有 XACK 的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Pending Entries List tracks entries that were delivered but not yet acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: idle time：一条 pending 任务距离上次交付或认领已经过去多久。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idle time is how long a pending entry has gone without being claimed or acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: XCLAIM：把超时未确认的 pending 条目改交给另一个 worker。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XCLAIM transfers a stale pending stream entry to another worker.

termDefinitions.meaning: XAUTOCLAIM：批量扫描并接管 idle 超时的 pending 条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XAUTOCLAIM scans and claims pending entries that have been idle too long.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一任务重复执行，最终结果仍然像执行一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means repeating the same job leaves the system in the same final state.

q_en: In a Redis Streams work queue, how does an unacknowledged task recover after the worker that claimed it crashes?
scenario_en: A producer writes tasks with XADD and workers claim them with XREADGROUP; a task only counts as done once it's processed successfully and XACKed.
optionExplanations: 错：未 XACK 的条目不会丢失，它会留在 PEL（pending entries list）里等着被接管，不是永久消失。
错：Redis 不会帮你重启崩溃的 worker 进程，它只负责保留和转交消息，恢复业务进程是运维/编排的事。
对：没确认的任务会挂在一个待处理列表里，谁领的、挂了多久都记着；等挂的时间超过阈值，别的 worker 就能把它接过去重做。
错：主节点不会重新广播让所有 worker 一起抢，消费组的分发和接管是按 PEL/idle 逐条精确转交，不是广播抢占。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: an un-acked entry isn't lost — it stays in the pending entries list (PEL) waiting to be taken over, not gone forever.
Wrong: Redis doesn't restart a crashed worker process for you — it only retains and hands off messages.
Right: an un-acked entry sits in the PEL tracking its owner and idle time; past a threshold, another worker uses XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM to take it over.
Wrong: the primary doesn't rebroadcast for every worker to race for — handoff is a precise per-entry transfer based on PEL/idle.

q: XCLAIM 接管机制带来的副作用是？
options: 同一条目可能被处理两次——Redis 分不清「慢」和「死」，处理逻辑必须幂等
超时的条目会被 Redis 静默丢弃，不再投递
整个消费组的消费顺序会被完全打乱
接管机制强制一个消费组只能有一个 worker
why: 慢 worker 没死却被判超时的话，条目会被第二个 worker 重做——这是 at-least-once 语义，幂等是消费端的义务。
why_en: Redis cannot tell a slow worker from a dead one, so an entry can occasionally be processed twice and your handler must be idempotent.
options_en: An entry can be processed twice, since Redis cannot tell slow from dead, so handlers must be idempotent
A timed-out entry gets silently dropped by Redis and never redelivered
The entire consumer group's processing order gets completely scrambled
The takeover mechanism forces a consumer group to have only one worker

termDefinitions.meaning: XCLAIM：把 pending 条目从一个消费者转交给另一个消费者重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XCLAIM transfers a pending stream entry to another consumer for retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: XACK：确认 Stream 条目处理完成，并把它从 PEL 中移除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK acknowledges a stream entry as processed and removes it from the PEL.

termDefinitions.meaning: PEL（Pending Entries List）：消费组里已投递但尚未 XACK 的条目列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The PEL is the pending entries list of messages delivered to a consumer group but not yet acknowledged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一个操作重复执行多次，结果和只执行一次一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means running the same operation multiple times produces the same result as running it once.

q_en: What side effect comes from the XCLAIM takeover mechanism?
codeSample:
# Worker A reads but does not XACK yet.
XREADGROUP GROUP g A COUNT 1 STREAMS jobs >
XPENDING jobs g

# After A is idle too long, B claims and retries.
XCLAIM jobs g B 60000 1710000000000-0
# If A was only slow, the job may run twice.
XACK jobs g 1710000000000-0
optionExplanations: 对：一个只是慢、并没真死的 worker 也可能被系统当成超时，任务就转给别人重做——这就是至少一次投递，业务逻辑得自己保证幂等。
错：超时的条目不会被静默丢弃，它会被 XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM 接管重做，而不是消失。
错：XCLAIM 只是把某条挂起条目的所有权转给另一个 worker，不会打乱整个消费组的处理顺序。
错：接管机制不限制消费组里的 worker 数量，多个 worker 并行消费本来就是消费组的设计初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a worker that's slow but not dead can get timed out anyway, and the entry gets redone by another worker — at-least-once; idempotency is the consumer's job.
Wrong: a timed-out entry isn't silently dropped — it gets taken over and redone via XCLAIM/XAUTOCLAIM.
Wrong: XCLAIM only transfers ownership of one pending entry to another worker — it doesn't scramble the group's order.
Wrong: the takeover mechanism doesn't cap a consumer group at one worker — parallel consumption is the whole point.

q: 把 Stream 当「可靠日志」用之前必须记住什么？
options: 条目的持久性只取决于你的 RDB/AOF 配置——默认下崩溃可能丢最近的条目
Stream 的写入总是同步落盘，绝不会丢失数据
Stream 会自动把条目复制一份镜像到 Kafka 集群
Stream 里写入的条目永远不可以被删除
why: Stream 再像日志，也逃不过 Redis 的持久化取舍：默认配置下崩溃丢最近写入——和页首的 durability 警告是同一件事。
why_en: Stream entries are only as durable as your persistence settings, so with defaults a crash can lose recent entries.
options_en: Entry durability depends entirely on your RDB/AOF settings, and a crash can lose recent entries under defaults
Stream writes are always synchronously flushed to disk and never lost
Streams automatically mirror a copy of every entry into a Kafka cluster
Once written, entries in a stream can never be deleted
q_en: What must you remember before treating a Stream as a 'reliable log'?
optionExplanations: 对：别看它长得像日志，落盘策略跟 Redis 其他数据一样受同一套取舍约束——默认配置崩溃照样会丢最近那批写入。
错：Stream 不会「总是同步落盘」，它的持久性仍受 RDB 快照间隔或 AOF fsync 频率约束，跟普通 key 一样有丢失窗口。
错：Redis 没有把 Stream 条目自动镜像到 Kafka 集群这种内建功能，这是要自己搭建的跨系统同步。
错：Stream 里的条目可以被删除——XDEL 删单条、XTRIM 按长度或时间裁剪，不是「永远不可删除」。
optionExplanations_en: Right: however log-like it looks, Stream still inherits Redis's persistence trade-offs — a crash under default config can lose the most recent entries.
Wrong: Stream isn't 'always synced to disk' — its durability still depends on RDB snapshot intervals or AOF fsync frequency.
Wrong: Redis has no built-in feature that auto-mirrors Stream entries to a Kafka cluster.
Wrong: entries in a Stream can be deleted — XDEL removes a single entry, XTRIM trims by length or time.

q: 什么时候该把 Redis Streams 换成 Kafka？
options: 只要队列规模比较小，就应该马上换掉
只要系统里已经部署了 Redis，就该顺便换掉
只要用到了消费组（consumer group）机制就该换
需要长期保留、多个独立消费者重放、以及一条都不能丢的持久有序吞吐时
why: Streams 适合已有 Redis、队列规模不大的场景（后台任务、通知扇出、工作分发）；长保留 + 重放 + 不可丢消息才值得付 Kafka 的运维成本。
why_en: Kafka earns its complexity when you need long retention, replay for many independent consumers, and durable ordered throughput where losing a message is unacceptable.
scenario: 你的设计已经在用 Redis Streams 做工作队列（后台任务、通知扇出），眼下数据量和独立消费者的数量都在持续增长。
options_en: You should switch the moment the queue is even moderately small
As soon as Redis happens to already be deployed in the system
As soon as you touch the consumer-group mechanism at all
When you need long retention, replay for many independent consumers, and durable ordered throughput where losing a message is unacceptable
tradeoff: 留在 Redis Streams 的低运维成本 vs 换 Kafka 换来的长保留与可靠重放
q_en: When should you switch from Redis Streams to Kafka?
scenario_en: Your design already uses Redis Streams as a work queue (background jobs, notification fan-out), and both data volume and the number of independent consumers keep growing.
optionExplanations: 错：规模小恰恰是 Streams 更划算的场景，为小队列换 Kafka 只是白白多背运维成本。
错：「已经在用 Redis」不是换 Kafka 的理由，选型要看队列本身的保留/重放/丢失要求，不是图省事。
错：消费组机制 Streams 自己就有（XREADGROUP），不是 Kafka 独有能力，用到消费组不构成换型理由。
对：一旦要求长期留存、好几拨互不相干的消费者各自从头重放、外加一条都不能少的可靠有序吞吐，这份额外的运维投入就值了。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: a small queue is exactly where Streams pays off — switching to Kafka for it just adds ops overhead for nothing.
Wrong: 'we already run Redis' isn't a reason to switch — the choice should follow retention/replay/loss requirements, not convenience.
Wrong: consumer groups are a Streams feature too (XREADGROUP), not Kafka-exclusive — using one is no reason to switch.
Right: it's worth Kafka's operational cost once you need long retention, multiple independent consumers replaying history, and durable throughput that can't drop a message.

q: Pub/Sub 和 Streams 的分工，一句话是？
options: Pub/Sub 会把消息持久化落盘，Streams 反而不落盘
Streams 服务「需要补课的消费者」；Pub/Sub 只投递给「此刻在线的听众」
两者的投递语义和可靠性完全等价，可以互换
Pub/Sub 天生持久可靠，更适合做工作队列
why: Streams 有历史可回读；Pub/Sub 即发即失、离线就错过——按「消费者要不要追赶历史」来选。
why_en: Streams serve consumers that must catch up on missed entries, while Pub/Sub only delivers to whoever is listening right now.
options_en: Pub/Sub persists messages to disk while Streams, oddly, does not
Streams serve consumers who need to catch up on history; Pub/Sub only delivers to whoever is listening right now
The two have fully equivalent delivery semantics and reliability, interchangeably
Pub/Sub is inherently durable and reliable, making it the better fit for work queues
tradeoff: Streams 的可回读历史 vs Pub/Sub 的即发即失
q_en: In one line, how do Pub/Sub and Streams divide responsibilities?
optionExplanations: 错：说反了——Pub/Sub 不落盘、即发即失；Streams 才有持久的历史条目可以回读。
对：一个能让消费者回头补看历史，服务的是「需要补课」的场景；另一个发出去就不管了，只送达「这一刻正在听」的人，按这个区别来分工。
错：两者投递语义差别很大——Streams 更接近 at-least-once 可回放，Pub/Sub 是 at-most-once，不能互换。
错：天生持久可靠、适合做工作队列描述的是 Streams，不是 Pub/Sub——Pub/Sub 没有持久化和重放能力。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that's backwards — Pub/Sub doesn't persist, it's fire-and-forget; Streams is the one with durable, replayable history.
Right: Streams keeps replayable history for 'consumers that need to catch up'; Pub/Sub only reaches 'listeners online right now' — pick by that need.
Wrong: their delivery semantics differ a lot — Streams is closer to at-least-once with replay, Pub/Sub is at-most-once.
Wrong: durable and reliable enough for a work queue describes Streams, not Pub/Sub — Pub/Sub has no persistence or replay.

q: Redis Pub/Sub 的投递语义是？
options: 恰好一次投递，Redis 会去重保证不重不漏
至少一次投递，离线消息会重试到送达为止
至多一次：订阅者离线期间发布的消息永久错过
带事务性保证的投递，要么全送达要么全不送
why: 消息不落盘、不可重放：连接断开或不在线就收不到，这就是 at-most-once。
why_en: Redis Pub/Sub is at-most-once delivery, so a subscriber offline at publish time misses the message entirely.
options_en: Exactly-once delivery, with Redis deduplicating so nothing repeats or is missed
At-least-once delivery, retrying offline messages until they land
At-most-once: a subscriber offline at publish time permanently misses the message
Transactional delivery guarantees where messages either all arrive or none do
q_en: What are Redis Pub/Sub's delivery semantics?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 不会去重也不保证恰好一次，Pub/Sub 甚至不保证消息一定能送到，比「恰好一次」弱得多。
错：离线不会有重试——消息不落盘，Redis 不会等订阅者上线后补投递，这不是 at-least-once。
对：消息压根不落盘也没法回放，断线或不在线就是彻底错过，投递上限就是「送到算送到，送不到也不补」。
错：Pub/Sub 没有跨订阅者的事务性保证，它是逐个投递给当前在线订阅者，不是「全送达或全不送」的原子操作。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis doesn't dedupe or guarantee exactly-once — Pub/Sub doesn't even guarantee delivery at all.
Wrong: there's no retry while offline — messages aren't persisted, so Redis won't hold them for a subscriber that comes back later.
Right: messages aren't persisted or replayable — disconnect or be offline and you miss it forever, which is at-most-once.
Wrong: Pub/Sub has no transactional guarantee across subscribers — it delivers to whoever's online individually.

scenario: 你听过一个老说法：Redis Cluster 里的 Pub/Sub 即使加节点也不加容量，因为消息会扩散到全体节点。现在团队准备用 Redis 7+，并且频道数很多、频道名能自然分散。
scenario_en: You have heard the old rule that Pub/Sub in Redis Cluster does not gain capacity when you add nodes because messages spread to every node. The team is now on Redis 7+ with many channels whose names can naturally spread across slots.
q: 「集群 Pub/Sub 加节点不加容量」这个老印象，现在的事实是？
options: 普通 Pub/Sub 仍全局传播；Redis 7+ 的 sharded 版才能按 shard 横向扩展
这个限制至今对所有 Pub/Sub 都成立，Redis 7+ 没有相关改变
只要给 Redis 加 replica，单个频道的发布吞吐就会自动分摊到所有副本
Pub/Sub 已经被 Streams 完全替代，后续 Redis 版本不能再用 Pub/Sub
why: Global Pub/Sub 仍跨节点传播，不能靠加节点扩。Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub 让频道按 slot 落到 shard；多频道可扩，单热频道仍卡单 shard。
why_en: Normal cluster Pub/Sub still propagates across nodes, while Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub routes channels by slot so many spread-out channels can scale, but one hot channel stays shard-bound.
whenOtherWins: 老版本、global/pattern 订阅、单热频道时，仍按“加节点不加容量”回答；新分片模式且频道分散时才说可扩。
options_en: Normal Pub/Sub is still globally propagated; Redis 7+'s sharded version can scale by shard
This limitation still applies to all Pub/Sub, and Redis 7+ made no related change
Adding Redis replicas automatically spreads one channel's publish throughput across all replicas
Pub/Sub has been fully replaced by Streams and cannot be used in later Redis versions
tradeoff: global Pub/Sub 的简单广播 vs sharded Pub/Sub 的可扩展但需按 shard 设计
codeSample:
# Normal/global Pub/Sub: simple, but cluster-wide propagation.
SUBSCRIBE orders.123
PUBLISH orders.123 msg

# Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub: channel hashes to a slot/shard.
SSUBSCRIBE orders.123
SPUBLISH orders.123 msg

# Spread many independent channels across slots/shards.
SPUBLISH chat:1001 msg
SPUBLISH chat:2042 msg
diagram:
flowchart LR
  P1["PUBLISH channel"] --> G["global Pub/Sub"]
  G --> N1["node A"]
  G --> N2["node B"]
  G --> N3["node C"]
  P2["SPUBLISH shardchannel"] --> H["hash slot"]
  H --> S["owning shard only"]
  S --> R1["primary"]
  S --> R2["replica subscribers"]

termDefinitions.meaning: SPUBLISH：Redis 7+ 分片 Pub/Sub 的发布命令，消息按 shard channel 的 slot 路由，只在对应 shard 内传播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SPUBLISH is the Redis 7+ sharded Pub/Sub publish command; the message is routed by the shard channel's slot and propagated only within that shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSUBSCRIBE：Redis 7+ 分片 Pub/Sub 的订阅命令，订阅一个会像 key 一样哈希到 slot 的 shard channel。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSUBSCRIBE is the sharded Pub/Sub subscribe command, hashing the channel to a slot just like a key.

termDefinitions.meaning: global Pub/Sub：普通 PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE 的集群传播模式，简单但会跨节点传播消息，不适合靠加节点线性扩 Pub/Sub 总线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Global Pub/Sub is the normal PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE cluster propagation mode; it is simple but sends messages across nodes, so it is not linear capacity scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: shard channel：分片 Pub/Sub 的频道名，会按 Redis Cluster 的 slot 算法归属到某个 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard channel is a sharded Pub/Sub channel name that is assigned to a shard using Redis Cluster's slot algorithm.

q_en: The old assumption is 'adding cluster nodes doesn't add Pub/Sub capacity' — what's actually true now?
optionExplanations: 对：得分两种情况——普通的发布订阅照样是全网广播；新版本另外那套按 slot 分片的命令，才真正能把频道摊开到不同分片上扩容。
错：新版本已经加了按分片走的发布订阅，能把很多频道的压力摊到不同分片上，老说法不再对所有情况都成立。
错：单个频道的发布压力不会因为加了 replica 就自动分摊，副本只是复制数据，不参与分担某个频道的 fanout。
错：Pub/Sub 没有被 Streams 完全替代，两者语义不同（即发即失 vs 持久可回放），后续版本仍然可以用 Pub/Sub。
optionExplanations_en: Right: split it in two — plain PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE still broadcasts cluster-wide, while Redis 7+'s SPUBLISH/SSUBSCRIBE lets channels land on one shard and scale horizontally.
Wrong: Redis 7+ introduced sharded Pub/Sub, spreading fanout load for many channels across shards — the old limitation doesn't hold for all Pub/Sub now.
Wrong: adding replicas doesn't auto-spread one channel's publish load — replicas just copy data, they don't share in that fanout.
Wrong: Pub/Sub hasn't been fully replaced by Streams — they have different semantics, and Pub/Sub is still usable in later versions.

q: 使用一个 Pub/Sub 频道之前需要什么创建或配置步骤？
options: 执行 CREATE CHANNEL 命令
在 CONFIG SET 里注册频道
先创建一个 consumer group
什么都不用：有人发布或订阅这个名字，频道就存在了
why: 频道只是个名字：发布者往这个名字上发、订阅者在这个名字上听，不需要任何预先创建。
why_en: A channel is just a name that comes into existence when someone publishes or subscribes; there is nothing to create.
options_en: Run a CREATE CHANNEL command
Register the channel via CONFIG SET
First create a consumer group for it
Nothing: the channel exists the moment someone publishes or subscribes to that name
q_en: What setup or creation step do you need before using a Pub/Sub channel?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 没有 CREATE CHANNEL 这条命令，频道不需要任何显式创建步骤。
错：CONFIG SET 是配置服务器参数的命令，不是用来注册 Pub/Sub 频道的。
错：consumer group 是 Streams 的概念，Pub/Sub 频道不需要消费组，两者是不同的机制。
对：频道说白了就是一个约定好的字符串——谁发谁听全靠对上这个名字，压根不用先注册或声明。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis has no CREATE CHANNEL command — a channel needs no explicit creation step at all.
Wrong: CONFIG SET tunes server parameters; it isn't used to register a Pub/Sub channel.
Wrong: a consumer group is a Streams concept — a Pub/Sub channel doesn't need one.
Right: a channel is just a name — a publisher sends to it and a subscriber listens on it, with no pre-creation step.

scenario: 一台 Chat Server 要订阅很多 Redis sharded Pub/Sub 频道，例如 user:1、user:2、chat:abc 这类频道一共有 100 万个。每个频道名会像 key 一样 hash 到某个 slot，slot 再归属于某个 Redis shard。
q: 一台订阅了 100 万个频道的服务器，需要多少条到 Redis 的连接？
options: 为每个频道单独开一条独立的 TCP 连接，总共 100 万条
严格按每个频道一条连接来计算连接开销
每个持有相关槽位的节点一条——连接开销按节点算，不按频道算
至少要开 16,384 条连接，正好对应哈希槽的数量
why: 频道不是 TCP 连接；一条到某个 Redis shard 的长连接可以承载很多 SSUBSCRIBE。连接数按涉及的节点/shard 算，不按频道数算；但 100 万频道仍会产生订阅状态和 fanout 成本。
why_en: One TCP connection to a Redis shard can carry many SSUBSCRIBE channels, so connections scale with involved shards, while subscription state and fanout still scale with channels.
options_en: Open one dedicated TCP connection per channel, a million separate connections in total
Overhead is counted strictly at one connection per channel, regardless of node
One connection per node holding the relevant slots — the overhead scales with nodes, not channels
At least 16,384 connections, exactly matching the hash slot count
tradeoff: 少量长连接承载大量订阅 vs 每个频道仍有订阅状态和消息 fanout 成本
codeSample:
# One connection to shard/node A can carry many channel subscriptions.
SSUBSCRIBE user:1 user:27 user:8801
SSUBSCRIBE chat:abc chat:def

# A different shard needs a different Redis connection.
# But it is still one connection for many channels on that shard.
SSUBSCRIBE user:42 user:99 chat:west

# Mental model:
# connection_to_node_A.subscriptions = {user:1, user:27, user:8801, chat:abc, chat:def}
# connection_to_node_B.subscriptions = {user:42, user:99, chat:west}
diagram:
flowchart LR
  CS["Chat Server"] -->|one TCP connection| A["Redis shard A"]
  CS -->|one TCP connection| B["Redis shard B"]
  CS -->|one TCP connection| C["Redis shard C"]
  A --> ASubs["many SSUBSCRIBE channels\nuser:1, user:27, chat:abc..."]
  B --> BSubs["many SSUBSCRIBE channels\nuser:42, user:99..."]
  C --> CSubs["many SSUBSCRIBE channels\nchat:west..."]

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 连接：客户端和 Redis 节点之间的一条长连接，可以承载很多条订阅命令和很多个频道的推送。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TCP connection is one long-lived connection between a client and a Redis node, and it can carry many subscription commands and channel messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: subscription state：Redis 记录某个连接订阅了哪些频道的内存状态；频道多会增加状态，但不等于连接多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Subscription state is Redis's in-memory record of which channels a connection subscribed to; more channels add state, not separate TCP connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: sharded Pub/Sub：Redis 7+ 的分片 Pub/Sub，频道按 slot 归属到 shard，消息只在该 shard 内传播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharded Pub/Sub is Redis 7+'s Pub/Sub mode where channels are assigned to slots/shards and messages propagate only inside the shard.

q_en: How many connections to Redis does a server subscribed to one million channels need?
scenario_en: A Chat Server needs to subscribe to many Redis sharded Pub/Sub channels, for example user:1, user:2, and chat:abc, totaling one million channels. Each channel name hashes to a slot like a key, and the slot belongs to a Redis shard.
optionExplanations: 错：一条连接可以承载很多个 SSUBSCRIBE，不需要为每个频道单独开一条 TCP 连接。
错：连接开销不是按频道数算的，而是按涉及的节点/shard 数算，100 万频道不等于 100 万条连接。
对：一个频道不等于一条连接；一条打到某个分片的长连接底下能挂很多订阅，真正花钱的是连了几个持槽节点，不是订阅了几个频道。
错：连接数跟哈希槽总数 16384 没有固定对应关系，一条连接同样能承载多个 shard 上分布的订阅。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: one connection can carry many SSUBSCRIBEs — you don't need a separate TCP connection per channel.
Wrong: connection overhead isn't billed per channel; it's billed per node/shard involved — 1M channels isn't 1M connections.
Right: a channel isn't a TCP connection; one long-lived connection to a shard can carry many SSUBSCRIBEs, and the cost scales with nodes holding relevant slots.
Wrong: connection count has no fixed relationship to the 16384 hash slots — one connection can carry subscriptions spread across shards.

scenario: 聊天系统用 Pub/Sub 做在线实时投递，但产品要求用户重新上线后能补看离线期间错过的消息。
q: 正确的补法是？
options: 只是把 Pub/Sub 内部的消息缓冲区调得更大一些而已
想尽各种办法保证客户端的连接永远都不会意外断开或掉线
把全部实时投递流程都直接改成客户端定时轮询查询
Pub/Sub 之外再落一份可回放存储：Streams、Kafka/SQS 或 outbox 表
why: Pub/Sub 只通知此刻在线的订阅者；离线补课要从持久化日志/队列或 Message+Inbox 表重读。outbox 表常用来保证「写消息」和「稍后发布事件」不丢。
why_en: Pub/Sub only notifies subscribers that are online right now; offline catch-up must read from a durable log/queue or Message+Inbox tables. An outbox table is often used to make 'write the message' and 'publish the event later' reliable.
whenOtherWins: 若消息只对「此刻在场」的人有意义（光标位置、正在输入提示），纯 Pub/Sub 反而是最省的正确答案；若已用 Kafka 做实时消费，也可以不用 Redis Pub/Sub。
options_en: Just make Pub/Sub's internal message buffer even bigger, nothing else
Find every possible way to guarantee client connections never accidentally drop or disconnect
Replace the entire real-time delivery flow directly with client-side timed polling
Pair Pub/Sub with a replayable store: Streams, Kafka or SQS, or an outbox table
tradeoff: Pub/Sub 的即时低延迟 vs 持久化补课路径的存储/重试成本
codeSample:
# One common chat write path: DB outbox + Pub/Sub notify.
sendMessage(chatId, senderId, body):
  tx.begin()
  msg = Messages.insert(chatId, senderId, body)
  for userId in Participants.of(chatId):
    Inbox.insert(userId=userId, msgId=msg.id, status="PENDING")
  Outbox.insert(type="MessageCreated", msgId=msg.id, chatId=chatId)
  tx.commit()

outboxRelayLoop():
  for event in Outbox.fetchUnsent(limit=100):
    redis.publish("chat:" + event.chatId, { "msgId": event.msgId })
    Outbox.markSent(event.id)

onReconnect(userId, lastSeenMsgId):
  return Inbox.query(userId=userId, after=lastSeenMsgId)
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["sender client"] --> API["Message API"]
  API -->|DB tx| M["Messages table"]
  API -->|DB tx| I["Inbox rows per recipient"]
  API -->|DB tx| O["Outbox table"]
  O --> Relay["outbox relay"]
  Relay -->|PUBLISH msgId| PS["Redis Pub/Sub"]
  PS --> CS["online Chat Servers"]
  CS --> Online["online clients"]
  Offline["reconnecting client"] --> Sync["sync API"]
  Sync --> I
  Sync --> M

termDefinitions.meaning: Pub/Sub：发布者把消息发到频道，当前在线订阅者立即收到；Redis 不为离线订阅者保存历史。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub sends a message to a channel and current subscribers receive it immediately; Redis does not keep history for offline subscribers.

termDefinitions.meaning: Message/Inbox 表：Message 保存消息正文，Inbox 记录某个用户或设备应该补看的消息指针。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Message/Inbox tables store the message body and per-user or per-device pointers to messages that should be delivered or caught up.

termDefinitions.meaning: outbox 模式：在同一个数据库事务里写业务数据和待发布事件；后台 relay 读 outbox 后再 publish，避免 DB 成功但消息没发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The outbox pattern writes business data and pending events in the same database transaction; a relay later publishes them, avoiding a DB success with a lost publish.

termDefinitions.meaning: outbox relay：轮询或订阅 outbox 表的后台进程，负责把未发布事件发到 Pub/Sub、Streams、Kafka 或 SQS。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An outbox relay is a background process that reads unpublished outbox rows and sends them to Pub/Sub, Streams, Kafka, or SQS.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Streams：Redis 的追加式日志，可保留一段历史并让消费者按 ID 追赶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Streams is an append-only Redis log that can retain history and let consumers catch up by ID.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQS（Simple Queue Service）：AWS 的托管消息队列服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQS, or Simple Queue Service, is AWS's managed message queue.

q_en: What's the correct fix?
scenario_en: A chat system uses Pub/Sub for online real-time delivery, but product requires that users coming back online can catch up on messages they missed while offline.
optionExplanations: 错：Pub/Sub 本身就不持久化，缓冲区调再大也没用——离线时消息压根没有落地保存，无从补发。
错：想尽办法不让连接断开不现实，手机切后台、网络抖动都会断线，这不是能靠工程手段消除的前提。
错：把实时投递全改成轮询会牺牲实时性、还加大压力，而且照样解决不了「离线期间的消息去哪查」这个根本问题。
对：广播机制天生只喊得到当下在线的人；想让人下线后还能补看，就得另外找个能持久化、可重读的地方存一份，比如日志/队列或收件箱表。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Pub/Sub itself isn't persistent — a bigger buffer doesn't help, since while offline the message was never stored to resend.
Wrong: guaranteeing a connection never drops isn't realistic — phones backgrounding and flaky networks will disconnect regardless.
Wrong: switching everything to polling sacrifices real-time delivery and adds load, and still doesn't answer where offline messages live.
Right: Pub/Sub only notifies subscribers online right now; catching up offline needs a separate durable log/queue or a Message+Inbox table.

scenario: 你不直接用 Redis 原生 SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH，而是自己在 Redis 里维护一个注册表：topic:room123 -> {chat-server-a:9000, chat-server-b:9000}。原生 Pub/Sub 也有 TCP/TLS，但那是 chat server 到 Redis 的 Redis client 连接；自制方案里，发布者查集合后还要自己逐个 HTTP/TCP/gRPC 直发给订阅者服务器。
q: 「自制 Pub/Sub」（Redis 里存 topic → 订阅者地址集合，发布者自己逐个直发）相比原生 Pub/Sub 的缺点有哪些？（多选）
options: 网络跳数从 2 跳变成 3 跳
发布者要维护到订阅者服务器的连接；没有连接池就要临时建 TCP/TLS
订阅者宕机后要靠心跳/TTL 清理注册表，复杂且啰嗦
发布的消息体大小会受到限制
why: 原生 Pub/Sub 复用 chat server 到 Redis 的 TCP/TLS 连接，Redis 维护订阅并 push。自制只让 Redis 存地址，发布者查表后自己 fanout；连接池、重试、背压和旧地址清理都归应用。
why_en: Native Pub/Sub still uses TCP/TLS, but it reuses established Redis client connections from chat servers to Redis; Redis maintains channel-to-connection state and pushes over those connections. In a homegrown design, Redis only stores addresses, so the publisher fans out itself and owns server-to-server pools, TLS, retries, backpressure, health checks, and stale-address cleanup.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经有一套成熟的 service mesh、长连接池、健康检查和路由层，自制直发可以降低 Redis 数据面压力；但这时你其实是在重建一个消息路由系统，复杂度要算进去。
options_en: The network hop count goes from two hops to three
The publisher must maintain connections to subscriber servers; without a pool it pays TCP/TLS setup
A dead subscriber needs heartbeats or a TTL to clean up the registry, which is complex and chatty
The published message body size becomes limited
tradeoff: 原生 Pub/Sub 复用 Redis 的订阅连接/生命周期管理 vs 自制方案把路由和清理责任推给应用
codeSample:
# Native Pub/Sub: chat server keeps one Redis client connection open.
# The connection may be plain TCP or Redis TLS, depending on config.
SUBSCRIBE room:123
PUBLISH room:123 '{"text":"hi"}'
# Redis pushes to subscribers on their existing Redis connections.

# Homegrown registry: Redis stores addresses, not live Pub/Sub pipes.
SADD topic:room:123:subscribers chat-server-a:9000 chat-server-b:9000
SMEMBERS topic:room:123:subscribers

# Publisher must fan out server-to-server itself.
# rpcPool.send("chat-server-a:9000", message)
# rpcPool.send("chat-server-b:9000", message)

# It must also clean stale subscriber addresses.
SET subscriber:chat-server-a:9000:heartbeat 1 EX 30
SREM topic:room:123:subscribers chat-server-a:9000  # when lease expires
diagram:
flowchart TB
  subgraph Native["Native Redis Pub/Sub"]
    S1["Subscriber server A"] <-->|"Redis client TCP/TLS"| R1["Redis\nchannel -> live connections"]
    S2["Subscriber server B"] <-->|"Redis client TCP/TLS"| R1
    P1["Publisher"] -->|PUBLISH room:123| R1
    R1 -->|push on existing connection| S1
    R1 -->|push on existing connection| S2
  end

  subgraph Homegrown["Homegrown registry"]
    P2["Publisher"] -->|SMEMBERS topic subscribers| R2["Redis registry\ntopic -> server addresses"]
    R2 -->|addresses| P2
    P2 -->|app-owned HTTP/TCP/gRPC| H1["Subscriber server A"]
    P2 -->|app-owned HTTP/TCP/gRPC| H2["Subscriber server B"]
    H2 -.crashes.-> Stale["stale address unless heartbeat/TTL cleanup"]
  end

termDefinitions.meaning: 原生 Pub/Sub：Redis 自己维护频道和订阅连接的关系，发布时 Redis 直接把消息推给当前在线订阅者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Native Pub/Sub means Redis maintains the channel-to-subscriber-connection mapping and pushes messages to currently connected subscribers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自制 Pub/Sub：应用自己用 Redis 存 topic 到订阅者地址的注册表，并由发布者自己 fanout 到这些地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Homegrown Pub/Sub stores topic-to-subscriber-address mappings in Redis and makes the publisher fan out to those addresses itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 注册表：记录谁订阅了哪个 topic 的元数据表；自制方案需要维护它的新鲜度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A registry is metadata recording who subscribes to which topic; a homegrown design must keep it fresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 订阅者服务器：这里指订阅某个 topic 的 chat server 实例，不是用户手机；它负责再把消息推给自己连接着的客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A subscriber server here is a chat-server instance subscribed to a topic, not the user's phone; it later pushes messages to its connected clients.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP（传输控制协议）：建立连接后可靠传输字节流的协议，新建连接有握手开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP, or Transmission Control Protocol, is a connection-based reliable byte-stream protocol whose handshake adds setup cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis client connection：应用服务器到 Redis 的已建立连接；SUBSCRIBE 后 Redis 会在这条连接上持续推送消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis client connection is an established connection from the application server to Redis; after SUBSCRIBE, Redis pushes messages over that same connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: TLS：给 TCP 连接加密和校验身份的一层；Redis 可以配置 TLS 端口，但这不改变 Pub/Sub 的订阅模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS encrypts a TCP connection and can authenticate peers; Redis can be configured with a TLS port, but that does not change the Pub/Sub subscription model.

termDefinitions.meaning: heartbeat/TTL：订阅者定期续租自己的注册记录；如果停止续租，系统认为它已死并清理地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat/TTL lease means subscribers periodically refresh their registry entry; if they stop, the system treats them as dead and cleans up the address.

q_en: Compared to native Pub/Sub, what are the drawbacks of a homegrown Pub/Sub built on Redis (storing topic-to-subscriber-address sets, with the publisher fanning out directly)? (multi-select)
scenario_en: Instead of using Redis native SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH, you maintain your own registry in Redis: topic:room123 -> {chat-server-a:9000, chat-server-b:9000}. Native Pub/Sub also uses TCP/TLS, but that is the Redis client connection from a chat server to Redis. In the homegrown design, after reading the set, the publisher must send directly to subscriber servers over HTTP, TCP, or gRPC.
optionExplanations: 对：原生只需 chat server→Redis 这一跳给 Redis 处理；自制多了「查完注册表再逐个直发」这一跳，变成三跳。
对：原生方案蹭的是 chat server 本来就连着 Redis 的那条线；自己搭的话，发布者得给每台订阅者服务器单独握手建连，没有连接池就更慢更重。
对：注册表里的地址不会自动过期，订阅者宕机后要么靠心跳、要么靠 TTL 主动清理，逻辑全部自己写，比原生零维护啰嗦得多。
错：消息体大小限制不是自制方案独有的缺点，原生 Pub/Sub 同样有类似的实现限制，这不是两者的关键差异点。
optionExplanations_en: Right: native only needs one hop, chat-server-to-Redis, and Redis handles delivery; homegrown adds a second hop of registry lookup plus direct fanout — three hops.
Right: native reuses the chat server's existing connection to Redis; homegrown makes the publisher open its own TCP/TLS to every subscriber server.
Right: registry addresses don't lapse on their own — a subscriber's crash needs heartbeats or a TTL to clean it up, all hand-rolled.
Wrong: a message-size limit isn't a homegrown-specific drawback — native Pub/Sub has comparable implementation limits too.

q: 原生 Pub/Sub 里，一个频道的最后一个订阅者断开后会发生什么？
options: 频道会在内存里继续保留 24 小时才清理
频道从内存移除，之后对它的 publish 直接被丢弃
没有订阅者时，消息会开始堆积排队等待
publish 会向发布者返回一个错误提示
why: Redis 只为有活跃订阅者的频道占内存；没人听的频道就不存在，发了也就丢了——零清理成本。
why_en: When the last subscriber disconnects the channel vanishes from memory and later publishes to it are simply dropped.
options_en: The channel stays reserved in memory for 24 hours before cleanup
The channel is removed from memory and later publishes to it are simply dropped
With no subscribers, messages start queuing up waiting to be read
The publish call returns an error back to the publisher
q_en: In native Pub/Sub, what happens when a channel's last subscriber disconnects?
optionExplanations: 错：频道没有「保留 24 小时」这种缓冲期，最后一个订阅者一走，频道立刻不再存在。
对：只有还有人在听的频道才会占一点内存；没人听了它就等于不存在，往上面发东西也是白发——不用你操心清理。
错：Pub/Sub 不落盘也不排队，没有订阅者时消息不会堆积等待，而是直接被丢弃。
错：往一个没人监听的频道 publish 不会报错，Redis 正常处理这次调用，只是没有订阅者能收到而已。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: there's no 24-hour grace period for a channel — the moment the last subscriber leaves, the channel simply stops existing.
Right: Redis only spends memory on channels with active subscribers; an unwatched channel doesn't exist, so a publish to it is just dropped.
Wrong: Pub/Sub doesn't persist or queue — with no subscriber, a message doesn't pile up waiting, it's just discarded.
Wrong: publishing to a channel nobody's listening on doesn't error — Redis processes the call fine, it just has no subscriber to deliver to.

q: 100 节点的 Redis 缓存集群，某个商品突然爆红、流量占到全站一半，会发生什么？
options: 集群检测到热点后会自动触发一次槽再均衡
这份流量会被所有 100 台节点平均分摊
Redis 检测到热点后自动把这个 key 复制到多个节点
拥有这个 key 的那台节点负载暴涨、开始失败，其余 99 台闲着
why: key 哈希决定归属：一个 key 只住一台节点，节点再多也分不走单 key 的流量——这就是 hot key 问题（Memcached、DynamoDB 同样有）。
why_en: A single hot key lives on one node, so that node melts while the other ninety-nine idle, a problem Memcached and DynamoDB share.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Hot key"] --> B["One slot node hot"]
  B --> C["Replicas or key copies"]
  C --> D["Fan out reads"]
options_en: The cluster detects the hot spot and automatically triggers a slot rebalance
That traffic gets evenly shared across all one hundred nodes
Redis detects the hot spot and automatically replicates this key across nodes
The one node owning this key sees load spike and starts failing while the other ninety-nine sit idle
q_en: In a 100-node Redis cache cluster, a single product suddenly goes viral and its traffic hits half the whole site — what happens?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 不会因为检测到某个 key 热就自动触发槽再均衡，槽的归属不会因流量突增而自己变化。
错：一个 key 的哈希结果固定映射到一个槽、一个节点，流量不会因为集群有 100 台节点就自动摊开。
错：Redis 没有内建「检测热点自动复制 key 到多节点」的机制，这是需要应用层自己做的缓解手段。
对：某个 key 归谁管是哈希算出来的、固定住在一台机器上，就算集群再大，这个 key 的流量也只会砸在那一台上，别的全在旁边看戏。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis doesn't auto-trigger slot rebalancing just because it detects a hot key — ownership doesn't shift itself from a traffic spike.
Wrong: a key's hash maps to a single fixed slot and node; traffic doesn't spread out just because the cluster has 100 nodes.
Wrong: Redis has no built-in 'detect hot key, auto-replicate it' mechanism — that's a mitigation you build in the app layer.
Right: key hashing fixes ownership — a key lives on exactly one node, so that one node absorbs the traffic while the rest sit idle.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 少数几个爆款商品被海量读取，可以容忍秒级陈旧，希望大部分读请求根本不打到 Redis。
q: 最合适的缓解是？
options: 应用服务器进程内缓存这几个最热 key（配短 TTL）
单纯加大拥有热 key 的那台 Redis 节点的内存
把持久化模式从 RDB 换成 AOF
把集群的哈希槽总数从 16384 再调大
why: 应用服务器进程本身有内存，可放一个很小的 TTL map。读路径先查本机内存，miss 才查 Redis/DB；题目要求多数读不碰 Redis，所以本地挡热比 Redis 副本更贴合。
why_en: The app server process has its own memory, so it can keep a tiny TTL map. Reads check local memory first, then Redis/DB on miss; because the prompt wants most reads to avoid Redis entirely, local hot-key caching fits better than Redis replicas.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标只是别打爆 Redis primary，显式副本读或 key 副本也对；如果库存、余额这类不能陈旧，就不要用本地 TTL 缓存做正确性来源。
options_en: Cache the handful of hottest keys in-process on the app servers, with a short TTL
Just give the Redis node that owns the hot key more memory
Switch the persistence mode from RDB to AOF
Increase the cluster's total hash slot count beyond 16384
tradeoff: 本机内存挡住 Redis 热读 vs 每台 app 都有一份短暂旧值
codeSample:
localCache = TTLCache(maxKeys=100, ttl=2s)

getProduct(id):
  if localCache.has(id):
    return localCache.get(id)      # no Redis hop

  v = redis.get("product:" + id)
  if v == nil:
    v = db.queryProduct(id)
    redis.setex("product:" + id, 30s, v)

  localCache.set(id, v)            # per app process memory
  return v
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Req["read product:123"] --> App["App server"]
  App --> L["in-process TTL cache"]
  L -- hit --> Done["return stale-ok value"]
  L -- miss --> R["Redis"]
  R -- miss --> DB["Database"]
  R -- value --> App
  DB -- row --> App
  App --> L

termDefinitions.meaning: in-process cache：缓存存在应用服务器进程自己的内存里；每台 app 实例各有一份，不跨实例自动共享。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-process cache lives in the app server process memory; each app instance has its own copy and it is not automatically shared.

termDefinitions.meaning: local TTL：本机缓存只活几秒，允许少量陈旧，用自动过期换极低延迟和少打 Redis。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A local TTL keeps a value only for a few seconds, accepting slight staleness in exchange for very low latency and fewer Redis hits.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis replica read：把读摊到 Redis 副本，能保护 primary，但请求仍然会进入 Redis。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis replica reads spread traffic across Redis replicas and protect the primary, but requests still hit Redis.

q_en: What's the best mitigation?
scenario_en: A handful of viral products get read at massive volume, second-level staleness is tolerable, and you want most reads to never hit Redis at all.
optionExplanations: 对：应用进程自己就有内存，拿一小块出来做个带过期时间的本地缓存；读的时候先看本机有没有，没有才去问 Redis/DB，大部分请求根本不用出这台机器。
错：加大内存能多存数据，但改变不了「一个 key 只住一台节点」这个事实，热点流量还是全打在那一台上。
错：换持久化模式解决的是数据落盘/丢失问题，跟一个 key 被海量读打爆没有关系。
错：哈希槽总数固定在 16384，调大槽数改变不了某个具体 key 归属哪个节点，热 key 依然集中在一台机器上。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the app server has its own memory — put a tiny TTL map there; reads check local memory first and only hit Redis/DB on a miss.
Wrong: more memory lets that node hold more data, but doesn't change the fact that a key lives on exactly one node.
Wrong: switching persistence mode addresses durability/data loss, unrelated to one key getting hammered by reads.
Wrong: the slot count is fixed at 16384; raising it wouldn't change which single node a given key belongs to.

scenario: 一个读热 key 想横向摊到多台节点上，读方代码可以配合改造。
q: 「key 副本」方案怎么做？
options: 只是把 key 的名字改得更短一点，指望能减少内存占用
同一份数据存成 product:123:1..10 多个 key 散到不同槽，读者随机挑后缀读
用 hash tag 反而把这些数据副本全部绑到同一个槽上
打开集群自带的代理转发模式，指望它来分摊流量
why: 带不同后缀的 key 哈希到不同节点，读流量被随机打散；代价是每次写要扇出到所有副本，读者还得知道哪些 key 被复制过。
why_en: Storing copies under suffixed keys spreads them across nodes and readers pick a random suffix, while every write must fan out to all copies.
whenOtherWins: 写频繁的 key 不适合（写扇出放大）；那种情况优先在数据模型上拆分，或用副本读扛读热。
options_en: Just shorten the key's name a little, hoping that alone uses less memory
Store the data under suffixed keys like product:123:1 through 10 spread across slots, readers pick a random suffix
Use a hash tag to pin all of these data copies onto that very same slot instead
Turn on the cluster's built-in proxy forwarding mode, hoping it spreads the traffic
tradeoff: 读流量摊到多节点 vs 每次写扇出到全部副本的额外成本
q_en: How does the 'key copies' approach work?
scenario_en: You want to spread a read-hot key horizontally across multiple nodes, and the reader code can be changed to cooperate.
optionExplanations: 错：把 key 名字改短只影响内存占用，不会改变它落在哪个槽，热点流量照样集中在同一台节点。
对：带不同后缀的多份同数据（如 product:123:1..10）哈希到不同节点，读者随机挑一个后缀读，流量被摊到多台机器上。
错：hash tag 是故意把相关 key 绑到同一个槽，跟「key 副本」要把流量分散到多个槽的目标正好相反。
错：Redis Cluster 本身没有内建的代理转发模式帮你自动分摊，路由和副本选择要客户端自己实现。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: shortening the key name only affects memory footprint, not which slot it lands on — the hot traffic still concentrates on one node.
Right: storing several copies of the same data under different suffixes (e.g. product:123:1..10) hashes them to different nodes; readers pick a suffix at random.
Wrong: a hash tag deliberately pins related keys to the same slot — the opposite of what key replication is trying to do.
Wrong: Redis Cluster has no built-in proxy-forwarding mode that auto-spreads traffic for you — routing is on the client.

scenario: 一个商品详情 key 读爆了，你给拥有该 slot 的 primary 加了两个 replica，期望读流量自动分摊到副本上。
scenario_en: A product-detail key becomes read-hot. You add two replicas for the primary that owns the slot and expect reads to automatically spread to replicas.
q: 用读副本（read replicas）抗热 key，面试官爱追问的两个坑是？
options: 副本运行成本更贵，读取延迟也比主节点更慢
副本节点根本无法部署到别的机房或可用区
集群客户端默认仍读主节点（须显式配置副本读）；且对写热 key 毫无帮助
只要存在多个副本就会直接导致集群出现脑裂
why: Redis Cluster 客户端默认把 GET 发到 slot primary；副本不会自动分担读流量。要显式启用 replica read/READONLY，且只帮读热 key；SET、INCR 等写热 key 仍打 primary。
why_en: Redis replicas do not automatically serve cluster reads; enable replica reads or READONLY explicitly, and remember this helps read-hot keys, not write-hot keys.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务必须读到刚写入的新值，如库存扣减后的立即校验、支付状态确认，就不要随便读 replica；可以读 primary、做读己之写路由，或用短 TTL 客户端缓存承受可控陈旧。
options_en: Replicas cost more to run and add extra read latency versus the primary
Replica nodes simply cannot be deployed to a different region or availability zone
Cluster clients still read the primary by default (replica reads must be explicit), and replicas do nothing for write-hot keys
The mere existence of multiple replicas directly causes cluster split-brain
tradeoff: 副本读扩展读吞吐 vs 异步复制带来的陈旧读风险
codeSample:
# Cluster protocol idea: a replica can serve reads only after READONLY.
redis-cli -c -h replica-node
READONLY
GET product:123

# Client-library idea: names vary by library.
# Java Lettuce:
connection.setReadFrom(ReadFrom.REPLICA_PREFERRED)

# Node ioredis:
new Redis.Cluster(nodes, { scaleReads: "slave" })  # library name for replica reads
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["Cluster client"] -->|default GET/SET product:123| P["primary for slot 9421"]
  P -->|async replication| R1["replica 1"]
  P -->|async replication| R2["replica 2"]
  C -.explicit replica read / READONLY.-> R1
  C -.explicit replica read / READONLY.-> R2
  W["write-hot traffic"] -->|still primary only| P

termDefinitions.meaning: read preference：客户端的读路由策略，比如只读 primary、优先读 replica、或 primary/replica 混读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read preference is the client's read-routing policy, such as primary-only, replica-preferred, or mixed primary/replica reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: READONLY：Redis Cluster 里发给 replica 连接的命令，允许该连接从 replica 读取它所复制的 slot 数据；读到的值可能落后 primary。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: READONLY is a Redis Cluster command sent on a replica connection to allow reads for the slots it replicates; returned data may lag behind the primary.

termDefinitions.meaning: replication lag：replica 落后 primary 的时间或数据量，是副本读可能读到旧值的根源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication lag is how far a replica trails the primary in time or data, which is why replica reads can be stale.

q_en: When using read replicas to absorb a hot key, what two pitfalls do interviewers love to probe?
optionExplanations: 错：这不是面试官爱追问的坑——真正的坑在于「加了副本流量并不会自动跟着分流」，而不是成本或延迟本身。
错：副本完全可以部署到别的机房/可用区做异地容灾，这不是它抗热 key 时的限制点。
对：默认情况下客户端的读请求照样直奔主节点，副本不会自动接手，得手动打开读副本这个开关；而且这招对写操作扎堆的热 key 完全没用。
错：多个副本本身不会直接导致脑裂，脑裂通常跟 failover/网络分区时的选主逻辑相关，不是「存在副本」这件事本身。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that's not the trap interviewers probe for — the real gotcha is that adding replicas doesn't automatically redirect any traffic to them.
Wrong: replicas can absolutely be deployed to a different region/AZ for disaster recovery — not the limitation for hot-key mitigation.
Right: a Redis Cluster client defaults to sending GET to the slot's primary; replicas need explicit reads enabled, and none of this helps a write-hot key like INCR/SET.
Wrong: having multiple replicas doesn't by itself cause split-brain — that's usually about failover/partition election logic.

q: 把「热 key 应对」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 缓解：客户端缓存 / key 副本 / 副本读，按读热还是写热选择
现象：单个爆款 key 的流量激增
代价：多副本会读到旧值，写入或删除也要同步到更多地方
诊断：key 哈希到唯一节点，单节点过载而集群其余空闲
why: 缓存一致性不是“建集群”，而是同一份值有多份缓存后，更新时如何避免长期读旧值。热 key 多副本能分散读流量，但每次写入、删除或失效都要同步更多地方。
why_en: Cache consistency is not just building a cluster. It is the problem of keeping multiple cached copies of the same value from staying stale after an update. Replicating a hot key spreads reads, but writes, deletes, and invalidations must touch more places.
q_en: Put the decision chain for handling a hot key in the correct order:
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Hot["hot key: product:123"] --> One["one Redis shard overloaded"]
    One --> A["client cache"]
    One --> B["key copies: product:123:0..N"]
    One --> C["replica reads"]
    A --> AC["risk: local stale value"]
    B --> BC["cost: write/delete fanout"]
    C --> CC["risk: replica lag"]

rows: App 本地短 TTL 直接命中
更新后本地副本可能短暂旧
读随机打到 N 份 copy
写入/删除要扇出到 N 份
读 Redis replica 分担主库
复制延迟下可能读旧值

termDefinitions.meaning: 少数 key 承接大量请求，导致它所在的 Redis 分片过载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a key that receives so many requests that the Redis shard owning it becomes overloaded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一份数据有多个缓存副本时，更新后如何让读请求别长期读到旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache consistency is the problem of preventing reads from seeing stale cached copies for too long after the data changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次业务写入需要更新、删除或失效多个缓存副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means one logical write has to update, delete, or invalidate multiple cached copies.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把读请求打到 Redis replica 来分担主节点压力，但可能受到复制延迟影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replica reads send reads to Redis replicas to reduce primary load, but can observe replication lag.

q: 哪些信号说明这个场景不该用 Redis？（多选）
options: 数据是唯一的真相源，一条都不能丢
工作集大到放内存不经济
需要 join、跨 key 的灵活查询
需要亚毫秒级读取
why: 异步复制 + 持久化窗口意味着已确认写可能消失；内存是最贵的存储位置；Redis 没有 join。亚毫秒读恰恰是「该用 Redis」的理由。
why_en: Avoid Redis as a system of record, for working sets too big for RAM, or when you need joins and cross-key queries; sub-millisecond reads are exactly why you would use it.
options_en: Data is the single source of truth and none of it can be lost
The working set is too big to fit in RAM economically
You need joins or flexible cross-key queries
You need sub-millisecond reads
q_en: Which signals indicate Redis is the wrong choice for this scenario? (multi-select)
optionExplanations: 对：异步复制+持久化窗口意味着已确认写入可能在 failover 时消失，不适合当唯一真相源。
对：内存是最贵的存储位置，工作集一旦大到放内存不经济，就该考虑磁盘型存储而不是硬塞进 Redis。
对：Redis 没有跨 key 的 join 能力，需要灵活关联查询的场景该用支持这类查询的数据库。
错：读取能做到亚毫秒级，正是选它的加分项，不是拒绝它的信号，这个选项说反了方向。
optionExplanations_en: Right: async replication plus a persistence window means a confirmed write can vanish on failover — not a fit as the single source of truth.
Right: memory is the most expensive place to store data — once the working set is too big to fit economically, look at disk-based storage instead.
Right: Redis has no cross-key join capability; a case needing flexible relational queries should use a database built for that.
Wrong: sub-millisecond reads are exactly the reason TO use Redis, not a signal against it — this option points the wrong direction.

scenario: Redis Cluster 把 key 分到 16384 个 hash slot，每个 slot 归一个主节点。你想一条命令同时写两个 key，比如 MSET user:1:name A user:1:age 20，或者用 MULTI/EXEC 把两个 key 一起改掉。
scenario_en: Redis Cluster maps keys into 16,384 hash slots, with each slot owned by one primary node. You want one command to touch two keys, such as MSET user:1:name A user:1:age 20, or a MULTI/EXEC transaction that updates two keys together.
q: 集群模式下多 key 操作（MSET、含多个 key 的 MULTI）的限制是？
options: 所有 key 必须落在同一个槽（hash tag 可以安排到）
集群模式完全不支持任何形式的多 key 命令
跨槽的多 key 操作会自动做两阶段提交协调
跨槽情况下只支持只读的多 key 命令
why: MSET/MULTI 必须在一个节点完成；不同槽归不同主，Redis Cluster 不做跨节点事务协调，会报 CROSSSLOT。用相同 hash tag 可把相关 key 放同槽。
why_en: MSET or a MULTI transaction must execute on one node. If the keys map to different slots, they belong to different primaries, and Redis Cluster does not run a cross-node transaction coordinator; it returns a CROSSSLOT error. Use a shared hash tag when those keys must be operated on together.
options_en: All keys must land in the same slot (a hash tag can arrange this)
Cluster mode does not support any form of multi-key command at all
A cross-slot multi-key operation automatically runs two-phase commit coordination
Across slots, only read-only multi-key commands are supported
codeSample:
# Same hash tag -> same slot -> one node can run the command.
MSET user:{1}:name A user:{1}:age 20

# Likely different slots -> different primaries -> CROSSSLOT.
MSET user:1:name A user:2:name B

# Same rule for MULTI/EXEC: all touched keys must share one slot.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["MSET key1 key2"] --> B{"same hash slot?"}
  B -->|yes| C["one primary executes it"]
  B -->|no| D["different primaries"]
  D --> E["CROSSSLOT, no 2PC"]

termDefinitions.meaning: MSET：一条 Redis 命令里同时设置多个 key-value；在 Cluster 中这些 key 必须同槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSET is a Redis command that sets multiple key-value pairs in one command; in Cluster, those keys must share one slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: MULTI/EXEC：Redis 事务，把多条命令排队后一次执行；在 Cluster 中事务触碰的 key 也必须同槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MULTI/EXEC is a Redis transaction that queues commands and executes them together; in Cluster, the touched keys must share one slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: CROSSSLOT：Redis Cluster 发现一条多 key 请求里的 key 不在同一个槽时返回的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CROSSSLOT is the error Redis Cluster returns when keys in one multi-key request do not hash to the same slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: hash tag：key 名里花括号包住的部分；Redis Cluster 只哈希这段，让相关 key 可以被安排到同槽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash tag is the part of a key inside braces; Redis Cluster hashes only that part so related keys can be placed in the same slot.

termDefinitions.meaning: two-phase commit：跨节点事务协调协议；Redis Cluster 不会为跨槽 MSET/MULTI 自动做这件事。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit is a cross-node transaction coordination protocol; Redis Cluster does not automatically do it for cross-slot MSET or MULTI.

q_en: What's the restriction on multi-key operations (MSET, a MULTI touching several keys) in cluster mode?
optionExplanations: 对：这类多 key 命令得在同一个节点上一口气做完；槽分给了不同的主节点就没法跨节点协调，会直接报错，用同一个 hash tag 能把它们摁进同一个槽。
错：同槽内的多 key 命令是支持的，只是要求这些 key 落在同一个槽，不是完全不支持。
错：集群不会主动帮跨槽的多 key 操作做两阶段提交，槽不一致直接就报错了，不存在自动协调这回事。
错：跨槽限制不区分读写——无论是读还是写，跨槽的多 key 命令都不支持，不是「只放行只读」。
optionExplanations_en: Right: MSET/MULTI must complete on one node; different slots belong to different primaries, so Redis Cluster throws CROSSSLOT — a shared hash tag fixes it.
Wrong: multi-key commands are supported as long as the keys land on the same slot — not a blanket 'no multi-key commands' rule.
Wrong: Redis Cluster doesn't auto-coordinate a two-phase commit across slots — a cross-slot op just throws CROSSSLOT, no help offered.
Wrong: the cross-slot restriction doesn't distinguish read from write — cross-slot multi-key commands fail either way.

scenario: Postgres/MySQL 这类数据库允许你写一条比较抽象的 SQL：查用户、过滤状态、按时间排序、再 join 订单表。数据库会先生成多个可能的执行方案，再选一个预计最便宜的方案。Redis 不走这条路：你要提前把数据放成合适的结构，比如 String、Hash、Set、Sorted Set，然后直接调用 GET/HGET/ZRANGE 这类明确命令。
scenario_en: Databases such as Postgres or MySQL let you write a fairly abstract SQL query: find users, filter by status, sort by time, and join an orders table. The database generates possible execution strategies and chooses the estimated cheapest one. Redis does not work this way: you pre-shape data into structures such as String, Hash, Set, or Sorted Set, then call explicit commands such as GET, HGET, or ZRANGE.
q: 相比自带优化器和查询计划器的数据库，Redis 的取向是？
options: 追求比别人更智能的自动优化
刻意保持简单：只把简单操作做到极快，组合方式留给你
把所有实现细节都藏起来
面向复杂的分析型查询设计
why: Redis 不像 SQL 数据库那样替你规划 join、索引选择和排序路径；GET/HGET/ZRANGE 的访问路径由数据结构决定。好处是性能透明、命令快；代价是复杂查询和二级索引要提前建模。
why_en: Redis favors explicit data-structure access over SQL-style planning, which keeps commands predictable but pushes joins, secondary indexes, and complex queries into your model.
options_en: Chasing smarter automatic optimization than everyone else
Deliberately staying simple: make simple operations very fast and leave composition to you
Hiding every implementation detail from you
Designed around complex analytical queries
tradeoff: 数据库自动规划复杂查询 vs Redis 明确数据结构带来的可预测性能
codeSample:
-- SQL database: declarative query; planner chooses indexes/join/order.
SELECT *
FROM orders o
JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE u.status = 'active'
ORDER BY o.created_at DESC
LIMIT 20;

# Redis: explicit access path chosen by your data model.
ZREVRANGE orders:active_users:by_created_at 0 19
HGETALL order:123
diagram:
flowchart LR
  SQL["SQL: what result do I want?"] --> P["Optimizer / query planner"]
  P --> E["Execution plan: index scan, join order, sort strategy"]
  E --> Rows["Rows returned"]

  RQ["Redis command: exact operation"] --> DS["Chosen data structure"]
  DS --> RR["Predictable command cost"]

termDefinitions.meaning: optimizer：数据库里负责比较多种执行方式并选择预计成本最低方案的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An optimizer compares possible execution strategies and chooses the one with the lowest estimated cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: query planner：把 SQL 变成具体执行计划的组件，例如决定用哪个索引、join 顺序和排序方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A query planner turns SQL into a concrete execution plan, such as index choice, join order, and sorting strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: execution plan：数据库最终采用的查询步骤清单，例如 index scan、table scan、hash join、sort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An execution plan is the list of query steps the database will run, such as index scan, table scan, hash join, or sort.

termDefinitions.meaning: access pattern：应用实际怎么读写数据，例如按用户查订单、按分数取排行榜、按时间取最近消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An access pattern is how the application actually reads or writes data, such as fetching orders by user, leaderboard by score, or recent messages by time.

q_en: Compared to databases with a built-in optimizer and query planner, what's Redis's orientation?
optionExplanations: 错：Redis 没有比传统数据库更智能的自动优化器，它反而是刻意不做这层规划，把选择权交给你。
对：它不会像 SQL 数据库那样帮你规划怎么 join、走哪个索引、怎么排序，只把几个基础读写命令做到飞快，怎么拼起来是你的事。
错：Redis 恰恰不藏实现细节——访问路径由你选的数据结构决定，命令直接对应底层操作，是透明的，不是黑盒。
错：面向复杂分析型查询设计的是列式 OLAP 引擎，Redis 的取向正相反，是面向简单高频操作。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: Redis doesn't have a smarter auto-optimizer than traditional databases — it deliberately skips that planning layer.
Right: unlike a SQL database planning joins, indexes, and sort paths for you, Redis just makes simple ops like GET/HGET/ZRANGE extremely fast and leaves composition to you.
Wrong: Redis doesn't hide implementation details — the access path is exactly the data structure you chose, transparent rather than a black box.
Wrong: designing for complex analytical queries describes a columnar OLAP engine — Redis's orientation is the opposite.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: Redis 是纯内存存储，重启会丢数据，靠 RDB 快照或 AOF 日志落盘持久化。
scenario_en: Redis keeps data in memory and loses it on restart, so it persists to disk via either RDB snapshots or the AOF log.
q: 关于 RDB 与 AOF 的对比，下面哪个说法正确？
q_en: Which statement about RDB vs AOF is correct?
options: AOF 丢数据窗口更小，RDB 恢复更快
RDB 记录每条写命令，AOF 存周期性全量二进制快照
两者都只把数据放在内存里、根本不写磁盘
AOF 与 RDB 都靠 SSTable 合并来压缩体积
options_en: AOF loses less data on a crash; RDB restores faster
RDB logs every write command while AOF stores periodic full snapshots
Both keep data only in memory and never write to disk
Both AOF and RDB rely on SSTable compaction to shrink in size
why: RDB = 周期性全量二进制快照，恢复快但会丢上次快照后的写；AOF = 顺序追加每条写命令、重放恢复，就是 Redis 的 WAL，最多丢约 1 秒。二者可同时开：AOF 保命 + RDB 快恢复。
why_en: RDB is a periodic full snapshot: fast restore but loses writes since the last one. AOF appends every write and replays on restart — Redis's WAL, losing ~1s. You can run both.
tradeoff: RDB（恢复快 / 可能丢更多） vs AOF（丢得少 / 文件大、恢复慢）

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 周期性把整个数据集存成一份二进制快照文件
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RDB is a periodic full binary snapshot of the entire Redis dataset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序追加每条写命令的日志，重启时重放恢复，相当于 Redis 的 WAL
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOF is an append-only log of every write command, replayed on restart — Redis's write-ahead log.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先把写顺序追加到日志再应用，崩溃后靠重放日志恢复
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records each write sequentially before applying it, so a crash recovers by replay.

optionExplanations: 对：AOF 每秒 fsync、丢数据窗口约 1 秒；RDB 直接载入快照、恢复更快。
错：说反了——RDB 才是周期性全量快照，AOF 才是逐条追加写命令。
错：两者都会落盘（AOF 日志 / RDB 快照文件），不是只放内存。
错：SSTable 合并是 LSM 存储的事，Redis 持久化不用 SSTable。
optionExplanations_en: Right: AOF fsyncs every second (~1s loss window); RDB loads a snapshot directly, so it restores faster.
Wrong: it is reversed — RDB is the periodic full snapshot, AOF is the append-per-write log.
Wrong: both write to disk (AOF log / RDB snapshot file), not memory only.
Wrong: SSTable compaction belongs to LSM storage; Redis persistence does not use SSTables.

scenario: 乘客请求要进消息队列——「崩溃也不能丢单」，还想把不同请求分给不同 matcher worker 并行处理。
scenario_en: Ride requests go through a message queue that must not drop a request even on a crash, and different requests should fan out to different matcher workers in parallel.
q: 用 Redis Streams vs Kafka 做这个队列，哪个说法对？
q_en: For this queue, which statement about Redis Streams vs Kafka is correct?
options: Redis Streams 纯内存、崩溃即全部丢失，这种绝对不能丢单的场景只能选 Kafka 来接收
消费组是 Kafka 独有的能力，Redis Streams 只能单消费者、无法把消息分给多个 worker 并行
两者都有消费组分发多 worker；耐久上 Kafka（磁盘+副本）更抗丢，Redis 内存快但保留有限
Redis 的 XACK 和 Kafka 提交 offset 是毫不相干的两套机制，语义上根本不能类比
options_en: Redis Streams is pure in-memory and loses everything on a crash, so a no-drop case must use Kafka
Consumer groups are Kafka-only; Redis Streams has a single consumer and can't fan out to workers
Both have consumer groups to fan out to workers; on durability Kafka (disk+replicas+long retention) is strongest, Redis is faster but retention is limited
Redis XACK and Kafka offset commit are unrelated mechanisms and can't be compared
optionExplanations: 错：有 AOF 持久化 + PEL 兜住在途消息，不是一崩全丢，只是耐久弱于 Kafka 磁盘+副本。
错：消费组（XREADGROUP GROUP）本就是 Streams 的能力，组内按 worker 负载均衡、能并行。
对：正是本题取舍点——分发能力两者都具备，胜负只在耐久强弱。
错：XACK 和提交 offset 语义相同——都是「标记已完成」，不标就会被重投（at-least-once），能类比。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: AOF persistence + a PEL hold in-flight messages, so it is not a total loss — just less durable than Kafka disk+replicas.
Wrong: consumer groups (XREADGROUP GROUP) are a Streams feature; the group load-balances across workers, so it parallelizes.
Right: this is the trade-off — both can fan out; the only real difference is how durable each is.
Wrong: XACK and committing an offset mean the same thing — "mark done"; skip it and the message is redelivered (at-least-once), so they are analogous.
why: 两者都用消费组把消息分给不同 worker（Redis XREADGROUP / Kafka partition）。选谁看耐久：Kafka 磁盘+副本可回放、最抗丢单；Redis Streams 内存快、不丢在途(PEL)，但保留受限。
why_en: Both fan out to workers via consumer groups (Redis XREADGROUP / Kafka partition assignment). Pick by durability: Kafka's disk + replicas + long retention + replay make it strongest for 'never drop a request'; Redis Streams is low-latency and doesn't lose in-flight work (PEL) but retention is memory-bound.
tradeoff: Redis Streams（内存·低延迟·保留有限） vs Kafka（磁盘+副本·高耐久·可回放·大吞吐）

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组 worker 共享一个队列，一条消息只发给组内一个 worker，从而把负载分给多台机器
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group lets a set of workers share a queue so each message goes to just one worker — spreading load.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 消费者在某个 partition 里的读取位置；提交 offset = 记下「读到这了」，重启从这继续
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a Kafka consumer's read position in a partition; committing it records progress so restarts resume there.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Streams 里标记一条消息「已处理完」，从 PEL 移除；作用等价于 Kafka 提交 offset
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XACK marks a Redis Streams message as processed and removes it from the PEL — analogous to committing a Kafka offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费组里「已投递但还没 XACK」的消息列表；worker 死了这些不丢，可被 XAUTOCLAIM 接管重做
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The PEL holds delivered-but-not-yet-acked messages; if a worker dies they survive and can be taken over via XAUTOCLAIM.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka topic 的分区，组内每个分区被一个消费者独占，是并行度与保序的单位（按 key 分区）
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is a slice of a Kafka topic; each is consumed by one consumer in a group — the unit of parallelism and per-key ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个逻辑事件类型一个 topic/stream（如 ride-requests 一个）；并行/保序靠 Kafka 的 partition 或 Redis 的多 stream/消费组——不是一个事件一条 stream
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model one topic/stream per logical event type (e.g. one ride-requests); parallelism/ordering comes from Kafka partitions or multiple Redis streams — not one stream per event.

termDefinitions.meaning: 至少一次投递：处理完才确认(ack/commit)，没确认就重投——保证不丢，但可能重复，业务要幂等
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once delivery: a message is redelivered until acknowledged, so nothing is lost but handlers must be idempotent.

scenario: 用 Redis TTL 锁保护派单，但锁可能在持有者 GC 卡顿时提前过期，两个 worker 都以为自己还持锁。
scenario_en: A Redis TTL lock guards dispatch, but it can expire during a holder GC pause, leaving two workers both thinking they hold it.
q: 光靠锁不够时，下游怎么保证只有一个写生效？
q_en: When the lock alone is not enough, how does the downstream ensure only one write takes effect?
options: 下游做原子条件写或校验 fencing token，拒掉旧持有者的迟到写
只要把锁 TTL 调得足够长，就永远不会在干活时过期，下游无需再防
让两个 worker 都写下游，用 last-write-wins 让最后写的那个覆盖生效
每个 worker 加锁前先随机 sleep 一段，从时间上错开就不会撞
options_en: The downstream does an atomic conditional write or checks a fencing token, rejecting a stale holder late write
Just make the lock TTL long enough that it never expires mid-work, so no downstream guard is needed
Let both workers write downstream and use last-write-wins so the last writer overwrites
Have each worker sleep a random time before locking so they never collide in time
optionExplanations: 对：这才是正确性的最终保证——CAS 或 fencing 让迟到的旧持有者写不进去。
错：再长的 TTL 也可能被 GC/暂停超过，只降低概率不消除，还拖慢故障恢复。
错：last-write-wins 恰好让旧持有者的过期写覆盖新结果，正是要防的。
错：sleep 只是碰运气错开，并发下照样撞，不是正确性保证。
optionExplanations_en: Right: this is the final correctness guarantee — CAS or fencing keeps a stale holder late write out.
Wrong: any TTL can be exceeded by a GC/pause; a longer TTL only lowers the odds and slows recovery.
Wrong: last-write-wins is exactly what lets the stale holder overwrite the new result — the thing to prevent.
Wrong: sleeping just staggers by luck; under concurrency they still collide — not a guarantee.
why: 锁可能在你干活时提前过期 → 两个 worker 都以为自己持锁。真正保正确的是下游：①原子 CAS（仅当状态没变才写，两人也只一个赢）②fencing token（下游只认更大编号，拒绝旧持有者的迟到写）。锁只是减竞争的优化。
why_en: A lock can expire while you are still working, so two workers may both think they hold it. Correctness comes from the downstream store: (1) an atomic CAS (write only if the state is unchanged, so only one wins) or (2) a fencing token (accept only a higher token, rejecting a stale holder late write). The lock is just a contention optimization.
tradeoff: CAS（简单·针对某个状态） vs fencing token（更通用·拒绝一切旧持有者写）
codeSample:
# ① 原子条件写(CAS)：仅当 ride 仍是 pending 才改 → 两个 worker 也只有一个赢
won = EVAL "if redis.call(GET,KEYS[1])==pending then
             redis.call(SET,KEYS[1],ARGV[1]); return 1 else return 0 end"
         1 ride:42:status assigned:driverB
if won == 1: notify(driverB)   # 赢了才真正派单
else:        skip()            # 已被别人派/接受 → 不做(幂等)

# ② fencing token：加锁发一个单调递增编号，下游只认更大的
token = INCR ride:42:fence     # …33, 34, 35 永远递增
write_status(ride 42, token)   # 下游: 若 token <= 已见过的最大值 → 拒绝(旧持有者的迟到写)

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子的条件写：仅当当前值等于预期(如仍是 pending)才更新，否则失败——并发下只有一个赢家
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set: an atomic conditional write that updates only if the value still equals the expected one, so only one racer wins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加锁时发的单调递增编号；下游记住见过的最大值，拒绝编号更小的写，从而挡住锁已过期的旧持有者
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing number issued at lock time; the store remembers the max seen and rejects smaller-token writes, blocking a stale holder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 冲突时让最后写入的覆盖之前的；对锁场景是错的，因为迟到的旧持有者会盖掉新结果
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-write-wins lets the latest write overwrite earlier ones — wrong for locking, since a late stale holder can clobber the new result.

scenario: 派单要保证「同一个 ride 只被处理一次」，在 Redis 分布式锁和数据库锁之间选。
scenario_en: Dispatch must ensure a ride is processed only once; choose between a Redis distributed lock and a database lock.
q: Redis 锁 vs 数据库锁，什么时候用哪个？
q_en: Redis lock vs database lock — when do you use which?
options: 高吞吐低延迟用 Redis 锁+下游 fencing；要和业务写同事务、强一致用 DB 锁
数据库锁在任何并发场景都又慢又弱，任何时候都应该用 Redis 锁去替代掉它
两种锁在性能和一致性上完全等价，随便选哪一个都不会有任何区别
Redis 锁天生和业务的数据库写在同一个事务里，所以一致性比 DB 锁更强
options_en: High throughput/low latency: Redis lock + downstream fencing; need the lock and the business write in one transaction / strong consistency: DB lock
A database lock is always slower and weaker in every case, so you should always replace it with a Redis lock
The two locks are completely equivalent in performance and consistency, so pick either one freely
A Redis lock is inherently in the same transaction as the database write, so it is more consistent than a DB lock
optionExplanations: 对：Redis 锁快但会过期、要下游兜底；DB 锁慢但锁和写同事务、天然一致——按吞吐 vs 强一致选。
错：当「锁+写要原子」时 DB 锁反而更强更简单，不是任何场景都劣。
错：两者差别很大——Redis 快但尽力而为，DB 慢但事务内强一致。
错：Redis 锁和 DB 业务写是两个系统、不在同一事务——这恰恰是它需要 fencing 的原因。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a Redis lock is fast but expires and needs a downstream guard; a DB lock is slower but atomic with the write — choose by throughput vs strong consistency.
Wrong: when the lock and write must be atomic, a DB lock is stronger and simpler — not inferior everywhere.
Wrong: they differ a lot — Redis is fast but best-effort, a DB lock is strongly consistent within its transaction.
Wrong: a Redis lock and the DB write are two systems, not one transaction — which is exactly why it needs fencing.
why: Redis 锁：快、尽力而为，会 TTL 过期 → 靠下游 CAS/fencing 保正确；DB 锁（SELECT FOR UPDATE）：事务内持有、随提交释放、和业务写同事务原子、无过期问题，但吞吐低、给 DB 加负载。高频选 Redis+兜底，强一致/锁写同事务选 DB。
why_en: A Redis lock is fast and best-effort — it can expire, so correctness relies on downstream CAS/fencing. A DB lock (SELECT FOR UPDATE) is held inside the transaction, released on commit, atomic with the business write, and never expires — but lower throughput and more DB load. Pick Redis+guard for high volume, DB when the lock and write must be one transaction.
tradeoff: Redis 锁（快·尽力而为·需下游兜底） vs 数据库锁（慢·锁写同事务·强一致）

rows: 会 TTL 过期→需兜底
和业务写同事务，天然一致
多一个 Redis 要监控

codeSample:
# Redis 锁：快、尽力而为（会 TTL 过期，需下游 fencing 兜底）
SET lock:ride:42 token NX EX 10     # 抢锁；持有者崩了靠 TTL 自动释放
...临界区...  再用 Lua 校验 token 后 DEL   # 只删自己的锁

# 数据库锁：在事务里，锁+写同提交，无过期问题
BEGIN;
SELECT * FROM rides WHERE id=42 FOR UPDATE;  # 行锁，持到事务结束
UPDATE rides SET driver=B WHERE id=42;       # 锁和写在同一事务，原子
COMMIT;                                       # 提交即释放锁

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库行级锁：在事务里锁住选中的行，直到 COMMIT/ROLLBACK 才释放，无 TTL 过期问题
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE takes a row lock held until the transaction commits or rolls back — no TTL expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 应用级咨询锁(pg_advisory_lock)，由应用自己约定用途、不锁具体行，可当分布式锁用
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Postgres advisory lock (pg_advisory_lock) is an app-defined lock not tied to a row, usable as a distributed lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加锁发的单调递增编号，下游只认更大的、拒绝旧持有者的迟到写——Redis 锁的正确性兜底
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing number; the store rejects smaller-token writes, backstopping a Redis lock.

scenario: Redis Cluster 里某个分片的 master 节点挂了,它有几个 replica。
scenario_en: In a Redis Cluster, a shard's master node dies; it has a few replicas.
q: 怎么选出这个分片的新 master?
q_en: How is a new master chosen for this shard?
options: 挂掉 master 的 replica 发起选举、向其他 master 拉票,得多数票者自升为 master 接管槽(集群内置)
由客户端投票,得票最多的那个 replica 被选为新的 master 节点
必须运维人工登录、手动把某个 replica 提升成 master 才行
由外部的 ZooKeeper / 协调服务来指定哪个 replica 当新 master
options_en: The dead master's replicas hold an election, requesting votes from the other masters; the one with a majority promotes itself and takes over the slots (built into the cluster)
Clients vote, and the replica with the most votes becomes the new master
An operator must manually SSH in and promote a replica by hand
An external ZooKeeper / coordination service designates which replica becomes master
optionExplanations: 对:Redis Cluster 内置故障转移——replica 向其他 master 拉票,拿多数 master 票就自升、接管哈希槽,gossip 广播。
错:投票的是「其他 master 节点」,不是客户端。
错:集群自动做,不需要人工手动提升(那是没做自动化才被迫的)。
错:Redis Cluster 不依赖外部协调服务;master 之间自己投票选。
optionExplanations_en: Right: built-in failover — a replica requests votes from the other masters, a majority makes it promote itself and take over the slots, then gossip broadcasts it.
Wrong: the voters are the other master nodes, not clients.
Wrong: the cluster does it automatically; manual promotion is only a fallback when automation is missing.
Wrong: Redis Cluster needs no external coordinator; the masters vote among themselves.
why: Redis Cluster 内置自动故障转移:master 失联被「多数 master」标 FAIL 后,它的 replica 发起选举、向其他 master 拉票(不是客户端、不是外部服务);数据最新的 replica 等待最短、通常先赢;拿到多数 master 票就自升为 master、接管哈希槽,gossip 广播新路由。非分片的主从则用 Sentinel(随 Redis 发布的独立进程)。
why_en: Redis Cluster has built-in failover: after a majority of masters mark a dead master FAIL, its replicas hold an election, requesting votes from the other masters (not clients, not an external service); the most up-to-date replica waits the least and usually wins; with a majority of master votes it promotes itself, takes over the hash slots, and gossips the new routing. A non-sharded master-replica setup uses Sentinel (a separate process shipped with Redis).
tradeoff: Sentinel(非分片主从·独立哨兵进程) vs Cluster 内置(分片·master 互相投票)
codeSample:
# Redis Cluster 自动故障转移(分片·内置·无需 Sentinel)
# 1) 检测:节点间 gossip 心跳;master A 失联
#    某 master 标 A=PFAIL;多数 master 认同 → FAIL(确认挂)
# 2) A 的 replica 发起选举(数据越新等待越短 → 最新的先发)
for r in A.replicas:
    wait(rank_by_repl_offset(r) * DELAY)   # 数据最新的 replica 先启动
    r.epoch += 1
    send FAILOVER_AUTH_REQUEST(epoch) -> 所有其他 master   # 向 master 拉票
# 3) 其他 master 投票(每个 epoch 只投一次)
on master recv REQUEST(epoch, r):
    if epoch > lastVoted and r.master == FAIL:
        vote ACK; lastVoted = epoch
# 4) 拿到「多数 master 票」的 replica 胜出
if r.votes >= majority(masters):
    r.promote_to_master(); take_over(A.slots)   # 自升 + 接管哈希槽
    gossip(new_config)                          # 广播新路由

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片集群内置的自动故障转移:master 挂了,它的 replica 向「其他 master」拉票,拿多数 master 票者自升为 master、接管哈希槽、gossip 广播。投票的是 master 不是 Sentinel,所以 master 数要奇数≥3 防脑裂
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster built-in failover: when a master dies, its replicas request votes from the other masters; a majority makes one self-promote, take over the slots, and gossip it. Masters vote (not Sentinels), so you want an odd number ≥3 to avoid split-brain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两套故障转移:Sentinel=给「非分片的主从」用,是单独跑的哨兵进程、哨兵们投票提升一个 replica;Cluster=给「分片」用、内置在节点里,由其他 master 投票提升。分片场景用 Cluster(自带)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two failover systems: Sentinel is for a non-sharded master-replica group — separate sentinel processes vote to promote a replica; Cluster is for sharding — built into the nodes, the other masters vote. For sharding, Cluster is built in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次故障转移递增的版本号:保证每个 epoch、每个 master 只投一票,防止双主/脑裂(和 Raft term、fencing token 一个思路)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version number bumped each failover so each master votes only once per epoch, preventing split-brain — the same idea as a Raft term or a fencing token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集群节点之间定期互相交换心跳和路由信息的协议;靠它发现节点挂、传播新的槽归属
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A protocol where cluster nodes periodically exchange heartbeats and routing info; used to detect failures and spread new slot ownership.

scenario: 系统要存储大量按时间追加的监控指标，查询通常按时间范围和少量标签筛选。
scenario_en: The system stores many append-only monitoring metrics, and queries usually filter by time range and a few tags.
q: 什么时候该选择时间序列数据库（TSDB）？
q_en: When should you choose a time-series database (TSDB)?
options: 只要数据里有 timestamp 字段就必须用 TSDB
当业务需要强事务和复杂外键约束时
当通用数据库在高写入、时间范围查询、保留策略和压缩上出现真实瓶颈时
当核心需求是跨全部 series 做 Top-K 排序时
why: 决定性约束是通用数据库先撑不住高写入、时间范围查询或保留/压缩需求；仅有 timestamp 字段不构成理由。先用 Postgres/DynamoDB 顶，顶不住再上专用系统。
why_en: A time-series database is worth adopting once a general-purpose database genuinely bottlenecks on write volume, time-range queries, or retention, not just because the data happens to have a timestamp.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询核心是跨海量 series 的全局排序或强事务/复杂 join，Postgres/DynamoDB 等通用方案通常更直接。
tradeoff: 专用 TSDB 的写入/压缩优化 vs 通用数据库的事务与关系能力
options_en: Any time your data has a timestamp field, you must use a TSDB.
When the business needs strong transactions and complex foreign keys.
When a general-purpose database hits real bottlenecks on high write volume, time-range queries, retention, and compression.
When the core need is Top-K ranking across all series.

termDefinitions.meaning: 时间序列数据库，为高吞吐追加写和按时间范围查询优化的专用数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB, or time-series database, is purpose-built for high-throughput append writes and time-range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用开源关系型数据库，强于事务和复杂查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database strong at transactions and complex queries.
