A client-side local cache speeds up reads — it is not the server-side mechanism that guarantees acknowledged updates survive.

q: 为什么内存交换（swapping）对 ZooKeeper 性能是灾难性的？
q_en: Why is swapping disastrous for ZooKeeper performance?
options: swap 会直接损坏磁盘上已经持久化的事务日志数据
swap 发生时 ZooKeeper 会强制断开所有已连接的客户端，逼大家重新连接
ZK 的所有操作是全序执行的：一个请求因 swap 卡在磁盘，后面排队的所有请求都被拖住
swap 只会让 watch 通知机制暂时失效几秒钟
options_en: Swapping directly corrupts the transaction log already persisted on disk.
Swapping forces ZooKeeper to disconnect every connected client immediately, forcing everyone to reconnect.
All operations execute in total order: one request stuck on disk due to swap delays every request queued behind it.
Swapping only makes the watch notification mechanism briefly stop working for a few seconds.
why: 全序流水线意味着「一人慢全队慢」；堆大小要保证数据集全在内存、绝不触发 swap。
why_en: Because all operations are totally ordered, one request hitting swap delays every queued request behind it.
optionExplanations: swap 是内存和磁盘之间的换页，不会直接损坏已经落盘的事务日志内容。
swap 发生时 ZooKeeper 不会主动断开全部客户端，它只是处理变慢了。
对：ZK 所有操作全序执行，一个请求因 swap 卡在磁盘 I/O 上，后面排队的全部请求都被一起拖住。
swap 影响的不只是 watch 通知，而是整条全序流水线，后果远不止『通知失效几秒』。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping is paging between memory and disk — it does not directly corrupt a transaction log already persisted.
Swapping does not make ZooKeeper actively disconnect every client — it just makes everything slower.
Right: all operations execute in total order, so one request stuck on swap-induced disk I/O drags down every request queued behind it.
Swapping does not just stall watch notifications — it stalls the entire total-order pipeline, a far bigger consequence than a few seconds of missed notifications.

q: 网络分区导致任何一组服务器都凑不齐多数派时，ZooKeeper 会怎样？
q_en: What does ZooKeeper do when no network partition can form a majority?
options: 分区两边的服务器各自继续独立处理写请求，等分区恢复后再合并数据，尽量减少停机时间
自动在云上现拉起几台新的服务器节点来补足所需的多数派
由系统随机挑其中一边的服务器组，继续处理这一边的写请求
停止处理写请求直到分区恢复——宁可不可用也要避免 split-brain（脑裂）
options_en: Both sides of the partition keep processing writes independently and merge the data after it heals, to minimize downtime.
It automatically spins up a few new servers in the cloud to restore a majority.
The system randomly picks one side of the partition to keep processing its writes.
It stops processing writes until the partition heals, choosing unavailability over split-brain.
why: 没有多数派就不写，防止系统两半各持一套「真相」；这是 CP 系统的典型选择。
why_en: Without a majority ZooKeeper refuses writes until the partition heals, preventing split-brain disagreement.

termDefinitions.meaning: split-brain（脑裂）：网络分区后系统两半各自独立接受写入，产生两份互相矛盾的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Split-brain is when a network partition lets both halves of a system independently accept writes, producing two conflicting copies of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: CP 系统：在 CAP 权衡中优先保证一致性和分区容忍、宁可牺牲可用性的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CP system is one that, in the CAP tradeoff, prioritizes consistency and partition tolerance even at the cost of availability.

optionExplanations: 两边都继续处理写请求正是脑裂本身，分区恢复后两份数据早就互相矛盾，合并不回去。
网络分区期间 ZooKeeper 不会自动在云上拉起新机器来凑多数派，这需要人工介入。
随机选一边继续写同样会制造出脑裂，被抛弃那边的写入还是丢了。
对：凑不齐多数派就停止处理写请求，直到分区恢复——宁可不可用也不让两边各自持有不同的『真相』。
optionExplanations_en: Both sides continuing to write is split-brain itself — once the partition heals, the two histories have already diverged and cannot simply merge back.
ZooKeeper does not auto-provision new cloud servers during a partition to restore a majority — that needs human intervention.
Randomly picking one side to keep writing still produces split-brain — the abandoned side's writes are still lost.
Right: without a majority it stops processing writes until the partition heals, choosing unavailability over letting the two sides hold different versions of the truth.

q: 把「聊天服务器崩溃后 ZooKeeper 的自动处理」排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put ZooKeeper's automatic handling of a crashed chat server in the right order.
steps: 其它 watch 这些节点的服务器收到通知，更新路由表、把用户标记下线
Server 2 崩溃
它创建的所有临时节点被自动删除（服务器注册节点 + 名下用户节点）
Server 2 的 ZK 会话超时（典型 10-30 秒后）
why: 崩溃 → 会话超时 → 临时节点消失 → watcher 收通知并响应。全程无需人工干预——这是 ZK 最强大的特性之一。
why_en: After a crash the session times out, its ephemeral nodes are deleted, and watching servers get notified and update their routing automatically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Server 2 崩溃"] --> T["会话超时"]
    T --> D["临时节点自动删除"]
    D --> N["watcher 收到通知\n更新路由/标记下线"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 会话超时：客户端超过约定时间没有发送心跳，ZooKeeper 判定其会话失效并清理其临时节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session timeout is when a client misses heartbeats for the agreed window, so ZooKeeper marks its session expired and cleans up its ephemeral nodes.

q: 今天哪些系统仍然依赖 ZooKeeper？
q_en: Which systems still depend on ZooKeeper today?
options: Apache 生态核心组件：HBase、Hadoop、Storm、Pulsar 等；ClickHouse 复制协调也依赖它
有人误以为 Kubernetes 的核心调度组件是直接构建在 ZooKeeper 协调服务之上的，其实用的是自研的 etcd
几乎所有主流的云托管数据库和缓存产品线，据说如今都还依赖它来做协调
有人认为已经完全没有任何生产系统还在实际使用 ZooKeeper 了
options_en: Core Apache-ecosystem components: HBase, Hadoop, Storm, Pulsar and more; ClickHouse also relies on it for replication coordination.
Some mistakenly believe Kubernetes' core scheduler is built directly on top of the ZooKeeper coordination service, when it actually uses its own etcd.
Some claim nearly every mainstream cloud-managed database and cache product line today still depends on it.
Some believe there is no production system left anywhere that actually still uses ZooKeeper.
why: ZK 在 Apache 生态依然是台柱；ClickHouse 的复制部署也要求它。它老了，但没退休。
why_en: ZooKeeper remains central to HBase, Hadoop, SolrCloud, Storm, NiFi, and Pulsar, and ClickHouse requires it for replication coordination.
optionExplanations: 对：HBase、Hadoop、Storm、Pulsar 这些 Apache 生态核心组件仍在用它，ClickHouse 做副本协调时同样离不开它。
Kubernetes 的调度核心是自研的 etcd 存储，不是构建在 ZooKeeper 之上，这是常见的误解。
主流云托管数据库和缓存产品线大多不依赖 ZooKeeper，这个说法把它的覆盖范围夸大了。
说没有生产系统还在用它并不准确，Apache 生态和 ClickHouse 复制仍然实实在在依赖它。
optionExplanations_en: Right: core Apache-ecosystem components like HBase, Hadoop, Storm, and Pulsar still use it, and ClickHouse relies on it for replication coordination too.
Kubernetes' scheduling core is built on its own etcd store, not on top of ZooKeeper — a common misconception.
Most mainstream cloud-managed databases and caches do not actually depend on ZooKeeper — that overstates its reach.
Claiming no production system uses it anymore is inaccurate — the Apache ecosystem and ClickHouse replication genuinely still depend on it.

q: Kafka 摆脱 ZooKeeper 的举动（KRaft）说明了什么趋势？
q_en: What trend does Kafka's move away from ZooKeeper with KRaft show?
options: 说明共识协议这类机制在分布式系统里已经变得不再重要
说明所有系统今后都应该反过来外挂一个 ZooKeeper 集群才对，而不是自己内置共识算法
转向「自带内置共识协议的自包含系统」：KRaft 消除了外部协调服务带来的运维复杂度、扩展瓶颈和故障点
说明 Kafka 已经彻底放弃了分布式架构，改回单机部署模式
options_en: It shows consensus mechanisms like this no longer matter in distributed systems.
It shows every system should now instead bolt on an external ZooKeeper cluster, rather than build in its own consensus algorithm.
A shift toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus: KRaft removes the ops complexity, scaling bottlenecks, and failure points of an external coordinator.
It shows Kafka has completely abandoned distributed architecture and gone back to single-node deployment.
why: 多年依赖后，Kafka 用内置 Raft 元数据模式替换 ZK——外部协调服务正在被内嵌共识取代，这是大势。
why_en: Kafka's move to KRaft reflects a broader trend toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus instead of external coordination services.

termDefinitions.meaning: KRaft：Kafka 内置的基于 Raft 的元数据管理模式，用来取代外部 ZooKeeper 依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KRaft is Kafka's built-in Raft-based metadata mode that replaces its former dependency on external ZooKeeper.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：分布式消息队列/事件流平台，曾长期用 ZooKeeper 管理集群元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and event-streaming platform that long relied on ZooKeeper for cluster metadata.

optionExplanations: KRaft 恰恰是换成另一套共识协议（Raft）内置进来，说明共识机制依然核心，不是变得不重要。
现实方向正相反：Kafka 正在移除对外部 ZooKeeper 的依赖，不是反过来让别人都依赖它。
对：转向『自带内置共识协议的自包含系统』，KRaft 消除了外部协调服务带来的运维复杂度、扩展瓶颈和故障点。
KRaft 之后 Kafka 仍是多 broker 分布式集群，只是元数据管理方式变了，不是退回单机部署。
optionExplanations_en: KRaft actually swaps in another consensus protocol, Raft, built-in — showing consensus is still core, not that it stopped mattering.
The real direction is the opposite: Kafka is removing its dependency on external ZooKeeper, not making others depend on it.
Right: it is a shift toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus — KRaft removes the ops complexity, scaling bottlenecks, and failure points of an external coordinator.
Post-KRaft Kafka is still a distributed multi-broker cluster; only metadata management changed, not a retreat to single-node deployment.

q: etcd 相对 ZooKeeper 的定位是？
q_en: How is etcd positioned relative to ZooKeeper?
options: 很多人误以为 etcd 只是把 ZooKeeper 原封不动地用 Java 语言重新实现了一遍而已，改个包名罢了
云原生世界的协调新贵：强一致分布式 KV，现代 HTTP/JSON 与 gRPC API，是 Kubernetes 的底座
很多人以为 etcd 只能拿来做服务发现，完全不支持用它存放配置数据
很多人误以为 etcd 本质是最终一致的存储系统，不提供任何强一致性保证
options_en: Many mistakenly believe etcd is just ZooKeeper reimplemented in Java, unchanged, one to one — just a different package name.
The cloud-native coordinator: a strongly consistent distributed key-value store with modern HTTP/JSON and gRPC APIs, the base of Kubernetes.
Many believe etcd can only be used for service discovery and does not support storing configuration at all.
Many mistakenly believe etcd is fundamentally an eventually consistent store with no strong consistency guarantee.
why: etcd 与 ZK 解决同类问题（配置管理、服务发现），但 API 更现代、与云原生生态深度绑定。
why_en: Etcd offers strongly consistent key-value coordination with modern HTTP and gRPC APIs and powers Kubernetes.
tradeoff: etcd 的现代云原生 API + Kubernetes 深度集成 vs ZooKeeper 的 Apache 生态成熟度 + 更丰富的原生配方（选举/锁）

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd：基于 Raft 协议的强一致分布式键值存储，是 Kubernetes 的核心元数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a strongly consistent distributed key-value store built on Raft that serves as Kubernetes' core metadata store.

termDefinitions.meaning: gRPC：Google 开源的高性能 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和 Protocol Buffers。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance remote-procedure-call framework built on HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP/JSON：用标准 HTTP 请求携带 JSON 格式数据的接口风格，浏览器和多数语言都能直接用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/JSON is an API style using standard HTTP requests with JSON payloads, directly usable from browsers and most languages.

optionExplanations: etcd 和 ZooKeeper 的协议、数据模型、API 完全不同，不是简单把 ZK 用 Java 重写一遍。
对：etcd 是云原生世界的协调新贵——强一致分布式 KV，现代 HTTP/JSON 与 gRPC API，是 Kubernetes 的底座。
etcd 的 KV 接口天然适合存配置，很多平台的配置中心底层就是它，不是『不支持』。
etcd 基于 Raft，和 ZAB 一样提供强一致写，不是最终一致存储。
optionExplanations_en: etcd's protocol, data model, and API are all different from ZooKeeper's — it is not simply ZooKeeper rewritten in Java.
Right: etcd is the cloud-native coordinator — a strongly consistent distributed key-value store with modern HTTP/JSON and gRPC APIs, powering Kubernetes.
etcd's key-value interface fits configuration naturally, and it backs many platforms' config centers — it does support this.
etcd is built on Raft and, like ZAB, gives strongly consistent writes — it is not an eventually consistent store.

q: Consul 与 ZooKeeper 相比的特色是？
q_en: What is Consul's distinguishing feature compared with ZooKeeper?
options: Consul 只是把 ZooKeeper 用 Go 语言重新实现了一遍
Consul 的能力范围比 ZooKeeper 更窄，只提供分布式锁一项功能，别的都做不了
Consul 不做健康检查，这方面反而不如 ZooKeeper
超出基础协调：服务发现 + 健康检查 + KV 存储，招牌是按服务变化自动重配负载均衡器和防火墙
options_en: Consul is just ZooKeeper reimplemented in Go with the same feature set.
Consul's scope is narrower than ZooKeeper's, offering only distributed locks and nothing else.
Consul does not do health checking, which is actually a gap compared to ZooKeeper.
It goes beyond basic coordination: service discovery, health checking, and a KV store, with automatic load-balancer and firewall reconfiguration as its signature feature.
why: Consul 走「更全家桶」路线；云厂商方案（AWS Parameter Store、Azure App Configuration 等）则以托管省心取胜。
why_en: Consul goes beyond coordination with service discovery, health checks, and network automation that reconfigures load balancers as services change.
tradeoff: Consul 的服务网格全家桶（服务发现+健康检查+网络自动化）vs ZooKeeper 的专注协调原语（ZNode+watch）

rows: 发现+健康检查+网络自动化

termDefinitions.meaning: Consul：HashiCorp 出品的协调服务，除服务发现外还内置健康检查和网络自动化能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consul is HashiCorp's coordination service that adds built-in health checking and network automation on top of service discovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 健康检查：持续探测服务实例是否正常运行，异常时自动从可用列表摘除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A health check continuously probes whether a service instance is functioning and removes it from the available list when it is not.

optionExplanations: Consul 的一致性协议、数据模型和功能范围都和 ZooKeeper 不同，不是简单换个语言重写。
Consul 的能力范围其实比 ZooKeeper 更宽，不只是分布式锁一项功能。
健康检查恰恰是 Consul 的内置能力，说它『不如 ZooKeeper』方向反了。
对：Consul 超出基础协调，内置服务发现、健康检查、KV 存储，招牌是按服务变化自动重配负载均衡器和防火墙。
optionExplanations_en: Consul's consensus protocol, data model, and feature scope all differ from ZooKeeper's — it is not just a Go rewrite.
Consul's scope is actually broader than ZooKeeper's, not narrower — distributed locks are just one small piece.
Health checking is actually a built-in Consul capability — claiming it falls short of ZooKeeper here has it backwards.

Right: Consul goes beyond basic coordination with service discovery, health checking, and a KV store, with its signature move being automatic load-balancer and firewall reconfiguration as services change.

q: ZooKeeper 的「热点问题（hot spotting）」指什么？
q_en: What does ZooKeeper hot spotting mean?
options: 服务器 CPU 长期处于持续高负载运行状态，触发了系统自动降频保护机制，跟 watch 完全无关
大量客户端 watch 同一个 ZNode（选举、锁的常态）时，通知流量可能压垮服务器——热门节点成为瓶颈
系统会自动把被频繁访问的热数据迁移到内存容量更大的机器上去
磁盘上的某个存储扇区因为被反复频繁写入而提前发生物理损坏
options_en: Servers throttle their own CPU frequency after sustained continuous high load, completely unrelated to watches.
When many clients watch the same znode, common in election or locks, notification traffic can overwhelm servers — popular nodes become bottlenecks.
The system automatically migrates frequently accessed hot data onto machines with larger memory capacity.
A specific storage sector wears out and fails early from being written to over and over.
why: 想象聊天例子里百万用户同时上线：同一节点的海量 watch 通知是规模化的天花板之一。
why_en: When many clients watch the same znode, notification traffic can overwhelm the servers and popular nodes become bottlenecks.

termDefinitions.meaning: hot spotting（热点问题）：大量请求或 watch 集中在同一个节点上，导致该节点及其所在服务器成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hot spotting is when a large volume of requests or watches concentrate on a single node, turning it and its server into a bottleneck.

optionExplanations: CPU 自动降频保护和这里问的『大量 watch 集中在同一节点』完全不是一回事。
对：大量客户端 watch 同一个 ZNode（选举、锁的常态）时，通知流量会压垮服务器，热门节点自己变成瓶颈。
ZooKeeper 不会自动把热数据搬到内存更大的机器上，它没有这种自动数据迁移能力。
磁盘扇区物理损坏是硬件层面的问题，和这里说的『大量客户端盯着同一节点』完全不相关。
optionExplanations_en: Automatic CPU throttling has nothing to do with what is being asked here — lots of watches piling onto one node.
Right: when many clients watch the same znode, common during elections or locks, the notification traffic can overwhelm servers and the popular node becomes the bottleneck itself.
ZooKeeper does not automatically migrate hot data to bigger-memory machines — it has no such auto-migration capability.
Physical disk-sector wear is a hardware-layer issue, unrelated to lots of clients watching the same node.

q: ZooKeeper 的主要局限有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are ZooKeeper's main limitations? (Select all that apply.)
options: 写昂贵：必须经 leader 传播到多数派
内存存储模型限制容量：ZNode 要 <1MB、数据集须装进内存
运维复杂：JVM 参数、磁盘布局、超时与连接监控——「用起来简单，运维起来复杂」
不支持 watch 通知，只能靠轮询感知变化
options_en: Writes are expensive: they must propagate through the leader to a majority.
Capacity is memory-bound: znodes must stay under one megabyte and the dataset must fit in memory.
Operationally complex: JVM tuning, disk layout, timeout and connection monitoring — simple to use, complex to operate.
It does not support watch notifications, so changes can only be detected by polling.
why: 存大量数据、扛超高写入、或想最小化运维时，都该考虑替代方案；watch 恰恰是它的招牌能力，不是局限。
why_en: ZooKeeper writes are expensive through leader and quorum, capacity is memory-bound with small znodes, and it is simple to use but complex to operate.

termDefinitions.meaning: JVM：运行 Java 程序的虚拟机；ZooKeeper 用 Java 实现，堆大小等 JVM 参数需要仔细调优。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The JVM is the runtime that executes Java programs; ZooKeeper is written in Java, so JVM settings like heap size need careful tuning.

optionExplanations: 写昂贵是真实限制：每次写都要经 leader 广播并等多数派确认，高频写入场景会先撑不住。
内存存储模型限制容量：单个 ZNode 要 <1MB，数据集必须整体能装进内存，大数据量不该塞进去。
运维复杂是真实痛点：JVM 堆调优、独立日志盘、超时和连接监控——用起来简单，运维起来处处是细节。
这个选项说反了——推送通知正是它的招牌能力，真没有它才需要靠轮询感知变化。
optionExplanations_en: Expensive writes are a real limit: every write has to broadcast through the leader and wait on a majority, so high-frequency writes hit the wall first.
The memory-bound storage model caps capacity: a single znode must stay under a megabyte and the whole dataset has to fit in memory — not for bulk data.
Operational complexity is a real pain point: JVM heap tuning, a dedicated log disk, timeout and connection monitoring — simple to use, full of detail to operate.
Watch support is actually its signature strength, not a limitation — it is the absence of watches that would force polling, so this has it backwards.

scenario: 设计 Facebook Live Comments / YouTube Live Chat：百万观众看同一直播，希望同一直播间的 websocket 连接尽量集中到同一台（组）服务器以减少跨服务器通信。
scenario_en: You are designing Facebook Live Comments or YouTube Live Chat. Millions of viewers watch the same stream, and you want connections for one room concentrated on the same server group to reduce cross-server traffic.
q: ZooKeeper 在这里扮演什么角色？
q_en: What role does ZooKeeper play in this live-chat routing design?
options: 让 ZooKeeper 直接充当消息队列，转发全部实时评论的消息本体内容，省去额外组件，架构看起来会更简单一些
把每一条历史评论的完整内容都存进 ZooKeeper 里，方便日后回放
作为 API 网关的协调点：维护「哪个房间/直播由哪台服务器负责」的映射；服务器带容量注册，新连接按房间查 ZK 定向
给每一条实时评论单独加一把分布式锁，用来防止重复展示
options_en: Have ZooKeeper act directly as the message queue forwarding every live comment's payload content, to skip an extra component and look simpler.
Store the full content of every historical comment inside ZooKeeper for later replay.
Act as the API gateway's coordination point, mapping which server handles which room, with capacity-aware registration and routing.
Put an individual distributed lock on each live comment to prevent it from being shown twice.
why: 这是「智能路由/同房间同服务器（colocation）」的高级用法——Staff+ 或深度分布式面试的加分项。
why_en: ZooKeeper coordinates smart routing by mapping rooms to servers so a gateway can colocate all viewers of a stream on the same server group.
whenOtherWins: 普通规模的聊天用 pub/sub 广播就能绕开大部分协调问题，不必上这套。
tradeoff: ZK 做房间→服务器的协调映射（轻量、可扩展）vs 把评论本体也塞进 ZK（违反小数据原则、写爆）

termDefinitions.meaning: colocation（同机集中路由）：把同一房间/直播的所有连接尽量路由到同一台或同一组服务器，减少跨服务器通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Colocation routing means directing all connections for the same room or stream to the same server or server group, minimizing cross-server chatter.

optionExplanations: 让 ZooKeeper 直接转发评论内容会把它当成高吞吐消息队列用，违背了它只放小量协调数据的定位。
把每条历史评论存进 ZooKeeper 同样违反小数据原则，量一大写路径直接被压垮。
对：ZK 作为网关的协调点，维护『哪个房间由哪台服务器负责』的映射，服务器带容量注册，新连接按房间查 ZK 定向。
给每条评论单独加锁是过度设计，评论展示不是需要互斥的临界资源，这解决的是另一个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Having ZooKeeper forward comment payloads directly treats it as a high-throughput message queue, against its small-coordination-data role.
Storing every historical comment in ZooKeeper also breaks the small-data principle — volume alone would crush the write path.
Right: ZooKeeper is the gateway's coordination point, mapping which server owns which room, with capacity-aware server registration and new connections routed by looking up the room.
Locking each individual comment is over-engineering — displaying a comment is not a critical section needing mutual exclusion; that solves a different problem.

q: 设计「分布式消息队列」时，ZooKeeper 可以作为共识大脑承担哪些职责？（多选）
q_en: In a distributed message queue, which responsibilities can ZooKeeper handle as the consensus brain? (Select all that apply.)
options: broker 注册与发现、topic 元数据（分区数、副本因子）存储
每个分区的 leader 选举（顺序临时节点保证单一 leader）
consumer group 成员关系与分区分配，broker 故障经临时节点触发分区重分配
存储全部消息本体，让 broker 直接从 ZK 读写消息内容
options_en: Broker registration and discovery, plus topic metadata like partition count and replication factor.
Per-partition leader election, using sequential ephemeral nodes to guarantee a single leader.
Consumer group membership and partition assignment, with broker failure triggering reassignment via ephemeral nodes.
Storing the full message payloads so brokers read and write message content directly from ZooKeeper.
why: KRaft 之前的 Kafka 正是这么用 ZK 的；HBase、Hadoop、Solr 也是类似模式。消息本体走 broker 自己的日志存储，绝不放 ZK。
why_en: In a distributed queue design ZooKeeper handles broker registration, topic metadata, partition leader election, consumer membership, and failure detection, never the message payloads.
tradeoff: ZK 管协调元数据（小、强一致）vs broker 自管消息日志（大、高吞吐）——两者不能互换

termDefinitions.meaning: broker：消息队列集群里负责接收、存储、转发消息的服务器节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broker is a server node in a message-queue cluster responsible for receiving, storing, and forwarding messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: consumer group（消费组）：一组共同消费同一批分区、彼此分摊负载的消费者客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumer clients that jointly consume a set of partitions, sharing the load among themselves.

optionExplanations: broker 注册与 topic 元数据是典型的协调元数据，量小、变化不频繁，正是 ZK 的强项。
分区 leader 选举靠顺序临时节点保证同一时刻只有一个 leader，崩溃后自动换人。
consumer group 成员和分区分配也走同一套机制：broker 故障后临时节点消失，触发重分配。
存储全部消息本体量太大，违反 ZNode 小数据的设计前提，这活儿该交给 broker 自己的日志。
optionExplanations_en: Broker registration and topic metadata is classic small, low-churn coordination data — exactly ZooKeeper's strength.
Partition leader election uses sequential ephemeral nodes to guarantee exactly one leader at a time, with automatic handoff on a crash.
Consumer group membership and partition assignment ride the same mechanism — a broker failure removes its ephemeral node and triggers reassignment.
Storing full message payloads is far too much data, violating the small-znode design premise — that belongs in the broker's own log.

scenario: 分布式文件系统需要「目录及其文件」的嵌套锁获取，要防死锁，还要能监控整个锁层级的变化。
scenario_en: A distributed file system needs nested locks for directories and files. It must avoid deadlocks and watch changes across the whole lock hierarchy.
q: 为什么这里 ZooKeeper 严格优于 Redis？
q_en: Why is ZooKeeper strictly better than Redis in this case?
options: 因为部署 ZooKeeper 集群的机器成本比部署 Redis 更加便宜
ZK 的层级命名空间天然表达父子锁结构，能同时 watch 多个节点监控整个锁层级；Redis 缺少层级与联动通知
因为 Redis 这个产品根本就没有实现过分布式锁的能力
因为 ZooKeeper 锁的整体写入吞吐量比 Redis 锁要高出许多，性能才是这里唯一要考虑的决定因素
options_en: Because running a ZooKeeper cluster costs less hardware than running Redis.
ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace naturally expresses parent-child lock structure and can watch multiple nodes across the whole hierarchy; Redis lacks that hierarchy and linked notification.
Because Redis as a product has never implemented any distributed-lock capability.
Because ZooKeeper locks have much higher overall write throughput than Redis locks, and throughput is the only thing that matters here.
why: 资源有父子关系、锁获取要尊重层级时，ZK 的树形结构 + 多点 watch 是量身定制；Redis 锁是平面的。
why_en: ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace and multi-node watches express nested directory-file locks with deadlock prevention, which flat Redis locks cannot.
whenOtherWins: 普通的单资源短锁（订单、座位）Redis 又快又简单，是默认选择。
tradeoff: ZooKeeper 的层级命名空间+多点 watch（表达父子锁结构）vs Redis 的平面 key 空间（无天然层级）
codeSample:
# 目录锁和文件锁按路径天然嵌套
create -e /locks/dir-a lock-owner
create -e /locks/dir-a/file-1 lock-owner

# 同时 watch 父路径和子路径，任一层变化都能感知
zk.exists("/locks/dir-a", true);
zk.exists("/locks/dir-a/file-1", true);
# Redis 的 key 空间是平面的，没有等价的父子层级可 watch

rows: 会话超时自动删除节点

termDefinitions.meaning: 层级命名空间：像文件系统一样用路径组织节点的结构，天然表达父子/嵌套关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hierarchical namespace organizes nodes by path like a filesystem, naturally expressing parent-child nested relationships.

optionExplanations: 机器成本从来不是这道题的决定性约束，问的是『能不能表达父子锁层级』这个能力差异。
对：ZK 的层级命名空间天然表达父子锁结构，能同时 watch 多个节点监控整个锁层级；Redis 是平面 key 空间，没有这种天然层级。
Redis 完全能做分布式锁（SETNX/TTL），说它『没实现过』是事实错误。
吞吐量恰恰是 ZK 锁的弱项而不是优势，这道题赢在层级表达而不是速度。
optionExplanations_en: Hardware cost was never the decisive constraint here — the question is about the ability to express parent-child lock hierarchy.

Right: ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace naturally expresses parent-child lock structure and can watch multiple nodes to monitor the whole hierarchy; Redis's flat key space has no such native hierarchy.
Redis can absolutely do distributed locks with SETNX and TTL — claiming it never implemented locking is factually wrong.
Throughput is actually ZooKeeper's weak point here, not its advantage — this scenario is won on hierarchy expression, not speed.

scenario: 普通产品向系统设计面试（非深度基础设施），你在考虑要不要把 ZooKeeper 画进架构图。
scenario_en: In a regular product-oriented system design interview, not a deep infrastructure interview, you are deciding whether to draw ZooKeeper into the architecture.
q: 正确的姿态是？
q_en: What is the right posture toward ZooKeeper in this interview setting?
options: 不管拿到什么题目，一上来就先在架构图里画一个 ZooKeeper 集群，显得自己考虑得很周全
干脆用 ZooKeeper 去替代设计里原本该用的所有数据库
别急着上 ZK：除非在设计深度基础设施系统、需要精细协调，或需求超出现代负载均衡器/内置服务发现的能力
不管遇到什么场景，面试全程都绝口不提 ZooKeeper 这个词
options_en: No matter what the prompt is, start every design by drawing a ZooKeeper cluster first, to look thorough.
Just go ahead and replace every database in the design with ZooKeeper instead.
Do not reach for ZooKeeper unless designing deep infrastructure, needing fine-grained coordination, or the need exceeds modern load balancers and built-in discovery.
No matter what scenario comes up, never mention the word ZooKeeper at all during the interview.
why: ZK 很少是第一选择：现代 LB、平台服务发现、云托管方案覆盖了多数场景；它的主场是深度 infra 题和高级协调需求。
why_en: Do not reach for ZooKeeper unless you are designing deep infrastructure or need coordination beyond what modern load balancers and built-in service discovery offer.
whenOtherWins: 设计分布式消息队列/任务调度器、或需要智能路由与层级锁时，ZK 就是合理选择。
tradeoff: ZK 的精细协调能力（重、需要额外运维）vs 现代 LB/托管服务发现（轻量、覆盖大多数产品场景）
optionExplanations: 不管题目是什么都先画 ZooKeeper，会让面试官觉得你缺乏『先问需求再选组件』的判断力。
把 ZooKeeper 当数据库替代品混淆了协调服务和数据存储两种不同定位，它扛不住高吞吐读写。
对：除非在设计深度基础设施、需要精细协调，或需求超出现代负载均衡器/内置服务发现的能力，否则别急着上 ZK。
完全不提这个知识点是矫枉过正，真遇到需要它的深度 infra 题时反而说不出方案。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing ZooKeeper into every design regardless of the prompt reads as lacking the judgment to ask requirements first.
Treating ZooKeeper as a database replacement conflates a coordination service with data storage — it cannot handle high-throughput reads and writes.
Right: do not reach for ZooKeeper unless you are designing deep infrastructure, need fine-grained coordination, or the need exceeds what modern load balancers and built-in service discovery cover.
Never mentioning it at all is overcorrecting — you would have nothing to say when a genuinely deep infra question calls for it.

q: 一次写请求（如注册 Bob 的 ZNode）在 ensemble 内部的流转是？
q_en: How does a write request, such as registering Bob's ZNode, flow through the ensemble?
options: 任意一台 follower 收到写请求后直接写本地磁盘，就可以立刻返回写成功
请求到 leader → leader 向所有 follower 广播变更 → 多数派确认已接受并保存 → leader 确认写成功
客户端把同一条写请求原样同时发送给 ensemble 里的每一台服务器
每台服务器先各自把数据写到本地磁盘，之后再统一去问 leader 这次写是否有效，顺序反过来，省了一次等待，效率反而更高
options_en: Any follower that receives the write just writes to its local disk and returns success right away.
The request reaches the leader, which broadcasts the change to followers, and it succeeds once a majority has accepted and saved it.
The client sends the exact same write request to every single server in the ensemble at once.
Every server first writes to its own local disk, then afterward asks the leader whether that write was valid — the order flipped, saving a wait and supposedly more efficient.
why: 写必须过 leader 并拿到 quorum 确认——这正是写比读贵、但一致性有保障的原因。
why_en: A write goes to the leader, which broadcasts it to followers and confirms success once a majority has accepted and saved it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Client write"] --> B["Leader proposal"]
  B --> C["Quorum ack"]
  C --> D["Commit"]
  D --> E["Watch events"]
optionExplanations: follower 收到写请求不能自己直接确认成功，那样多个 follower 各自确认会破坏全序保证。
对：请求先到 leader，leader 向所有 follower 广播变更，多数派确认已接受并保存后 leader 才确认写成功。
客户端不会把同一条写请求原样同时发给每台服务器，写入必须先经过 leader 统一排序。
每台服务器各自先写本地磁盘再问 leader，顺序反了——必须先经 leader 排序广播，服务器才落盘。
optionExplanations_en: A follower cannot just confirm a write itself — if several followers each confirmed independently, the total-order guarantee would break.
Right: the request goes to the leader first, which broadcasts the change to all followers, and only confirms success once a majority has accepted and saved it.
The client does not fire the same write to every server at once — writes must first be ordered through the leader.
Having each server write locally first and ask the leader afterward has the order backwards — the leader must broadcast and order it before servers persist it.

scenario: 团队在讨论要不要把一份几 MB 大小的完整用户资料 JSON 直接存进一个 ZNode，还是只存一个指向对象存储的引用；ZooKeeper 的设计前提是 ZNode 只放协调元数据，不放大文件。
scenario_en: The team is deciding whether to store a multi-MB user profile JSON directly in one ZNode or store only a pointer to object storage. ZooKeeper is meant for coordination metadata, not large files.
q: 遵循这个设计边界，单个 ZNode 承载的数据量上限应该设为？
q_en: Under this design boundary, what data-size limit should a single ZNode follow?
options: 1KB，比官方建议严格得多，几乎存不下任何真实配置
10MB，远超官方建议，容易在快照/日志里造成额外压力
1MB，符合官方建议：ZNode 只放小量协调数据，数据集要能整个装进内存
1GB，把 ZNode 当文件存储用，完全违背 ZooKeeper 的设计前提
options_en: 1KB, far stricter than the guideline, barely enough for any real config.
10MB, well past the guideline, adding extra pressure to snapshots and logs.
1MB, matching the guideline: znodes hold only small coordination data and the dataset must fit in memory.
1GB, treating a znode like file storage, which defeats ZooKeeper's whole design premise.
why: ZNode 定位是小协调数据：保持在 1MB 以下，整个数据集要能装进内存；超过这个量级就该把大对象放对象存储/DB，ZNode 只存一个引用指针。
why_en: Keep each znode under one megabyte and ensure the whole dataset fits in memory; anything bigger belongs in object storage with just a reference stored in the znode.

scenario: 配置聊天服务器的 ZooKeeper 客户端会话超时参数，要在「网络抖动误判」和「故障发现太慢」之间找平衡。
scenario_en: You are configuring the ZooKeeper client session timeout for chat servers and need to balance false failure detection from network jitter against slow real-failure detection.
q: ZooKeeper 会话超时的典型配置区间是？
q_en: What is the typical ZooKeeper session timeout range?
options: 10-30 毫秒，几乎任何一次网络抖动都会触发误判
10-30 秒，兼顾故障发现速度和抗网络抖动能力
10-30 分钟，故障发现会慢到影响用户体验
10-30 小时，几乎等于关闭了故障检测能力
options_en: 10-30 milliseconds, where almost any network blip triggers a false failure.
10-30 seconds, balancing fast failure detection against tolerance for network blips.
10-30 minutes, slow enough to noticeably hurt user experience during a real failure.
10-30 hours, which effectively disables failure detection.
why: 10-30 秒是「误报 vs 检测速度」的常见折中——短于此网络抖动就会引发误判切换，长于此真故障要等太久才被发现，而这个窗口也正是临时节点消失、下游 watcher 收到通知的时间量级。
why_en: Session timeouts are typically ten to thirty seconds, balancing false-positive failovers against how long real failure detection via ephemeral nodes takes.

q: 补全 ZooKeeper 的三大基础原语：
q_en: Fill in ZooKeeper's three basic primitives.
text: ZooKeeper 靠三个简单原语组合出所有协调能力：{{ZNode}}（层级命名空间中的数据节点）、可靠的服务器 {{ensemble}}（多数派容错）、{{watch}}（变更实时通知）。
why: 数据模型 + 可靠集群 + 通知机制——三件套组合出配置管理、服务发现、选举与锁的全部配方。
why_en: ZooKeeper combines znodes in a hierarchical namespace, a reliable server ensemble, and watches for change notification.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZNode：层级命名空间里的一个数据节点，能存少量数据、能有子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A znode is a node in the hierarchical namespace that can hold a small amount of data and have children.

termDefinitions.meaning: ensemble：一组协同工作、以多数派（quorum）容错的 ZooKeeper 服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble is the group of ZooKeeper servers working together with majority-based fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: watch：客户端登记在 ZNode 上的一次性变更通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watch is a one-time change notification a client registers on a znode.

q: 「核心概念」与具体技术（Redis、Kafka）的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between core concepts and specific technologies like Redis or Kafka?
options: 核心概念就是记住产品名（Redis、Kafka 叫什么）
核心概念是技术无关的通用构件，面试处处会用到
核心概念只在学校课堂里出现，工作中用不到
核心概念和具体技术没有区别，学会一个就等于学会另一个
options_en: Core concepts are just the product names, like Redis or Kafka.

Core concepts are technology-agnostic building blocks — caching, sharding, consistency — that show up in almost every design problem; interviewers assume you know them and will probe once you propose a specific technology.
Core concepts only show up in academic courses, not real work.
There is no difference; learning one technology means you already know the concepts.
why: 核心概念是系统设计的「词汇与语法」：缓存是什么、何时分片、网络如何工作——先有这些才谈得上设计 Instagram。
why_en: Core concepts are technology-agnostic building blocks that interviewers assume you know and will probe when you propose using them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息队列/流处理平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming and message-queue platform.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    API["APIs"] --> Data["Data model"]
    Data --> Scale["Scaling"]
    Scale --> Consistency["Consistency"]
    Consistency --> Numbers["Numbers"]
optionExplanations: 只背产品名撑不住追问：换成 Kafka 照样答不出该不该分片、要不要缓存。
对，缓存、分片、一致性这些构件跟具体产品无关，换哪家都用得上。
线上系统和面试天天在考这些构件，不是学校才用得到的东西。
会用 Redis 不代表懂缓存原理，换个产品名思路照样断掉。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing product names alone breaks down under follow-ups — swap in Kafka and you still cannot answer whether to shard or cache.
Right — caching, sharding, and consistency are product-agnostic, so they carry over no matter which vendor you name.
These ideas get probed daily in production and interviews alike, not just in a classroom.
Knowing Redis's API is not the same as understanding caching; rename the product and the reasoning falls apart.

scenario: 常规的客户端-服务通信，没有实时推送需求，也没有极端的内部性能要求，要选通信协议。
scenario_en: Routine client-to-service communication has no real-time push need and no extreme internal performance requirement, so you need to choose a protocol.
q: 默认应该选什么？
q_en: For routine client-server communication, what should you choose by default?
options: 自研 UDP 协议
WebSocket
HTTP over TCP
FTP
options_en: A custom protocol built on UDP.
WebSocket.
HTTP over TCP, which is universal, mature, and covers ninety percent of use cases.
FTP.
why: 没有特殊理由就默认 HTTP over TCP：人人都懂、到处能跑；面试官也默认你会这么选。
why_en: Default to HTTP over TCP, which is well understood, works everywhere, and covers ninety percent of use cases.
whenOtherWins: 需要实时推送时才引入 SSE/WebSocket；内部服务间性能关键时用 gRPC。

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，不保证送达和顺序，换来更低开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a transport-layer protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees for lower overhead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 早期用于文件传输的协议，现代系统间通信很少用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTP is an older protocol for transferring files, rarely used for modern service communication.

tradeoff: 通用协议覆盖 90% 场景 vs 为特定需求换专用协议的额外收益
optionExplanations: 只有极端延迟场景、且能自己扛丢包和乱序时，自研 UDP 才划算，普通 API 不值得。
客户端和服务端都要频繁主动发消息（聊天、协作）时才上 WebSocket，常规请求响应用不着。
常规客户端-服务通信没有特殊要求时，HTTP over TCP 工具链和团队都现成，默认选它。
FTP 只服务纯文件传输场景，业务 API 不会选它。
optionExplanations_en: Custom UDP only pays off for extreme-latency cases where you're willing to handle loss and reordering yourself — not worth it for a normal API.
WebSocket earns its keep when both sides need to push messages often, like chat or collaboration, not routine calls.
With no special latency or push requirement, HTTP over TCP is the default because tooling and teams already support it everywhere.
FTP is built for file transfer, not the kind of request/response API this scenario needs.

scenario: 系统要给客户端做服务器推送（server push），在 SSE 和 WebSocket 之间选通信方式。
scenario_en: The system needs server push to clients, and you are choosing between SSE and WebSocket.
q: SSE 与 WebSocket 的关键区别是？
q_en: What is the key difference between SSE and WebSocket?
options: SSE 单向推送，WebSocket 双向
SSE 更快
WebSocket 是无状态的
两者完全等价
options_en: SSE is one-way: after the client opens the HTTP connection, only the server pushes down it; WebSocket is truly bidirectional and both sides can send freely.
SSE is faster.
WebSocket is stateless.
The two are completely equivalent.
why: SSE 里客户端无法在同一连接上继续发数据，适合比分/通知这类下行推送；聊天、实时协作这类双向场景要 WebSocket。
why_en: Server-sent events are unidirectional with the server pushing down one HTTP connection, while WebSockets are truly bidirectional.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant S as 服务器
    Note over C,S: SSE：单向
    C->>S: HTTP 请求（打开连接）
    S-->>C: 持续推送事件
    Note over C,S: WebSocket：双向
    C->>S: 消息
    S-->>C: 消息
tradeoff: 单向推送的简单性 vs 双向实时通信能力
optionExplanations: 对，SSE 只能服务器往下推；WebSocket 两边都能随时发消息。
速度不是分界线，方向才是——先问谁能发消息，不是谁更快。
正相反，WebSocket 是有状态长连接，要占住服务器资源。
两者一个单向一个双向，能不能双发就区分开了，不是等价协议。
optionExplanations_en: Right — SSE only lets the server push down, while WebSocket lets both sides send anytime.
Speed is not the deciding factor here; direction of communication is.
The opposite is true — WebSocket holds stateful connection resources on the server.
One is one-way and the other two-way, so they cannot be interchangeable.

scenario: 做直播比分 / 站内通知：服务器持续往客户端推数据，客户端不需要频繁往回发。
scenario_en: You are building live scores or in-app notifications: the server keeps pushing updates, and clients rarely send messages back.
q: 更合适的实时方案是？
q_en: For one-way live updates, which real-time approach fits better?
options: WebSocket
SSE，实现更简单
定时整页刷新
gRPC 流
options_en: WebSocket.
Server-sent events, which are simpler to implement and work better with standard HTTP infrastructure.
Full-page polling on a timer.
A gRPC stream.
why: 单向下行推送用 SSE 就够：更简单、能复用标准 HTTP 设施，别为「实时」两个字直接上 WebSocket。
why_en: For one-way server push like live scores or notifications, server-sent events are simpler and fit standard HTTP infrastructure better.
whenOtherWins: 客户端需要频繁上行发数据（聊天、协作编辑）时，才需要 WebSocket 的双向通道。

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化，常用于内部服务间调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an RPC framework built on HTTP/2 with binary serialization, commonly used for internal service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

tradeoff: 实现简单 + 复用标准 HTTP 设施 vs 双向实时通信能力
optionExplanations: 只有客户端也要频繁上行（聊天、协作编辑）时才值得上 WebSocket 的双向通道。
服务器只需往下推分数或通知时，SSE 用更少的协议复杂度就够，还能复用标准 HTTP 设施。
低频后台数据可以轮询，但直播级更新会浪费延迟和带宽。
gRPC 流适合内部服务间的二进制通信，浏览器通知不走这条路。
optionExplanations_en: WebSocket's two-way channel is only worth it when the client also sends frequently, like chat or collaborative editing.
For server-only pushes like live scores, SSE solves it with less protocol complexity and rides on plain HTTP infrastructure.
Polling can work for infrequent updates, but live-level refresh wastes latency and bandwidth.
gRPC streams fit internal binary service calls, not browser-facing notifications.

scenario: SSE/WebSocket 连接要接入生产环境的负载均衡与容量规划。
scenario_en: SSE and WebSocket connections need to run in production behind load balancing and capacity planning.
q: SSE 和 WebSocket 都是有状态连接，这带来的设计后果是？
q_en: What design consequence follows because SSE and WebSocket are stateful connections?
options: 没有影响，照常部署
只能单机部署
必须换成 UDP
不能直接放负载均衡器后面
options_en: No impact, deploy as usual.
It can only run on a single machine.
You must switch to UDP.
You cannot just drop it behind a standard load balancer — you must plan for connection persistence and for a server dying with thousands of active connections.
why: 有状态连接绑定在具体服务器上：LB 策略、连接迁移、宕机时成千上万条连接的重连风暴都要提前设计。
why_en: Both are stateful connections, so you must plan for connection persistence and for a server dying with thousands of active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

optionExplanations: 有状态长连接绑定在具体服务器上，LB 策略、宕机重连都得提前规划，不是照常部署。
多机部署可以做，只是要靠一致性哈希或 sticky session 把连接钉在固定实例上。
换协议不解决连接状态问题，UDP 本身也不管连接归属。
对，得规划连接保持策略，还要预案宕机时成千上万条连接同时重连的风暴。
optionExplanations_en: Stateful long connections tie to one server, so LB routing and reconnect storms need advance planning — it is not business as usual.
Multi-server deployment still works, it just needs sticky routing or consistent hashing to pin each connection to one instance.
Switching transport does not decide which server holds a connection; UDP itself says nothing about that either.
Right — you need a connection-persistence plan and a playbook for a reconnect storm when a server holding thousands of connections dies.

scenario: 内部服务与服务之间的调用，性能关键，接口不对浏览器/外部用户暴露。
scenario_en: Internal service-to-service calls are performance-critical and are not exposed to browsers or external users.
q: 值得提出的通信方案是？
q_en: For performance-critical internal service calls, what communication option is worth mentioning?
options: gRPC——二进制更快
对外 REST 原样复用
SOAP
服务间直接共享同一个数据库读写，跳过 API 调用
options_en: gRPC, with binary serialization over HTTP/2, much faster than JSON over HTTP.
Reuse the public REST API as-is.
SOAP.
Have the services share one database directly and skip the API call.
why: 性能关键的内部通信用 gRPC；常见模式是「对外 REST + 对内 gRPC」。
why_en: Use gRPC for internal service-to-service communication when performance is critical, since binary serialization over HTTP/2 beats JSON over HTTP.
whenOtherWins: 对外公开 API 仍用 REST——浏览器不原生支持 gRPC（gRPC-Web 需要代理且功能不全）。

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化，常用于内部服务间调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an RPC framework built on HTTP/2 with binary serialization, commonly used for internal service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 协议的第二代主要版本，支持多路复用等特性，是 gRPC 的传输基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the second major HTTP version with multiplexing support and is the transport gRPC runs on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把资源映射到 URL、用 HTTP 方法操作它们的 API 设计风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that maps resources to URLs and manipulates them with HTTP methods.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 XML 信封的老式远程调用协议，企业遗留系统里常见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOAP is an older XML-envelope RPC protocol common in legacy enterprise systems.

tradeoff: 二进制 + HTTP/2 的性能 vs 浏览器原生兼容性
optionExplanations: 内部高 QPS、强类型接口、同团队掌控两端时，gRPC 的二进制序列化比 JSON 更省开销。
对外公开的 REST/JSON 接口是给浏览器和第三方设计的，内部调用没必要照搬这套开销。
SOAP 多见于老系统集成，新建的内部服务基本不会主动选它。
共享数据库会让服务边界消失，一方改表结构另一方就崩，规模一大就很危险。
optionExplanations_en: For high-QPS, strongly typed internal calls under one team's control, gRPC's binary serialization beats JSON's overhead.
The public REST/JSON API is shaped for browsers and third parties; internal calls don't need to carry that overhead.
SOAP mostly shows up in legacy integrations; new internal services rarely pick it on purpose.
Sharing one database erases the service boundary — one team's schema change breaks the other, which gets dangerous at scale.

q: L7 与 L4 负载均衡器的区别是？
q_en: How do L7 and L4 load balancers differ?
options: L4 更智能，L7 更快
L7 懂内容能路由；L4 更快但不看内容
两者完全一样
L4 能读取 HTTP 路径来决定路由到哪个服务
options_en: Layer four is smarter and layer seven is faster.

Layer seven works at the application layer and can route by HTTP content, like sending API calls to one service and pages to another; layer four works at the TCP level, faster but content-blind, just distributing connections.
The two are exactly the same.
Layer four can read the HTTP path to decide which service to route to.
why: L7 看得懂请求内容所以能做内容路由；L4 只管 TCP 连接分发所以更快。WebSocket 这类持久 TCP 连接通常配 L4。
why_en: Layer seven balancers route based on HTTP content while layer four balancers work at the TCP level, faster but content-blind, which suits WebSockets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层负载均衡，能读懂 HTTP 内容按路径/头部路由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-seven load balancer reads application content like HTTP paths and headers to route traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层负载均衡，只按 TCP 连接分发，不看内容，速度更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-four load balancer distributes TCP connections without inspecting content, which makes it faster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

tradeoff: 内容感知路由能力 vs 传输层转发速度
optionExplanations: 能力和速度说反了：是 L7 更懂内容，L4 转发更快。
对，L7 能读 HTTP 内容按路径路由；L4 只看连接和端口，所以更快。
两者看到的信息层级不同：一个懂 HTTP，一个只懂 TCP 包。
读 HTTP 路径是 L7 的能力，L4 只转发 TCP 连接，看不到应用层内容。
optionExplanations_en: The capabilities are swapped — L7 is the content-aware one, L4 is the faster one.
Right — L7 reads HTTP content to route by path, while L4 only sees connections and ports, which makes it faster.
They operate at different layers: one understands HTTP, the other only sees TCP packets.
Reading the HTTP path is an L7 capability; L4 just forwards TCP connections without seeing application content.

q: 题目一提「real-time」就上 WebSocket，为什么是常见错误？
q_en: Why is it a common mistake to jump to WebSocket whenever a prompt says real-time?
options: WebSocket 协议已经过时，工程实践里不会再用它
把 real-time 目标当成技术上不可能做到的事
长轮询/SSE 够用时，WebSocket 只是多余复杂度
WebSocket 协议本身不支持任何形式的加密传输
options_en: WebSocket the protocol is obsolete and no longer used in practice.
Treat the real-time target as something technically impossible to achieve.
When long polling or server-sent events would do, WebSocket only adds needless complexity.
WebSocket the protocol has no support for encrypted transport of any kind.
why: WebSocket 的代价是规模化的有状态连接管理；不是「实时」都要它，先问是否真需要客户端频繁上行。
why_en: Proposing WebSockets when long polling or server-sent events would do adds needless stateful-connection complexity at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

optionExplanations: WebSocket 没过时，聊天、协作、多人游戏这些双向场景还是靠它。
real-time 只是延迟目标，不等于必须上双向长连接。
对，只需要下行推送时上 WebSocket，等于白背有状态连接管理和扩容成本。
加密走 TLS/WSS 就能解决，不是弃用 WebSocket 的理由。
optionExplanations_en: WebSocket is not obsolete — chat, collaboration, and multiplayer games still rely on it.
Real-time is just a latency target; it does not mean you must have a bidirectional long connection.
Right — reaching for WebSocket when you only need downstream push means carrying stateful-connection and scaling costs for nothing.
Encryption is handled by TLS or WSS; that's not a reason to avoid WebSocket.

scenario: 设计面向全球用户的低延迟系统，服务器在纽约，部分用户在伦敦访问。
scenario_en: You are designing a low-latency global system; servers are in New York, and some users access it from London.
q: 纽约到伦敦的请求，仅光纤中的光速就决定了最低延迟约是？
q_en: For a New York to London request, what latency floor does fiber propagation alone create?
options: ~1ms
RTT 约 70-90ms
options_en: About one millisecond.
A practical round trip of about seventy to ninety milliseconds, with a pure physical floor around sixty.
About two seconds.
About one hundredth of a millisecond.
why: 纽约到伦敦纯物理 RTT 下限约 55-60ms，实践中常在 70-90ms；还没开始处理就有这个级别的跨洋成本，所以全球低延迟必须区域化部署、按地理复制或分区数据。
why_en: A New York to London round trip has a physical lower bound around 55-60ms and practical network latency often around 70-90ms, which is why regional deployments and CDNs exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求从发出到收到响应的往返时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the round-trip time from sending a request to receiving its response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on edge servers close to users.

q: 面试官对 API 设计环节的真实期待是？
q_en: What does an interviewer usually expect from the API-design section?
options: 完美的 API 规范文档
每个字段都定义好类型
跳过 API 直接画架构
端点合理即可，快速推进
options_en: A perfect API specification document.
Every field with its type fully defined.
Skip the API and go straight to the architecture.
Reasonable endpoints so you can move quickly to the harder architecture problems — though sloppy API design signals inexperience.
why: 多数考官不纠结完美 API，他们想看你给出合理端点后把时间留给难点；基本功还是要在，否则显得生疏。
why_en: Most interviewers just want reasonable endpoints so you can move on to harder problems, though sloppy API design signals inexperience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序之间约定好的调用接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the agreed-upon interface programs use to call each other.

optionExplanations: 正式 OpenAPI 文档是给生产系统写的，面试时间根本不够磨这个。
字段能说清主流程就行，边界字段不用逐个抠。
跳过 API 会让考官看不到你定义的核心对象和主路径。
对，给出合理端点就该往下走，把时间留给存储、扩展、一致性这些难点。
optionExplanations_en: A full OpenAPI spec belongs in production docs — interview time simply does not allow for that polish.
Fields just need to convey the main flow; edge-case fields don't need individual scrutiny.
Skipping the API hides the core objects and main flow the interviewer wants to see.
Right — sketch reasonable endpoints and move on, saving time for storage, scaling, and consistency.

scenario: 面试进行到 API 设计环节，时间有限，要决定投入多少精力。
scenario_en: In the API-design part of an interview, time is limited and you need to decide how deep to go.
q: API 设计环节的合理节奏是？
q_en: What is a reasonable pace for the API-design section?
options: 开场就花 10 分钟反复打磨每一个端点的细节
用 20 分钟把每个端点的全部字段都写清楚
几分钟内画出 4-5 个关键端点然后继续推进
整个 API 设计环节完全跳过，什么都不画
options_en: Spend ten minutes right away polishing every single endpoint's details.
Spend twenty minutes writing out every field for every endpoint.
Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes, then move on.
Skip the whole API-design section entirely and draw nothing.
why: 两三分钟给出 4-5 个关键端点即可；开场 10 分钟还在磨 API 细节说明陷得太深了。
why_en: Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes and move on; ten minutes on API details is going too deep.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client"] --> Page["GET page?cursor"]
    Page --> DB["Query next N"]
    DB --> Token["Return next cursor"]
optionExplanations: 开场就花 10 分钟反复打磨每一个端点的细节。
用 20 分钟把每个端点的全部字段都写清楚。
几分钟内画出 4-5 个关键端点就继续推进。
整个 API 设计环节完全跳过，什么都不画。
optionExplanations_en: Spend ten minutes right away polishing every single endpoint's details.
Spend twenty minutes writing out every field for every endpoint.
Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes, then move on.
Skip the whole API-design section entirely and draw nothing.

q: 分页方式的选择：cursor-based vs offset-based，正确的判断是？
q_en: How should you choose between cursor-based and offset-based pagination?
options: cursor 适合实时插入；offset 够用
offset 永远更好
cursor 无法用 SQL 实现
两者不能混用于同一系统
options_en: Cursor-based pagination works better for real-time data where items are added frequently, while offset-based is fine for most cases.
Offset is always better.
Cursor-based pagination cannot be implemented in SQL.
The two cannot coexist in the same system.
why: 返回大结果集需要分页：数据实时增长时 offset 会漂移，cursor 更稳；一般场景 offset 简单够用。
why_en: Cursor-based pagination works better for real-time data where items are added frequently, while offset-based is fine for most cases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条记录的位置作为下一页起点的分页方式，不受新插入影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor-based pagination uses the last item's position as the start of the next page, so new inserts don't shift it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用「跳过前 N 条」定位页码的分页方式，实现简单但新增数据会导致漂移/重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset-based pagination skips the first N rows to find a page; it's simple but drifts when new rows are inserted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

codeSample:
-- cursor-based, stable under inserts
SELECT * FROM posts
WHERE id < :last_id
ORDER BY id DESC
LIMIT 20;
tradeoff: 插入场景下的稳定性 vs 实现的简单程度
optionExplanations: 对，高频插入的列表用 cursor 防漂移；稳定后台表格 offset 简单够用。
offset 在小而稳定的列表能用，高速插入的列表会重复或漏读。
cursor 完全能用 SQL 写：WHERE id < last_id 就是一个稳定范围查询。
同一系统按端点混用没问题，不必把一种分页方式全局化。
optionExplanations_en: Right — use cursors where inserts are frequent to avoid drift, and plain offset where the list is small and stable.
Offset works on small, stable lists, but fast-changing ones can repeat or skip rows under it.
Cursor pagination is plain SQL — `WHERE id < last_id` is a perfectly stable range query.
Mixing pagination styles per endpoint in one system is fine; you don't need to force one style everywhere.

scenario: 系统既有用户登录会话，又有内部服务之间的调用，要给两者选认证方式。
scenario_en: The system has both user login sessions and internal service-to-service calls, so you need auth for each path.
q: 标准搭配是？
q_en: What is the standard auth pairing for user sessions and service-to-service calls?
options: 都用明文密码
都用 IP 白名单
用户会话用 API key、服务间用 JWT
用户会话 JWT，服务间 API key
options_en: Use plaintext passwords for both.
Use IP allowlists for both.
Use an API key for user sessions and a JWT for service-to-service calls.
Use a JWT token for user sessions and an API key for service-to-service calls.
why: 面试口径：JWT 管用户会话、API key 管 service-to-service；点到为止，除非被追问不必展开。
why_en: Use JWT tokens for user sessions and API keys for service-to-service calls.
whenOtherWins: 若有第三方开发者生态，才需要展开 OAuth 之类的授权协议——一般面试不用主动深入。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息编码进一段签名令牌、服务端验签即可信任内容的认证方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes user info so any service can verify it without a database lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 颁发给调用方（通常是服务或第三方）的长期凭证字符串，用于识别调用者身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a long-lived credential string issued to a caller, usually a service, to identify who is calling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 授权协议，让第三方应用在用户同意下访问资源而不拿到密码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OAuth is an authorization protocol that lets a third-party app access resources with user consent, without seeing the password.

tradeoff: 用户会话免查库验签 vs 服务间凭证的可轮换/可吊销
optionExplanations: 明文密码只在本地临时调试能忍，线上认证绝不能这样做。
固定 IP 白名单能当额外防线，但替代不了身份凭证。
把两者用途对调了：JWT 更适合带身份和过期时间的用户会话，不是服务间调用。
对，用户会话要能免查库验签就用 JWT，服务间调用更常用可轮换的 API key 或 mTLS。
optionExplanations_en: Plaintext passwords might survive a local debug session, but production auth can never work that way.
A fixed IP allowlist can be an extra layer, but it never replaces an actual credential.
This swaps the two use cases — JWT fits identity-plus-timeout user sessions, not service-to-service calls.
Right — JWT lets any service verify a user session without a database hit, while API keys give service calls a rotatable credential.

scenario: 你的系统可能被机器人刷接口或恶意滥用打爆。
scenario_en: Your system may be abused by bots or malicious callers that can flood the API.
q: API 层面应该主动提的一句是？
q_en: What API-layer point should you proactively mention for an abuse-prone system?
options: 把 API 下线
提到限流，点到为止
换一种编程语言
禁止所有匿名访问
options_en: Take the API offline.
Mention rate limiting, but don't go deep unless the interviewer asks.
Switch to a different programming language.
Block all anonymous access.
why: 可能被滥用的系统值得提一句限流；分页/认证/限流这些点都是「提到即可」，深挖等考官发起。
why_en: If the system could get hammered by bots or abuse, mention rate limiting but do not go deep unless asked.
whenOtherWins: 纯内部、流量完全可信的系统就不必主动展开限流，把时间留给核心架构。

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单位时间内允许的请求数量，防止接口被刷爆或滥用的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate limiting caps how many requests are allowed in a time window to prevent abuse or overload.

tradeoff: 展现生产意识的成本 vs 深挖占用有限的面试时间
optionExplanations: 下线只适合真的无法服务，不是面试里的常规架构答案。
对，接口可能被刷时提一句限流，说明你想到了滥用和下游保护，别深挖占时间。
换语言不改变请求量、配额或滥用风险，这不是相关手段。
全面禁止匿名会砍掉合法的公开读路径，用限流比强制登录更精细。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the service offline only fits an inability to serve at all, not a normal interview architecture answer.
Right — mention rate limiting when abuse is plausible to show you considered it, then move on without a deep dive.
Changing languages doesn't touch request volume, quotas, or abuse risk, so it's unrelated.
Blocking every anonymous request kills legitimate public reads too; rate limiting is the more precise tool.

scenario: 数据是结构化的、关系清晰（用户账户→订单→商品），需要强一致、事务和复杂查询。
scenario_en: The data is structured with clear relationships, such as users to orders to products, and needs transactions and strong consistency.
q: 最合适的存储是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits structured relational data with transactions?
options: MongoDB，文档型数据库，schema 灵活
DynamoDB，键值/宽列数据库，按 key 强项
关系型数据库（如 Postgres），支持事务和复杂查询
S3 对象存储，适合存大文件
options_en: MongoDB, a document store with a flexible schema.
DynamoDB, a key-value/wide-column store strong at key access.
A relational database like Postgres, with transactions and complex queries.
S3 object storage, built for large files.
why: 结构化 + 清晰关系 + 强一致，正是关系型的主场：SQL 表达复杂查询、事务保一致、外键约束护关系。
why_en: Relational databases like Postgres excel with structured data, clear relationships, strong consistency, transactions, and complex SQL queries.
whenOtherWins: schema 频繁变化、或需要不依赖复杂 join 的水平扩展时，NoSQL（DynamoDB/MongoDB）更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档型 NoSQL 数据库，schema 灵活，常用 JSON 风格文档存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database with a flexible schema, storing JSON-like documents.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，用来存文件/二进制大对象，不是给结构化查询用的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is AWS's object storage service for files and blobs, not built for structured queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库强制「这个引用必须指向一条真实存在的记录」的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key constraint forces a reference to point to a row that actually exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组操作要么全部成功要么全部回滚的执行单元，保证数据一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a unit of operations that either all succeed or all roll back, keeping data consistent.

tradeoff: 结构化强一致 + 复杂查询 vs 灵活扩展能力
optionExplanations: 文档库适合半结构化数据，但强 join 和事务主路径不是它的强项。
键值/宽列库按 key 高吞吐访问很强，但不擅长跨实体的复杂关系查询。
对，结构清楚、关系多、要强一致时，SQL、事务和外键正是关系型的主场。
对象存储适合大文件二进制数据，不是给订单这类关系查询设计的。
optionExplanations_en: Document stores fit semi-structured data, but heavy joins and transaction-critical paths are not their strength.
Key-value or wide-column stores excel at fast key access, not queries that span relationships across entities.
Right — clear structure, many relationships, and strong consistency are exactly where SQL, transactions, and foreign keys shine.
Object storage is built for large binary files, not for relational queries across orders and users.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流
shard key 选错导致 scatter query

scenario: 数据结构频繁变化（schema 灵活），并且要跨多台服务器水平扩展，不依赖复杂 join。
scenario_en: The data shape changes often, must scale horizontally across machines, and does not rely on complex joins.
q: 更匹配的存储是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits flexible schema and horizontal scaling without complex joins?
options: NoSQL（DynamoDB / MongoDB）
单机 Postgres，不做任何扩展准备
强一致的分布式 SQL（如 Spanner），join 成本依旧高
关系型 + 只读副本，schema 变化仍要迁移脚本
options_en: NoSQL, such as DynamoDB or MongoDB.
A single Postgres instance with no scaling plan.
A strongly consistent distributed SQL database like Spanner, where joins still cost the same.
Relational plus read replicas, still needing migration scripts for schema changes.
why: 灵活 schema 与横向扩展是 NoSQL 的两大主场；代价是放弃复杂 join 和部分关系型保证。
why_en: NoSQL databases shine when you need flexible schemas or horizontal scaling across many servers without complex joins.
whenOtherWins: 需要强一致、事务与复杂关系查询时回到关系型——别为扩展性提前放弃这些保证。

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档型 NoSQL 数据库，schema 灵活，常用 JSON 风格文档存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database with a flexible schema, storing JSON-like documents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

tradeoff: 灵活 schema + 水平扩展 vs 复杂 join / 强一致保证
optionExplanations: 对，schema 常变又要横向扩展、不依赖复杂 join 时，文档或宽列 NoSQL 正合适。
单机不做扩展准备撑不住并发和数据增长，这不是应对扩容需求的方案。
分布式 SQL 保的是强关系和事务，不是为了甩掉 schema 设计成本。
只读副本能扩读不扩写，schema 变化照样要跑迁移脚本。
optionExplanations_en: Right — when schema shifts often and you need horizontal scale without heavy joins, document or wide-column NoSQL fits.
A single instance with no scaling plan can't absorb rising concurrency or data growth; it doesn't answer the scaling need.
Distributed SQL preserves strong relationships and transactions; it's not meant to shed schema-design cost.
Read replicas scale reads, not writes, and schema changes still need migration scripts either way.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流
shard key 选错导致 scatter query

q: 「规范化（normalization）」的含义与代价是？
q_en: What does normalization mean, and what does it cost?
options: 把所有数据塞进一张宽表，不做任何拆分
拆表避免重复，读取需要 join
给每个字段单独建一张表来省空间
把重复字段做压缩存储，但仍然保留每处的拷贝
options_en: Put all data into one wide table with no splitting.

Split data across tables to avoid duplication, so orders reference a user ID instead of copying user data: updating once updates everywhere, but reading full data needs joins, which get expensive at scale.
Give every single field its own table to save space.
Compress duplicate fields but still keep a copy in every place.
why: 规范化保一致性（改一次商品名全站生效），代价是读取要 join；表巨大或跨多表 join 时开销显著。
why_en: Normalization splits data across tables to avoid duplication, keeping it consistent but requiring joins that get expensive at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的数据拼在一起返回的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库强制「这个引用必须指向一条真实存在的记录」的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key constraint forces a reference to point to a row that actually exists.

optionExplanations: 全塞一张表是反规范化的极端，会让重复数据和更新不一致更严重。
对，拆实体表用引用代替拷贝，更新更一致，但读取常常要 join。
每个字段单独成表是过度拆分，查询要 join 太多张表，成本很高。
压缩只省字节，不解决实体关系或重复的事实数据。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming everything into one wide table is the extreme opposite of normalization, and it makes duplication and inconsistent updates worse.
Right — splitting entities and using references instead of copies keeps updates consistent, though reads often need joins.
A table per field is over-splitting; queries end up joining far too many tables and get expensive.
Compression just saves bytes; it doesn't resolve entity relationships or duplicate facts.

q: 反规范化（denormalization）与规范化在「读写」上的取舍是？
q_en: What is the read/write tradeoff between denormalization and normalization?
options: 反规范化会让读和写两条路径都变得更慢
规范化因为省去冗余，读取反而更快
两者在读性能和写性能上其实完全一样
反规范化省 join 换读快，但写要改多处更贵
options_en: Denormalization makes both the read path and the write path slower.
Normalization skips redundancy, so reads end up faster.
The two are actually identical on both read and write performance.
Denormalization skips joins for faster reads, but every write must now update multiple copies.
why: 把 username 直接冗余进订单，展示订单不用再 join users 表；读重、数据少变的系统这笔账通常划算。
why_en: Denormalization duplicates data to avoid joins and speed up reads, at the cost of updating every copy when the source changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据冗余拷贝进多处以省去 join、换取更快读取的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization duplicates data in multiple places to skip joins and speed up reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的数据拼在一起返回的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

tradeoff: 读性能（免 join） vs 写一致性维护成本（改多处）
optionExplanations: 反规范化通常是为了少 join、读更快，不是让两条路径都变慢。
规范化读取常常要 join 多张表，反而不是读得更快的那一边。
读路径要不要 join、更新要改几处，两者的成本形状完全不同。
对，把字段冗余进多处能省 join、读更快，但源数据一变就要改所有拷贝。
optionExplanations_en: Denormalization is usually meant to cut joins and speed reads, not slow down both paths.
Normalized reads often require joining several tables, so it's not actually the faster side for reads.
Whether reads need a join and how many places a write must update — their cost shapes are quite different.
Right — duplicating a field in multiple places skips joins and speeds reads, but every source change must now update every copy.

scenario: 面试中要给数据建模起手式，还没发现任何具体的性能问题。
scenario_en: You are starting data modeling in an interview and have not found a specific performance bottleneck yet.
q: 安全的默认策略是？
q_en: What is the safer default when you start data modeling in an interview?
options: 一上来就全面反规范化
全部数据放进一张宽表
先规范化，按需反规范化热路径
先反规范化冲刺上线，等出现数据不一致问题再回头改规范化
options_en: Denormalize everything from the start.
Put all data into one wide table.
Start with a normalized relational model and denormalize specific hot paths only after identifying read performance issues.
Denormalize first to ship faster, then fix it back to normalized once inconsistency shows up.
why: 别无缘无故上来就反规范化；考官要看的是你懂取舍，而不是盲套技巧。
why_en: Start with a normalized relational model and denormalize specific hot paths only after identifying read performance issues.
whenOtherWins: 如果有明确理由（读极重、数据几乎不变的展示路径），可以更早论证反规范化——关键是给出理由。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据冗余拷贝进多处以省去 join、换取更快读取的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization duplicates data in multiple places to skip joins and speed up reads.

tradeoff: 先保正确性再优化热路径 vs 一步到位追求读性能
optionExplanations: 还没量出读瓶颈就全面反规范化，等于提前替不存在的问题背复杂度。
完全不拆表会让重复和不一致从第一天就存在，不是起步该选的建模方式。
对，先保证正确性和一致更新，再对被证实的热路径做小范围冗余。
先冗余后补救等于先制造一致性问题，再花更大代价往回修。
optionExplanations_en: Going all-in on denormalization before measuring a read bottleneck means paying complexity for a problem you don't have yet.
Skipping table splits entirely bakes in duplication and inconsistency from day one — not a sound starting model.
Right — normalize first for correctness and consistent updates, then denormalize narrowly once a hot path is proven.
Denormalizing first just creates the consistency problem sooner, then costs more to walk back later.

q: 社交 App 用 user_id 做 DynamoDB 分区键（匹配「取用户 X 的全部帖子」），那「查提到 hashtag Y 的帖子」会怎样？
q_en: If DynamoDB is partitioned by user_id for fetching a user posts, what happens when you query posts by hashtag?
options: 要扫描整张表——因为没为这个访问模式设计
自动走索引，很快
DynamoDB 会拒绝该查询语法
和分区键查询一样快
options_en: It scans the entire table, because you did not design for this access pattern.
It automatically uses an index and stays fast.
DynamoDB rejects that query syntax outright.
It's just as fast as a partition-key query.
why: NoSQL 必须预先知道查询、围绕访问模式设计 partition/sort key：匹配的查询是单分区秒查，没设计过的查询就是全表扫描。
why_en: With user id as the partition key, a hashtag query scans the whole table because you did not design for that access pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 用来决定数据落在哪个分区的主键字段，决定了哪些查询是单分区秒查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which partition an item lands in, which in turn decides which queries are fast single-partition lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    Query1["by user_id"] --> Hit["single partition"]
    Query2["by hashtag"] --> Scan["table scan unless indexed"]
optionExplanations: 对，partition key 只加速按它查询的路径；hashtag 查询没被设计进去，只能全表扫。
DynamoDB 不会自动为你没设计的访问模式建索引，得手动加 GSI 才行。
语法本身是合法的，只是没有索引支撑，代价是扫描整张表而不是报错。
分区键查询是单分区秒查，hashtag 查询没有这个优势，速度差距很大。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the partition key only accelerates lookups by that key; a hashtag query wasn't designed for, so it's a full table scan.
DynamoDB doesn't auto-index access patterns you never designed for; you'd need to add a GSI yourself.
The query syntax itself is valid — it's just unindexed, so the cost is a full scan, not a rejection.
A partition-key query is a fast single-partition lookup; a hashtag query has none of that advantage, so the gap is large.

q: 补全关系型 vs NoSQL 的取向：
q_en: Fill in the relational versus NoSQL design bias.

why: 这是数据建模的第一层选型直觉，之后再用具体的访问模式和一致性需求收敛。

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.
