scenario: 你没有练习伙伴，但想先自己模拟白板设计流程。
scenario_en: You do not have a practice partner yet, but you want to simulate the whiteboard design flow by yourself.
q: 没有练习伙伴时，可行替代是什么？
q_en: What is a workable substitute before you have a mock partner?
options: 什么都不做，只是干等 mock 搭子出现
只截图收藏别人写好的完整答案，不自己动手
用 Guided Practice 或白板自己讲一遍
只写代码，完全跳过画架构图这一步
options_en: Do nothing at all and just wait around for a mock partner to show up.
Only screenshot and collect other people's complete answers, without doing any work yourself.
Use Guided Practice or a whiteboard to narrate it yourself.
Only write code and skip the step of drawing an architecture diagram entirely.
why: 没有 peer 时也能用 guided practice 或白板练结构化输出；重点是不要停留在只读的模式。
why_en: Guided practice or a virtual whiteboard lets you practice structured output even before you find a mock partner.
whenOtherWins: 能独立讲完整后，仍应尽快找 mock，因为真实追问很难自我模拟。
tradeoff: 自己动手画讲 vs 被动等待搭子

termDefinitions.meaning: HelloInterview 提供的分步骤引导式练习工具，边做边给反馈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guided Practice is a step-by-step exercise tool that gives feedback as you design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一人模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mock is a timed practice interview with another person.

optionExplanations: 干等搭子出现，等待的这段时间完全练不到任何东西。
截图收藏别人的答案不会训练你自己的表达或设计能力，跟没练一样。
没有搭子时用 Guided Practice 或白板自己边画边讲，照样能练到结构化输出这一步。
只写代码跳过架构图，漏掉了需求、组件和取舍这几个真正要练的环节。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting around for a partner to show up produces zero practice volume in the meantime.
Screenshotting and saving other people's answers trains neither your explanation nor your design skill — it's the same as not practicing.
Without a partner, narrating your own design with Guided Practice or a whiteboard still trains structured output.
Writing only code and skipping the diagram misses the requirements, components, and tradeoffs that actually need practice.

scenario: 你在练题时没有固定推进顺序，想到哪讲到哪。
scenario_en: When practicing, you have no fixed answer order and just say whatever comes to mind.
q: 没有清晰 roadmap 的系统设计回答最容易出现什么问题？
q_en: What problem does a system design answer without a clear roadmap most often run into?
options: 所有问题都会自动收敛，完全不用管它
已经不再需要澄清任何需求，可以跳过
即兴发挥的效果必然比用框架更快更好
scope creep：不断发散、偏离核心需求
options_en: All problems will automatically converge on their own, no effort needed at all.
You no longer need to clarify any requirements, so that step can be skipped.
Improvising is guaranteed to work out faster and better than using a framework.
Scope creep: the discussion keeps drifting away from core requirements.
why: 面试时间有限，发散会吃掉高层设计和关键深潜的时间；框架的作用就是让你知道下一步该讲什么。
why_en: Without a roadmap, answers tend to drift into scope creep and lose time needed for the core design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 讨论不断扩散、偏离核心需求的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when the discussion keeps expanding beyond the core requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试回答时预先规划好的阶段顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A roadmap is the pre-planned sequence of stages for answering the interview.

optionExplanations: 现实恰恰相反，没有框架讨论更容易发散，不会自动收敛。
没有 roadmap 不等于不用澄清需求，跳过这步反而更容易让设计整体跑偏。
即兴发挥来回摸索方向，实际比按框架推进更费时间，不是更快。
没有 roadmap 时讨论会不断发散、偏离核心需求，高层设计和深潜的时间就被无关话题占用了。
optionExplanations_en: In reality the opposite happens — without a framework, discussions drift instead of converging on their own.
No roadmap doesn't mean skipping clarification; skipping it actually makes the whole design more likely to drift off target.
Improvising and backtracking usually costs more time than following a framework, not less.
Without a roadmap, discussion keeps expanding away from core requirements, eating the time meant for high-level design and deep dives.

scenario: 你只有两周准备系统设计，基础薄弱，但每天能练习。
scenario_en: You have only two weeks to prepare for system design, your foundation is weak, but you can practice every day.
q: 最合理的时间分配倾向是什么？
q_en: What time-allocation strategy makes the most sense?
options: 快速过一遍基础，再用 easy/medium 题主动输出
两周时间全部拿来看书面题解，完全不做任何输出练习
只做 hard 难度的题目，完全不补任何基础概念
只死记硬背一整份系统设计技术名词列表
options_en: Skim the foundations fast, then drill active output on easy/medium problems.
Spend the entire two weeks only reading write-ups, with no output practice at all.
Only work on hard-difficulty problems, without filling in any foundational concepts.
Only rote-memorize one entire list of system design terminology.
why: 短期备考要先建最低可用框架，再尽快进入输出练习；短板通常在讲题过程中才暴露。
why_en: With limited time, build the minimum framework quickly and spend most effort on active easy-to-medium practice.
whenOtherWins: 如果基础已经扎实，可以把更多时间投入 hard 题 mock 和深潜复盘。
tradeoff: 快速搭框架转向输出 vs 长时间只做输入阅读

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

optionExplanations: 两周时间紧、基础薄弱时，先快速过一遍基础再转向 easy/medium 输出练习，能同时补上概念缺口和表达短板。
两周全花在阅读上，面试现场才会暴露的表达短板完全没机会被发现。
基础还不牢就直接冲 hard 题，复杂约束会把人卡在半路。
背下名词列表不等于会用它们做设计判断，两周时间这样花性价比很低。
optionExplanations_en: With two weeks and weak basics, skim the foundations fast then shift into easy/medium output practice, closing both the concept gap and the speaking gap.
Spending the whole two weeks reading never exposes the speaking weakness that only shows up when you actually explain a design.
Rushing into hard problems before the basics are solid means heavy constraints stall you partway through.
Memorizing a list of terms isn't the same as using them to make design calls — a poor use of two weeks.

q: 按正确顺序排列一条完整的准备路线：
q_en: Put the full preparation path in the right order:
steps: 做 peer mock，训练在时间压力下沟通
补基础：core concepts、key technologies、patterns
理解面试形式并选择 delivery framework
从题单选择 easy/medium 题，先自己做再看答案
why: 完整路线是先知道怎么答，再补概念词汇，然后靠做题输出，最后用 mock 逼近真实面试。
why_en: The full path is understanding the format and framework, filling in the foundations, practicing problems actively, and finishing with mock interviews.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    I["Interview shape"] --> F["Framework"]
    F --> B["Basics"]
    B --> P["Easy/medium practice"]
    P --> M["Mock"]
tradeoff: 先搭路线图再逐步深入 vs 直接从做题开始

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

q: 系统设计面试本质上在考察什么能力？
q_en: What ability does a system design interview mainly test?
options: 把模糊的高层问题拆解成所需的基础设施组件
反复背诵标准的架构设计模板
在白板上手写一份可运行代码
记住尽可能多的数据库产品名称
options_en: Breaking an ambiguous, high-level problem into the infrastructure pieces it needs.
Reciting a memorized standard architecture template over and over.
Handwriting a piece of runnable code on the whiteboard.
Memorizing as many database product names as possible.
why: 题目故意留白、规格不全，考的是你能否拆出服务、数据库、负载均衡等构件并推进出解；比算法题更贴近真实工程判断。
why_en: A system design interview mainly tests whether you can turn an ambiguous problem into the infrastructure pieces needed to solve it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Fuzzy["Fuzzy prompt"] --> Decompose["Decompose"]
    Decompose --> Parts["Services + storage"]
    Parts --> System["Working system"]
optionExplanations: 对，这正是核心能力——面试官故意把需求说得模糊，就是要看你能不能独立拆出所需的服务、存储这些构件并往前推进。
模板背得再熟，遇到没见过的变体照样卡壳，面试真正看的是临场拆解，不是背诵套路。
手写可运行代码是编码轮的要求，设计轮通常只要接口和数据流清楚，不用抠语法。
记住再多数据库产品名也代替不了权衡判断，选型要靠约束推理，不是知识竞赛。
optionExplanations_en: Right — interviewers deliberately keep the prompt vague to see if you can independently break it into the services and storage you need and push forward.
A memorized template collapses the moment the question varies; what gets tested is on-the-spot decomposition, not recitation.
Runnable code is a coding-round ask; design rounds just need clear interfaces and data flow, not syntax.
Knowing many database names does not replace trade-off reasoning — picking one still needs constraint-driven judgment.

q: 关于「标准答案」，系统设计面试的正确认知是？
q_en: What is the right mindset about standard answers in system design interviews?
options: 每道题都有唯一标准答案，必须精确命中
回答内容不重要，只要讲话时间够长
很多题有多个可行答案，考官看重权衡与表达
只要猜中面试官心中的方案就能过关
options_en: Every question has one exact standard answer you must hit.
Content doesn't matter as long as you talk for a long time.
Many questions have multiple workable answers; interviewers value trade-offs and clarity.
You just need to guess the architecture the interviewer has in mind.
why: 设计面试没有唯一正解；考官评估你在复杂问题里怎么权衡取舍、怎么把思路讲清楚。
why_en: Design interviews are not about one right answer — interviewers assess how you weigh trade-offs and communicate your thinking.
optionExplanations: 误解：以为有单一标准答案，遇到题目一变体就懵，其实设计题常有多种可行解。
误解：以为靠拖时间就能过关，考官在意的是内容的推理质量，不是时长。
对，考官更看重你能不能把利弊说清楚、讲出让人信服的理由，而不是刚好蒙对某个固定答案。
误解：把面试当成猜谜游戏不可控，稳妥做法是澄清约束、自己推出合理方案。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: assuming one exact answer exists — the moment the prompt varies you get stuck, but most design prompts allow several workable solutions.
Misconception: assuming talk time matters more than content — interviewers grade the quality of your reasoning, not how long you speak.
Right — interviewers care more about whether you can lay out the trade-offs and argue for your choice than whether you land on one fixed answer.
Misconception: treating it as a guessing game is unreliable; the safer move is clarifying constraints and deriving a reasonable design yourself.

q: 与 LeetCode 式算法面试相比，系统设计面试的定位差异是？
q_en: How is a system design interview positioned differently from a LeetCode-style algorithm interview?
options: 更学术、更理论
更看重语法细节
更实践、更接近日常真实工作
在评估中的权重更低
options_en: More academic and theoretical.
More focused on exact syntax details.
More practical and closer to everyday engineering work.
Weighted less heavily in the overall evaluation.
why: 系统设计是实践型面试，多数工程师觉得它比刷题更贴近真实工作，考的是工程判断而非算法技巧。
why_en: System design interviews are practical and feel closer to real engineering work than LeetCode-style algorithm interviews.
tradeoff: 贴近真实工程判断 vs 贴近算法解题技巧
whenOtherWins: 若面试明确是刷题轮（考算法复杂度和边界条件），考察重点确实换成解题技巧而非架构判断。

termDefinitions.meaning: 以算法与数据结构刷题、面试练习著称的在线平台，常用来代称算法式面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LeetCode is an online platform for algorithm and data-structure practice, often used to describe algorithm-style interviews.

optionExplanations: 误解：把设计面试想成偏理论研究，其实它考的是能不能落地成可行架构。
误解：以为像编码题一样抠语法，系统设计其实很少纠结具体语法对错。
对，系统设计更贴近日常工程决策——选组件、权衡取舍，比刷算法题更像真实工作。
误解：以为权重更低，实际上级别越高，这轮的权重往往越大，不是越小。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: treating it as academic research — it actually tests whether you can land on a workable architecture.
Misconception: expecting it to hinge on exact syntax like coding rounds — system design rarely cares about syntax correctness.
Right — system design mirrors day-to-day engineering decisions like picking components and weighing trade-offs, closer to real work than algorithm drills.
Misconception: assuming lower weight — for senior roles this round is often weighted more heavily, not less.

q: 关于职级与系统设计面试的关系，正确的有？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about level and system design interviews are correct?
options: 入门级岗位通常没有系统设计面试（有例外）
到了中级，系统设计面试开始变得常见
高级级别基本必考，且权重格外大
职级越高，系统设计面试越不重要
options_en: Entry-level roles usually skip the system design round, with exceptions.
At mid-level, system design interviews become common.
At senior level, it is essentially mandatory and weighted heavily.
The higher the level, the less system design matters.
why: 入门级基本不考、中级渐多、高级是常态且权重不成比例地高；职级越高，系统设计信号反而越关键。
why_en: Entry-level rarely has system design, it becomes common at mid-level, and at senior level it is the norm with outsized weight.
optionExplanations: 对，入门岗大多直接跳过这一轮，但也有公司是例外，投递前最好先确认。
对，到中级这轮就变成常规环节，备考要正式把它排进计划。
对，高级岗基本必考，而且权重往往不成比例地高，是筛选的核心信号。
误解：级别越高系统设计权重不是变小反而变大，这个说法和实际相反。
optionExplanations_en: Right — entry-level roles usually skip this round, though a few companies are the exception, so it's worth confirming before you apply.
Right — at mid-level it becomes a standard part of the loop, so it belongs in serious prep plans.
Right — at senior level it is essentially mandatory and carries outsized weight as a core signal.
Misconception: the opposite is true — system design weight tends to grow, not shrink, at higher levels.

q: 绝大多数系统设计面试属于哪一类？
q_en: What category do most system design interviews fall into?
options: 低层设计（类结构 / OOD）
前端设计
ML 系统设计
产品设计 / 基础设施设计
options_en: Low-Level Design (class structure / OOD).
Frontend design.
ML system design.
Product design / infrastructure design.
why: 压倒性多数题目是产品/基础设施设计，如设计 Uber、限流器，靠服务、负载均衡、数据库这类构件求解。
why_en: The overwhelming majority of system design interviews are product or infrastructure design questions like designing Uber or a rate limiter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计：考类结构、对象与接口设计，也叫面向对象设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-Level Design (LLD) is an interview type about designing class structures, objects, and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象设计：LLD 面试的另一个称呼。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object-Oriented Design (OOD) is another name for the LLD interview format.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习，这里指以建模、特征工程为核心的系统设计面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ML stands for Machine Learning, referring here to the interview type centered on modeling and feature engineering.

optionExplanations: 误解：LLD 单独聚焦类和接口设计，是专门指南覆盖的题型，不属于本指南的主线范围。
误解：前端设计是独立类别，聚焦客户端状态和渲染，同样只占很小比例。
误解：ML 系统设计专攻建模和特征工程，是少数题目才会遇到的类型。
对，这类题目占了绝大多数——像打车调度或限流器这种，答案要靠服务、存储和流量分发这些基础设施构件拼出来。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: LLD focuses narrowly on class and interface design — it has its own dedicated guide, not this one.
Misconception: frontend design is a separate category about client state and rendering, and it's also a small slice.
Misconception: ML system design centers on modeling and feature engineering, which only a minority of prompts need.
Right — most prompts fall here: things like ride-hailing dispatch or a rate limiter get solved with services, storage, and traffic-distribution pieces.

scenario: 面试官要求你为停车场系统设计类结构：对象、接口、继承与方法，不涉及服务器、数据库等部署问题。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to design the class structure for a parking lot system: objects, interfaces, inheritance, and methods, with no server or database deployment concerns.
q: 这属于哪类面试，该按什么准备？
q_en: What type of interview is this, and how should you prepare?
options: 产品设计，用本指南
基础设施设计，也走本指南
低层设计LLD，走专门指南
ML系统设计，走专门指南
options_en: Product design — this guide fits.
Infrastructure design — also this guide.
Low-Level Design (LLD) — needs its own dedicated guide.
ML system design — needs the dedicated ML guide.
why: 题目在设计类结构、对象与接口，属于低层设计（LLD/OOD），备考路径要走专门的 LLD 指南，不是本指南。
why_en: Designing class structure, objects, and interfaces is a Low-Level Design interview, which needs its own dedicated LLD guide.
whenOtherWins: 若题目要求设计 Uber 后端这类画服务、数据库、负载均衡的题，才回到本指南覆盖的产品/基础设施设计。
tradeoff: 类结构与对象设计 vs 服务、数据库这类基础设施设计

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计：考类结构、对象与接口设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-Level Design (LLD) is an interview type about designing class structures, objects, and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象设计：LLD 面试的另一个称呼。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object-Oriented Design (OOD) is another name for the LLD interview format.

optionExplanations: 产品设计适合让你画服务、用户流程和后端组件的题，比如设计后端服务，这道类结构题不属于这类。
基础设施设计适合考容量、存储和流量分发的题，同样不是这道只画类和接口的题目。
对，题目在设计对象、接口和继承关系，这是 LLD/OOD 的典型信号，应该参考专门的 LLD 备考资料。
ML 系统设计适合考建模、特征工程的题，这里没有任何模型或数据管道，用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Product design fits prompts about drawing services, user flows, and backend components — not this class-structure question.
Infrastructure design fits capacity, storage, and traffic-distribution prompts, which this class-and-interface question isn't either.
Right — designing objects, interfaces, and inheritance is the classic LLD/OOD signal, so it calls for dedicated LLD prep material.
ML system design fits modeling and feature-engineering prompts — there is no model or data pipeline here to apply it to.

scenario: 面试内容包含 ML 建模、特征工程等应用机器学习工程师的核心职责。
scenario_en: The interview covers ML modeling and feature engineering, which are core responsibilities for applied machine learning engineers.
q: 应按哪类面试准备？
q_en: Which interview type should you prepare for?
options: ML系统设计，走专门ML指南
产品设计，走本指南
低层设计，走LLD指南
前端设计，找专门资源
options_en: ML system design — use the dedicated ML guide.
Product design — use this guide.
Low-Level design — use the LLD guide.
Frontend design — find dedicated frontend resources.
why: 面试考建模、特征工程等应用 ML 工程职责，属于 ML 系统设计，要走专门的 ML System Design 指南。
why_en: Interviews covering ML modeling and feature engineering are ML system design interviews and need the dedicated ML guide.
whenOtherWins: 若 ML 只是产品里接入的黑盒组件、不深挖建模细节，那仍属于产品设计面试范畴。
tradeoff: ML 建模与特征工程能力 vs 服务/基础设施设计能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习，这里指以建模、特征工程为核心的系统设计面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ML stands for Machine Learning, referring here to the interview type centered on modeling and feature engineering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习系统设计：考建模、特征工程等应用 ML 工程能力的面试类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ML System Design is an interview type covering modeling, feature engineering, and applied ML engineering.

optionExplanations: 对，题目要深挖建模和特征工程，这是 ML 系统设计的核心边界，按 ML 系统设计专门指南来准备最合适。
产品设计适合把 ML 当成黑盒服务接入、不深挖建模细节的题，这里明显要求深入建模。
LLD 适合考对象、接口和类关系，这里没有类结构问题，用不上。
前端设计适合客户端状态、渲染和交互的题，和这里的建模、特征工程完全不搭边。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the prompt digs into modeling and feature engineering, squarely ML system design, so the dedicated ML guide is the right prep path.
Product design fits when ML is just a black-box service you plug in without diving into modeling, which is not the case here.
LLD fits object, interface, and class-relationship prompts — there is no class structure here to design.
Frontend design fits client state, rendering, and interaction — unrelated to the modeling and feature-engineering focus here.

q: 无论什么级别，候选人在系统设计面试中共同的底线要求是？
q_en: What baseline expectation applies to every level in a system design interview?
options: 至少说出三种消息队列
写出核心模块伪代码
把所有组件讲到源码级深度
完成一个满足需求的完整设计
options_en: Name at least three message queue products.
Write pseudocode for the core modules.
Explain every component down to source-code depth.
Deliver a complete design that satisfies the requirements.
why: 所有级别都要交付一个满足需求、能工作的完整设计；级别差异体现在深度，不是「能不能做完」。
why_en: Every level is expected to deliver a complete, working design that satisfies the requirements, with depth as the only differentiator.
optionExplanations: 误解：报菜名式列举消息队列产品和是否达标无关，考官不会按这个打分。
误解：伪代码只在少数题目里用得上，不是所有级别都要求写出来。
误解：时间根本撑不到源码级深度，级别差异体现在深挖广度而非讲到多细。
对，不管什么级别，都要先交付一个满足需求、能跑起来的完整设计，深度差异是后话。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: rattling off message-queue product names has nothing to do with passing the bar — it's not what gets scored.
Misconception: pseudocode only helps on a handful of prompts, not a universal requirement across levels.
Misconception: there is rarely enough time for source-code depth — level differences show up in how deep you go, not whether you go that deep.
Right — every level must first deliver a complete, working design that satisfies the requirements; depth is what varies after that.

q: 同一道题，中级与高级工程师的达标表现差异主要在？
q_en: For the same prompt, what mainly separates a mid-level answer from a senior-level answer?
options: 中级不必收集需求，高级才需要
高级必须堆更多组件数量
中级基础覆盖广，高级快过基础换深挖时间
高级可以跳过高层设计直接细化
options_en: Mid-level doesn't need to gather requirements, only senior does.
Senior engineers must stack in more components.
Mid-level covers the basics broadly; senior moves fast through basics to buy deep-dive time.
Senior engineers can skip high-level design and go straight to detail.
why: 中级把基础做扎实即可；高级要迅速过完基础，把省下的时间投入 deep dive 来展示深度。
why_en: A mid-level engineer nails the fundamentals broadly, while a senior engineer moves through them quickly to leave time for deep dives.
tradeoff: 基础覆盖的广度 vs 深挖展示的深度

termDefinitions.meaning: 深挖：面试中针对某个组件展开的深度追问环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the part of the interview where you go into depth on one specific component.

optionExplanations: 误解：需求收集是所有级别的起点，不是高级才需要。
误解：组件数量不代表水平，堆砌反而会让设计显得臃肿。
对，两者的差异主要在时间分配：中级把基础打牢就行，高级会压缩基础环节，把挪出来的时间用在深挖上。
误解：高层设计仍是进入细节前的共同骨架，跳过会让设计缺少导航。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: requirements gathering is the starting point at every level, not something senior candidates add on.
Misconception: component count does not signal seniority — stacking more in just makes the design bloated.
Right — mid-level candidates cover fundamentals thoroughly, while seniors move through them fast to spend the saved time on a deep dive.
Misconception: high-level design is still the shared skeleton before details — skipping it leaves the design without navigation.

q: 关于 staff+ 级别的系统设计面试，正确的是？
q_en: What is true about staff-plus system design interviews?
options: staff 级打法不同，需按级别调整
与低级别完全一样
staff 级不考系统设计
staff 级只考编码
options_en: Staff-level play is different and needs its own adjustments.
It's exactly the same as lower levels.
Staff level doesn't test system design at all.
Staff level only tests coding.
why: staff 级面试和更低级别有实质差异，不能照搬同一套打法，要按 staff 专门指导调整策略。
why_en: Staff-level system design interviews differ substantially from lower levels, so you need to adjust your approach accordingly.

termDefinitions.meaning: Staff 及以上级别的工程师，通常要影响跨团队的技术方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staff-plus refers to staff-level and above engineers, who are expected to influence technical direction across teams.

optionExplanations: 对，staff 级面试要求展示跨团队、更高杠杆的判断，打法和更低级别有实质差异。
误解：照搬中级/高级的套路会失分，staff 期待的信号明显更高。
误解：staff+ 岗位通常更依赖系统设计信号，完全不考的情况很少见。
误解：编码只覆盖实现能力，替代不了这轮要考察的架构判断力。
optionExplanations_en: Right — staff-level interviews expect cross-team, higher-leverage judgment, substantially different from lower levels.
Misconception: reusing mid/senior tactics loses points — staff level expects a visibly stronger signal.
Misconception: staff-plus roles usually lean on system design even more, not less — skipping it entirely is rare.
Misconception: coding only covers implementation skill and cannot substitute for the architectural judgment this round tests.

q: 补全所有公司评分标准共有的四大主题：
q_en: Fill in the four themes shared by company system design rubrics:
text: 四大评估主题：{{Problem Navigation}} 问题导航、{{Solution Design}} 方案设计、{{Technical Excellence}} 技术卓越、{{Communication}} 沟通与协作。
why: 各公司 rubric 措辞不同，但都绕不开这四件事；准备时可对照这四项逐一自查。
why_en: Every company's rubric touches the same four themes: problem navigation, solution design, technical excellence, and communication and collaboration.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Rubric["Rubric"] --> Nav["Navigation"]
    Rubric --> Sol["Solution"]
    Rubric --> Tech["Technical"]
    Rubric --> Comm["Communication"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 问题导航：把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive it toward a solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方案设计：用核心概念解决拆出的子问题，并拼成协调的整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design means solving each subproblem with core concepts and assembling them into a coherent whole.

termDefinitions.meaning: 技术卓越：了解现行技术与公认模式，并能应用到问题上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem at hand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沟通与协作：能讲清概念、接住反馈、并与面试官协作解题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Communication and Collaboration means explaining ideas clearly, receiving feedback, and working with the interviewer to solve the problem.

q: 「问题导航（Problem Navigation）」考察的核心是？
q_en: What is the core skill tested by Problem Navigation?
options: 尽快先画出最终架构图
拆小问题、排优先级、推进到解
多问问题来拖延时间
证明题目出得有问题
options_en: Rush to draw the final architecture diagram.
Decompose the problem, prioritize, and drive toward a solution.
Ask lots of questions just to stall for time.
Argue that the question itself is flawed.
why: 面试官想看你能否拆解、排序、推进一个规格不全的问题；这常是整场最重要、最拉开差距的一环。
why_en: Problem navigation means decomposing an under-specified problem, prioritizing it, and driving it toward a solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 问题导航：把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive toward a solution.

optionExplanations: 误解：架构图适合放在需求和优先级理清楚之后画，一上来就画容易返工。
对，考官想看你能不能把规格不全的问题拆解、排序、并持续往前推进到方案。
误解：提问只有服务于决策时才算导航，纯粹拖时间不会加分。
误解：就算题目有瑕疵，也要澄清约束继续推进，而不是纠结题目本身。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the diagram belongs after requirements and priorities are clear — jumping straight to it often means redoing work.
Right — interviewers want to see you decompose the under-specified problem, prioritize it, and keep driving toward a solution.
Misconception: questions only count as navigation when they drive a decision — stalling with questions does not score points.
Misconception: even with an imperfect prompt, the move is to clarify constraints and keep going, not dwell on the flaw.

q: 问题导航维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Problem Navigation dimension?
options: 对问题探索不足、需求收集不充分
把时间花在琐碎无趣的部分而不是最重要的部分
卡死在某一块上无法向前推进
使用了过时的技术选型
options_en: Under-exploring the problem and not gathering enough requirements.
Spending time on trivial parts instead of the important ones.
Getting stuck on one piece and unable to move forward.
Choosing outdated technology.
why: 第四种被点名的失败是没能交付一个能工作的系统；用过时技术属于技术卓越维度，不算导航失败。
why_en: Common navigation failures are under-exploring requirements, focusing on trivial parts, and getting stuck; outdated tech choices belong to a different competency.
optionExplanations: 对，前期探索不够会让后续设计建立在不完整的理解上，是导航失败的典型表现。
对，优先级错位会让琐碎细节挤占关键路径的时间，也算导航失败。
对，卡在一处又没有备选推进路线，会拖垮整场面试的节奏。
误解：技术选型过时属于技术卓越维度的问题，不算作问题导航的失败。
optionExplanations_en: Right — under-exploring the problem upfront leaves the later design resting on an incomplete understanding, a classic navigation failure.
Right — bad prioritization lets trivial details crowd out time for the critical path, also a navigation failure.
Right — getting stuck with no fallback path drags down the pace of the whole interview.
Misconception: outdated technology choices belong to the technical-excellence dimension, not a navigation failure.

q: 许多候选人在面试中无法推进，最常见的根因是？
q_en: What is the most common root cause when candidates cannot make progress in a design interview?
options: 英文词汇量不够
缺乏结构化方法，没有跑道
面试官故意刁难
题目内容超纲
options_en: Not enough English vocabulary.
No structured method — no track to run on.
The interviewer is deliberately being harsh.
The question is beyond what's expected.
why: 缺结构会让你把时间烧在错的问题上；缓解办法是跟随 Delivery Framework，给自己一条固定跑道。
why_en: Most candidates stall because they lack structure, which a delivery framework fixes by giving them a track to run on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

optionExplanations: 误解：词汇会影响表达流畅度，但通常不是推进失败的根因。
对，没有结构化方法时，模糊的题目很容易让人跑偏或原地卡住。
误解：考官刻意刁难的情况其实很少见，不是常见根因。
误解：多数题目其实在合理范围内，超纲很少是真正的卡壳原因。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: vocabulary affects delivery, but it is rarely the root cause of stalling.
Right — without a structured method, an ambiguous prompt easily makes you drift or freeze.
Misconception: interviewers being deliberately harsh is actually rare, not a common cause.
Misconception: most prompts are reasonably scoped — going beyond expectations is rarely the real culprit.

q: 「方案设计（Solution Design）」维度考察什么？
q_en: What does the Solution Design dimension evaluate?
options: 背熟所有云厂商服务名
架构图画得多美观
讲解时的台风与语调
用核心概念逐块求解并拼成整体
options_en: Memorizing every cloud vendor's service names.
How aesthetically pleasing the diagram looks.
Stage presence and vocal tone while presenting.
Solving each piece with core concepts and assembling a coherent whole.
why: 拆完问题后，考官看你怎么用核心概念逐块求解，且各块能拼成连贯系统，而不是零件堆砌。
why_en: Solution design assesses whether you can solve each piece with core concepts and fit the pieces into a cohesive whole.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Problem["Subproblems"] --> Concepts["Core concepts"]
    Concepts --> Blocks["Components"]
    Blocks --> Whole["Coherent system"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 方案设计：用核心概念解决拆出的子问题并拼成整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design means solving each subproblem with core concepts and assembling them into a coherent whole.

optionExplanations: 误解：服务名只有在能解释取舍时才有价值，单纯背熟没意义。
误解：图形美观能帮助沟通，但不能替代架构逻辑本身。
误解：讲解台风属于沟通维度，不属于方案设计要考的内容。
对，方案设计看的是你能不能用核心工具把每块子问题都解决掉，再让这些解法互相咬合成一个整体，而不是各管一段。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: service names only matter when you can explain the trade-off behind them — memorizing the list alone doesn't help.
Misconception: visual polish can aid communication, but it can't substitute for sound architecture logic.
Misconception: presentation style belongs to the communication dimension, not what solution design evaluates.
Right — after decomposing the problem, the interviewer watches whether you solve each piece with core concepts and assemble a coherent whole.

q: 方案设计维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Solution Design dimension?
options: 核心概念功底不足，撑不起方案
忽略扩展性与性能问题
『意大利面设计』：结构混乱、难以理解
过早向面试官确认需求
options_en: Fundamentals too weak to support the design.
Ignoring scaling and performance considerations.
A "spaghetti design" — tangled and hard to follow.
Confirming requirements with the interviewer too early.
why: 三大失败是基础不牢、无视 scaling/性能、结构混乱的意大利面设计；确认需求恰恰是好行为。
why_en: Solution design fails through weak fundamentals, ignoring scaling and performance, or a tangled spaghetti design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组件关系混乱、难以理解的设计，即英文说的 spaghetti design。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spaghetti design is a system whose components are tangled together and hard to follow.

optionExplanations: 对，核心概念弱时，任何组件选择一被追问就容易露馅。
对，流量和数据增长明确时还不谈扩展性，系统就扛不住真实压力。
对，组件关系混乱到考官都跟不上，就是典型的意大利面设计。
误解：提前对齐需求属于良好的沟通行为，反而会帮助方案设计站得住脚。
optionExplanations_en: Right — with weak fundamentals, any component choice tends to fall apart under follow-up questions.
Right — when traffic or data growth is stated, ignoring scaling means the system can't handle real load.
Right — when component relationships are so tangled the interviewer can't follow, that's a textbook spaghetti design.
Misconception: confirming requirements early is good collaboration and actually strengthens the solution, not a failure.

q: 面试官怀疑你在背答案时，通常会怎么做？
q_en: What will interviewers usually do if they suspect you are reciting a memorized answer?
options: 当场直接结束面试
换成更简单的题目
追问推理、故意质疑、要求讲权衡
直接跳过这一部分
options_en: End the interview on the spot.
Switch to an easier question.
Probe your reasoning, express doubt, and ask you to walk through trade-offs.
Skip this section entirely.
why: 考官对背题高度警觉，会 probe 推理、故意表示怀疑、要你讲 trade-off；只有扎实基本功才顶得住。
why_en: Interviewers test for memorized answers by probing your reasoning, expressing doubt, and asking you to walk through trade-offs.
optionExplanations: 误解：只有严重违规时才会直接终止面试，背答案通常只是被追问，不会当场结束。
误解：换简单题验证不了你是否真的会推理，考官不会这样处理。
对，考官会 probe 你的推理、故意表示怀疑、要你讲权衡，只有真懂才能扛住。
误解：直接跳过会漏掉考官最想验证的推理信号，不符合常见流程。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: only serious issues end an interview outright — a memorized answer usually just gets probed, not ended.
Misconception: switching to an easier question can't test whether you can actually reason, so interviewers don't do this.
Right — interviewers probe your reasoning, push back on purpose, and ask you to walk through trade-offs; only real understanding survives that.
Misconception: skipping the section would miss exactly the reasoning signal the interviewer is trying to verify.

q: 「技术卓越（Technical Excellence）」维度考察什么？
q_en: What does the Technical Excellence dimension evaluate?
options: 懂现行技术与公认模式并能应用
背熟每种硬件的参数
会写汇编级性能优化
熟悉考官公司内部工具
options_en: Knowing current technologies and recognized patterns, and applying them.
Memorizing every hardware's specific parameters.
Writing assembly-level performance optimizations.
Being familiar with the interviewer's internal company tools.
why: 要设计出好系统，需要知道现在有哪些技术、有哪些公认模式，并能把它们落到手头问题上。
why_en: Technical excellence means knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem at hand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 技术卓越：了解现行技术与公认模式，并能应用到问题上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem at hand.

optionExplanations: 对，好设计得先摸清楚当下有哪些可用技术和被验证过的模式，再把它们套到眼前这道题的约束上。
误解：硬件参数只有在影响容量估算时才需要粗略了解，不用背到细节。
误解：汇编级优化属于性能工程范畴，不是系统设计轮的考察重点。
误解：内部专属工具对不同公司背景的候选人不公平，不该成为门槛。
optionExplanations_en: Right — good design starts with knowing what technologies and proven patterns exist now, then mapping them onto the constraints in front of you.
Misconception: hardware parameters only matter as rough capacity anchors, not something you need memorized in detail.
Misconception: assembly-level tuning belongs to performance engineering, not what a design round is testing.
Misconception: knowledge of internal company-only tools would be unfair across candidates and should not be a bar.

q: 技术卓越维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Technical Excellence dimension?
options: 不知道有哪些可用的现行技术
用过时的方法、被十年前的硬件约束框住
识别不出常见模式与最佳实践
没有背出具体云服务的定价
options_en: Not knowing what current technologies are available.
Using outdated approaches bound by decade-old hardware limits.
Failing to recognize common patterns and best practices.
Not having memorized specific cloud pricing.
why: 还有一种失败是知道技术却不会应用到手头问题；背云服务定价从来不是考点。
why_en: Failures include not knowing available technologies, reasoning from outdated hardware constraints, and not recognizing common patterns.
optionExplanations: 对，不知道有哪些可用技术，方案选择的空间一开始就变窄了。
对，用十年前的硬件假设做决策，容量和延迟判断都会被带偏。
对，认不出常见模式时，知道积木也拼不出可靠方案。
误解：云服务定价从来不是评估内容，顶多在做成本模型时粗略估计。
optionExplanations_en: Right — not knowing which technologies are available narrows the solution space from the start.
Right — reasoning from decade-old hardware assumptions distorts your capacity and latency judgment.
Right — without recognizing common patterns, you know the pieces but can't assemble a reliable design.
Misconception: cloud pricing was never part of the evaluation, at most a rough input for a cost model.

q: 沿用 2015 年前后的老系统设计材料，最大的风险是？
q_en: What is the main risk of relying on system design material from around 2015?
options: 内容太多学不完
按过时硬件假设做决策，显陈旧
考官不认识老技术
没风险，经典不过时
options_en: There's too much content to finish learning.
Decisions rest on outdated hardware assumptions and look stale.
The interviewer won't recognize the old technology.
No risk — classics never go stale.
why: 硬件这十年进步巨大，老材料的容量/延迟假设已失效；要用最新的 numbers to know 校准决策。
why_en: Hardware has advanced enormously in the last decade, so reasoning from outdated constraints makes your design choices look stale.
optionExplanations: 误解：内容量大只影响学习计划安排，不是老材料本身的风险。
对，过去十年硬件突飞猛进，旧教材里对容量和延迟的假设早就不成立了，照着老数字做设计选择自然显得脱节。
误解：考官通常会跟着技术进步走，不太可能不认识常见的新技术。
误解：经典概念可以复用，但数字类的约束必须重新校准，不是完全没风险。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: too much content only affects your study schedule, not a risk of the old material itself.
Right — hardware has advanced enormously in a decade, so stale capacity and latency assumptions make your design choices look outdated.
Misconception: interviewers usually keep up with newer technology, so this is unlikely to be the real issue.
Misconception: classic concepts do transfer, but numeric constraints need recalibrating — so it is not risk-free.

q: 「沟通与协作」维度实质上在评估什么？
q_en: What does the Communication and Collaboration dimension really evaluate?
options: 讲话时台风与语调
讲清概念、接反馈、协作解题
外语表达流利度
画架构图的速度快慢
options_en: Stage presence and vocal tone while speaking.
Explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and collaborating to solve the problem.
Fluency in a foreign language.
How fast you can draw the architecture diagram.
why: 技术面试也是同事体验预演：考官看你能否清晰表达、接住反馈、和他协作把问题解掉。
why_en: The communication dimension gauges what you'd be like as a colleague: explaining ideas, taking feedback, and collaborating on the problem.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Explain["Explain"] --> Feedback["Receive feedback"]
    Feedback --> Adjust["Adjust design"]
    Adjust --> Shared["Shared solution"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 能讲清概念、接住反馈、并与面试官协作解题的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Communication and Collaboration means explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and working with the interviewer to solve the problem.

optionExplanations: 误解：演讲风格能加分，但代替不了协作解题本身。
对，考官在看你能不能讲清概念、接住反馈、并和他协作把问题解掉——这是同事体验的预演。
误解：非母语表达可以慢一点，逻辑清楚比流利度更重要。
误解：画图速度只有在拖慢沟通时才会影响体验，不是核心评分点。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: presentation style can help, but it can't substitute for actually collaborating on the problem.
Right — this dimension previews what you'd be like as a colleague: explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and solving the problem together.
Misconception: non-native delivery can be slower — clear logic matters more than fluency.
Misconception: drawing speed only matters if it slows the conversation down, not a core scoring point.

q: 沟通协作维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Communication and Collaboration dimension?
options: 讲不清楚复杂概念
收到反馈时变得防御、跟面试官争辩
陷进细节泥潭，无法与面试官协作推进
主动和面试官对齐优先级
options_en: Can't clearly explain complex concepts.
Gets defensive and argues when given feedback.
Gets lost in the weeds and can't collaborate forward.
Proactively aligns priorities with the interviewer.
why: 表达不清、反馈激起防御心、迷失在细节里，是沟通维度的三大失败；主动对齐优先级恰恰是加分项。
why_en: Communication failures include unclear explanations, getting defensive about feedback, and getting lost in the weeds instead of collaborating.
optionExplanations: 对，概念讲不清时，考官没法信任后面的设计推进。
对，被反馈触发防御或争辩，会让协作体验迅速变差。
对，陷在细节里走不出来，会挤掉和考官一起往前推进方案的时间。
误解：主动对齐优先级是良好协作的表现，反而会减少误解、加快推进。
optionExplanations_en: Right — when concepts aren't clear, the interviewer can't trust the design that follows.
Right — getting defensive or arguing over feedback quickly hurts the collaboration.
Right — getting stuck in detail crowds out the time needed to move the design forward together.
Misconception: proactively aligning priorities is good collaboration and speeds progress, not a failure mode.

q: 面试官对你的设计提出质疑，最好的反应是？
q_en: What is the best response when the interviewer challenges your design?
options: 坚守原方案寸步不让
立刻全盘推翻设计
沉默等待进一步提示
当作协作试探，回应并解释调整理由
options_en: Defend the original design without budging.
Immediately abandon the entire design.
Stay silent and wait for more hints.
Treat it as collaboration: respond, adjust if needed, and explain your reasoning.
why: 防御与争辩是沟通维度被点名的失败项；质疑常是在测试推理或给提示，接住反馈才是加分姿态。
why_en: Treat pushback as collaboration — respond to the feedback and adjust your design with reasons instead of getting defensive.
optionExplanations: 误解：只有确认质疑站不住脚时才该坚持，一味不让步会显得听不进反馈。
误解：全盘推翻只适合发现核心假设确实错了的情况，不该是默认反应。
误解：沉默只适合短暂停顿思考，不能当作对质疑的正式回应。
对，把质疑当协作输入，回应、按需调整并解释理由，才能展示推理力和开放度。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: only hold your ground once you've confirmed the pushback is wrong — refusing to budge reads as not listening.
Misconception: a full reset fits only when a core assumption really is wrong, not the default reaction.
Misconception: silence is fine for a brief pause but is not a real response to pushback.
Right — treat pushback as collaborative input: respond, adjust if needed, and explain your reasoning, showing both conviction and openness.

q: 「看了大量材料但从不动手练」的典型下场是？
q_en: What usually happens if you read a lot but never practice applying the material?
options: 真上场应用知识时卡壳
知识反而更牢固
对结果毫无影响
面试难度自动降低
options_en: Freezes up when it's time to actually apply the knowledge.
Knowledge actually becomes more solid.
Has no effect on the outcome at all.
The interview automatically gets easier.
why: 这是被点名的常见失败：吸收很多、应用不出来；要靠 worked solutions 和模拟练习把知识转成能上场的输出。
why_en: A common failure mode is consuming lots of material but stumbling when it's time to apply it, which only practice fixes.
optionExplanations: 对，只读不练时知识变不成输出，真上场会在应用这一步卡住。
误解：知识变牢通常靠提取练习，被动阅读反而记不住多少。
误解：准备方式会直接影响能否把知识转成口头设计，不是毫无影响。
误解：面试难度不会因为你练得少就自动下降。
optionExplanations_en: Right — reading without practicing means the knowledge never turns into output, so you freeze up applying it live.
Misconception: retention usually comes from retrieval practice — passive reading alone sticks far less.
Misconception: how you prepare directly affects whether knowledge turns into a spoken design, so it is not a non-factor.
Misconception: interview difficulty does not drop just because you practiced less.

scenario: 你此前完全没接触过系统设计，正在规划从今天到面试日之间怎么分配学习时间。
scenario_en: You have never studied system design before and need to plan how to use the time between today and the interview.
q: 系统设计完全零基础的候选人，建议的准备节奏是？
q_en: What preparation pace is recommended for someone completely new to system design?
options: 一两天速成
至少半年
全职冲刺或摊开3-4周
无法准备，全凭经验
options_en: Cram it in one or two days.
At least six months.
A dedicated sprint, or spread over three to four weeks.
Can't be prepared for — it's all down to experience.
why: 零基础建议全职冲刺，或摊开到 3-4 周；已经熟悉核心概念、经验丰富的人一周内备好也很常见，这个节奏决定你怎么排学习日历。
why_en: If system design is entirely new, plan either a dedicated sprint or three to four weeks, while experienced candidates often prepare in under a week.
optionExplanations: 一两天顶多够刷个概览，零基础想扎实建立框架和核心概念，这个节奏来不及。
半年更像是没有明确截止日期时的从容节奏，面试通常等不了这么久，会拖慢投递进度。
对，零基础比较现实的是全职集中冲刺，或者拆成 3-4 周稳步推进，足够覆盖框架、技术和核心概念。
经验能替代一部分刷题量，但完全不做主动准备，零基础的人大概率会在框架和术语上卡住。
optionExplanations_en: One or two days is barely enough for a skim — building the framework and core concepts from zero needs more runway than that.
Six months fits a wide-open timeline with no real deadline; most interview processes can't wait that long, so it stalls momentum.
Right — for zero background, a realistic pace is a dedicated sprint or spreading it over three to four weeks, enough to cover the framework, key tech, and core concepts.
Experience can substitute for some drilling, but skipping deliberate prep entirely usually leaves a true beginner stuck on framework and terminology.

scenario: 面试日期已排定，但你评估自己还需要更多准备时间，感觉来不及。
scenario_en: The interview date is already scheduled, but you believe you need more preparation time and feel behind.
q: 最合理的第一步是？
q_en: What is the most reasonable first step?
options: 硬着头皮按期上场
直接放弃这家公司
请招聘官把面试往后推
前夜通宵突击材料
options_en: Push through and interview on the original date anyway.
Give up on this company entirely.
Ask the recruiter to push the interview date back.
Pull an all-nighter cramming before the interview.
why: 招聘官通常宁可你晚点面但通过率更高；主动请求推迟日期，大多数会痛快答应。
why_en: Recruiters usually prefer a higher chance of you passing over an earlier date, so ask them to push the interview out.
whenOtherWins: 若基础扎实、只差查漏补缺，按期面试完全合理，不必推迟。
tradeoff: 用一次沟通换更充分的准备时间 vs 按原计划上场应对不确定性

termDefinitions.meaning: 招聘方的招聘协调人，负责面试流程和岗位信息沟通。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recruiter is the hiring-side contact who coordinates the interview process and can share role expectations.

optionExplanations: 基础明显不足时硬着头皮上场，只会带着仓促感进场、放大失败概率。
放弃只适合岗位已经不再匹配的情况，光是准备不够就放弃太可惜。
对，招聘官通常更在意你通过率高不高，主动申请推迟日期换更充分的准备，大多会痛快答应。
通宵突击只适合轻量复盘，补不了系统性的知识缺口，反而会疲劳影响发挥。
optionExplanations_en: Pushing through while clearly underprepared just means walking in rushed, which raises your odds of failing.
Giving up only makes sense once the role is no longer a fit — quitting just because you're behind on prep is premature.
Right — recruiters usually care more about your pass rate than the original date, so asking to push it back for real prep time is often granted.
An all-nighter only works for light review; it can't close a systemic knowledge gap and leaves you tired instead.

scenario: 距离面试只剩几天，时间只够覆盖一小部分材料。
scenario_en: You only have a few days before the interview, and there is time to cover only a small slice of the material.
q: 时间最紧时的学习优先级是？
q_en: What should you prioritize when preparation time is extremely tight?
options: 精读全部问题拆解
先框架、再略读技术、后补概念
只背三道经典题答案
全部时间刷算法题
options_en: Deeply study every problem-breakdown article.
Learn the delivery framework first, skim key technologies, then cover core concepts.
Memorize the answers to three classic questions.
Spend all the time drilling algorithm problems.
why: 极限时间下：交付框架给你答题跑道收益最高，关键技术略读认积木，剩余时间补核心概念深度。
why_en: If you're really short on time, master the delivery framework first, skim the key technologies, and spend the rest on core concepts.
whenOtherWins: 时间充足（3-4 周）时应按顺序完整过指南并配合大量练习，而不是只抓框架。
tradeoff: 先建立答题结构 vs 先积累知识深度
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Time["Very little time"] --> Framework["Delivery framework"]
    Framework --> Tech["Skim key tech"]
    Tech --> Concepts["Core concepts"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键技术：当前主流、可直接用于设计的技术清单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the current, widely used technologies you can apply directly in your design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 核心概念：缓存、分片等构成系统设计答案的基础知识模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the foundational building blocks, like caching and sharding, used to answer design questions.

optionExplanations: 精读全部拆解文章确实有用，但时间根本不够，知道怎么拆却拼不出完整方案。
对，时间极紧时先拿到答题结构收益最高，再快速认识可用技术，剩下时间补概念深度。
只背三道经典题遇到变体就无招可用，考官也很擅长识破背答案。
算法练习适合编码轮，解决不了系统设计要交付完整架构的诉求。
optionExplanations_en: Deeply reading every breakdown article is useful, but there's not enough time — you'd know how to decompose without being able to assemble an answer.
Right — with very little time, structure first pays off most, then a fast pass on usable tech, then whatever is left on core concepts.
Memorizing three classic answers falls apart the moment the question varies, and interviewers are good at spotting recitation.
Algorithm drills fit coding rounds; they don't address the need to deliver a full architecture in a design round.

q: 把「时间极紧时的备考优先级」按先后排序：
q_en: Order the study priorities when preparation time is extremely tight:
steps: 剩余时间投入 Core Concepts（补概念深度）
先掌握 Delivery Framework（先有答题跑道）
略读 Key Technologies（认识可用积木）
why: 框架决定 50 分钟怎么花、收益最高所以先学；再认积木，最后用剩余时间补概念深度。
why_en: Learn the delivery framework first for structure, then skim the key technologies, and spend any remaining time on core concepts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键技术：当前主流、可直接用于设计的技术清单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the current, widely used technologies you can apply directly in your design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 核心概念：缓存、分片等构成系统设计答案的基础知识模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the foundational building blocks, like caching and sharding, used to answer design questions.

q: 把「缺乏结构如何导致面试失败、又如何自救」排成因果顺序：
q_en: Put the causal chain in order: how lack of structure causes interview failure and how to recover:
steps: 把时间烧在错误的问题上，交不出完整系统
题目天生模糊、规格不全
缓解：跟随 Delivery Framework，给自己一条固定跑道
缺乏结构化的推进方法
why: 模糊问题 + 缺结构 → 时间烧错地方、交付失败；缓解 = 用交付框架当轨道跑。
why_en: An ambiguous problem plus no structure burns time on the wrong things and fails to deliver, which the delivery framework prevents.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["模糊、规格不全的问题"] --> B["缺乏结构化方法"] B --> C["时间烧错地方
交不出完整系统"] C --> M["缓解：Delivery Framework"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 交付框架：给面试推进提供固定步骤的方法论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Delivery Framework is a step-by-step method that gives you a track to run on during the interview.

q: 补全问题导航的正确姿势：
q_en: Fill in the correct Problem Navigation posture:
text: 把复杂问题{{拆解}}成更小、可管理的部分，按{{重要性}}排出优先级，并最终交付一个{{能工作}}的系统。
why: 拆解、排序、交付——这三步就是 Problem Navigation 的评分点，漏任何一步都算导航失败。
why_en: Good problem navigation means decomposing the problem, prioritizing the most important pieces, and delivering a working system.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    D["Decompose"] --> P["Prioritize"]
    P --> M["Move forward"]
    M --> W["Working design"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力，即 Problem Navigation。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive toward a solution.

q: 四大评估主题中，被点名「往往最重要、新手最容易栽」的是？
q_en: Among the four evaluation themes, which one is often the most important and hardest for beginners?
options: 技术卓越
沟通与协作
方案设计
问题导航
options_en: Technical Excellence.
Communication and Collaboration.
Solution Design.
Problem Navigation.
why: Problem Navigation 常是整场最重要的部分，也是新手最挣扎的；导航失败会烧错时间、留下坏印象。
why_en: Problem navigation is often the most important competency and the one candidates new to system design struggle with most.

termDefinitions.meaning: 了解现行技术与公认模式，并能应用到问题上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能讲清概念、接住反馈、并与面试官协作解题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Communication and Collaboration means explaining ideas clearly, taking feedback, and collaborating with the interviewer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用核心概念解决拆出的子问题并拼成整体，即 Solution Design。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design means solving each subproblem with core concepts and assembling them into a coherent whole.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力，即 Problem Navigation。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive toward a solution.

optionExplanations: 误解：技术积累再多，遇到没见过的新题依然可能先卡在推进路径上。
误解：表达能力再强，拆解不出方案方向也没用。
误解：整合能力再强，方向一开始就错了，拼装也救不回来。
对，问题导航常是整场最重要、新手最容易栽的一环，决定先做什么、舍弃什么。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: no amount of technical depth helps if you're already stuck on how to move forward on an unfamiliar prompt.
Misconception: strong communication does not help if you never decompose the problem in the right direction.
Misconception: strong assembly skill cannot rescue a design if the direction was wrong from the start.
Right — problem navigation is often the single most important piece and where beginners most often trip up, deciding what to tackle first and what to skip.

q: 高级别候选人把大部分时间耗在基础环节、没进入任何深挖，会怎样？
q_en: What happens if a senior-level candidate spends most of the interview on basics and never reaches a deep dive?
options: 只要基础对就算达标
考官会主动延长时间
自动按中级标准重评
达不到该级别的深度预期
options_en: Getting the basics right is enough to pass.
The interviewer will proactively extend the time.
You get automatically re-evaluated by mid-level standards.
Falls short of the level's depth expectation.
why: 高级别的评分预期是快速过基础、把时间留给 deep dive 展示深度；全场耗在基础上等于没机会展示信号。
why_en: A senior candidate who spends the whole interview on basics never gets to show the depth expected at that level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试中针对某个组件展开的深度追问环节，即英文说的 deep dive。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the part of the interview where you go into depth on one specific component.

optionExplanations: 误解：基础正确只是门槛，高级候选人还要额外展示深度判断。
误解：面试时间通常固定，考官不会因为你慢就主动加时。
误解：评分通常按目标级别的信号来看，不会自动降档重评。
对，全场耗在基础上就没机会做深挖，等于没能展示这个级别该有的深度。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: correct basics are only the floor — senior candidates are also expected to show depth of judgment.
Misconception: interview time is usually fixed, so the interviewer won't add time just because you're slow.
Misconception: scoring looks for the target level's signal, it does not automatically downgrade to a lower bar.
Right — spending the whole interview on basics leaves no room for a deep dive, so the depth expected at that level never gets shown.

q: 「设计 Uber」「设计限流器」这类题，典型要用到的构件是？
q_en: What building blocks do prompts like designing Uber or a rate limiter typically use?
options: 服务、负载均衡、数据库等构件
只有客户端代码
类图与设计模式
特征工程管道
options_en: Infrastructure like services, load balancers, and databases.
Only client-side code.
Class diagrams and design patterns.
A feature-engineering pipeline.
why: 产品/基础设施设计题的解由服务、负载均衡、数据库、缓存、队列这类构件组成，不是类图也不是 ML 管道。
why_en: Product and infrastructure design questions are solved with pieces like services, load balancers, and databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把请求分发到多台服务器的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把原始数据加工成模型可用输入特征的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature engineering is turning raw data into input features a model can use.

optionExplanations: 对，这类题的解法通常靠服务、存储和流量分发这些基础设施构件组合出来。
误解：客户端代码适合前端题，答不到后端系统架构层面。
误解：类图适合 LLD/OOD 题，解决不了分布式服务的设计问题。
误解：特征工程管道属于 ML 系统设计，不是通用产品架构的主线。
optionExplanations_en: Right — these prompts are typically solved by combining infrastructure pieces like services, storage, and traffic distribution.
Misconception: client-side code fits frontend prompts, not the backend system-architecture level being tested here.
Misconception: class diagrams fit LLD/OOD prompts, not distributed-service design problems.
Misconception: a feature-engineering pipeline belongs to ML system design, not generic product architecture.

q: 面试官对关键技术的追问深度，主要取决于什么？
q_en: What mainly determines how deeply an interviewer will probe key technologies?
options: 你选的是不是最新的技术
面试官个人的技术偏好
你面试的级别：中级/高级要求不同
公司用不用这项技术
why: 追问深度与级别成正比：中级候选人能把 Elasticsearch 描述成搜索索引就够了；高级候选人讲不出倒排索引、说不清它怎么扩展就是黄旗。总体原则是先广度、后深度。
why_en: Interviewers probe technology depth in proportion to your level, so a rough description is fine for mid-level but a senior who cannot explain the inverted index is a yellow flag.
options_en: Whether you picked the newest technology
The interviewer's personal technology preference
The level you are interviewing at (mid-level and senior expectations differ)
Whether the company actually uses that technology
optionExplanations: 面试官考察的是你对技术的理解深度，不是你是否追新，选新技术并不会换来更少追问。
追问深度背后是标准化的分级预期，不是某位面试官的个人喜好在起作用。
对，追问深度按你面试的级别走：中级说清概念就够，高级答不出扩展细节就会被继续追问。
公司实际用不用这项技术，不会改变面试官按你的级别来决定追多深。
optionExplanations_en: Depth of follow-up tracks how well you understand the tech, not whether you picked something trendy.
The probing depth follows a leveling standard, not one interviewer's personal taste.
Right - depth scales with your level: mid-level can stay at a rough description, senior gets pushed on internals like scaling.
Whether the company happens to use that tech doesn't change how deep your level gets probed.

q: 对每一类构建块（队列、缓存、搜索……），备考的正确目标是？
q_en: For each building-block category such as queues, caches, and search, what is the right prep goal?
options: 每一类至少掌握一个能拿来用的具体方案
把每一类的所有方案都背下来并能横向对比
只准备数据库，其他现场发挥
熟记各家云厂商的产品名
why: 面试官通常不在乎你用的是哪个队列方案，只要你有一个会用的；但如果任何队列方案都不知道，需要队列的题就没法做。每类至少备一个。
why_en: Interviewers rarely care which queueing solution you pick, but you must know at least one option in every key category.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Need["Need a block"] --> Know["Know one option"]
    Know --> Use["Use it in design"]
    Use --> Trade["Explain tradeoff"]
options_en: Have at least one usable option for every building-block category
Memorize every option in every category and be able to compare them
Only prepare databases and improvise the rest
Memorize the product names of every cloud vendor
optionExplanations: 对，目标是每类构建块都能拿出一个能落地的方案，面试官通常不在意你具体选了哪个。
背下每类的所有方案再横向对比超出面试要求，面试官很少要求你逐一比较同类工具。
只准备数据库、其余现场发挥太冒险：一旦考到队列或搜索，你连一个能用的方案都拿不出来。
记住云厂商的产品名字不等于会用它解决问题，面试官想看的是你怎么用，而不是背产品目录。
optionExplanations_en: Right - the goal is one usable option per building-block category; which exact one you pick rarely matters.
Memorizing every option in every category to compare them is overkill; interviewers rarely ask for a full lineup.
Prepping only databases and winging the rest is risky - a queue or search question would leave you with nothing usable.
Knowing vendor product names isn't the same as knowing how to use them; interviewers care about application, not a name list.

scenario: 你接下来主要面产品设计（product design）类的系统设计题，要提前选定一个默认数据库带进面试。
scenario_en: You are mainly interviewing for product-design system design questions, and you want to pick one default database to use consistently.
q: 推荐的默认选型是？
q_en: What default database should you bring into the interview?
options: 图数据库（擅长关系遍历）
关系型数据库（如 Postgres）
内存缓存，直接当主库使用
自研的文件存储系统
why: 建议只选一种带进面试：产品设计面试默认关系型数据库（如 Postgres），基础设施设计面试默认 NoSQL（如 DynamoDB）。没有偏好的话关系库选 Postgres。
why_en: Pick one database for your interviews: a relational database like Postgres for product design, or a NoSQL database like DynamoDB for infrastructure design.
whenOtherWins: 以基础设施设计面试为主时，选 NoSQL（DynamoDB）更顺手，因为这类题更强调水平扩展和灵活模型。
tradeoff: 关系型（Postgres）vs NoSQL（DynamoDB）默认选型
options_en: A graph database (suited to relationship traversal)
A relational database, e.g. Postgres
An in-memory cache used directly as the primary store
A homegrown file storage system

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持 SQL、事务和丰富索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database with SQL, transactions, and rich indexing.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 NoSQL 数据库，支持键值/文档模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database from AWS supporting key-value and document models.

optionExplanations: 图数据库擅长处理节点和关系密集的查询，但这不是产品设计面试默认要解决的问题，没必要当默认库。
对，产品设计面试默认关系库最稳妥：事务、Join、索引这些能力覆盖大多数场景，基础设施面试再切到 NoSQL。
内存缓存适合加速读、不适合当主库：断电或重启容易丢数据，不满足持久化要求。
自己写一套文件存储系统是重新发明轮子，面试时间有限，不值得在这上面自证工程能力。
optionExplanations_en: A graph database shines at relationship-heavy traversal, but that isn't the default problem product-design interviews test, so it's not the safe default.
Right - a relational database is the safest default for product design: transactions, joins, and indexes cover most scenarios, switching to NoSQL for infra design.
An in-memory cache is for speeding up reads, not for being the primary store - it risks losing data on restart and lacks durability guarantees.
Building your own file storage system reinvents the wheel; interview time is too short to prove engineering skill by writing storage from scratch.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 在回答里主动插入一段「SQL vs NoSQL 大对比」，通常的后果是？
q_en: What usually happens if you volunteer a generic SQL vs NoSQL comparison?
options: 面试官会加分，因为显得知识全面
没有影响
面试必备环节，不讲会扣分
容易踩坑，暴露经验不足
why: 多数面试官并不需要这段对比，它是该完全绕开的坑。更好的做法是谈你选的库怎么解决眼前问题，比如「我用 Postgres，它的 ACID 特性能保证数据完整性」就是很好的开场。
why_en: Most interviewers do not want a generic SQL versus NoSQL comparison; talk instead about how your chosen database solves the problem at hand.
tradeoff: 主动讲 SQL vs NoSQL 对比 vs 直接讲你选的库怎么解决问题
options_en: The interviewer gives bonus points for showing broad knowledge
It has no effect either way
It's a required step and skipping it costs points
It's an easy pitfall that exposes inexperience

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于查询和操作关系型数据库的声明式语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language used to query and manipulate relational databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不用传统表结构、常无固定 schema 的一大类数据库统称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL refers to a broad family of databases that skip the traditional fixed table schema.

optionExplanations: 面试官很少会因为你多讲一段通用对比而加分，这段内容对回答眼前问题没有增量价值。
说这段话并非无害：占用宝贵时间去讲和当前设计无关的背景知识，会显得没有抓住重点。
面试并不要求你背这段对比，跳过它完全不会被扣分，该讲的是你选的库怎么解决问题。
对，主动讲这段通用对比容易被面试官视为经验不足的信号，更好的做法是直接说你选的库怎么解决眼前问题。
optionExplanations_en: Interviewers rarely give bonus points for a generic comparison; it adds no signal about how you're solving the actual problem.
It isn't harmless either - spending time on background unrelated to the current design makes you look unfocused.
There's no requirement to recite this comparison, and skipping it costs nothing; better to explain how your chosen database solves the problem.
Right - volunteering this generic comparison tends to read as inexperience; talk instead about how your chosen database solves the problem at hand.

q: 以下哪些说法是暴露经验不足的「黄旗」？（多选）
q_en: Which statements are yellow flags for lack of system design experience? (Select all that apply)
options: 「我的数据有关系，所以必须用关系型数据库」
「我需要规模和性能，所以必须用 NoSQL」
「NoSQL 也能很好地承载有关系的数据」
「用得得当的关系型数据库同样能出色地扩展」
why: 这两句都是黄旗：NoSQL 处理关系型数据可以很好，关系库用对了也能极好地扩展和高性能。两类技术高度重叠，绝对化的选型理由说明缺乏实战。
why_en: Claiming you must use relational for relationships or NoSQL for scale is a yellow flag because the two technologies overlap heavily.
options_en: "My data has relationships, so I must use a relational database"
"I need scale and performance, so I must use NoSQL"
NoSQL can also model relational data well
A relational database used correctly can also scale and perform excellently

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于查询和操作关系型数据库的声明式语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language used to query and manipulate relational databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不用传统表结构、常无固定 schema 的一大类数据库统称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL refers to a broad family of databases that skip the traditional fixed table schema.

optionExplanations: 对，这是黄旗：有关系的数据 NoSQL 也能处理好，把选型说成非此不可暴露的是经验不足。
对，这也是黄旗：关系库用对了同样能扩展和高性能，把规模当成必须上 NoSQL 的理由太绝对。
这句话是对的，承认 NoSQL 能处理关系数据反而说明理解到位，不是黄旗。
这句话也是对的，承认关系库用得当也能扩展说明你没有把两类技术对立起来，不是黄旗。
optionExplanations_en: Right - this is a yellow flag: NoSQL can model relational data well too, so framing relational as mandatory shows inexperience.
Right - also a yellow flag: a relational database used well can scale and perform too, so treating NoSQL as mandatory for scale is too absolute.
This statement is actually accurate - admitting NoSQL can model relational data well shows good judgment, not inexperience.
This statement is also accurate - admitting a relational database can scale well shows you aren't pitting the two technologies against each other.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 关系型数据库自带的、面试里最该记住的特性有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which built-in relational database features matter most in interviews? (Select all that apply)
options: SQL Join：跨表任意组合数据
索引：数量不限，支持多列索引和专用索引
内置的发布-订阅消息通道
事务：把多个操作打包成一个原子操作
why: 关系库的三大面试特性：任意 Join、丰富的索引（多列、地理空间、全文等专用索引）、事务（要么全成要么全败）。发布订阅不是关系库的内置卖点。
why_en: The key relational features are arbitrary SQL joins, unlimited and specialized indexes, and atomic transactions.
options_en: SQL Join: combine data across tables arbitrarily
Indexes: unlimited count, with multi-column and specialized indexes
A built-in publish-subscribe messaging channel
Transactions: bundle multiple operations into one atomic operation

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于查询和操作关系型数据库的声明式语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language used to query and manipulate relational databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务的四个保证：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID stands for atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability, the guarantees a transaction provides.

optionExplanations: 对，任意跨表 Join 是关系库的招牌能力，查某用户的所有帖子这类需求靠它一步到位。
对，关系库支持数量不限的索引，包括多列索引和地理空间、全文这类专用索引。
发布-订阅消息通道不是关系库自带的东西，这是消息队列/流平台的能力，别混进关系库特性里。
对，事务把多个操作打包成一个原子操作，要么全成要么全败，避免半途而废的脏数据。
optionExplanations_en: Right - arbitrary joins across tables are a relational hallmark, letting you fetch a user's posts in one query.
Right - relational databases support unlimited indexes, including multi-column and specialized ones like geospatial or full-text.
A built-in publish-subscribe channel isn't something relational databases ship with - that's a queue or streaming platform's job.
Right - transactions bundle multiple operations atomically, either all succeed or all fail, avoiding half-finished dirty data.

q: SQL Join 虽然强大，但在系统设计里要注意什么？
q_en: SQL joins are powerful, but what should you watch for in system design?
options: Join 可能成为主要性能瓶颈，能省则省
Join 只能在同一列类型间进行
Join 会自动创建索引
Join 不支持超过两张表
why: Join 是跨表组合数据的利器（比如查某用户的所有帖子），但它也可能是系统的主要性能瓶颈，设计时应尽量减少。
why_en: Joins are powerful for combining tables but can become a major performance bottleneck, so minimize them where possible.
options_en: Joins can become the main performance bottleneck, so minimize them
A join can only combine columns of the identical type
A join automatically creates an index
A join can't span more than two tables
optionExplanations: 对，Join 越多、表越大，查询就越可能变成系统的性能瓶颈，设计时应该尽量减少。
Join 并不要求两侧列类型完全相同，这个限制是编出来的误解。
Join 本身不会自动帮你建索引，没建索引的列做 Join 反而会很慢。
Join 可以一次串联两张以上的表，不存在只能两表的限制。
optionExplanations_en: Right - the more joins and the bigger the tables, the more likely a join becomes the system's performance bottleneck, so minimize them.
A join doesn't require both sides to be the identical column type; that constraint is a made-up limitation.
A join doesn't automatically build an index for you - joining unindexed columns is exactly what makes it slow.
A join can chain more than two tables together; there's no such two-table ceiling.

q: 补全关系型数据库索引的要点：
q_en: Fill in the key points about relational database indexes:
text: 索引通常用 {{B-Tree}} 或{{哈希表}}实现；关系库的优势是支持任意多个索引，还支持{{多列}}索引与专用索引（地理空间、全文）。
why: 索引让查询绕开全表扫描。关系库可以按不同查询建任意多个索引，多列索引和地理空间、全文等专用索引是它的加分项。
why_en: Indexes are typically B-trees or hash tables, and relational databases shine by supporting arbitrarily many indexes including multi-column and specialized ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种平衡树索引结构，让按范围/等值查询避免全表扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced tree index structure that avoids full table scans for lookups and range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 键到存储位置的映射结构，等值查询接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash table maps keys to storage locations for near constant-time equality lookups.

q: 「同时创建新用户和该用户的第一篇帖子」放进一个事务里，能保证什么？
q_en: If creating a new user and their first post runs in one transaction, what does it guarantee?
options: 两个操作一定都成功
帖子会先于用户创建
要么都成功、要么都失败
两个操作并行执行以提高速度
why: 事务把多个操作合成一个原子操作：要么全部成功、要么全部失败，从而避免「帖子挂在不存在的用户下」这类脏数据。
why_en: A transaction groups operations atomically so either both succeed or both fail, preventing invalid data like a post from a nonexistent user.
options_en: Both operations are guaranteed to succeed
The post is guaranteed to be created before the user
Either both succeed or both fail
The two operations run in parallel for speed

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务的四个保证：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID stands for atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability, the guarantees a transaction provides.

optionExplanations: 事务不保证两个操作都成功，它保证的是失败时两个操作一起回滚，而不是承诺都成功。
事务不规定执行的先后顺序，它只保证结果的原子性，不是谁先谁后。
对，事务保证要么两个操作都成功、要么都失败，避免出现帖子挂在不存在用户下的脏数据。
事务里的操作不是为了并行提速设计的，它们仍按顺序执行，只是失败时一起回滚。
optionExplanations_en: A transaction doesn't guarantee both operations succeed - it guarantees that if one fails, both roll back together, not that success is assured.
A transaction doesn't dictate execution order; it only guarantees atomicity of the outcome, not which operation runs first.
Right - a transaction guarantees either both operations succeed or both fail, preventing a post from being left under a nonexistent user.
Operations inside a transaction aren't run in parallel for speed; they still execute in order, just roll back together on failure.

q: NoSQL 数据库最常见的四种数据模型是？
q_en: What are the four common NoSQL data models?
options: 行式、列式、树形、堆
键值、文档、列族、图
关系表、视图、索引、触发器
队列、栈、集合、映射
why: NoSQL 是一大类数据库的统称，四种主流数据模型：键值存储、文档存储、列族存储、图数据库。它们通常无固定 schema、便于水平扩展。
why_en: The common NoSQL data models are key-value, document, column-family, and graph.
options_en: Row store, column store, tree, heap
Key-value, document, column-family, graph
Table, view, index, trigger
Queue, stack, set, map
optionExplanations: 行式、列式、树形、堆是数据存储的物理组织方式，不是 NoSQL 惯用的四类数据模型划分。
对，NoSQL 的四种主流数据模型是键值、文档、列族、图，各自适合不同的访问模式。
关系表、视图、索引、触发器是关系型数据库的概念，不是 NoSQL 数据模型的分类。
队列、栈、集合、映射是编程语言里的数据结构，不是数据库层面的数据模型划分。
optionExplanations_en: Row store, column store, tree, and heap describe physical storage layouts, not the usual NoSQL data-model taxonomy.
Right - the four common NoSQL data models are key-value, document, column-family, and graph, each suited to a different access pattern.
Table, view, index, and trigger are relational database concepts, not the NoSQL model taxonomy.
Queue, stack, set, and map are in-memory programming data structures, not a database-level data model classification.

q: 强一致与最终一致的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between strong consistency and eventual consistency?
options: 强一致只在单机可用，最终一致只在集群可用
两者等价，只是叫法不同
强一致允许短暂不一致，最终一致不允许
强一致=同一时刻数据相同；最终一致=最终收敛
why: NoSQL 提供从强到最终的一系列一致性模型：强一致保证所有节点同一时刻数据相同；最终一致只保证「最终」收敛，中间可能读到旧值。
why_en: Strong consistency means every node sees the same data at the same time, while eventual consistency only guarantees nodes converge eventually.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Write["Write"] --> Strong["Strong: all nodes see it now"]
    Write --> Eventual["Eventual: replicas converge later"]
tradeoff: 强一致（同一时刻一致）vs 最终一致（延迟收敛换可用性/吞吐）
options_en: Strong consistency only works on a single machine, eventual only in a cluster
They are equivalent, just different names
Strong consistency allows brief inconsistency, eventual does not
Strong = every node sees the same data at once; eventual = nodes converge over time

termDefinitions.meaning: 不用传统表结构、常无固定 schema 的一大类数据库统称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL refers to a broad family of databases that skip the traditional fixed table schema.

optionExplanations: 强一致和最终一致都可以在单机或集群里实现，两者的区别不在于部署形态，而在于读到的数据新鲜度。
两者绝不是同一回事换了个名字：强一致要求所有节点同一时刻看到相同数据，最终一致允许短暂滞后。
这句话把两个模型的容忍度说反了：允许短暂不一致的其实是最终一致，不是强一致。
对，两者的定义边界就在「什么时候看到一致结果」：一份写入后所有节点立刻同步可见，跟允许延迟后再趋同，是两种不同的承诺。
optionExplanations_en: Both models can run on a single machine or a cluster; the difference isn't deployment topology, it's how fresh the data you read is.
They are not the same idea under different names: strong consistency means every node sees identical data at once, eventual allows brief lag.
This gets the tolerance backwards - it's eventual consistency that allows brief inconsistency, not strong consistency.
Right - strong consistency means every node sees the same data at the same time, while eventual consistency only promises convergence over time, with stale reads possible in between.

q: 补全 NoSQL 的扩展机制：
q_en: Fill in the NoSQL scaling mechanisms:
text: NoSQL 数据库靠{{一致性哈希}}和/或{{分片}}把数据分布到多台服务器上，实现水平扩展。
why: 水平扩展是 NoSQL 的核心卖点之一：一致性哈希让节点增减时数据迁移量最小，分片把数据切分到多台机器。
why_en: NoSQL databases scale horizontally by distributing data across servers with consistent hashing and sharding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种哈希方案，节点增减时只需迁移少量数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing is a hashing scheme that minimizes data movement when nodes are added or removed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分到多台服务器，靠分片键决定归属。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple servers based on a shard key.

scenario: 你在设计一个写入量很大的事件/日志型系统：数据主要追加写入，偶尔按 key 或时间范围读取，不需要复杂 join，也可以接受按业务选择一致性等级。
scenario_en: You are designing a write-heavy event or log system: data is mostly appended, reads are occasional by key or time range, complex joins are unnecessary, and consistency can be chosen by business need.
q: 在这个写多读少的 NoSQL 场景里，为什么 Cassandra 比 MongoDB、Redis、Neo4j 更直接？
q_en: In this write-heavy NoSQL scenario, why is Cassandra a better fit than MongoDB, Redis, or Neo4j?
options: Cassandra——去中心化，追加写扛高吞吐
MongoDB——文档模型灵活多变
Redis——内存存储，读写延迟低
Neo4j——图遍历能力强，擅长路径查询
why: Cassandra 的强项是把大量写入水平分散到多节点，用追加写/LSM 风格存储承接高吞吐。MongoDB 偏文档灵活，Redis 偏低延迟内存态，Neo4j 偏图遍历，都不是这个写密集场景的第一反应。
why_en: Cassandra is the most direct fit because the workload is write-heavy, append-oriented, and partitionable, while MongoDB, Redis, and Neo4j optimize for different primary access patterns.
whenOtherWins: 灵活文档选 MongoDB；低延迟内存态选 Redis；图遍历选 Neo4j。

termDefinitions.meaning: 新数据主要追加到日志或新行里，而不是频繁原地更新旧记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: New data is mostly appended rather than repeatedly updating existing records in place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来决定一条数据落到哪个分片/节点的 key；它直接影响扩展性和热点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The key used to place data on shards or nodes; it controls scalability and hot spots.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  W["many writes"] --> P{"partition key"}
  P --> N1[("node A")]
  P --> N2[("node B")]
  P --> N3[("node C")]
  N1 --> R["query by access pattern"]
  N2 --> R
  N3 --> R
tradeoff: 按访问模式选型：写密集追加写（Cassandra）vs 文档灵活性（MongoDB）vs 内存低延迟（Redis）vs 图遍历（Neo4j）
options_en: Cassandra - decentralized, append-heavy writes handle high throughput
MongoDB - a flexible, adaptable document model
Redis - in-memory storage with low read/write latency
Neo4j - strong graph traversal, good at path queries
optionExplanations: 对，Cassandra 是去中心化的宽列存储，靠分区键把写入水平打散到多节点，天然匹配追加写为主的高吞吐场景。
MongoDB 的文档模型确实灵活，但灵活字段不是这里的痛点，它没有直接回答高吞吐追加写要怎么水平分散。
Redis 常驻内存、延迟最低，但把海量持续写入的数据长期放进内存态系统会把存储成本和容量都推向不合理的方向。
Neo4j 为节点、边和路径查询做了优化，而这里的负载是追加写和按 key/时间读，用不上图遍历的强项。
optionExplanations_en: Right - Cassandra is a decentralized wide-column store that spreads writes across nodes by partition key, a natural fit for append-heavy high-throughput workloads.
MongoDB's document model is genuinely flexible, but flexible fields aren't the bottleneck here - it doesn't directly solve how to spread high-throughput appends across nodes.
Redis is fast because it lives in memory, but keeping a continuous flood of durable writes in a memory-first system pushes cost and capacity in the wrong direction.
Neo4j is optimized for node, edge, and path queries, but this workload is append-heavy writes with key/time reads, which never touches graph traversal's strength.

numberAnchors.risk: shard key 选错导致 scatter query

scenario: 设计一个视频/图片产品：用户上传的是几 MB 到几 GB 的大文件；页面加载时还要按标题、作者、权限、时间排序等元数据快速查询。
scenario_en: You are designing a video or image product: users upload files from a few MB to a few GB, while pages still need fast metadata queries by title, author, permissions, and time.
q: 大文件本体和可查询元数据应该怎样拆分存储？
q_en: How should you split large file bodies from searchable metadata?
options: 视频和元数据都放 Postgres
视频和元数据都放 S3
视频放 Blob 存储，元数据放数据库存指针
视频放 Redis，元数据放 S3
why: 要学的不是"S3 这个名字"，而是职责拆分：对象存储负责便宜可靠地保存大二进制；数据库负责索引、过滤、权限和低延迟点查，库里只存指针。
why_en: The design principle is to split responsibilities: blob storage holds large binary objects cheaply and durably, while the database stores searchable metadata and pointers.
whenOtherWins: 数据是小而结构化的记录时直接进数据库即可，没必要引入 Blob 存储这一层。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    File["Large file"] --> Blob["S3 / Blob store"]
    Meta["Metadata"] --> DB["Database"]
    DB --> Ptr["URL pointer"]
    Ptr --> Blob

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向大块非结构化文件的存储，比如图片、视频、备份文件；通常通过 object key 读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Storage for large unstructured objects such as images, videos, and backups, usually addressed by object key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述文件的结构化信息，如作者、标题、权限、状态、URL、创建时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Structured information describing the file, such as owner, title, permissions, status, URL, and creation time.

tradeoff: 大文件走 Blob 存储 vs 可查询字段走数据库——两者各管一半
options_en: Store both video and metadata in Postgres
Store both video and metadata in S3
Video in blob storage, metadata plus a pointer in the database
Store video in Redis, metadata in S3
optionExplanations: 把视频和元数据都塞进 Postgres 意味着大二进制文件会拖慢查询库，备份和复制成本也会跟着暴涨。
把两者都放 S3 能存下文件，但按作者、权限、状态、时间做检索会变得很别扭，S3 不是为这类查询设计的。
对，职责拆分才对：大文件交给 Blob 存储负责便宜可靠地保存，数据库只存指针和可查询的元数据字段。
把角色反过来放——大文件进 Redis、元数据进 S3——会让热缓存和持久存储的边界完全乱套，系统又贵又难查。
optionExplanations_en: Putting both video and metadata in Postgres means large binary blobs bloat the query database and drive up backup and replication cost.
Storing both in S3 can hold the files, but querying by author, permission, status, or time becomes awkward - S3 isn't built for that kind of lookup.
Right - split responsibilities: blob storage cheaply and durably holds the file, while the database stores only the pointer and searchable metadata fields.
Reversing the roles - video in Redis, metadata in S3 - blurs the line between hot caching and durable storage, leaving a system that's both expensive and hard to query.

q: 为什么 S3 这类 Blob 存储不适合作为业务主数据库？
q_en: Why is S3-style blob storage a poor fit as the primary business database?
options: S3 的存储成本太高
Blob 存储不擅长低延迟查询和索引
S3 不支持超过 1GB 的文件
Blob 存储没有持久性保证
why: S3 的优势是持久、便宜、适合大对象，不是低延迟复杂查询。业务主库要维护索引、权限、状态、分页和一致的元数据更新；对象存储通常只保存大文件本体，数据库保存 object key 和可查询字段。
why_en: Blob storage is excellent for durable large objects, but the business database still needs to handle indexes, permissions, state, pagination, and metadata updates.
scenario: 你已经把图片/视频文件放进 S3，但产品还需要“按用户列出文件、按状态筛选、按时间排序、校验权限、分页返回”。有人提议直接把 S3 当主数据库用。
scenario_en: Images and videos are already stored in S3, but the product must list by user, filter by status, sort by time, check permissions, and paginate. Someone suggests using S3 as the primary database.
tradeoff: 对象存储管大文件本体 vs 数据库管索引/权限/分页查询
options_en: S3's storage cost is too high
Blob storage is not built for low-latency queries and indexing
S3 doesn't support files over 1GB
Blob storage has no durability guarantee
optionExplanations: 把问题归结成价格掩盖了真正的短板：就算存储便宜，按用户、权限、状态查询的需求依然没被解决。
对，Blob 存储的强项是便宜持久地存大对象，不是低延迟索引查询；按用户/权限/状态/分页这类查询该交给数据库。
S3 并没有 1GB 这样的文件大小硬限制，用对象大小当理由说不通这里的查询问题。
这低估了 S3：复制加纠删码正是它持久性的卖点，耐久性从来不是这里要解决的短板。
optionExplanations_en: Framing this as a price problem hides the real gap - even if storage is cheap, user, permission, and status queries remain unsolved.
Right - blob storage is built for storing large objects cheaply and durably, not low-latency indexed queries; queries by user, permission, status, and page belong in the database.
S3 has no such 1GB file-size ceiling, so object size isn't a real reason for the query problem described here.
This underrates S3: replication plus erasure coding is exactly its durability pitch, so durability was never the actual weakness.

q: 把「客户端经预签名 URL 上传大文件」的流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the presigned-URL large-file upload flow in the correct order:
steps: 客户端把文件直接上传到预签名 URL
客户端向服务器请求一个上传用的预签名 URL
Blob 存储回调通知服务器上传完成，服务器把状态更新为已完成
服务器返回预签名 URL 给客户端，并在数据库记下这条记录
why: 标准四步：请求预签名 URL → 服务器发 URL 并落库 → 客户端绕过服务器直传 Blob 存储 → 存储回调通知、更新状态。文件本体不过应用服务器，省带宽。
why_en: The client requests a presigned URL, the server returns it and records it, the client uploads directly to blob storage, and a completion notification updates the status.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant S as 服务器
    participant B as Blob存储(S3)
    C->>S: 1. 请求预签名 URL
    S->>S: 2. 落库并返回 URL
    C->>B: 3. 直接上传文件
    B->>S: 4. 上传完成通知
    S->>S: 5. 更新状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器签发的临时授权链接，客户端可直接用它上传/下载大文件，不经过应用服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a temporary signed link that lets a client upload or download directly without routing through the app server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向大块非结构化文件的存储服务，通过 object key 读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage holds large unstructured files and is addressed by object key.

q: 预签名 URL 架构下，客户端下载大文件的标准路径是？
q_en: With a presigned-URL architecture, what is the standard path for downloading a large file?
options: 向服务器要预签名 URL，经 CDN 下载
服务器把文件读进内存再转发给客户端
客户端直连数据库读取文件二进制
必须先把文件复制回应用服务器磁盘
why: 下载时客户端向服务器请求文件，拿到预签名 URL，然后经 CDN 下载；CDN 未命中时代理请求到底层 Blob 存储。文件流量同样不经过应用服务器。
why_en: The client asks the server for a presigned URL and downloads through the CDN, which proxies to the underlying blob storage.
options_en: Ask the server for a presigned URL, then download via the CDN
The server reads the file into memory and forwards it to the client
The client connects directly to the database to read the file bytes
The file must first be copied back onto the application server disk

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器签发的临时授权链接，客户端可直接用它上传/下载大文件，不经过应用服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a temporary signed link that lets a client upload or download directly without routing through the app server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a content delivery network that caches content on edge servers near users.

codeSample:
# 客户端向服务器要下载地址，再走 CDN
GET /files/video123/download-url -> { url: "https://cdn.example.com/v123?sig=..." }
GET https://cdn.example.com/v123?sig=...
# CDN 命中直接返回；未命中则回源到 Blob 存储再缓存
optionExplanations: 对，下载走的是预签名 URL 加 CDN：服务器发个签名链接，客户端直接从 CDN 拿文件，未命中再回源到 Blob 存储。
让服务器把文件读进内存再转发，等于把大文件流量重新塞回应用服务器，白白浪费了直传架构省下来的带宽。
数据库里存的是元数据和指针，不是文件二进制，客户端直连数据库读不出文件内容。
文件已经在 Blob 存储里了，没有必要先复制回应用服务器磁盘再转发，这一步纯属多余。
optionExplanations_en: Right - downloads go through a presigned URL plus CDN: the server hands back a signed link, the client pulls straight from the CDN, and a miss falls back to blob storage.
Having the server read the file into memory and forward it pushes large-file traffic back through the app server, undoing the bandwidth savings direct upload was meant to buy.
The database only holds metadata and pointers, not file bytes, so connecting to it directly can't return the file content.
The file already lives in blob storage, so copying it back to the app server's disk first is a pointless extra hop.

q: 按公开定价量级对比：S3 Standard 约 $0.023/GB/月，DynamoDB Standard 表存储约多少？
q_en: If S3 Standard is about $0.023 per GB-month, roughly how much is DynamoDB Standard table storage?
options: $0.01/GB/月，比 S3 便宜
$0.023/GB/月，和 S3 一样
$0.25/GB/月——比对象存储贵约 10 倍
why: DynamoDB 表存储约 $0.25/GB/月，比 S3 的 $0.023 贵约 10 倍——这是「大文件进 Blob、库里只存指针」的成本依据，不是要背的精确数字。
why_en: DynamoDB Standard table storage is about $0.25/GB-month, roughly 10x the S3 price of $0.023, which is the cost argument for keeping large blobs out of the database.
