optionExplanations_en: This statement swaps which one is synchronous and which is asynchronous.
Right — synchronous invalidation updates or deletes cache entries inline for consistency but slows writes; asynchronous queues the event, faster but leaving a stale window.
Whether the write path waits for invalidation to finish directly affects write latency — saying neither is affected isn't accurate.
Write-behind is exactly the asynchronous, queued approach, trading consistency for write speed, not gaining it.

scenario: 缓存里有大量与「用户 123 的帖子」相关的条目（列表页、详情页、聚合页），一次帖子改动要让它们全部失效。
scenario_en: The cache has many entries related to user 123's posts, including list pages, detail pages, and aggregate pages; one post update must invalidate all of them.
q: 最合适的失效策略是？
q_en: Which invalidation strategy fits best?
options: 标签失效：按标签一键失效所有关联条目
逐个记住所有 key 再一一删除
把这些条目的 TTL 都设成 1 秒
干脆不缓存这些数据
why: 标签失效专治「一份数据牵连多个缓存条目」的复杂依赖（如给相关条目挂 user:123:posts 标签），代价是要维护标签与条目的关系。
why_en: Tagged invalidation associates entries with tags so one change can invalidate every related entry, at the cost of maintaining tag relationships.
whenOtherWins: 若只是单实体缓存（一条记录一个 key），版本化 key 更简单，不用维护标签关系。
options_en: Tagged invalidation: tag related entries and invalidate them all at once by tag.
Remember every key individually and delete them one by one.
Set all these entries' TTL to one second.
Just stop caching this data.
optionExplanations: 对，给相关条目挂同一个标签，一次失效就能清掉所有关联缓存，不用逐个记 key。
逐个记住并删除每个 key 在条目数量增长后会迅速变得难以维护。
把 TTL 压到 1 秒等于放弃缓存的收益，用极端妥协换取"看起来新鲜"。
不缓存意味着列表页、详情页、聚合页全部退回到每次现查，读压力直接打回数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Right — tag related entries once, and a single tag-based invalidation clears everything linked to it without tracking keys individually.
Manually tracking and deleting every key becomes unmanageable as the number of related entries grows.
Dropping TTL to one second gives up most of the caching benefit, trading it for the illusion of freshness.
Not caching means list pages, detail pages, and aggregate pages all fall back to live queries, dumping load straight onto the database.

q: 「版本化 key (versioned keys)」失效策略的机制是？
q_en: How do versioned cache keys work?
options: 定期把整个缓存全量清空一遍，简单粗暴
给每一个 key 单独加上一把分布式锁
把同一份数据写两份，互相当作备份
版本号编进 key；更新递增，旧 key 失效
why: 版本化不删除旧缓存，而是换 key 让旧条目变得不可达——简单可靠，但需要跟踪版本号。
why_en: Versioned keys include a version number in the cache key and increment it on update, so old entries become unreachable instead of being deleted.
options_en: Periodically flush the entire cache wholesale, simple and blunt.
Add a separate distributed lock to every single key.
Write the same data twice so each copy backs up the other.
Bake a version number into the cache key; bumping it on update leaves the old key unreachable.
optionExplanations: 定期全量清空是个粗暴的兜底手段，跟"给 key 编版本号"这个精确机制不是一回事。
给每个 key 加锁解决的是并发写冲突，跟让旧缓存条目不可达没有关系。
写两份互为备份是容灾手段，不是让旧版本数据自然失效的方式。
对，版本号编进 key，更新时递增，旧 key 因为没人再拼出它而自然失效。
optionExplanations_en: A periodic full flush is a blunt fallback, not the same precise mechanism as tagging keys with a version number.
Adding a lock per key addresses concurrent write conflicts, not making old cache entries unreachable.
Writing two backup copies is a redundancy tactic, not a way to let old versions naturally lapse.
Right — bake a version number into the key and bump it on update, so nobody constructs the old key anymore and it goes stale on its own.

scenario: 生产系统要定失效方案：既有用户资料、库存这类关键数据，也有推荐分数这类次要数据。
scenario_en: You need a production invalidation plan for both critical data like profiles and inventory and secondary data like recommendation scores.
q: 工程上最常见的组合是？
q_en: What combination is most common in production?
options: 全部只靠长 TTL
全部用写时失效、不设任何 TTL
短 TTL 兜底，关键数据主动失效
所有数据都不缓存
why: 多数生产系统组合使用：TTL 兜底保证最终会刷新，主动失效保证关键数据及时更新。
why_en: Production systems combine short TTLs of five to fifteen minutes as a safety net with active invalidation for critical data.
whenOtherWins: 若全部数据的陈旧容忍都宽松且一致，只靠 TTL 是最简单的方案。
options_en: Use only long TTLs everywhere.
Use write-time invalidation everywhere with no TTL at all.
Short TTL as a safety net, with active invalidation layered on top for critical data.
Don't cache any data at all.
tradeoff: 简单统一 vs 按数据分层保护
optionExplanations: 只靠长 TTL 对用户资料、库存这类关键数据的陈旧窗口太大，兜不住实时性要求。
全部写时失效意味着每次写都要触碰缓存层，对次要数据这个成本没必要。
对，短 TTL 兜底保证最终刷新，关键数据再叠加主动失效，两者分层保护。
完全不缓存等于放弃缓存带来的全部收益，用极端方式规避一致性问题。
optionExplanations_en: Relying only on a long TTL leaves too wide a staleness window for critical data like profiles and inventory.
Write-time invalidation everywhere means every write touches the cache layer — unnecessary cost for secondary data.
Right — a short TTL as a safety net covers eventual freshness, with active invalidation layered on for critical data.
Not caching at all throws away every benefit of caching just to sidestep the consistency question.

scenario: 需求文档写明：搜索结果的陈旧不得超过 30 秒，用户资料可容忍 5 分钟陈旧。
scenario_en: The requirements say search results may be stale for at most 30 seconds, while user profiles may be stale for 5 minutes.
q: 缓存 TTL 应该怎么定？
q_en: How should you choose cache TTLs?
options: 由陈旧性需求驱动：搜索 30 秒、资料 5 分钟
统一设成 1 小时，图个省事不用多想
全部设成 1 秒，反正越短肯定越好
随便挑一个数字设上，出问题以后再调整
why: 理想的 TTL 由非功能需求的 staleness 上限直接给出：这让一致性保证有界，缓存决策不用拍脑袋。
why_en: Drive TTLs from your staleness requirements, so a thirty-second staleness budget means exactly a thirty-second TTL.
whenOtherWins: 若需求是「写后立即可见」，多短的 TTL 都不够，要改用主动失效或版本化 key。
options_en: Drive it directly from staleness requirements: 30 seconds for search, 5 minutes for profiles.
Set one hour everywhere, simplest thing to not think about it.
Set one second everywhere, since shorter always has to be better.
Pick a number at random and just fix it later if something breaks.
tradeoff: 一致性保证 vs 缓存收益
optionExplanations: 对，30 秒和 5 分钟直接对应各自的陈旧容忍上限，TTL 就该照这个设。
统一 1 小时会让搜索结果的陈旧远超 30 秒的要求，违反了给定约束。
全设 1 秒会让缓存命中率暴跌，等于交了缓存的税却没拿到缓存的好处。
拍脑袋定 TTL 意味着一致性保证是不确定的，出问题时说不清是哪里错了。
optionExplanations_en: Right — 30 seconds and 5 minutes map directly to each item's staleness budget, so set TTLs from that.
A blanket 1-hour TTL would leave search results stale far past the required 30 seconds, violating the given constraint.
Setting everything to one second would tank the hit rate — paying caching's overhead without getting its benefit.
Picking TTLs arbitrarily means the consistency guarantee is undefined, so failures are hard to trace back to a cause.

q: 关于现代 CDN 的能力，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about modern CDNs is correct?
options: 只能缓存静态文件，不支持任何动态数据
必须自建全球边缘机房才能用
缓存内容不能设置过期时间
除静态资源外，也能缓存动态内容
why: CDN 起家于静态资源，但现代 CDN 也缓存动态内容，把缓存从你的机房延伸到全球边缘节点。
why_en: Modern CDNs cache dynamic content such as API responses and query results, not just static assets.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["User"] --> E["Nearest CDN edge"]
    E -->|hit| U
    E -->|miss| O["Origin / API"]
    O --> E
options_en: It can only cache static files and never handles dynamic data.
It requires building your own global edge data centers.
Cached content can never have an expiration set.
Beyond static assets, modern CDNs also cache dynamic content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers located near users.

optionExplanations: 现代 CDN 早已能缓存 API 响应、查询结果这类动态内容，不止静态文件。
主流 CDN 服务本身就提供全球边缘网络，不需要自建机房才能用。
缓存内容设置过期时间（如 Cache-Control）正是 CDN 控制新鲜度的常规手段。
对，现代 CDN 除了静态资源，也能缓存 API 响应等动态内容。
optionExplanations_en: Modern CDNs can already cache dynamic content like API responses and query results, not just static files.
Mainstream CDN providers already run a global edge network for you — no need to build your own data centers.
Setting an expiration via headers like Cache-Control is exactly how CDNs normally control freshness.
Right — beyond static assets, modern CDNs also cache dynamic content such as API responses.

q: 东京用户访问弗吉尼亚源站 vs 就近的东京边缘节点，延迟量级变化是？
q_en: What latency change do you expect from a Virginia origin to a Tokyo edge node?
options: 约 200ms 降到 10ms 以内
没有变化
从 1 秒降到 500ms
从 10ms 升到 200ms
why: 地理分布是 CDN 的核心价值：跨洲往返约 200ms，就近边缘 10ms 以内，且命中的请求完全不打源站。
why_en: Edge caching cuts response times from around two hundred milliseconds cross-continent to under ten milliseconds locally.
scenario: 服务部署在美国弗吉尼亚，东京用户抱怨页面慢，你在评估是否要上 CDN 边缘节点。
scenario_en: The service is hosted in Virginia and Tokyo users complain about slow pages; you are evaluating CDN edge nodes.
options_en: From about 200 milliseconds down to under 10 milliseconds.
No change at all.
From 1 second down to 500 milliseconds.
From 10 milliseconds up to 200 milliseconds.
optionExplanations: 对，跨洲往返约 200ms，换到就近的东京边缘节点能压到 10ms 以内，命中的请求完全不打源站。
地理距离直接决定网络往返时间，从弗吉尼亚到东京不可能毫无变化。
1 秒和 500ms 都远高于实际跨洲往返延迟的量级，估得太夸张。
这个方向反了——边缘节点离用户更近，延迟应该是降而不是升。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a cross-continent round trip is roughly 200 milliseconds, and a local Tokyo edge node brings that under 10 milliseconds.
Geographic distance directly drives round-trip time; going from Virginia to Tokyo can't leave latency unchanged.
Both 1 second and 500 milliseconds are far above the real magnitude of a cross-continent round trip — overestimated.
This has it backwards — an edge node is physically closer to the user, so latency should drop, not climb.

q: 读密集应用配好 CDN 缓存后，源站负载大致能降多少？
q_en: Roughly how much can a well-configured CDN reduce origin load in a read-heavy app?
options: 90% 或更多
基本不变
正好一半
why: 商品页、公开资料、搜索结果这类多人共读的内容都能边缘化，命中的请求完全不到源站，降 90%+ 很常见。
why_en: For read-heavy applications CDN caching can offload ninety percent or more of origin traffic.
scenario: 读密集应用给公开内容加上 CDN 边缘缓存后，你要向团队量化能省下多少源站压力。
scenario_en: After adding CDN edge caching for public content in a read-heavy app, you need to quantify the origin-load reduction.
options_en: About 10%.
90% or more.
Essentially unchanged.
Exactly half.
optionExplanations: 10% 低估了共享型公开内容能被边缘化命中的比例，实际收益比这大得多。
对，商品页、公开资料这类多人共读内容命中缓存后完全不打源站，降 90%+ 很常见。
配好 CDN 后源站流量基本不变说明缓存根本没生效，跟题设矛盾。
读密集内容的命中率通常远高于 50%，"正好一半"低估了 CDN 的效果。
optionExplanations_en: 10% understates how much shared, publicly-read content gets offloaded to the edge — the real gain runs much higher.
Right — shared content like product pages and public profiles never touches the origin on a cache hit, so 90%+ reduction is common.
Origin traffic staying essentially unchanged would mean the CDN isn't actually caching anything — contradicts the premise.
Read-heavy content typically sees a hit rate well above 50%; 'exactly half' undersells what a CDN delivers.

scenario: 决定哪些内容进 CDN：候选有公开帖子、商品目录、搜索结果、用户私信、个人偏好设置。
scenario_en: You are deciding what should go into the CDN: public posts, product catalogs, search results, private messages, and personal settings.
q: 正确的取舍是？
q_en: What is the right CDN caching tradeoff?
options: 全部进 CDN，越多越好
只缓存私信，因为它最敏感
全都不进 CDN
公开内容进 CDN，私有数据不进
why: CDN 只对「多用户共读」的内容有意义；私信、个人设置这类单用户数据只有本人访问，放 CDN 没有命中率收益。
why_en: CDNs only make sense for content many users share, so cache public posts and catalogs but never user-specific data that only one person requests.
whenOtherWins: 单用户数据要提速应放应用层缓存或客户端缓存，而不是共享型的 CDN。
options_en: Put everything in the CDN, the more the better.
Only cache private messages since they're the most sensitive.
Don't use a CDN for anything.
Cache public posts, catalogs, and search results; skip single-user data like DMs and settings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 靠近用户的 CDN 节点，命中时直接返回内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge server is a CDN node near users that returns cached content directly.

optionExplanations: 把私信、个人设置这些只被一位用户访问的数据也塞进 CDN，命中率极低，白白浪费边缘容量。
私信恰恰是最不该进 CDN 的数据——它只被一个人访问，不存在多用户共读的收益。
完全不用 CDN 等于放弃公开内容能带来的巨大命中率和延迟收益。
对，把帖子、商品目录这类会被很多人重复访问的内容放进 CDN，只有本人会看的数据留在应用层就好。
optionExplanations_en: Stuffing data only one user ever sees, like DMs or settings, into the CDN gets near-zero hit rate — wasted edge capacity.
Private messages are exactly the wrong candidate — only one person reads them, so there's no shared-read benefit.
Skipping the CDN entirely throws away the huge hit-rate and latency win available for public content.
Right — put content many people repeatedly read, like posts and catalogs, in the CDN, and leave anything only one person ever sees at the application layer.

scenario: 面试进入扩展性讨论环节，你的系统是读密集型。
scenario_en: The interview has moved into scalability, and your system is read-heavy.
q: 最加分的切入方式是？
q_en: What is the strongest way to start the scalability discussion?
options: 直接宣布「加 Redis 和 CDN」
主动指出读瓶颈，按查询优化到缓存副本展开
等面试官点名再讨论
先谈微服务拆分
why: 强候选人主动识别读瓶颈：画 API 时就在会被打爆的端点停下来量化问题（如「资料页每天数十亿读」），然后按查询优化 → 缓存/副本的顺序展开。
why_en: Strong candidates proactively flag high-volume endpoints, quantify the read load, and then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
whenOtherWins: 若系统是写密集（如 Uber 位置上报），应先谈写扩展而不是读扩展。
options_en: Just announce 'add Redis and a CDN'.
Proactively call out read bottlenecks at high-traffic endpoints, then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
Wait for the interviewer to bring it up.
Start by talking about microservice decomposition.
optionExplanations: 直接宣布方案却没有先量化瓶颈，会让面试官看不到你判断问题的过程。
对，画到高流量端点时主动停下量化问题，再按查询优化到缓存/副本的顺序展开。
被动等面试官点名会显得你没有主动发现问题的习惯，这是候选人该主动做的事。
系统是读密集型时先讲微服务拆分是跑题，没有先处理眼下真正的瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Announcing a solution without first quantifying the bottleneck leaves the interviewer unable to see your reasoning process.
Right — pause at the high-traffic endpoint to quantify it, then work through query optimization before caching and replicas.
Waiting passively for the interviewer to raise it signals you don't proactively spot problems — that's on the candidate to drive.
Leading with microservice decomposition on a read-heavy system is off-topic when the actual bottleneck hasn't been addressed yet.

scenario: 设计 Bitly：一条短链创建一次却可能被点击数百万次，长短链映射一旦生成从不改变。
scenario_en: Designing Bitly: a short link is created once, may be clicked millions of times, and the long-to-short mapping never changes.
q: 缓存策略应该是？
q_en: What caching strategy fits Bitly?
options: 设一个很短的 TTL，让它频繁刷新保持新鲜
干脆不缓存，用不缓存的方式防止数据陈旧
Redis 激进缓存不过期，配 CDN 扛流量
只把热门链接缓存 1 分钟，冷门链接不管
why: 极端读写比 + 不可变数据 = 缓存梦想场景：不设过期也不会陈旧，命中率极高。
why_en: Bitly is a caching dream because the mapping never changes, so cache it aggressively with no expiration and let the CDN absorb global traffic.
whenOtherWins: 只要数据可能变（比如允许修改目标地址），「永不过期」就不成立，必须引入失效机制。
options_en: Set a very short TTL and refresh it frequently to stay fresh.
Don't cache at all, so staleness simply can't happen.
Cache the mapping aggressively in Redis with no expiration, backed by a CDN for global traffic.
Only cache popular links for one minute and leave the rest uncached.
tradeoff: 激进缓存命中率 vs 数据不可变前提
optionExplanations: 设一个很短的 TTL 让它频繁刷新，映射从不改变，白白丢弃缓存收益。
不缓存会让每次点击都直接打数据库，白白浪费了这份数据天生的缓存友好性。
对，映射不可变，Redis 可以激进缓存不设过期，CDN 再兜住全球流量。
只缓存 1 分钟等于人为制造陈旧风险，而这份数据其实从不会陈旧。
optionExplanations_en: Set a very short TTL and refresh it frequently — the mapping never changes, so this just throws away caching benefit.
Not caching sends every click straight to the database, wasting data that's naturally perfect for caching.
Right — the mapping is immutable, so cache it aggressively in Redis with no expiration, backed by a CDN for global traffic.
Capping it at one minute manufactures staleness risk for data that, in reality, never goes stale.

scenario: 设计 Ticketmaster：开票瞬间几千人狂刷同一活动页；页面包含活动详情、场馆信息、座位图，也包含实时座位余量。
scenario_en: Designing Ticketmaster: at sale time thousands of users refresh the same event page; it includes event details, venue info, seat maps, and live seat availability.
q: 正确的缓存边界是？
q_en: Where should the caching boundary be?
options: 稳定内容激进缓存，余量近似，购买查权威库存
把整个页面不分内容全部缓存 10 分钟，图省事
什么都不缓存，靠这个办法保证绝对正确
把座位余量也一起缓存 60 秒，跟其他内容一视同仁
why: 关键是划清「可缓存内容」和「必须强一致的库存路径」：活动详情、场馆、座位图可激进缓存，余量只做短 TTL 近似展示。购买路径必须查权威库存，用锁或事务原子预留。
why_en: Cache stable event details aggressively; seat availability can be approximate for display, but checkout must read authoritative inventory and reserve atomically.
whenOtherWins: 若展示允许近似余量（如「少量余票」标签），可短缓存近似值，但下单扣减路径必须强一致。
options_en: Cache stable content like event and venue details aggressively; keep seat counts approximate, and read authoritative inventory at checkout.
Cache the entire page indiscriminately for 10 minutes, the simple way out.
Cache nothing at all across the board, relying on that alone for correctness.
Cache seat availability too for 60 seconds, treating it just like everything else.
tradeoff: 缓存吞吐 vs 库存强一致性
optionExplanations: 对，活动详情、场馆、座位图激进缓存，余量只做近似展示，购买时查权威库存并原子预留。
整页缓存 10 分钟会让座位余量长时间不准，购买路径也可能读到过期库存。
完全不缓存会让开票瞬间的巨大读压力直接打向数据库，正确性没问题但撑不住流量。
座位余量缓存 60 秒对购买决策仍然太陈旧，超卖风险没有真正被消除。
optionExplanations_en: Right — cache event, venue, and seat-map details aggressively, keep availability approximate, and route checkout through authoritative inventory with an atomic reservation.
Caching the whole page for 10 minutes leaves seat availability stale for a long stretch, and checkout could read outdated inventory too.
Caching nothing keeps correctness but sends the sale-moment read spike straight at the database, which won't hold up.
Even a 60-second cache on seat availability is too stale for a purchase decision — the overselling risk isn't actually gone.

scenario: 设计 Facebook 信息流：读极其密集，用户通常只看头几条。
scenario_en: Designing a Facebook feed: reads are extremely heavy, and users usually only look at the first few items.
q: 读扩展的关键手法是？
q_en: What is the key read-scaling technique?
options: 每次请求都从头全量重新计算一遍完整 feed
把整个 feed 内容一次性全部发给客户端
完全不缓存任何一条帖子，只为保证绝对新鲜
预计算 feed，缓存近期帖子，用分页避免全量加载
why: 关键洞察：用户通常只读头几条，所以激进缓存近期内容回报巨大；预计算 + 分页避免每次现算和全量传输，把资源砸在头部内容上。
why_en: Pre-compute feeds for active users, cache recent posts, and paginate, because users typically only read the first few items.
whenOtherWins: 规模小或 feed 要求绝对实时时，请求时现算更简单，预计算反而是浪费。
options_en: Recompute the whole feed completely from scratch on every single request.
Send the entire feed content to the client all at once in one shot.
Cache absolutely no posts at all, purely to guarantee freshness.
Precompute feeds for active users, cache recent posts, and paginate instead of loading everything at once.
tradeoff: 预计算与缓存成本 vs 实时全量计算
optionExplanations: 每次现算意味着每个请求都要重新拉取和排序全部候选内容，白白浪费"只看头几条"这个规律。
把整个 feed 一次性发给客户端会传输用户根本不会看到的内容，带宽被浪费掉。
不缓存任何帖子会让每次刷新都直接打数据库，读极其密集时这撑不住。
对，预计算 feed、缓存近期帖子、分页加载，把资源集中在用户真正会看的头几条上。
optionExplanations_en: Recomputing from scratch means every request re-pulls and re-ranks the full candidate set, wasting the fact that users only see the top few.
Sending the whole feed in one shot ships content the user will never scroll to, wasting bandwidth.
Caching no posts sends every refresh straight to the database, which can't hold up under this much read volume.
Right — precompute feeds, cache recent posts, and paginate, concentrating resources on the items users actually see.

scenario: 设计 YouTube：每次打开首页都要查推荐视频、频道信息、播放量；标题/描述/缩略图很少变化。
scenario_en: Designing YouTube: each home-page load needs recommended videos, channel info, and view counts; titles, descriptions, and thumbnails rarely change.
q: 合理的读扩展组合是？
q_en: What is a reasonable read-scaling mix?
options: 播放量必须在每一次播放后都实时精确更新一次
激进缓存元数据；播放量最终一致；缩略图走 CDN
元数据完全不缓存，缩略图直接存放在数据库里
全站统一走强一致路径，禁止任何形式的缓存
why: 元数据很少变 → 激进缓存；播放量不需要精确实时 → 最终一致批量更新；缩略图是静态媒体 → CDN。按数据特性分层处理。
why_en: Cache video metadata aggressively, let view counts be eventually consistent with periodic updates, and serve thumbnails from a CDN.
whenOtherWins: 若计数用于计费等要求精确的场景，就不能用最终一致的缓存计数。
options_en: View counts must be updated in real time and exactly after every single play.
Cache metadata aggressively; let view counts be eventually consistent; serve thumbnails via CDN.
Don't cache metadata at all, and store thumbnails directly in the database.
Enforce strong consistency uniformly site-wide and forbid any form of caching.
tradeoff: 缓存新鲜度分层 vs 全站强一致
optionExplanations: 每次播放都精确实时更新播放量，等于为一个不需要精确的数字承担巨大写压力。
对，标题描述这类元数据激进缓存，播放量批量最终一致，缩略图走 CDN，按数据特性分层。
元数据几乎不变却不缓存，等于放弃了最容易拿到的那部分缓存收益。
全站强一致会连很少变的元数据也强制走一致性路径，付出的代价和收益完全不成比例。
optionExplanations_en: Updating view counts precisely on every single play pays a huge write cost for a number that doesn't need to be exact.
Right — cache rarely-changing metadata aggressively, batch view counts as eventually consistent, and serve thumbnails via CDN, layered by data behavior.
Not caching metadata that barely changes gives up the easiest caching win available.
Site-wide strong consistency forces even barely-changing metadata through the same heavy path, a cost wildly out of proportion to the benefit.

q: 哪些场景「不该」把读扩展当作主攻方向？（多选）
q_en: Which scenarios should not make read scaling the main focus? Select all that apply.
options: Uber 司机位置追踪：每几秒上报一次位置，读写比只有 2:1 甚至 1:1
面试官限定「为 1000 个用户设计」的小规模系统
Google Docs 这类实时协作系统：每次击键都要立即对他人可见
Bitly 短链接跳转服务
why: 写密集系统先做写扩展；小规模一个索引良好的单库就能扛几千 QPS；实时协作要的是实时更新，缓存反而有害。Bitly 恰恰是读扩展的梦想场景。
why_en: Skip read scaling for write-heavy systems, small-scale designs a single indexed database can handle, and real-time collaboration where caching actively hurts.
options_en: Uber driver location tracking: pings every few seconds, read-write ratio only 2:1 or even 1:1.
An interviewer-specified small system for 1000 users.
Google Docs-style real-time collaboration where every keystroke must be visible immediately.
Bitly-style URL shortener redirects.
tradeoff: 写扩展优先 vs 读扩展优先
optionExplanations: 对，读写比接近 1:1 时写路径才是真正的瓶颈，该先做写扩展而不是读扩展。
对，就 1000 个用户这个体量，普通索引配单库轻松应付，上读扩展纯属杀鸡用牛刀。
对，每次击键都要立即让别人看到，缓存的陈旧窗口正好破坏这个实时性要求。
Bitly 读写比极端悬殊、映射又不可变，恰恰是最该做读扩展的场景，不该排除。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a near 1:1 read-write ratio means the write path is the real bottleneck, so scale writes first.
Right — at a scale of 1000 users, an ordinary index on a single database handles it easily; read-scaling machinery here is overkill.
Right — every keystroke needs to be visible immediately, and a cache's staleness window directly breaks that requirement.
Bitly's read-write ratio is extreme and the mapping never changes — it's the poster child for read scaling, not an exception.

q: 「读扩展」的真正目标是什么？
q_en: What is the real goal of read scaling?
options: 让系统里所有请求的响应速度都变得更快
彻底把数据库从整个系统架构里消灭掉
减少数据库读负载；低延迟是另一类问题
把写入的吞吐量尽可能地提高上去
why: 读扩展解决的是「数据库被读垮」；「延迟不够低」是另一个问题、另一套解法，别混为一谈。
why_en: Read scaling is about reducing database load, and pure latency problems call for different solutions like edge computing.
options_en: Make every single request in the system respond faster.
Eliminate the database from the architecture entirely.
Reduce the read load the database carries; pure latency problems are a different kind of issue.
Push write throughput as high as it can possibly go.
optionExplanations: 让每个请求都更快涉及延迟优化，跟"数据库扛不住读压力"是不同的问题。
彻底消灭数据库不现实，也不是读扩展要解决的目标。
对，读扩展的目标是减少数据库承受的读负载；纯延迟问题要用别的手段解决。
写吞吐是写扩展的目标，跟读扩展要解决的问题方向不同。
optionExplanations_en: Making every request faster is a latency-optimization goal, a different problem from the database buckling under read load.
Eliminating the database entirely isn't realistic, and it isn't what read scaling is trying to achieve.
Right — read scaling's goal is reducing the read load the database carries; pure latency problems need different tools.
Write throughput is what write scaling targets, a different problem from what read scaling addresses.

q: 1000 万用户后「按 email 登录」的查询拖到 30 秒、DB CPU 100%，最可能的原因是？
q_en: At 10 million users, email login takes 30 seconds and DB CPU is 100%; what is the likely cause?
options: 是网络出现了故障，跟数据库本身无关
缺索引导致每次登录都全表扫描千万行数据
是内存条损坏了，硬件本身出了问题
是 SQL 语句本身写错了语法
why: 无索引 = 每个查询全表扫盘；join 会再乘一层（先扫 users 再扫 orders，数十亿次行比较）。解法很直接：给频繁查询的列加索引。
why_en: Without an index every login scans all ten million rows, about two gigabytes of data per lookup, multiplied by concurrent logins.
options_en: It's a network outage, unrelated to the database itself.
Missing an index forces a full table scan on every login across all ten million rows.
It's faulty RAM, a hardware problem underneath everything.
It's a plain SQL syntax error in the query itself.
optionExplanations: 网络故障通常表现为连接失败或超时，不会让 CPU 打满、查询变慢这样持续拖着。
对，没有索引意味着每次登录都要扫过一千万行找匹配的 email，CPU 被拖满。
硬件损坏会表现为随机崩溃或数据错误，不会稳定地拖成"越查越慢"这种模式。
语法错误会直接报错让查询失败，不会是"查询能跑但慢到 30 秒"这种表现。
optionExplanations_en: A network outage usually shows up as failed connections or timeouts, not a sustained CPU-pegged slow query.
Right — no index means every login scans all ten million rows looking for a matching email, pegging the CPU.
Faulty hardware tends to cause random crashes or data corruption, not a consistent 'gets slower under load' pattern.
A syntax error would fail the query outright, not let it run — just slowly, taking 30 seconds.

scenario: users 表 1000 万行，按 email 查询走的是全表扫描 (Seq Scan)，登录高峰时数据库 CPU 打满。
scenario_en: The users table has 10 million rows; email lookups are doing a full table scan, and login spikes max out database CPU.
q: 正确的修复是？
q_en: What is the right fix?
options: CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);
VACUUM FULL users;
SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 1;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email_backup TEXT;
why: 在 email 列上建索引，把千万行扫描变成几次索引查找；EXPLAIN 里 Seq Scan 变成 Index Scan、成本骤降就是证据。
why_en: Creating an index on the email column turns the full table scan into a few index lookups, visible in EXPLAIN as the plan switches to an index scan.
whenOtherWins: 若查询是 status + created_at 的组合过滤，需要对应的复合索引，单列 email 索引帮不上。
options_en: Create an index on the email column.
Run a full vacuum on the users table.
Select one row with a limit clause.
Add a new email_backup text column.
tradeoff: 查询延迟 vs 索引维护成本
optionExplanations: 对，给 email 列建一个索引，查询计划就能从全表扫描切换成走索引定位，代价从千万行降到几次比较。
VACUUM 清理的是死元组、回收空间，跟"按 email 查找慢"这个问题不是一回事。
只查一行验证不了整表扫描的问题，也不会让后续的正常查询变快。
加一列跟"按 email 查找要扫全表"没有任何关系，解决不了瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Right — indexing the email column lets the query planner switch from a full scan to an index lookup, cutting the cost from ten million rows to a few comparisons.
VACUUM reclaims dead tuples and space; it doesn't address why lookups by email are slow.
Selecting just one row doesn't verify or fix the full-table-scan problem for normal queries.
Adding a new column has nothing to do with why an email lookup scans the whole table — it won't fix the bottleneck.

q: 复合索引 (status, created_at) 能加速哪些查询？
q_en: Which queries can a compound index on status and created_at speed up?
options: 只加速单独按 created_at 过滤或排序的查询，跟 status 无关，因为它不在索引最左侧
只要用到 status 或 created_at 任意一列的查询都能被这个复合索引加速
只加速直接用 id 主键做等值匹配的点查，其它列都用不上
能加速 status 及联合 status+created_at 过滤，仅 created_at 不行
why: 复合索引按列顺序（最左前缀）生效：先按 status 排、再按 created_at 排，所以跳过 status 就用不上。列顺序很重要。
why_en: Column order matters in a compound index: an index on status and created_at helps status filters and combined filters, but not created_at alone.
options_en: It only speeds up queries filtering or sorting by created_at alone, unrelated to status, since it's not the leftmost column.
Any query touching status or created_at, in any combination, gets accelerated by this compound index.
It only speeds up point lookups on the id primary key, not other columns.
It speeds up status filters and combined status-plus-created_at filters; created_at alone gets no benefit.
optionExplanations: 复合索引没有最左列 status 时用不上，单独按 created_at 查询同样帮不上忙。
跳过最左列 status、只用 created_at 过滤时，这个复合索引根本用不上。
复合索引不是只服务主键点查，status 和联合过滤都能吃到它的加速。
对，最左前缀规则下它能加速 status 单独过滤和 status+created_at 联合过滤，但跳过 status 单查 created_at 用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Without the leftmost column status present, the index can't be used — filtering by created_at alone doesn't help either.
Skipping the leftmost column status and filtering only by created_at means this compound index can't be used at all.
A compound index isn't limited to primary-key point lookups — status filters and combined filters both benefit from it.
Right — under the leftmost-prefix rule it speeds up status filters and status-plus-created_at filters, but not created_at alone.

q: 名人发帖后，单个缓存 key 从 5 万 QPS 冲到 50 万 QPS 并开始超时——这是什么问题？
q_en: A celebrity post pushes one cache key from 50k to 500k QPS and timeouts; what problem is this?
options: 热 key 打满单个缓存节点
缓存穿透
复制延迟
磁盘 I/O 瓶颈
why: 数据在内存不代表无限吞吐：把同一份数据序列化并通过网络发送 50 万次/秒，单台服务器就是扛不住。
why_en: This is the hot-key problem: one key gets all the traffic and overwhelms a single cache server's CPU and network even though the data is in memory.
options_en: The hot-key problem: one key's flood overwhelms a single node.
Cache penetration.
Replication lag.
A disk I/O bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问、可能压垮单个节点的缓存 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a cache key receiving unusually high traffic that can overwhelm a single node.

optionExplanations: 对，同一个 key 被打到 50 万 QPS，单台缓存节点的 CPU 和网络先扛不住了。
缓存穿透指的是查不存在的数据绕过缓存直击数据库，跟单 key 被打爆是不同的现象。
复制延迟发生在数据同步阶段，跟单个热点 key 的瞬时流量洪峰不是同一件事。
数据在内存里，瓶颈根本不在磁盘 I/O，是网络和 CPU 先撑不住了。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the same key gets hit at 500k QPS, and a single cache node's CPU and network give out first.
Cache penetration is when lookups for nonexistent data bypass the cache and hit the database — a different failure mode.
Replication lag happens during data sync; it's unrelated to a sudden traffic spike on one hot key.
The data is in memory, so disk I/O was never the bottleneck — network and CPU give out first.

q: 请求合并 (request coalescing) 能把「百万用户同时要同一个 key」的后端压力降到多少？
q_en: How far can request coalescing reduce backend load when a million users ask for the same key?
options: 降到零请求，完全不查后端
恰好 N 个请求，N 是服务器数
降到大约一半
不变，仍是百万级
why: 合并把「无上限的相同请求」压缩成「每台应用服务器一个」：百万用户等同一个结果，后端只看到 N 次查询。
why_en: Request coalescing reduces backend load from potentially unlimited to exactly one request per application server doing the coalescing.
diagram:
flowchart LR U1["用户 x 100 万"] --> A1["应用服务器 1
合并为 1 个在途请求"] U1 --> A2["应用服务器 2
合并为 1 个在途请求"] A1 --> B[(后端 / 缓存)] A2 --> B B -.->|共 N 个请求| B
options_en: It drops to zero requests, never touching the backend.
Exactly N requests, where N is the number of servers.
It drops to roughly half.
It stays unchanged at the million level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一 key 的多个并发请求合并成一次后端调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Request coalescing merges multiple concurrent requests for the same key into a single backend call.

optionExplanations: 彻底不查后端会导致数据永远拿不到最新结果，合并的目标不是完全跳过后端。
对，每台应用服务器最多让一个请求真正穿透到后端，其余的都在等同一个结果。
降到一半仍然是随用户量线性增长，没有把重复请求真正压缩掉。
如果流量完全不变，说明合并根本没生效，这不是它该有的效果。
optionExplanations_en: Never querying the backend at all means you'd never get a fresh result — that's not what coalescing is for.
Right — at most one request per application server actually reaches the backend; the rest just wait on that same result.
Dropping to half still scales linearly with user count — the duplicate requests haven't actually been collapsed.
If traffic stayed completely unchanged, coalescing clearly isn't working — that's not the intended effect.

q: 这段请求合并代码里，inflight 字典的作用是？
q_en: What role does the inflight map play in this request-coalescing code?
options: 缓存最终结果，供之后所有请求长期使用
限制全局并发数
记录哪个 key 在途，后来者共享 Future
统计每个 key 的 QPS
why: inflight 是 key → Future 的映射：第一个请求负责真正取数，后续同 key 请求共享那个 Future 的结果，取完即删。
why_en: The inflight map tracks keys already being fetched so concurrent requests await the same future instead of issuing duplicate backend calls.
codeSample:
class CoalescingCache:
    def __init__(self):
        self.inflight = {}  # key -> Future

    async def get(self, key):
        if key in self.inflight:          # 已有请求在取
            return await self.inflight[key]
        future = asyncio.Future()
        self.inflight[key] = future
        try:
            value = await fetch_from_backend(key)
            future.set_result(value)
            return value
        finally:
            del self.inflight[key]
scenario: 你在实现请求合并 (request coalescing) 来抵御热点 key 的并发洪峰，下面是核心 Python 代码。
scenario_en: You are implementing request coalescing to handle a concurrent flood on a hot key; this is the core Python code.
options_en: Cache the final result for all future requests long-term.
Limit the global concurrency count.
Track which keys already have a request in flight so later callers await the same future.
Count QPS per key.
optionExplanations: 取完立刻在 finally 里删掉了 key，它不是长期缓存，只在请求进行中才存在。
字典里没有任何并发数计数逻辑，它记录的是"哪个 key 在途"，不是限流器。
对，key 存在于 inflight 时说明已有请求在取，后来者直接 await 同一个 Future，不重复打后端。
代码里没有任何计数或统计逻辑，inflight 只负责标记在途状态，不是 QPS 统计器。
optionExplanations_en: The key is deleted in the finally block right after fetching — it's not a long-lived cache, only present while in flight.
There's no concurrency-counting logic in the dict — it tracks which keys are in flight, not a rate limiter.
Right — a key present in inflight means a fetch is already underway, so later callers just await that same future instead of hitting the backend again.
There's no counting or stats logic here at all; inflight only marks in-flight state, it isn't a QPS tracker.

scenario: 已做请求合并，但单 key 仍有 50 万 QPS 持续流量，超出单台缓存节点约 5 万 QPS 的能力。
scenario_en: Request coalescing is already in place, but one key still has sustained 500k QPS, above a single cache node's roughly 50k QPS capacity.
q: 下一步该怎么办？
q_en: What should you do next?
options: 把这个热 key 的 TTL 设得更长一些
咬牙换一台更贵、性能更强的缓存机器
干脆关闭缓存，让请求直接连数据库
缓存 key 扇出：复制多份分摊到多节点
why: 合并解决「重复请求」，扇出解决「单 key 持续洪峰」：把一个热 key 拆成多份副本分摊到多台节点。
why_en: Cache key fanout stores identical copies under multiple keys so clients randomly pick one, spreading the hot key's load across servers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Clients"] --> Pick["random shard key"]
    Pick --> K1["feed:taylor:1"]
    Pick --> K2["feed:taylor:2"]
    Pick --> K10["feed:taylor:10"]
    K1 --> N1["Cache node A"]
    K2 --> N2["Cache node B"]
    K10 --> N3["Cache node C"]
whenOtherWins: 若洪峰只出现在过期重建的瞬间而非持续流量，请求合并或提前刷新就够了，不必付扇出的内存与失效成本。
options_en: Just extend this hot key's TTL a bit longer.
Grit your teeth and move to a pricier, more powerful cache machine.
Just turn off the cache and let requests hit the database directly.
Cache key fanout: store copies under several keys and let clients randomly pick one to spread the load.
tradeoff: 多副本分摊负载 vs 内存与失效成本

termDefinitions.term: 缓存 key 扇出 / cache key fanout
termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一数据复制到多个 key 上分散热点流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache key fanout duplicates data under multiple keys to spread hot-key traffic.

optionExplanations: TTL 延长解决的是刷新频率，不改变单个 key 承受的持续 QPS 总量。
换更贵的机器只是把单点瓶颈的上限抬高一点，持续洪峰迟早会再次打满它。
关掉缓存直连数据库会让数据库直接承受这 50 万 QPS，情况只会更糟。
对，把这份数据复制成多个 key 分散到不同缓存节点，客户端随机挑一个，单点压力被摊开。
optionExplanations_en: Extending the TTL affects refresh frequency; it doesn't change the sustained QPS one key has to absorb.
A pricier machine only raises the single-node ceiling slightly — sustained flood traffic will saturate it again eventually.
Turning off the cache sends that same 500k QPS straight at the database instead, making things worse, not better.
Right — duplicate the data under several keys spread across cache nodes, and let clients pick one at random to spread the load.

q: 缓存 key 扇出（一份数据存十个 key）的代价是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of cache key fanout?
options: 读请求的延迟会因此大幅上升
缓存命中率会因此必然下降
内存占用成倍增加，失效要清掉所有副本
所有写入操作都会因此被阻塞住
why: 扇出用冗余换可用性：多份拷贝多占内存、失效要全清；但在热 key 威胁可用性时，这点冗余是保命的小代价。
why_en: Fanout costs extra memory for duplicate copies and makes invalidation harder since every copy must be cleared, a small price for staying online.
options_en: Read latency rises sharply as a result.
Hit rate is bound to drop because of this.
Memory usage multiplies since data is duplicated, and invalidation must clear every copy.
All write operations end up getting blocked.
optionExplanations: 扇出后单次读仍然只打一个副本，读延迟本身不会因此变慢。
命中率不会因为多存了几份同样数据而下降，读的仍然是同一份内容。
对，十份拷贝占十倍内存，数据一变还要把所有副本都清掉，这是扇出真正的代价。
扇出只影响读路径的分布，跟写入是否被阻塞没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: After fanout, a single read still hits just one copy — read latency itself doesn't get worse from this.
Hit rate doesn't drop just because the same data is stored under more keys — clients still find the same content.
Right — ten copies means ten times the memory, and any update has to clear every one of them — that's the real cost.
Fanout only changes how reads are distributed; it has nothing to do with whether writes get blocked.

q: 缓存击穿/惊群 (cache stampede) 的根本触发机制是？
q_en: What triggers a cache stampede?
options: 过期是二元的：一瞬间全部涌向数据库
是数据库本身处理速度太慢导致的
是 TTL 设置得太长了导致的问题
是缓存容量本身不够大导致的
why: 越热门的条目雪崩越大、重建越贵（10 表 join、外部 API）伤害越大——等于自己对自己发起 DDOS，10 万并发同一瞬间涌向数据库。
why_en: Cache expiration is binary, so the instant a hot entry expires every concurrent request misses at once and floods the database like a self-inflicted DDoS.
options_en: Cache expiry is binary — one moment it's there, the next it's gone, so every concurrent request misses at once.
It's caused by the database itself being too slow.
It's caused by the TTL being set too long.
It's caused by the cache simply not having enough capacity.

termDefinitions.term: 缓存击穿 / 惊群 / cache stampede
termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存过期瞬间大量并发请求同时未命中、一起打向数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede happens when many concurrent requests miss at the exact instant a cache entry expires.

optionExplanations: 对，缓存条目要么在要么不在，没有中间状态，过期那一刻所有并发请求同时未命中。
数据库慢会让重建变慢、加重击穿的后果，但它不是击穿这个现象本身的触发原因。
TTL 长短决定多久发生一次击穿，不是击穿这个机制存在的根本原因。
容量不足会导致条目被提前驱逐，但击穿的根源是过期这个二元事件本身。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a cache entry is either present or gone with no in-between, so the instant it lapses every concurrent request misses at once.
A slow database makes the rebuild take longer and worsens the fallout, but it isn't what triggers the stampede itself.
TTL length affects how often a stampede happens, not why the mechanism exists in the first place.
Insufficient capacity causes early eviction, but the root cause of a stampede is the binary nature of expiry itself.

q: 用分布式锁防击穿（只许第一个请求重建，其他人等待）的主要缺点是？
q_en: What is the main downside of using a distributed lock to stop a stampede?
options: 数据库负载会因此完全不降，白忙一场
缓存会因此永远无法再被更新
锁本身会占用掉太多的内存空间
若重建失败或太慢，成千上万等待者一起超时
why: 锁保护了后端，但把风险转嫁给等待者：重建一慢，全体请求挂起超时，需要复杂的超时与兜底逻辑，高负载下很脆弱。
why_en: With a distributed lock a slow or failed rebuild leaves thousands of waiting requests to time out, making the approach fragile under load.
options_en: Database load doesn't drop at all despite all this effort.
The cache can never be updated again after this.
The lock itself ends up using far too much memory.
If the rebuild fails or is slow, thousands of waiters time out together, requiring fragile fallback logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨进程/服务器协调的锁，只让一个请求执行重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across processes so only one request performs the rebuild.

optionExplanations: 锁本身就是为了把并发重建收窄成一个，数据库负载确实降下来了，问题出在别处。
锁只是限制谁能重建，缓存条目仍然会被那一个成功的请求正常更新。
锁的内存开销通常很小，真正的风险不在这里。
对，如果那一个重建者失败或太慢，成千上万等待的请求会一起超时，还得设计复杂的兜底逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: The lock is exactly meant to narrow concurrent rebuilds down to one, so database load does drop — the problem lies elsewhere.
The lock only restricts who can rebuild; the cache entry still gets updated normally by that one successful request.
A lock's memory footprint is usually tiny — that's not where the real risk sits.
Right — if that one rebuilder fails or is slow, thousands of waiting requests time out together, requiring fragile fallback logic.

scenario: 首页缓存 10 万 QPS、1 小时 TTL；你想避免到点集体未命中，又不想引入锁的脆弱性。
scenario_en: A homepage cache gets 100k QPS with a one-hour TTL; you want to avoid a synchronized miss without the fragility of locks.
q: 更聪明的做法是？
q_en: What is the smarter approach?
options: 干脆把 TTL 缩短到只有 10 分钟
概率化提前刷新：越接近过期触发概率越高，重建摊开
过期以后就放任所有请求直接打向数据库
每一次读取都强制重新刷新一遍数据
why: 概率化提前刷新把「同一瞬间的 10 万次重建」摊成「十几分钟里的零星刷新」，多数用户仍拿缓存、少数触发后台刷新。
why_en: Probabilistic early refresh gives each request a growing chance to refresh the entry as expiry nears, spreading rebuilds over minutes instead of one instant.
whenOtherWins: 对绝不容许击穿的最关键数据，用后台定时刷新彻底不让用户触发重建。
options_en: Just shorten the TTL down to only 10 minutes.
Probabilistic early refresh: the closer an entry is to expiry, the higher the chance each request triggers a background refresh.
After it lapses, just let every request hit the database directly.
Force a full refresh on every single read, no exceptions.
tradeoff: 确定性防击穿 vs 分散刷新概率

termDefinitions.term: 概率化提前刷新 / probabilistic early refresh
termDefinitions.meaning: 越接近过期，请求触发后台刷新的概率越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Probabilistic early refresh gives requests a growing chance to trigger a background refresh as an entry nears expiry.

optionExplanations: 缩短 TTL 只是让集体未命中发生得更频繁，没有解决"同一瞬间全部未命中"这件事。
对，越接近过期触发刷新的概率越高，把重建从一瞬间摊开到几分钟里零星发生。
过期后放任所有请求直接打库，正是要避免的那个"同一瞬间全部涌向数据库"场景。
每次读都强制刷新等于放弃了缓存本身的意义，读多快数据库就被打多快。
optionExplanations_en: Shortening the TTL just makes the synchronized miss happen more often — it doesn't stop everyone missing at the same instant.
Right — the closer to expiry, the higher the chance a request triggers a refresh, spreading rebuilds over minutes instead of one instant.
Letting every request hit the database right after it lapses is exactly the synchronized-flood scenario you're trying to avoid.
Forcing a refresh on every single read defeats caching's whole purpose — the database gets hit as fast as reads come in.

scenario: 最关键的首页缓存：不能冒任何击穿风险，也不接受概率化方案的不确定性。
scenario_en: This is the most critical homepage cache: no stampede risk is acceptable, and probabilistic behavior is not acceptable.
q: 该用什么方案？
q_en: Which approach should you use?
options: 后台持续提前刷新，用户永不触发重建
干脆把这个条目的 TTL 设得再长一些
用分布式锁来控制谁能重建这个条目
干脆放弃缓存这个条目，每次都现查
why: 后台持续刷新是最强保险：用户请求永远命中新鲜缓存。代价是基础设施复杂度和「刷新了没人读的数据」的浪费，只留给最关键内容。
why_en: A background process continuously refreshes critical entries before expiry so users never trigger rebuilds, at the cost of extra infrastructure and wasted refreshes.
whenOtherWins: 普通热度的数据用概率化提前刷新就够了，专职后台刷新的成本不值得。
options_en: A background process keeps refreshing entries before they lapse, so users never trigger a rebuild.
Just set this entry's TTL to something even longer.
Use a distributed lock to control who gets to rebuild it.
Just stop caching this entry and query live every time.
optionExplanations: 对，后台在过期前持续刷新，用户请求永远命中新鲜缓存，代价是额外的基础设施和一些浪费的刷新。
更长的 TTL 只是把集体未命中推迟发生，风险本身并没有被消除，跟"绝不冒风险"的要求不符。
分布式锁仍然把风险转嫁给等待者——重建一慢，等待者集体超时，跟"不接受不确定性"的要求相悖。
放弃缓存这个条目意味着每次读都直接打数据库，对最关键的首页数据这代价太大。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a background process keeps refreshing before expiry so requests always hit a fresh entry, at the cost of extra infrastructure and some wasted refreshes.
A longer TTL just postpones the synchronized miss — the risk itself isn't removed, at odds with a 'zero risk accepted' requirement.
A distributed lock still shifts risk onto waiters — a slow rebuild still times them out together, at odds with 'no uncertainty accepted'.
Dropping the cache entirely sends every read straight to the database — too costly for the most critical homepage data.

q: 「写完数据库就删缓存」这种朴素失效方式有哪些真实问题？（多选）
q_en: What real problems does naive delete-cache-after-write create? Select all that apply.
options: 该删哪些缓存说不清：应用缓存、CDN、浏览器缓存都可能存着旧值
失效请求本身可能失败
删除之后、新值写入之前，另一个请求可能读到旧数据并把它重新缓存回去（竞态条件）
删除操作会锁住整张表
why: 多层缓存、失效失败、删后重缓存竞态——这三个坑让「直接删」在需要立即可见的场景不可靠，于是才有版本化方案。
why_en: Naive delete-on-write fails because caches live in many layers, invalidations can fail, and a racing read can re-cache stale data right after the delete.
options_en: It's unclear which caches to clear — app cache, CDN, and browser cache may all hold stale values.
The invalidation request itself can fail.
Between the delete and the new write, another request can re-cache the stale value — a race condition.
The delete operation locks the entire table.
optionExplanations: 对，应用缓存、CDN、浏览器缓存可能各自都存了一份旧值，光删一处根本不够。
对，失效请求本身可能因为网络或服务故障失败，旧值就这样留下来了。
对，删除和新值写入之间有个窗口，另一个请求正好可能在这个窗口把旧值重新缓存回去。
删除一行缓存数据是极快的键值操作，不会去锁住整张数据库表。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the app cache, CDN, and browser cache may each hold their own stale copy, so deleting just one isn't enough.
Right — the invalidation request itself can fail from a network hiccup or service outage, leaving the stale value in place.
Right — there's a window between the delete and the new write where another request can re-cache the stale value.
Deleting one cache entry is a fast key-value operation; it has no reason to lock an entire database table.

q: 缓存版本化 (cache versioning) 的读写流程是？
q_en: What is the read/write flow for cache versioning?
options: 每一次读取都直接绕开缓存去查数据库
写入时主动向所有缓存层广播一条失效消息
版本号存放在缓存里，由缓存自己负责自增
版本号存数据库，随更新递增；读时用版本拼 key
why: 核心是「不删除、改路由」：旧缓存条目从不被删，只是版本一变就没人再读它；CDN 和浏览器缓存也随 key/URL 变化自然过期。
why_en: Each record's version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction, so reads build a versioned cache key and old entries simply become unreachable.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["读请求"] --> V["取版本号
(版本 key 或 DB)"] V --> K["拼 key: event:123:v42"] K --> C{"缓存命中?"} C -->|是| Out["返回"] C -->|否| DB[(数据库)] --> F["回填 v42"] --> Out
options_en: Every single read bypasses the cache and hits the database directly.
Writes actively broadcast an invalidation message to every cache layer.
The version number lives in the cache itself and increments on its own.
The version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction; reads use it to build the cache key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把版本号编进缓存 key，更新后旧 key 自然不可达。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Versioned keys embed a version number in the cache key so old keys become unreachable after an update.

optionExplanations: 如果每次读都直接查库，缓存版本化这一整套机制就没有存在的意义了。
广播失效消息到所有缓存层正是版本化想避开的做法，它靠 key 自然不可达而不是主动通知。
版本号若由缓存自己维护，写入数据库的变更就没法可靠触发它递增。
对，版本号存在数据库、跟数据同一事务递增，读时用这个版本号拼出缓存 key。
optionExplanations_en: If every read hit the database directly, the whole point of cache versioning would disappear.
Broadcasting invalidation to every cache layer is exactly what versioning avoids — it relies on keys becoming unreachable, not active notification.
If the cache itself owned the version number, a database write couldn't reliably trigger it to increment.
Right — the version lives in the database and increments in the same transaction as the data, and reads use it to build the cache key.

q: 为什么版本化能整类地绕开失效竞态？
q_en: Why does versioning avoid a whole class of invalidation races?
options: 因为它给每一次读请求都加上了全局锁
因为版本递增是原子的，旧缓存被绕开而非删除
因为缓存从这一刻起就再也不会失效了
因为它彻底禁止了任何形式的并发写入
why: 没有删除就没有「删了又被写回旧值」的竞态；版本变化原子发生，读者自动切到新 key，无需广播失效。
why_en: Version changes are atomic in the database so keys never collide and readers move to the new key automatically, eliminating the whole class of invalidation races.
options_en: Because it adds a global lock to every single read request.
Because version increments are atomic in the database, so old cache entries are bypassed rather than deleted.
Because the cache stops going stale from this point onward, permanently.
Because it forbids any form of concurrent writing whatsoever.
optionExplanations: 全局锁会把所有读串行化，代价太大，而且版本化压根不需要靠锁来避免竞态。
对，版本递增和数据更新在同一事务里原子发生，旧 key 没人再拼出来，自然被绕开而不是被删除。
版本化条目仍然可以设 TTL 自然失效，说"永不失效"不准确。
版本化不禁止并发写，它只是让每次写都产生一个新版本号，写照样能并发发生。
optionExplanations_en: A global lock would serialize every read, far too costly, and versioning doesn't need a lock to avoid races anyway.
Right — the version increment and the data update happen atomically in the same transaction, so nobody constructs the old key anymore and it's simply bypassed, not deleted.
Versioned entries can still carry a TTL and go stale on their own — saying it never lapses isn't accurate.
Versioning doesn't forbid concurrent writes; it just means each write produces a new version number, and writes can still happen concurrently.

q: 缓存版本化的代价包括？
q_en: What costs come with cache versioning?
options: 多一次查找、旧版本堆积，只适合单实体缓存
读性能会因此直接下降整整十倍
数据库的写入吞吐量会因此直接减半
版本号一旦溢出就会直接导致系统故障
why: 版本化的三笔账：多一跳查版本、旧条目靠 TTL 清、只覆盖单实体缓存——计算型数据的失效要另想办法（如删除项缓存）。
why_en: Versioning costs an extra lookup per read, lets old versions accumulate until TTLs clean them, and only really fits single-entity caches.
options_en: Every read needs two cache lookups, old versions accumulate, and it only fits single-entity caches.
Read performance ends up dropping by a full factor of ten.
Database write throughput ends up getting cut in half.
A version-number overflow would directly crash the whole system.
optionExplanations: 对，每次读要多查一次版本号，旧版本条目靠 TTL 慢慢清，而且这套机制主要适合单实体缓存。
多出的只是一次额外查找，不至于把读性能拖慢十倍这么夸张。
版本化发生在读路径和 key 构造上，跟数据库的写吞吐没有直接关系。
版本号一般是整数或时间戳，正常场景下不会轻易溢出到让系统故障的地步。
optionExplanations_en: Right — each read needs one extra version lookup, old versions linger until TTL cleans them, and this mainly suits single-entity caches.
The added cost is one extra lookup — nowhere near enough to make reads ten times slower.
Versioning affects the read path and key construction, not the database's write throughput directly.
Version numbers are typically integers or timestamps and don't realistically overflow into a system failure.

scenario: 内容审核场景：帖子被删除后必须立刻从所有已缓存的 feed 中消失，但逐一失效所有包含它的 feed 缓存太贵。
scenario_en: In a content-moderation flow, deleted posts must disappear from all cached feeds immediately, but invalidating every feed containing the post is too expensive.
q: 高效的折中方案是？
q_en: What is the efficient compromise?
options: 清空全部 feed 缓存
把 feed 缓存 TTL 降到 1 秒
停止缓存所有 feed
维护小的「已删除条目缓存」，出 feed 时过滤
why: 小而快的删除项缓存让你立即遮蔽被删内容、继续服务「大体正确」的缓存数据，复杂结构的真正失效异步完成。
why_en: A small deleted-items cache filters recently removed IDs at serve time so cached feeds stay usable while the expensive invalidation happens in the background.
whenOtherWins: 单实体数据（用户资料、活动详情）用版本化 key 更干净；删除项缓存专攻计算型/聚合缓存的快速遮蔽。
options_en: Wipe the entire feed cache.
Drop the feed cache TTL to one second.
Stop caching feeds altogether.
Keep a small deleted-items cache of recently removed post IDs and filter them out when serving feeds.
tradeoff: 即时遮蔽 vs 后台彻底失效

termDefinitions.term: 已删除条目缓存 / deleted items cache
termDefinitions.meaning: 一份记录近期被删除或隐藏内容 ID 的小缓存，用于过滤。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deleted-items cache is a small cache of recently removed or hidden IDs used to filter results.

optionExplanations: 清空整个 feed 缓存会让所有用户瞬间全部未命中，代价远大于问题本身。
把 TTL 压到 1 秒等于放弃 feed 缓存的大部分收益，为了一个删除场景牺牲太多。
彻底停止缓存 feed 意味着每次刷新都直接查库，读压力直接反弹到数据库。
对，维护一份小的已删除 ID 缓存，出 feed 时顺手过滤掉，真正的失效可以异步慢慢做。
optionExplanations_en: Wiping the entire feed cache sends every user into a miss at once — a cost far bigger than the problem it solves.
Dropping TTL to one second gives up most of the feed cache's benefit just to handle deletion.
Stopping feed caching entirely means every refresh hits the database directly, bouncing the read load right back.
Right — keep a small cache of recently deleted IDs and filter them out at serve time, while the real invalidation happens asynchronously.

q: 全球 CDN 场景下的缓存失效有什么额外难点与对策？
q_en: What extra challenge does cache invalidation have with a global CDN, and what is the response?
options: CDN 的失效指令会瞬间在全球所有节点生效，无需特殊处理
要清数百个边缘节点，传播有延迟；关键更新可跳过 CDN
CDN 这类基础设施完全不支持任何形式的主动失效
只能被动等待所有边缘节点各自的 TTL 慢慢自然过期
why: CDN 失效是「清几百个边缘」而非一个缓存，传播要时间；所以关键数据宁可不进 CDN，次要数据靠边缘短 TTL + 应用层长 TTL 分层。
why_en: Invalidating a CDN means clearing hundreds of edge locations with propagation delay, so critical updates may bypass CDN caching entirely via cache headers.
options_en: A CDN invalidation instantly takes effect at every global node with no special handling needed.
You must clear hundreds of edge nodes with propagation delay; critical updates can bypass the CDN via cache headers.
CDN infrastructure like this doesn't support any form of active invalidation at all.
You can only passively wait for every edge node's own TTL to lapse naturally over time.
optionExplanations: 边缘节点数百个，清理指令传播到每一个都要时间，说瞬间全球生效不准确。
对，要逐一清理数百个边缘节点，传播有延迟；对必须立即可见的关键更新可以绕开 CDN 缓存。
主流 CDN 都提供失效/清除接口，说完全不支持是不准确的。
被动等 TTL 自然过期对紧急更新太慢，主动失效或跳过 CDN 都是可用的对策。
optionExplanations_en: There are hundreds of edge nodes, and propagating a purge to every one takes time — 'instant globally' isn't accurate.
Right — clearing hundreds of edge nodes takes propagation time, so truly critical updates can bypass CDN caching via headers.
Mainstream CDNs all expose invalidation or purge APIs — saying they support none isn't accurate.
Waiting for natural TTL expiry everywhere is too slow for urgent updates; active invalidation or bypassing the CDN are real options.

q: 把「场馆地址更新必须立即可见」的缓存决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the cache decision chain for venue address updates that must be visible immediately in order.
steps: 缓解：给旧版本条目设 TTL 兜底清理，接受每次读多一跳
需求：更新后立刻可见，而数据缓存在 Redis / CDN / 浏览器多层，直接删缓存有竞态
代价：每次读要先取版本号再取数据，旧版本条目会堆积
选型：缓存版本化——版本号入库、同事务递增、key 携带版本
why: 需求（立即可见 + 多层缓存）→ 选型（版本化 key）→ 代价（双查找、旧条目堆积）→ 缓解（TTL 清理）。决策链四段式。
why_en: The chain runs requirement, choice, cost, mitigation: immediate visibility across cache layers leads to versioned keys, whose double lookup and accumulation are bounded by TTL cleanup.

q: 补全 Bitly 缓存策略的推理：
q_en: Complete the reasoning for Bitly's cache strategy.
text: Bitly 是缓存的梦想场景：长短链映射{{不可变}}（创建后从不改变）、读写比{{极端悬殊}}（建一次、读百万次），所以可以激进缓存甚至{{不设过期}}，数据库只接冷门链接的未命中。
why: 「不可变 + 读爆炸」意味着缓存零陈旧风险、命中率极高——这是判断「能多激进地缓存」的标尺。
why_en: Because the mapping is immutable and read millions of times per write, Bitly can cache aggressively with no expiration at all.

scenario: 同一个系统里：用户资料可容忍 5 分钟陈旧，活动场馆地址更新必须立即可见。
scenario_en: In one system, user profiles may be stale for 5 minutes, while event venue address updates must be visible immediately.
q: 正确的整体缓存设计原则是？
q_en: What is the right overall caching design principle?
options: 全站统一 5 分钟 TTL 省事
全站都用最强的失效方案以防万一
按数据设计：不同数据一致性需求不同，别一刀切
干脆都不缓存
why: 缓存策略应围绕各类数据的一致性需求分层设计；一刀切要么太贵、要么太陈旧。
why_en: Design caching around each data type's consistency needs instead of applying one approach everywhere.
whenOtherWins: 若系统里所有数据的陈旧容忍确实一致，统一策略当然更简单。
options_en: Use one uniform 5-minute TTL everywhere for simplicity.
Apply the strongest invalidation strategy everywhere just in case.
Design per data type: different data has different consistency needs, so don't apply one approach everywhere.
Just don't cache anything.
tradeoff: 统一简单 vs 按需分层保护
optionExplanations: 统一 5 分钟 TTL 会让场馆地址这类要求立即可见的数据也拖上 5 分钟陈旧，违反需求。
全站都上最强失效方案会让用户资料这类能忍陈旧的数据也背上不必要的复杂度和成本。
对，按每类数据自己的一致性需求分层设计——资料可以 TTL，场馆地址要主动失效或跳过缓存。
都不缓存等于放弃用户资料这类能忍陈旧数据的全部缓存收益，代价过大。
optionExplanations_en: A blanket 5-minute TTL would leave venue-address updates, which must be visible immediately, stale for 5 minutes too — violating the requirement.
Applying the strongest invalidation everywhere saddles tolerant data like user profiles with needless complexity and cost.
Right — design per data type's own consistency needs: profiles can use a TTL, venue addresses need active invalidation or no caching at all.
Caching nothing throws away all caching benefit for data like profiles that can easily tolerate staleness — too costly.

q: 写入吞吐撞到单机极限时，最典型的三个硬件瓶颈是？
q_en: When write throughput hits a single machine's ceiling, what are the three classic hardware bottlenecks?
options: 内存容量、GPU、显存
磁盘 I/O、CPU、网络带宽
DNS、TLS 握手、负载均衡器
线程数、文件句柄、连接池
options_en: Memory capacity, GPU, and video RAM
Disk I/O, CPU, and network bandwidth
DNS, the TLS handshake, and the load balancer
Thread count, file handles, and the connection pool
why: 写入受限于磁盘 I/O、CPU 和网络带宽三堵墙；面试里谈扩展写入前，先确认到底撞的是哪一堵。
why_en: Writes are bottlenecked by disk I/O, CPU, and network bandwidth, so confirm which wall you're actually hitting before proposing any redesign.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理器，执行计算指令；写入路径上的序列化、校验、事务处理都要占用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, runs computation, and write-path work like serialization and transaction handling consumes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据落盘的读写操作，机械寻道或 SSD 写放大都会拖慢它，是写入最常见的瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Disk I/O is the read/write traffic to storage, and mechanical seeks or SSD write amplification make it the most common write bottleneck.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器，擅长并行计算，不是典型数据库写入路径的瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU, or Graphics Processing Unit, is built for parallel compute and is not a typical bottleneck on a database write path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建立加密连接时的一次性协商，不会随每次写入重复发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The TLS handshake is the one-time negotiation that sets up an encrypted connection, not something repeated on every write.

optionExplanations: 内存、GPU 和显存是训练或渲染类任务吃紧的资源，数据库写入路径基本用不上它们。
写入撞的通常就是这三处物理上限：顺序写盘能力、CPU 处理速度、网卡带宽，先确认卡在哪一处。
DNS 查询和加密握手只发生在建连那一刻，不会随每条写入重复，负载均衡器也不是存储层瓶颈。
线程数、文件句柄、连接池是并发配置的上限，调大能缓解排队，但换不掉底层硬件的物理限制。
optionExplanations_en: Memory, GPU, and VRAM matter for training or rendering, not a database write path — they're not the pressure point here.
Writes typically hit one of these three ceilings: sequential disk throughput, CPU speed, or NIC bandwidth — name which one first.
DNS lookups and the encryption handshake only happen once when the connection is first set up, not on every write, and a load balancer isn't a storage-layer limit.
Thread count, file handles, and the connection pool are concurrency caps you can raise; they don't change the underlying hardware ceiling.

q: 在「扩展难度」这个维度上，为什么写扩展通常比读扩展更棘手？
q_en: On the axis of "how hard is it to scale", why is scaling writes usually harder than scaling reads?
scenario: 面试官已经问完读扩展（副本、缓存），现在追问「写呢」，想看你是否理解两边难度不对称。
scenario_en: The interviewer already covered read scaling (replicas, caching) and now asks "what about writes", checking whether you see the asymmetry.
options: 读侧有副本、缓存等成熟工具，写侧突发、高吞吐、竞争更难扩
写请求携带的网络数据包天生比读请求大得多，所以写更难扩展
不管什么场景，读请求几乎都不占用 CPU 和内存资源
写扩展没有任何专门工具或框架，只能整体换掉数据库才能解决
options_en: Reads have mature tools like replicas and caching, while bursty, high-throughput, contention-heavy writes are much harder
Write request payloads are inherently much bigger than read payloads, which is why writes are harder to scale
In every scenario, read requests barely use any CPU or memory at all
There is no dedicated tooling or framework for scaling writes, so the only fix is replacing the database entirely
why: 读侧有读副本、缓存等成熟套路；写侧面对突发、高吞吐和竞争，一次错误选择还可能让情况更糟，所以面试官爱在这里追问。
why_en: Reads scale with familiar tools like replicas and caching, while bursty, high-contention writes are much harder and invite interviewer probing.
tradeoff: 读扩展的现成工具箱 vs 写扩展的突发/竞争难度

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库的只读拷贝，用来分摊读流量，不承担写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a read-only copy of the database used to absorb read traffic, not writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理器，执行计算指令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, runs computation.

optionExplanations: 这是本题的核心不对称：读扩展沿用副本/缓存这套现成打法，写扩展要面对突发和写写竞争，没有同等成熟的套路。
误解：写入包确实常带更多字段，但真正卡脖子的是磁盘 I/O 和写写竞争，不是包大小本身。
误解：读也要占 CPU 解析查询、占内存做缓存和排序，只是通常比写轻，不是「几乎不占用」。
误解：分片、队列、批处理都是成熟的写扩展手段，换库只是众多选项之一，不是唯一出路。
optionExplanations_en: This names the real asymmetry: reads reuse a mature replica/cache playbook, while writes face bursts and write-write contention with no equally mature toolkit.
Misconception: write payloads can carry more fields, but the real chokepoint is disk I/O and write contention, not packet size.
Misconception: reads still spend CPU parsing queries and memory on caching or sorting — they're usually lighter, not weightless.
Misconception: sharding, queues, and batching are all mature write-scaling tools; swapping databases is one option among many, not the only path.

q: 补全扩展写入的四大策略：
q_en: Fill in the four write-scaling strategies:
text: 扩展写入的四大策略：{{垂直扩展}}与数据库选型、{{分片}}与分区、用队列和{{load shedding}}处理突发、{{批处理}}与层级聚合。
text_en: The four write-scaling strategies: {{vertical scaling}} and database choices, {{sharding}} and partitioning, queues and {{load shedding}} for bursts, and {{batching}} with hierarchical aggregation.
why: 这四招组合起来，能把写入扩展到单台未优化的数据库/服务器远达不到的量级；面试时按这个顺序逐层升级。
why_en: The four write-scaling strategies are vertical scaling with database choices, sharding and partitioning, queues with load shedding for bursts, and batching with hierarchical aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统过载时主动丢弃部分不重要的写入，保住整体可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding is deliberately dropping some low-value writes when the system is overloaded, to keep the rest of it available.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一份数据横向拆到多台服务器，每台只处理一部分写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across multiple servers so each one only handles a portion of the writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给单台机器换更强的硬件来提升上限，例如更多 CPU 核或更高网络带宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical scaling means giving one machine stronger hardware, such as more CPU cores or more network bandwidth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多条写入合成一批提交，减少每条写入都单独付出的事务和刷盘开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batching combines multiple writes into one submission, reducing per-write transaction and flush overhead.

scenario: 面试官问「写入怎么扩展」，你还没算过当前写入 QPS，也没确认单机是否真的撑不住。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks "how would you scale writes", but you haven't yet computed the current write QPS or confirmed a single machine can't handle it.
q: 第一步应该做什么？
q_en: What should be your first move?
options: 跳过估算，直接在写路径前加一层 Kafka 队列缓冲
跳过估算，立刻按 userID 把数据分片到多台机器
先粗略估算写吞吐，看是否真超出单机硬件能力
跳过估算，直接把数据库整体换成 Cassandra
options_en: Skip the math and immediately put a Kafka queue in front of the database
Skip the math and immediately shard the data by userID across machines
Do a rough estimate of write throughput first to see if it truly exceeds one machine's capacity
Skip the math and immediately switch the whole database to Cassandra
why: 先做 back-of-the-envelope：算出实际写吞吐，对照硬件上限，确认真的撞墙了再加复杂度。这向面试官证明你不会过早架构化。
why_en: First do quick back-of-the-envelope math to check whether the write volume actually exceeds modern hardware before adding any architectural complexity.
whenOtherWins: 如果估算显示写入量确实远超单机（比如百万级 QPS），就直接进入分片、队列等横向策略，不必在垂直扩展上纠缠。
tradeoff: 先估算再动手 vs 直接上架构复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，常用来在写入高峰时缓冲请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue often used to buffer write bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户的唯一标识符，常被选作分片或分区的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: userID is a user's unique identifier, commonly chosen as the sharding or partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里快速估算量级的简化计算，用来判断是否真的需要复杂架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Back-of-the-envelope math is a quick order-of-magnitude estimate used to check whether you actually need a more complex architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库，靠追加写而非原地更新拿到写性能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database that trades read performance for write throughput by appending data instead of updating in place.

optionExplanations: Kafka 适合已确认吞吐超限后缓冲突发写入；跳过估算直接上队列等于用缓冲掩盖还没搞清楚的问题。
按 userID 分片是常见写扩展手段，但没算清容量就分片，平白多出运维复杂度换不来收益。
先算清楚写吞吐和单机上限的差距，再决定要不要加复杂度，这是面试里证明你不会过早架构化的第一步。
Cassandra 是为高写吞吐取舍的数据库，但换库前得先确认现有硬件到底撑不撑得住，不能先斩后奏。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka fits once you've confirmed throughput exceeds capacity and need burst buffering; reaching for it before estimating just masks an unconfirmed problem.
Sharding by userID is a real write-scaling move, but doing it before sizing the load just adds operational complexity you may not need.
Sizing the gap between write throughput and single-machine capacity first is what shows the interviewer you won't over-architect prematurely.
Cassandra trades read performance for write throughput, but you should confirm current hardware can't handle it before committing to a swap.

scenario: 你算出目标写入量约为每秒数万次简单写，正打算判断这在不在单机能力范围内，再决定要不要分片。
scenario_en: You calculated a target load of roughly tens of thousands of simple writes per second and need to judge whether that fits on one machine before deciding to shard.
q: 拿什么单机硬件基准来对照，才不会过早下「必须分片」的结论？
q_en: Which single-machine hardware baseline should you compare against so you don't prematurely conclude "we must shard"?
options: 现代云单机常见约 200 核、10Gbit 网卡，可作对照估算的基准
很多人还停留在 4-8 核、机械硬盘的旧印象，误以为几万写/秒就必须立刻分片
云厂商机器和十年前自建机房的规格完全一样，可以直接套用旧的容量经验
硬件规格无所谓，写入量一多就该先加消息队列做缓冲
why: 这是给定的硬件锚点，不是公式推导结果：把你算出的写入 QPS 和约 200 核、10Gbit 网卡的现代单机对照，再决定是否真的要分片。
why_en: Treat 200 cores and a 10Gbit NIC as a sizing anchor, then compare your estimated write QPS against it before jumping to sharding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理器，执行计算指令；写入路径上的序列化、校验、事务处理都要占用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, runs computation, and write-path work like serialization and transaction handling consumes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒可传输约 10 千兆比特数据的网络接口，决定了单机能吞吐多少写入流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A 10Gbit NIC, or Network Interface Card, moves about ten gigabits of data per second and caps how much write traffic one machine can absorb.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐分布式消息队列，用于缓冲突发写入，不是硬件规格问题的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed message queue used to buffer write bursts, not an answer to a hardware-sizing question.

options_en: Modern cloud machines often reach ~200 cores and a 10Gbit NIC — a rough baseline for estimating, not a number to memorize
Many people still picture 4-8 cores and a spinning disk, so they assume tens of thousands of writes/sec must mean sharding right away
Cloud provider machines have the exact same specs as a decade-old self-hosted data center, so old capacity assumptions still apply
Hardware specs don't matter — once write volume rises at all, just add a message queue to buffer it
optionExplanations: 这只是一个粗量级锚点：把算出的写 QPS 拿去和它对照，而不是当成必须背下的精确参数。
误解：这是十年前小机器的印象，现代云主机核数和网卡带宽已经高出一个数量级，几万写/秒未必要分片。
误解：云厂商机型持续迭代，核数、内存、网络带宽都比十年前自建机房高出许多，不能直接套旧经验。
误解：加队列解决的是突发缓冲，不解决稳态硬件是否够用的问题，回答硬件基准题不能跳过硬件本身。
optionExplanations_en: This is just an order-of-magnitude anchor: compare your calculated write QPS against it, not something to memorize as an exact spec.
Misconception: that's a decade-old mental picture; modern cloud cores and NIC bandwidth are an order of magnitude higher, so tens of thousands of writes/sec may not need sharding at all.
Misconception: cloud hardware keeps improving — cores, memory, and bandwidth today dwarf a decade-old self-hosted rig, so old assumptions don't transfer.
Misconception: a queue buffers bursts, it doesn't answer whether steady-state hardware is sufficient — you can't skip the hardware question.

scenario: 你已经论证过现代硬件能扛住当前写入量，但面试官不断把规模往上加码，逼你转向横向扩展。
scenario_en: You already argued modern hardware can absorb the current write load, but the interviewer keeps raising the scale to push you toward horizontal scaling.
q: 正确的应对是？
q_en: What's the right way to respond?
options: 继续和面试官反复辩论，坚持说硬件应该够用
讲清垂直扩展的理由后就顺势转向横向方案
直接拒绝回答面试官提出的横向扩展问题
假装没听到规模在变化，继续只讲垂直扩展
options_en: Keep arguing back and forth with the interviewer that the hardware should be enough
State the case for vertical scaling once, then move on to horizontal strategies
Flatly refuse to answer the interviewer's horizontal-scaling question
Pretend not to notice the scale keeps changing and keep talking only about vertical scaling
why: 很多面试官的评分卡就是考横向扩展，会不断移动球门柱。该做的是先展示垂直扩展的判断力，然后见好就收、转向其他扩展手段。
why_en: Make the case for vertical scaling once, but if the interviewer keeps raising the scale, move on to horizontal strategies instead of arguing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给单台机器换更强的硬件（更多核、更大内存/网卡）来扛更高负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical scaling means giving one machine stronger hardware (more cores, memory, or network capacity) to handle more load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增加更多机器分摊负载，例如分片、多副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling means adding more machines to share the load, such as sharding or replication.

optionExplanations: 误解：面试官的评分卡本就打算考横向扩展，会不断加码，纠缠辩论只会浪费时间、显得不够灵活。
先亮出判断力再顺势转向，是面试官期待的节奏：既展示了垂直扩展的思考，又没有在原地打转。
误解：拒答等于放弃展示后续扩展能力，面试官只会认为你只有一招。
误解：无视追问信号，继续讲已经讲完的内容，等于没听懂面试官在引导话题往下走。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the interviewer's rubric is designed to keep raising the scale — digging in to argue just wastes time and looks inflexible.
Making the case once and then pivoting is the rhythm interviewers expect: it shows judgment on vertical scaling without stalling there.
Misconception: refusing to answer means giving up the chance to show you know the next move, not staying firm.
Misconception: ignoring the follow-up and repeating what you already said means missing that the interviewer is steering you forward.

scenario: 系统写多读少，团队在纠结要不要把主存储从传统关系型数据库换成 Cassandra 来提升写吞吐。
scenario_en: The workload is write-heavy, and the team is debating whether to switch the primary store from a traditional relational database to Cassandra for higher write throughput.
q: Cassandra 写吞吐远超传统关系型数据库，核心机制是？
q_en: Cassandra's write throughput far exceeds a traditional relational database's — what's the core mechanism behind that?
options: 把连接池调得更大，减少每次建立连接的握手开销
把整张表都常驻内存缓存，写入先落内存再异步落盘
追加式 commit log，顺序写盘避开原地更新的寻道
给每一列都自动建二级索引，加快后续按列查询
options_en: Make the connection pool bigger to cut per-connection handshake overhead
Keep the whole table resident in memory and write to memory first, flushing to disk asynchronously
An append-only commit log writes sequentially, skipping the seeks in-place updates need
Automatically build a secondary index on every column to speed up later column-based queries
why: Cassandra 写入先追加到 commit log 并进 memtable，稍后 flush 成 SSTable；顺序写避开随机寻道，所以吞吐高。代价是读路径常要合并多个 SSTable。
why_en: Cassandra appends to a commit log and memtable first, then flushes SSTables later, trading easier writes for more read-side merging.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    W[写请求] --> M[Memtable]
    W --> L[(Append-only commit log)]
    L -->|顺序写盘| D[(磁盘)]
    M -->|稍后 flush| S[(SSTable)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 落盘前先顺序写入的持久化日志，保证写入不丢失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A commit log is an append-only, sequentially written log a database writes to first so a committed write is never lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 内存里的有序写缓冲，写入先进入这里，之后批量刷成磁盘上的 SSTable。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is Cassandra's in-memory sorted write buffer, later flushed to disk as an SSTable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先建立并复用的数据库连接集合，减少连接建立开销，不改变磁盘写入模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection pool is a reused set of open database connections that cuts connection-setup overhead but doesn't change how data is written to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系库常用的索引结构，更新时通常要改写已有页面，容易带来随机 I/O。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is the balanced index structure relational databases commonly use, and updates often rewrite existing pages, causing random I/O.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 把 memtable 定期刷到磁盘生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable, or Sorted String Table, is the immutable sorted file Cassandra periodically flushes a memtable to on disk.

optionExplanations: 误解：连接池只省连接建立的握手开销，不改变数据落盘的方式，撑不起数量级的写吞吐提升。
误解：真正常驻内存的是 memtable 这块写缓冲，不是整张表；异步落盘的是 SSTable，不是缓存命中逻辑。
顺序追加写盘绕开了原地更新的随机寻道，这正是 Cassandra 写吞吐远超关系库的核心机制。
误解：自动建二级索引反而会拖慢写入——每次写都要多维护一份索引结构，方向正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: a bigger connection pool only saves handshake overhead, it doesn't change how data hits disk — nowhere near enough for an order-of-magnitude gain.
Misconception: what actually stays in memory is the memtable write buffer, not the whole table; what flushes asynchronously is the SSTable, not a cache-hit path.
Sequential append-only writes skip the random seeks of in-place updates — that's the actual mechanism behind Cassandra's write throughput.
Misconception: auto-building a secondary index on every column slows writes down further, since each write must now update more index structures — the opposite direction.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 面试官追问「Cassandra 到底比关系型数据库快多少」，想看你是背答案还是懂前提。
scenario_en: The interviewer presses "exactly how much faster is Cassandra than a relational database", testing whether you recite a number or understand the caveats.
q: 同等普通硬件下，Cassandra 与传统关系型数据库的写吞吐量级对比约是？
q_en: On comparable commodity hardware, roughly how does Cassandra's write throughput compare to a traditional relational database's?
options: Cassandra 在追加写、扩展场景通常写吞吐更高；数字只作数量级锚点
两者写吞吐差不多，同等硬件下都大约是 1,000 写/秒
同等硬件下，Cassandra 大约 100 写/秒，关系型能到 10,000 写/秒
同等硬件下，Cassandra 能到 100 万写/秒，而关系型只有 1 写/秒
why: 可以把「Cassandra 常比传统关系库高一个数量级」当口头锚点，但它不是固定公式。真实吞吐取决于硬件、批量写、索引、事务/fsync 和数据模型。
why_en: Use Cassandra being roughly an order of magnitude easier to scale for writes as an anchor, not a fixed benchmark.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于面试估算的粗量级参照，只帮助判断方向，不代表固定 benchmark。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An order-of-magnitude anchor is a rough sizing reference for interview math, not a fixed benchmark.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用表、行、列和关系约束组织数据的数据库，例如 MySQL 或 PostgreSQL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relational database stores data in tables, rows, columns, and relationships, such as MySQL or PostgreSQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 强制把内存中的写入刷到磁盘的系统调用，直接影响持久化写入的实际速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: fsync is the system call that forces buffered writes to disk, and it directly caps real-world durable write speed.

options_en: Cassandra usually reaches higher write throughput in append-heavy, horizontally-scaled workloads; treat the exact number only as an order-of-magnitude anchor
Write throughput is roughly the same for both, at about 1,000 writes/sec on comparable hardware
On comparable hardware, Cassandra reaches about 100 writes/sec while the relational database reaches 10,000
On comparable hardware, Cassandra reaches about 1,000,000 writes/sec while the relational database reaches only 1
optionExplanations: 这只是数量级锚点：真实吞吐还要看硬件、批量写、索引和 fsync 策略，不是固定 benchmark。
误解：两者数量级并不接近——追加写和横向扩展让 Cassandra 通常领先一个数量级以上。
误解：方向刚好反了，Cassandra 靠顺序追加写，写吞吐通常比关系型数据库更高，不是更低。
误解：这组数字夸张到失真，真实差距一般在一个数量级左右，不是六个数量级。
optionExplanations_en: It's only an order-of-magnitude anchor: real throughput still depends on hardware, batching, indexing, and fsync policy — not a fixed benchmark.
Misconception: the two are not actually close — append-only writes and horizontal scaling usually put Cassandra an order of magnitude ahead.
Misconception: this reverses the direction — Cassandra's sequential appends usually give it higher write throughput than a relational database, not lower.
Misconception: this gap is wildly exaggerated; the real difference is usually about one order of magnitude, not six.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 团队把写重的主存储换成了 Cassandra，写吞吐明显上去了；现在要评估这笔交换的代价。
scenario_en: The team switched the write-heavy primary store to Cassandra and write throughput clearly improved; now you need to weigh what that trade cost.
q: 选了 Cassandra 换来高写吞吐，代价是什么？
q_en: Choosing Cassandra for high write throughput comes at what cost?
options: 换成 Cassandra 后写入依然只能在单机上纵向扩容
读性能变差：读常要查多个文件并合并结果，可能比索引良好的关系库慢
写入完全不落盘，进程一重启数据就会消失
Cassandra 不支持任何副本机制，单点故障就会丢数据
options_en: Even after switching to Cassandra, writes can still only scale vertically on one machine
Read performance gets worse: reads often have to check multiple files and merge results, which can be slower than a well-indexed relational database
Writes are never persisted to disk, so data disappears the moment the process restarts
Cassandra has no replication mechanism at all, so a single node failure loses data
why: Cassandra 读一条数据常要检查多个文件再合并，读性能不如索引良好的关系库。用读性能换写性能，正是写重系统想要的交换。
why_en: Cassandra trades read performance for write performance, since reads often check multiple files and merge results.
tradeoff: 写入顺序追加换吞吐 vs 读取合并多个文件的成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高写入吞吐做了取舍的宽列存储 NoSQL 数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column NoSQL database built to trade read performance for high write throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增加更多机器分摊负载；Cassandra 恰恰是为水平扩展设计的，不是它的弱点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling means adding more machines to share load, and it's actually a strength Cassandra is designed around, not a weakness.

optionExplanations: 这其实是反过来的：Cassandra 正是为水平扩展设计的，换库后写入依然能继续横向加节点，不会被困在单机。
读一条数据常要查多个 SSTable 再合并，这正是用读性能换写性能的代价，也是本题要点名的交换。
误解：写入先进 commit log 再落盘，是持久化的，不是纯内存、进程重启就丢。
误解：Cassandra 支持多副本和可调一致性，不是没有副本机制的单点系统。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: Cassandra is built for horizontal scaling, so writes still spread across nodes after the switch — they're not stuck on one machine.
Reads often have to check multiple SSTables and merge them — that's the actual cost of trading read performance for write throughput this question is pointing at.
Misconception: writes go to a commit log before anything else, so they're durable — a restart doesn't wipe them like pure in-memory storage would.
Misconception: Cassandra supports replication with tunable consistency, it's not a single-point system with no replicas.

q: 「写读张力」（write vs. read tension）指的是？
q_en: What does "write vs. read tension" mean?
options: 系统设计里写请求和读请求物理上互斥，不能重叠执行
无论什么场景，读操作的资源开销都必然高于写操作
只要写入量大，就可以完全不设计任何读接口
为写优化往往损害读性能，反之亦然，必须先认清自己的瓶颈是哪边
options_en: Reads and writes are physically mutually exclusive in system design and can never overlap
Read operations always cost more resources than write operations, in every scenario
As long as write volume is high, you can skip designing any read interface at all
Optimizing for writes usually hurts read performance and vice versa, so you must first identify which side is your actual bottleneck
why: 这是扩展写入的根本矛盾：写优化伤读、读优化伤写。先确定瓶颈在哪边再优化，系统的不同部分可能需要不同的取舍。
why_en: Optimizing for writes usually degrades reads and vice versa, so identify which side is your bottleneck and optimize accordingly.
tradeoff: 写优化（追加写/少约束） vs 读优化（索引/约束）

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查询而维护的额外数据结构；每多一个索引，每次写入就要多更新一份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is extra structure maintained to speed up queries, and every added index means one more thing to update on every write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写路径和读路径的优化目标互相牵制：让一边更快，常会让另一边付出代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-versus-read tension means optimizing one path often makes the other path pay a cost.

optionExplanations: 误解：读写请求在系统里是并发处理的，物理互斥不是这里说的张力，真正的张力是优化目标互相牵制。
误解：开销高低取决于负载形态，不是读操作天然更贵；很多写重系统的写路径开销明显更大。
误解：写入量大只是决定要不要扩展写路径，跳过读接口设计和这个问题不是一回事。
这正是写读张力的定义：给写让路（如追加写、少索引）常牺牲读，给读让路又反过来拖慢写。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: reads and writes are handled concurrently in real systems; physical exclusivity isn't the tension being described here.
Misconception: cost depends on the workload shape, not an inherent read/write ranking — many write-heavy systems have the pricier write path.
Misconception: high write volume only decides whether the write path needs scaling; it says nothing about skipping read-interface design.
This is the actual definition of write-vs-read tension: favoring writes (append-only, fewer indexes) often costs reads, and favoring reads costs writes back.

q: 下面哪些数据库类型是为写重/顺序写场景做的取舍？（多选）
q_en: Which of these database types are built as trade-offs for write-heavy, sequential-write workloads? (select all)
options: 时序数据库（InfluxDB、TimescaleDB）：为大量带时间戳的顺序写而生，还内置 delta 编码省存储
日志结构数据库（LevelDB）：追加新数据而非原地更新
列存（ClickHouse）：为分析负载高效地批量写入
传统单机 OLTP 关系库：默认为极端写负载优化
options_en: Time-series databases (InfluxDB, TimescaleDB): built for high-volume timestamped sequential writes, with built-in delta encoding to save storage
Log-structured databases (LevelDB): append new data instead of updating in place
Column stores (ClickHouse): batch writes efficiently for analytics workloads
Traditional single-node OLTP relational databases: optimized by default for extreme write load
why: 时序库、日志结构库、列存都在各自方向上为写做了取舍；通用关系库是为混合负载设计的，并不为极端写负载优化。
why_en: Time-series databases, log-structured stores like LevelDB, and column stores like ClickHouse all trade toward write efficiency, unlike general-purpose relational databases.

rows: 读写混合，非极端写优化

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为带时间戳的高频顺序写入优化的时序数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InfluxDB and TimescaleDB are time-series databases optimized for high-frequency, timestamped sequential writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只存相邻数值之间的差，而不是完整数值，用来压缩时序数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta encoding stores only the difference between consecutive values instead of full values, to compress time-series data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志结构存储引擎，靠追加写和后台合并代替原地更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LevelDB is a log-structured storage engine that appends writes and merges them in the background instead of updating in place.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向分析场景的列式数据库，擅长批量写入和大范围扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ClickHouse is a column-oriented database built for analytics, good at batched writes and large scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列而不是按行组织数据的存储方式，适合批量写入和大范围分析扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A column store organizes data by column rather than row, which suits batched writes and large analytical scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向高频小事务读写的工作负载类型，例如下单、转账。
